params.name: early_media
params.doc: Should be early media (any provisional reply with body) accounted too ?

params.name: failed_transaction_flag
params.doc: Per transaction flag which says if the transaction should be accounted also in case of failure (SIP status code >= 300). This flag triggers accounting when the whole transaction fails (on the server side).

params.name: failed_filter
params.doc: A string of failure response codes from 300 to 999 separated by commas. Failed transaction will not be accounted if its response code is in the list even when failed_transaction_flag is set.

params.name: report_ack
params.doc: Shall acc attempt to account e2e ACKs too ? Note that this is really only an attempt, as e2e ACKs may take a different path (unless RR enabled) and mismatch original INVITE (e2e ACKs are a separate transaction). The flag for accounting has to be set for each ACK as well.

params.name: report_cancels
params.doc: By default, CANCEL reporting is disabled -- most accounting applications wants to see INVITE's cancellation status. Turn on if you explicitly want to account CANCEL transactions.

params.name: detect_direction
params.doc: Controls the direction detection for sequential requests. If enabled (non zero value), for sequential requests with upstream direction (from callee to caller), the FROM and TO will be swapped (the direction will be preserved as in the original request).

params.name: acc_prepare_flag
params.doc: Per transaction flag which says if the transaction may be accounted later, with flags set in TM module specific routes (e.g., like failure_route). If this flag is not set and acc or missed_call flag are not set either in request route block, there is no way to mark the request for transaction later unless you set acc_prepare_always. If either acc or missed_call flags are set in request route block, there is no need to set this flag.

params.name: acc_prepare_always
params.doc: Prepare all request even if acc_prepare_flag is not set to mark the request for transaction later.

params.name: acc_extra_nullable
params.doc: If set to 1, the database acc extra fields are set to NULL if the corresponding script variable is not defined or has $null value. If set to 0, the value is saved as empty string (the existing behavior).

params.name: multi_leg_info
params.doc: Defines the AVP set to be used in per-call-leg accounting. See Section 3, “Multi Call-Legs accounting” for a detailed description of the Multi Call-Legs accounting.

params.name: log_flag
params.doc: Request flag which needs to be set to account a transaction via syslog.

params.name: log_missed_flag
params.doc: Request flag which needs to be set to account missed calls via syslog. This can be used to e.g. account failures during the call setup phase from the callee (client) side, for example if you do forking to several destinations.

params.name: log_level
params.doc: Log level at which accounting messages are issued to syslog.

params.name: log_facility
params.doc: Log facility to which accounting messages are issued to syslog. This allows to easily separate the accounting specific logging from the other log messages.

params.name: log_extra
params.doc: Extra values to be logged. See section Section 2, “Extra accounting” for more details.

params.name: db_flag
params.doc: Request flag which needs to be set to account a transaction -- database specific.

params.name: db_missed_flag
params.doc: Request flag which needs to be set to account missed calls via database. This can be used to e.g. account failures during the call setup phase from the callee (client) side, for example if you do forking to several destinations.

params.name: db_table_acc
params.doc: Table name of accounting successful calls -- database specific. It can contain config variables that will be evaluated at runtime.

params.name: db_table_missed_calls
params.doc: Table name for accounting missed calls -- database specific. It can contain config variables that will be evaluated at runtime.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: SQL address -- database specific. If it is set to NULL or empty string, the SQL support is disabled.

params.name: db_version_check
params.doc: Whether to validate database schema versions when the module initializes or not.

params.name: acc_method_column
params.doc: Column name in accounting table to store the request's method name as string.

params.name: acc_from_tag_column
params.doc: Column name in accounting table to store the From header TAG parameter.

params.name: acc_to_tag_column
params.doc: Column name in accounting table to store the To header TAG parameter.

params.name: acc_callid_column
params.doc: Column name in accounting table to store the request's Callid value.

params.name: acc_sip_code_column
params.doc: Column name in accounting table to store the final reply's numeric code value in string format.

params.name: acc_sip_reason_column
params.doc: Column name in accounting table to store the final reply's reason phrase value.

params.name: acc_time_column
params.doc: Column name in accounting table to store the time stamp of the transaction completion in date-time format.

params.name: db_extra
params.doc: Extra values to be logged into database - DB specific. See section Section 2, “Extra accounting” for more details.

params.name: db_insert_mode
params.doc: If set to 1, use INSERT DELAYED to add records to accounting tables when the DB driver has support for it. If no INSERT DELAYED support is offered by DB driver, then standard INSERT is used. Beware that MySQL InnoDB engine doesn't support INSERT DELAYED, thus be sure the acc tables are defined with different type (e.g., MyISAM).

params.name: cdr_enable
params.doc: Enable CDR reporting - one record per call reported to "acc_cdrs" table, relying on dialog module.

params.name: cdr_skip
params.doc: Skip cdr generation for dialogs with this dlg_var set.

params.name: cdr_expired_dlg_enable
params.doc: Should CDR-based logging be enabled in case of expired dialogs? * 0 - off (default). * 1 - on.

params.name: cdr_start_on_confirmed
params.doc: Should the start time be taken from the time when the dialog is created, or when the dialog is confirmed? * 0 - use time of dialog creation (default). * 1 - use time of dialog confirmation.

params.name: cdr_facility
params.doc: Log facility to which CDR messages are issued to syslog. This allows to easily separate CDR-specific logging from the other log messages.

params.name: cdr_extra
params.doc: Set of pseudo-variables defining custom CDR fields. See Section 4.2, “CDR Extra” for more details.

params.name: cdr_extra_nullable
params.doc: Should custom CDR fields be saved as NULL?

params.name: cdr_start_id
params.doc: Modifying the id which is used to store the start time.

params.name: cdr_end_id
params.doc: Modifying the id which is used to store the end time.

params.name: cdr_duration_id
params.doc: Modify the id which is used to store the duration.

params.name: cdr_duration_mode
params.doc: Modify the precision of the duration stored for the call.

params.name: cdr_log_enable
params.doc: Control if CDR-based accounting should be written to syslog.

params.name: cdrs_table
params.doc: Name of db table to store dialog-based CDRs.

params.name: time_mode
params.doc: Store additional value related to the time of event.

params.name: time_attr
params.doc: Name of the syslog attribute or database column where to store additional value related to the time of event.

params.name: time_exten
params.doc: Name of the syslog attribute or database column where to store extended value related to the time of event.

params.name: time_format
params.doc: Specify the format to print the time for time_mode 3 or 4.

params.name: reason_from_hf
params.doc: Tells where to take sip_reason from. If value is 0, sip_reason is taken from status line. Otherwise, sip_reason is taken from Reason header field(s) if present. Currently only the first Reason header is used.

params.name: clone_msg
params.doc: If set to 1, request structure from transaction is cloned temporarily in the callback to get acc attributes. It is required if you account values from SIP headers to avoid concurrent access to the shared memory transaction structure, specially when accounting 1xx events. If set to 0, it uses directly the shared memory structure, be sure you store all needed attributes in AVPs/XAVPs inside request route.

params.name: cdr_on_failed
params.doc: If set to 1, the module stores the CDR for a failed dialog (calls not answered). If set to 0, those records are not stored, only those for answered calls.

params.name: acc_extra_size
params.doc: Set the maximum number of extra attributes that can be stored in the accounting record (event accounting record). It is related to log_extra and db_extra module parameters.

params.name: cdr_extra_size
params.doc: Set the maximum number of extra attributes that can be stored in the call data record (cdr by dialog module). It is related to cdr_extra module parameter.

functions.name: acc_log_request
functions.doc: acc_request reports on a request, for example, it can be used to report on missed calls to off-line users who are replied 404 - Not Found. To avoid multiple reports on UDP request retransmission, you would need to embed the action in stateful processing.

functions.name: acc_db_request
functions.doc: Like acc_log_request, acc_db_request reports on a request. The report is sent to database at “db_url”, in the table referred to in the second action parameter.

functions.name: acc_request
functions.doc: Wrapper around acc_log_request and acc_db_request functions, writing the accounting record to LOG and DATABASE backends. If “db_url” parameter is not set, the acc record is written only to LOG backend.

params.name: diameter_flag
params.doc: Request flag which needs to be set to account a transaction -- DIAMETER specific.

params.name: diameter_missed_flag
params.doc: Request flag which needs to be set to account missed calls -- DIAMETER specific.

params.name: diameter_client_host
params.doc: Hostname of the machine where the DIAMETER Client is running -- DIAMETER specific.

params.name: diameter_client_port
params.doc: Port number where the Diameter Client is listening -- DIAMETER specific.

params.name: diameter_extra
params.doc: Extra values to be logged via DIAMETER - DIAMETER specific. See section the section about extra accounting in 'acc' module for more details.

functions.name: acc_diam_request
functions.doc: Like acc_log_request, acc_diam_request reports on a request. It reports to the configured Diameter server.

params.name: acc_flag
params.doc: Request flag which needs to be set to account a transaction in acc_json. See acc_output_mqueue and acc_output_syslog

params.name: acc_missed_flag
params.doc: Request flag which needs to be set to account missed calls in acc_json. See acc_output_mqueue and acc_output_syslog

params.name: acc_extra
params.doc: Extra values to be added to the json dictionary.

params.name: acc_pre_encoded_prefix
params.doc: Prefix to identify values that will be considered to be already json encoded.

params.name: acc_time_mode
params.doc: Store additional value related to the time of event.

params.name: acc_time_format
params.doc: Specify the format to print the time for time_mode 3 or 4.

params.name: acc_output_mqueue
params.doc: Requires the mqueue module. The acc module will queue json acc events in the specified mqueue. Using a rtimer module exec you can access the queue and process them.

params.name: acc_output_syslog
params.doc: Control if the output of acc json should be sent to syslog. This is not dependent on Kamailio global logging settings, we can use syslog even if Kamailio is not daemonized and/or logging is done to sdtout stderr.

params.name: acc_log_facility
params.doc: Log facility to which accounting messages are issued to syslog. This allows to easily separate the accounting specific logging from the other log messages.

params.name: acc_log_level
params.doc: Log level at which accounting messages are issued to syslog.

params.name: cdr_enable
params.doc: Enable CDR reporting - one record per call is reported, relying on dialog module.

params.name: cdr_skip
params.doc: Skip cdr generation for dialogs with this dlg_var set.

params.name: cdr_extra
params.doc: Set of pseudo-variables defining custom CDR fields.

params.name: cdr_pre_encoded_prefix
params.doc: Prefix to identify values that will be considered to be already json encoded.

params.name: cdr_expired_dlg_enable
params.doc: Should CDR-based logging be enabled in case of expired dialogs?

params.name: cdr_output_mqueue
params.doc: Requires the mqueue module. The acc module will queue json cdr events in the specified mqueue. Using a rtimer module exec you can access the queue and process them.

params.name: cdr_output_syslog
params.doc: The acc module will log json cdr events to syslog.

params.name: cdr_log_facility
params.doc: Log facility to which accounting messages are issued to syslog. This allows to easily separate the accounting specific logging from the other log messages.

params.name: cdr_log_level
params.doc: Log level at which accounting messages are issued to syslog.

params.name: radius_config
params.doc: This parameter is radius specific. Path to radius client configuration file, set the referred config file correctly and specify there address of server, shared secret (should equal that in /usr/local/etc/raddb/clients for freeRadius servers) and dictionary, see etc for an example of config file and dictionary.

params.name: radius_flag
params.doc: Request flag which needs to be set to account a transaction -- RADIUS specific.

params.name: radius_missed_flag
params.doc: Request flag which needs to be set to account missed calls -- RADIUS specific.

params.name: service_type
params.doc: Radius service type used for accounting.

params.name: radius_extra
params.doc: Extra values to be logged via RADIUS - RADIUS specific.

params.name: rad_time_mode
params.doc: Radius Event-Timestamp for accounting.

functions.name: acc_rad_request
functions.doc: Like acc_log_request of acc module, acc_rad_request reports on a SIP request event. It reports to radius server as configured in “radius_config”.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: Database URL.

params.name: user_column
params.doc: Name of the column storing username.

params.name: domain_column
params.doc: Name of the column storing user's domain.

params.name: alias_user_column
params.doc: Name of the column storing alias username.

params.name: alias_domain_column
params.doc: Name of the column storing alias domain.

params.name: use_domain
params.doc: Specifies whether to use or not the domain from R-URI when searching for alias. If set to 0, the domain from R-URI is not used, if set to 1 the domain from R-URI is used.

params.name: domain_prefix
params.doc: Specifies the prefix to be stripped from the domain in R-URI before doing the search.

params.name: append_branches
params.doc: If the alias resolves to many SIP IDs, the first is replacing the R-URI, the rest are added as branches.

functions.name: alias_db_lookup
functions.doc: The function takes the R-URI and search to see whether it is an alias or not. If it is an alias for a local user, the R-URI is replaced with user's SIP uri.

functions.name: alias_db_find
functions.doc: The function is very similar to alias_db_lookup(), but instead of using fixed input (RURI) and output (RURI) is able to get the input SIP URI from a pseudo-variable and place the result back also in a pseudo-variable.

params.name: load
params.doc: Set the path to the JavaScript file to be loaded at startup. Then you can use jsdt_run(function, params) to execute a function from the script at runtime. If you use it for KEMI configuration, then it has to include the required functions.

params.name: loaddir
params.doc: Set the path to the folder containing JavaScript files to be loaded at startup. All .js files in the folder will be loaded and combined into a single javascript script. Then you can use jsdt_run(function, params) to execute a function from the script at runtime. If you use it for KEMI configuration, then it has to include the required functions.

params.name: mode
params.doc: Control if the API to load JavaScript module (nodejs interface) is initialized or not.

functions.name: jsdt_dofile
functions.doc: Execute the JavaScript script stored in 'path'. The parameter can be a string with pseudo-variables evaluated at runtime.

functions.name: jsdt_dostring
functions.doc: Execute the JavaScript script stored in parameter. The parameter can be a string with pseudo-variables.

functions.name: jsdt_run
functions.doc: Execute the JS function 'func' giving params as parameters. There can be up to 3 string parameters. The function must exist in the script loaded at startup via parameter 'load'. Parameters can be strings with pseudo-variables that are evaluated at runtime.

functions.name: jsdt_runstring
functions.doc: Execute the JS script stored in parameter. The parameter can be a string with pseudo-variables. The script is executed in JS context specific to loaded JS files at startup.

params.name: load
params.doc: Set the path to the Lua script to be loaded at startup. Then you can use lua_run(function, params) to execute a function from the script at runtime. The script can be in Lua-source or bytecode.

params.name: reload
params.doc: If reload is 1 enables the ability to reload the scripts using the RPC app_lua.reload command. To disable reload feature, set this parameter to 0.

params.name: log_mode
params.doc: Control what is printed in log messages. If bit 1 is set, then the module prints debug messages for each KEMI export.

functions.name: lua_dofile
functions.doc: Execute the Lua script stored in 'path'. The parameter can be a string with pseudo-variables evaluated at runtime.

functions.name: lua_dostring
functions.doc: Execute the Lua script stored in parameter. The parameter can be a string with pseudo-variables.

functions.name: lua_run
functions.doc: Execute the Lua function 'func' giving 'params' as parameters. There can be up to 3 string parameters after 'func' (overall, max 4 params, first is the function). The function must exist in the Lua script loaded at startup via parameter 'load'. Parameters can be strings with pseudo-variables that are evaluated at runtime.

functions.name: lua_runstring
functions.doc: Execute the Lua script stored in parameter. The parameter can be a string with pseudo-variables. The script is executed in Lua context specific to loaded Lua files at startup.

params.name: filename
params.doc: This is the file name of your script. This may be set once only, but it may include an arbitrary number of functions and “use” as many Perl module as necessary.

params.name: modpath
params.doc: The path to the Perl modules included (Kamailio.pm et.al). It is not absolutely crucial to set this path, as you may install the Modules in Perl's standard path, or update the “%INC” variable from within your script. Using this module parameter is the standard behavior, though. Multiple paths may be specified by separating them with a “:” character. The maximum is 10 paths.

params.name: reset_cycles
params.doc: The number of execution cycles after which the embedded perl interpreter is reset. Sometimes is hard to track the scope of variables in all used perl modules and that can result in leaks of system memory. Resetting the interpreter cleans the memory space.

params.name: perl_destroy_func
params.doc: The name of Perl function to be executed before the interpreter is re-initialized (reset -- see reset_cycles parameter) at runtime. This could be useful to clean global variables or file descriptors from the Perl script.

params.name: parse_mode
params.doc: Control how to behave on perl_parse() return code - on some versions it is the value for application exit and can break reloading.

params.name: warn_mode
params.doc: Allows to enable warning for perl_parse(). If set to 1, "-w" is passed to perl_parse() and detected warnings in the Perl script should be printed to the log. If set to 1, then "-W" is passed to perl_parse().

functions.name: perl_exec_simple
functions.doc: Calls a perl function without passing it the current SIP message. May be used for very simple simple requests that do not have to fiddle with the message themselves, but rather return information values about the environment.

functions.name: perl_exec
functions.doc: Calls a perl function with passing it the current SIP message. The SIP message is reflected by a Perl module that gives you access to the information in the current SIP message (Kamailio::Message).

params.name: load
params.doc: The path to the file with Python code to be executed from configuration file.

params.name: script_name
params.doc: This is same as "load" parameter, kept for backward compatibility with the older versions of the module.

params.name: mod_init_function
params.doc: The Python function to be executed by this module when it is initialized by Kamailio.

params.name: child_init_method
params.doc: The Python function to be executed by this module when a new worker process (child) is initialized by Kamailio.

functions.name: python_exec
functions.doc: Execute the Python function with the name given by the parameter 'method'. Optionally can be provided a second string with parameters to be passed to the Python function.

params.name: load
params.doc: The path to the file with Python code to be executed from configuration file.

params.name: script_name
params.doc: This is same as "load" parameter, kept for backward compatibility with the older versions of the module.

params.name: mod_init_function
params.doc: The Python function to be executed by this module when it is initialized by Kamailio.

params.name: child_init_method
params.doc: The Python function to be executed by this module when a new worker process (child) is initialized by Kamailio.

params.name: threads_mode
params.doc: Control how locking for Python interpreter threads in done. If set to 1, use Py_BLOCK_THREADS/Py_UNBLOCK_THREADS (new mode added for v6.0.x). If set to 0, use PyGILState_Ensure()/PyGILState_Release() (the mode implemented initially).

functions.name: python_exec
functions.doc: Execute the Python function with the name given by the parameter 'method'. Optionally can be provided a second string with parameters to be passed to the Python function.

params.name: load
params.doc: The path to the file with Python code to be executed from configuration file.

params.name: script_init
params.doc: The name of the Python function to be executed when the script is loaded or reloaded.

params.name: script_child_init
params.doc: The name of the Python function to be executed when Kamailio forks child processes at startup and when the script is reloaded.

params.name: threads_mode
params.doc: Control how locking for Python interpreter threads in done. If set to 1, use Py_BLOCK_THREADS/Py_UNBLOCK_THREADS (new mode added for v6.0.x). If set to 0, use PyGILState_Ensure()/PyGILState_Release() (the mode implemented initially).

functions.name: app_python3s_exec
functions.doc: Execute the Python function with the name given by the parameter 'method'. Optionally can be provided a second string with the parameter to be passed to the Python function.

params.name: load
params.doc: Set the path to the Ruby file to be loaded at startup. Then you can use Ruby_run(function, params) to execute a function from the script at runtime. If you use it for KEMI configuration, then it has to include the required functions.

params.name: xval_mode
params.doc: Control if the external sub-module functions returning extended-values should propagate their string return value (when set to 0) or be replaced by NULL/nil (when set to 1).

params.name: modproc
params.doc: The name of or the path to the required per-process API module.

functions.name: ruby_run
functions.doc: Execute the Ruby function 'func' giving params as parameters. There can be up to 3 string parameters. The function must exist in the script loaded at startup via parameter 'load'. Parameters can be strings with pseudo-variables that are evaluated at runtime.

params.name: workers
params.doc: Number of worker processes to be started to handle the asynchronous tasks for async_route() and async_sleep().

params.name: ms_timer
params.doc: Enables millisecond timer for async_ms_sleep() and async_ms_route() functions. The integer value is the timer resolution in milliseconds. A smaller timer resolution will generate a higher load on the system. If you set ms_timer to 1 you will get a timer with 1 millisecond resolution, a setting of 20 provides a resolution of 20ms.

params.name: return
params.doc: The value to be returned by async functions on success. It does not apply for async data functions, only for those that suspend the SIP transaction.

params.name: mode
params.doc: Control if the module should bind (0) to tm or not (1). It may not be needed to use tm functions (e.g., when needing async_tkv_emit() only).

functions.name: async_route
functions.doc: Simulate a sleep of 'seconds' and then continue the processing of the SIP request with the route[routename]. In case of internal errors, the function returns false, otherwise the function exits the execution of the script at that moment (return 0 behaviour).

functions.name: async_ms_route
functions.doc: Simulate a sleep of 'milliseconds' and then continue the processing of the SIP request with the route[routename]. In case of internal errors, the function returns false, otherwise the function exits the execution of the script at that moment (return 0 behaviour). This function works only if the ms_timer parameter has a value greater than 0.

functions.name: async_sleep
functions.doc: Simulate a sleep of 'seconds' and then continue the processing of SIP request with the next action. Note that the processing continues till the last action in the current route block. Consider using async_route() instead if you want to control better what is executed after the wait time. Beacuse the execution is resumed in another process, do not use private memory variables before and after the async sleep.

functions.name: async_ms_sleep
functions.doc: Similar to async_sleep(), but with a 'milliseconds' parameter. This function works only if the ms_timer parameter has a value greater than 0.

functions.name: async_task_route
functions.doc: Continue the processing of the SIP request with the route[routename] in one of the processes from first group of core asynchronous framework. The core parameter async_workers has to be set to enable asynchronous framework. The task is executed as soon as a process from asynchronous framework is idle, there is no wait time for the task like for async_route(...).

functions.name: async_task_group_route
functions.doc: Similar to async_task_route(), but allows to specify the name of the group for asynchronous workers. See also 'async_workers_group' core global parameter.

functions.name: async_task_data
functions.doc: Send the data to an asynchronous task process (in the first group) that executes the route[rountename] and makes the data available via $async(data).

functions.name: async_task_group_data
functions.doc: Similar to async_task_data(), but allows to specify the name of the group for asynchronous workers. See also 'async_workers_group' core global parameter.

functions.name: async_tkv_emit
functions.doc: Emit a type-key-value event.

params.name: auth_checks_register
params.doc: See description of parameter auth_checks_in_dlg.

params.name: auth_checks_no_dlg
params.doc: See description of parameter auth_checks_in_dlg.

params.name: auth_checks_in_dlg
params.doc: These three module parameters control which optional integrity checks will be performed on the SIP message carrying digest response during SIP MD5 digest authentication. auth_checks_register controls integrity checks to be performed on REGISTER messages, auth_checks_no_dlg controls which optional integrity checks will be performed on SIP requests that have no To header field or no To tag (in other words the requests either establishing or outside dialogs). auth_checks_in_dlg controls which integrity checks will be performed on SIP requests within dialogs, such as BYE or re-INVITE. The default value for all three parameters is 0 (old behaviour, no extra checks). The set of integrity checks that can be performed on REGISTERs is typically different from sets of integrity checks that can be performed for other SIP request types, hence we have three independent module parameters.

params.name: qop
params.doc: If set, enable qop for challenges: each challenge will include a qop parameter. This is the recommended way, but some older non rfc3261 compliant UAs might get confused and might not authenticate properly if qop is enabled.

params.name: nonce_count
params.doc: If enabled the received nc value is remembered and checked against the older value (for a successful authentication the received nc must be greater than the previously received one, see rfc2617 for more details). This will provide protection against replay attacks while still allowing credentials caching at the UA side.

params.name: one_time_nonce
params.doc: If set to 1 nonce reuse is disabled: each nonce is allowed only once, in the first response to a challenge. All the messages will be challenged, even retransmissions. Stateful mode should be used, to catch retransmissions before the authentication checks (using t_newtran() before the authentication checks and sending all the replies with t_reply()).

params.name: nid_pool_no
params.doc: Controls the number of partitions for the nonce_count and one_time_nonce arrays (it's common to both of them to reduce the nonce size).

params.name: nc_array_size
params.doc: Maximum number of in-flight nonces for nonce_count. It represents the maximum nonces for which state will be kept. When this number is exceeded, state for the older nonces will be discarded to make space for new ones (see nonce_count for more details).

params.name: nc_array_order
params.doc: Equivalent to nc_array_size, but instead of directly specifying the size, its value is the power at which 2 should be raised (log2(nc_array_size)).

params.name: otn_in_flight_no
params.doc: Maximum number of in-flight nonces for one_time_nonce. It represents the maximum number of nonces remembered for the one-time-nonce check. When this number is exceeded, information about older nonces will be discarded and overwritten with information about the new generated ones (see one_time_nonce for more details).

params.name: otn_in_flight_order
params.doc: Equivalent to otn_in_flight_no, but instead of directly specifying the size, its value is the power at which 2 should be raised (log2(otn_in_flight_no)).

params.name: secret
params.doc: Secret phrase used to calculate the nonce value used to challenge the client for authentication.

params.name: nonce_expire
params.doc: Nonces have limited lifetime. After a given period of time nonces will be considered invalid. This is to protect replay attacks. Credentials containing a stale nonce will be not authorized, but the user agent will be challenged again. This time the challenge will contain stale parameter which will indicate to the client that it doesn't have to disturb user by asking for username and password, it can recalculate credentials using existing username and password.

params.name: nonce_auth_max_drift
params.doc: Maximum difference in seconds between a nonce creation time and the current time, if the nonce creation time appears to be in the future.

params.name: force_stateless_reply
params.doc: If set to 1, www_challenge() and proxy_challenge() functions send reply statelessly no matter if transaction exists or not. If set to 0 (default), reply is sent statefully if transaction exists and statelessly otherwise.

params.name: realm_prefix
params.doc: Prefix to be automatically stripped from the realm. As an alternative to SRV records (not all SIP clients support SRV lookup), a subdomain of the master domain can be defined for SIP purposes (like sip.mydomain.net pointing to same IP address as the SRV record for mydomain.net). By ignoring the realm_prefix “sip.”, at authentication, sip.example.com will be equivalent to example.com .

params.name: use_domain
params.doc: If set to 1, pv_auth_check() uses domain parts of the URIs to check user identity.

params.name: algorithm
params.doc: Configure hash algorithm used for digest authentication. Possible values are "MD5", "SHA-256", "SHA-512" or "SHA-512-256". If left empty MD5 is used. If specified, the specified algorithm is used and is also put in the 'algorithm' field of the challenge header.

params.name: add_authinfo_hdr
params.doc: Should an Authentication-Info header be added on 200 OK responses? The Authentication-Info header offers mutual authentication. The server proves to the client that it knows the user's secret.

functions.name: consume_credentials
functions.doc: This function removes previously authorized credential headers from the message being processed by the server. That means that the downstream message will not contain credentials there were used by this server. This ensures that the proxy will not reveal information about credentials used to downstream elements and also the message will be a little bit shorter. The function must be called after www_authorize, proxy_authorize, www_authenticate or proxy_authenticate.

functions.name: has_credentials
functions.doc: This function returns true if the request has Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header with provided realm. The parameter can be string with pseudo-variables.

functions.name: www_challenge
functions.doc: The function challenges a user agent. It will generate a WWW-Authorize header field containing a digest challenge, it will put the header field into a response generated from the request the server is processing and send the 401 reply. Upon reception of such a reply the user agent should compute credentials and retry the request. For more information regarding digest authentication see RFC2617. See module parameter force_stateless_reply regarding sending of the reply.

functions.name: proxy_challenge
functions.doc: The function challenges a user agent. It will generate a Proxy-Authorize header field containing a digest challenge, it will put the header field into a response generated from the request the server is processing and send the 407 reply. Upon reception of such a reply the user agent should compute credentials and retry the request. For more information regarding digest authentication see RFC2617. See module parameter force_stateless_reply regarding sending of the reply.

functions.name: auth_challenge
functions.doc: The function challenges a user agent for authentication. It combines the functions www_challenge() and proxy_challenge(), by calling internally the first one for REGISTER requests and the second one for the rest of other request types. In other words, it challenges for authentication by sending a 401 reply for REGISTER requests and 407 reply for the other types of SIP requests.

functions.name: pv_www_authenticate
functions.doc: The function verifies credentials according to RFC2617. If the credentials are verified successfully then the function will succeed and mark the credentials as authorized (marked credentials can be later used by some other functions). If the function was unable to verify the credentials for some reason then it will fail and the script should call www_challenge which will challenge the user again.

functions.name: pv_proxy_authenticate
functions.doc: The function verifies credentials according to RFC2617. If the credentials are verified successfully then the function will succeed and mark the credentials as authorized (marked credentials can be later used by some other functions). If the function was unable to verify the credentials for some reason then it will fail and the script should call proxy_challenge which will challenge the user again. For more about the negative return codes, see the above function.

functions.name: pv_auth_check
functions.doc: The function combines the functionalities of pv_www_authenticate and pv_proxy_authenticate, first being executed if the SIP request is a REGISTER, the second for the rest.

functions.name: auth_get_www_authenticate
functions.doc: Build WWW-Authentication header and set the resulting value in 'pvdest' pseudo-variable parameter.

functions.name: auth_algorithm
functions.doc: Set hash algorithm used for digest authentication thus overriding algorithm parameter. Possible values are the same as those of algorithm parameter. The parameter may be a pseudo variable.

params.name: ens_registry_address
params.doc: ENS Registry contract address for the target blockchain network. This contract is used to resolve ENS domain ownership and handle the initial ownership lookup.

params.name: rpc_url
params.doc: RPC endpoint URL for blockchain network communication. Used for all ENS registry and contract calls via JSON-RPC eth_call method. The module automatically detects and interacts with Name Wrapper contracts when needed.

params.name: signature_timeout
params.doc: Timeout in seconds for signature validation. Signatures older than this timeout will be rejected to prevent replay attacks. The timestamp is extracted from the X-Data header and compared against the current system time.

params.name: debug_mode
params.doc: Enable debug logging for authentication operations. When enabled, detailed information about ENS resolution, signature verification, and authentication steps will be logged. Warning: May log sensitive authentication data.

functions.name: arnacon_authenticate
functions.doc: Authenticates a user by verifying ENS domain ownership through cryptographic signature validation. This function implements the core authentication logic by resolving ENS ownership, recovering the signer's address from the provided signature, and validating that the signer owns the specified ENS domain.

functions.name: arnacon_user_exists
functions.doc: Checks if an ENS domain has an owner, effectively verifying if the user exists in the ENS system. This function performs ENS resolution to determine if the domain is registered and has a valid owner address (not the zero address).

params.name: db_url
params.doc: This is URL of the database to be used. Value of the parameter depends on the database module used. For example for mysql and postgres modules this is something like mysql://username:password@host:port/database. For dbtext module (which stores data in plaintext files) it is directory in which the database resides.

params.name: user_column
params.doc: This is the name of the column holding usernames. Default value is fine for most people. Use the parameter if you really need to change it.

params.name: domain_column
params.doc: This is the name of the column holding domains of users. Default value is fine for most people. Use the parameter if you really need to change it.

params.name: password_column
params.doc: This is the name of the column holding passwords. Passwords can be either stored as plain text or pre-calculated HA1 strings. HA1 strings are MD5 hashes of username, password, and realm. HA1 strings are more safe because the server doesn't need to know plaintext passwords and they cannot be obtained from HA1 strings.

params.name: password_column_2
params.doc: As described in the previous section this parameter contains name of column holding pre-calculated HA1 string that were calculated including the domain in the username. This parameter is used only when calculate_ha1 is set to 0 and user agent send a credentials containing the domain in the username.

params.name: calculate_ha1
params.doc: This parameter tells the server whether it should use a pre-calculated HA1 string or plaintext passwords for authentication.

params.name: use_domain
params.doc: If true (not 0), domain will be also used when looking up in the subscriber table. If you have a multi-domain setup, it is strongly recommended to turn on this parameter to avoid username overlapping between domains.

params.name: load_credentials
params.doc: This parameter specifies of credentials to be fetch from database when the authentication is performed. The loaded credentials will be stored in AVPs. If the AVP name is not specifically given, it will be used a NAME AVP with the same name as the column name.

params.name: version_table
params.doc: If set to 0, the module will skip checking the version for subscriber table.

params.name: force_generate_avps
params.doc: If set to different than 0, the module will fetch user DB attributes even if authentication failed.

functions.name: www_authenticate
functions.doc: Name alias: www_authorize(realm, table)

functions.name: www_authorize
functions.doc: It is same function as www_authenticate(realm, table). This name is kept for backward compatibility, since it was named this way first time by it actually does user authentication.

functions.name: proxy_authenticate
functions.doc: Name alias: proxy_authorize(realm, table)

functions.name: proxy_authorize
functions.doc: It is same function as proxy_authenticate(realm, table). This name is kept for backward compatibility, since it was named this way first time but it actually does user authentication.

functions.name: auth_check
functions.doc: The function combines the functionalities of www_authenticate and proxy_authenticate, first being executed if the SIP request is a REGISTER, the second for the rest.

functions.name: is_subscriber
functions.doc: The function checks if there is a subscriber corresponding to the AoR in uri parameter. It uses same database connection as for authentication functions.

params.name: diameter_client_host
params.doc: Hostname of the machine where the DIAMETER Client is running.

params.name: diameter_client_port
params.doc: Port number where the DIAMETER Client is listening.

params.name: use_domain
params.doc: Specifies whether the domain name part of URI is used when checking the user's privileges.

functions.name: diameter_www_authorize
functions.doc: SIP Server checks for authorization having a DIAMETER server in backend. If no credentials are provided inside the SIP request then a challenge is sent back to UAC. If the credentials don't match the ones computed by DISC then “403 Forbidden” is sent back.

functions.name: diameter_proxy_authorize
functions.doc: SIP Proxy checks for authorization having a DIAMETER server in backend. If no credentials are provided inside the SIP request then a challenge is sent back to UAC. If the credentials don't match the ones computed by DISC then “403 Forbidden” is sent back. For more about the negative return codes, see the above function.

functions.name: diameter_is_user_in
functions.doc: The method performs group membership checking with DISC.

params.name: secret
params.doc: The shared secret to use for generating credentials. This parameter can be set multiple times - this enables the secret used for new credentials to be changed without causing existing credentials to stop working. The last secret set is the first that will be tried.

params.name: username_format
params.doc: The format of the username in the web-service response.

params.name: sha_algorithm
params.doc: The SHA algorithm to be used for the Hash.

functions.name: autheph_proxy
functions.doc: This function performs proxy authentication.

functions.name: autheph_www
functions.doc: This function performs WWW digest authentication.

functions.name: autheph_check
functions.doc: This function combines the functionalities of autheph_www and autheph_proxy, the first being executed if the SIP request is a REGISTER, the second for the rest.

functions.name: autheph_authenticate
functions.doc: This function performs non-digest ephemeral authentication. This may be used when digest authentication cannot. For example, during WebSocket handshake the username may be part of the requested URI and the password presented in a Cookie: header.

functions.name: autheph_check_from
functions.doc: This function checks that the username (or username and domain) in the From: URI matches the credentials.

functions.name: autheph_check_to
functions.doc: This function checks that the username (or username and domain) in the To: URI matches the credentials.

functions.name: autheph_check_timestamp
functions.doc: This function checks that the timestamp in the username parameter has not expired. The autheph_(check|proxy|www) functions all do this automatically, but in a scenario when individual SIP requests are not authenticated (for example, when they are over WebSockets and the connection was authenticated during the handshake) you may want to re-check for each new out-of-dialog request. In this scenario the username should be cached (perhaps in a hash-table) at the point authentication occurs.

params.name: radius_config
params.doc: This is the location of the configuration file of radius client libraries.

params.name: service_type
params.doc: This is the value of the Service-Type radius attribute to be used. The default should be fine for most people. See your radius client include files for numbers to be put in this parameter if you need to change it.

params.name: auth_extra
params.doc: Semi-colon separated list of extra RADIUS attribute name=pseudo variable pairs. When radius_www_authorize() or radius_proxy_authorize() function is called, listed extra attributes are included in RADIUS request with current values of corresponding pseudo variables.

params.name: use_ruri_flag
params.doc: When this parameter is set to the value other than "-1" and the request being authenticated has flag with matching number set via setflag() function, use Request URI instead of uri parameter value from the Authorization / Proxy-Authorization header field to perform RADIUS authentication. This is intended to provide workaround for misbehaving NAT / routers / ALGs that alter request in the transit, breaking authentication. At the time of this writing, certain versions of Linksys WRT54GL are known to do that.

params.name: radius_avps_mode
params.doc: If set to 1, all RADIUS AVPs returned by RADIUS server are stored in Kamailio AVPs list. If set to 0, only the SIP_AVP type of RADIUS AVPs are stored in Kamailio AVPs list.

params.name: append_realm_to_username
params.doc: If set to 1, the username passed to the RADIUS server will have the digest realm appended to it, if no domain is provided in the digest username.

functions.name: radius_www_authorize
functions.doc: The function verifies credentials according to RFC2617. If the credentials are verified successfully then the function will succeed and mark the credentials as authorized (marked credentials can be later used by some other functions).

functions.name: radius_proxy_authorize
functions.doc: The function verifies credentials according to RFC2617. If the credentials are verified successfully then the function will succeed and mark the credentials as authorized (marked credentials can be later used by some other functions).

params.name: xkey
params.doc: Specify the attributes for a shared secret. The value is in the format 'name1=value1;name2=value2;...'. The attributes can be: * id - the id of the group for keys * name - the name of the key within group * value - the value of the key * expires - expiration time (seconds)

functions.name: auth_xkeys_add
functions.doc: Add a header computed with the first key in the group kid, hashing with algorithm alg over the content of parameter data. The parameters can include variables.

functions.name: auth_xkeys_check
functions.doc: Check if the value of header hdr matches the value computed with the first key in the group kid, hashing with algorithm alg over the content of parameter data. The parameters can include variables.

params.name: xlbuf_size
params.doc: Defines size of internal buffer for all xprint formatting calls. If you don't use xprint formatting calls, you can set it to 0 to preserve some memory, if you get errors while formatting due to buffer size, you can enlarge it.

functions.name: set_iattr
functions.doc: Create an AVP of type integer.

functions.name: flags2attr
functions.doc: Store the current state of Kamailio flags into the specified AVP.

functions.name: set_sattr
functions.doc: Create an AVP of type string.

functions.name: print_attr
functions.doc: Print the value of an AVP to syslog.

functions.name: attr2uri
functions.doc: Rewrite the whole Request-URI of the message being processed with the value of an AVP, or if an uri-part is specified, rewrite only that specific part.

functions.name: attr_exists
functions.doc: Test for the existence of AVP with given name. The function returns 1 if given AVP exists and -1 if not.

functions.name: attr_equals
functions.doc: Test whether an AVP with given name and value exists. The function returns 1 if the AVP with given name and value exists and -1 if not. The value of the AVP is compared string-wise. The comparison is case sensitive.

functions.name: attr_equals_xl
functions.doc: Test whether an AVP with given name and value exists. The function returns 1 if the AVP with given name and value exists and -1 if not. The value of the AVP is compared string-wise to the result of xprint formatting call. The comparison is case sensitive.

functions.name: dump_attrs
functions.doc: Dumps all AVPs in user lists to the debug output (with level INFO).

functions.name: xlset_attr
functions.doc: Creates new AVP identified by attribute and assigns the result string of xprint formatting rules as its value.

functions.name: xlfix_attr
functions.doc: Fixes an xl formatted attribute value to pure string.

functions.name: insert_attr_hf
functions.doc: Inserts new header into the request, which is being forwarded. The AVP name is the name of the header field. If you need to insert header with name which differs from the AVP name use insert_attr_hf(header_name, $avp_name) instead.

functions.name: insert_attr_hf
functions.doc: Inserts new header into the request, which is being forwarded.

functions.name: append_attr_hf
functions.doc: Appends new header into the request, which is being forwarded. The AVP name is the name of the header field. If you need to append header with name which differs from the AVP name use append_attr_hf(header_name, $avp_name) instead.

functions.name: append_attr_hf
functions.doc: Appends new header into the request, which is being forwarded.

functions.name: replace_attr_hf
functions.doc: Replaces header in the request, which is being forwarded. The AVP name is the same as the name of the header field. If you need to replace header with name which differs from the AVP name use replace_attr_hf(header_name, $avp_name) instead.

functions.name: replace_attr_hf
functions.doc: Replaces header in the request, which is being forwarded.

functions.name: attr_to_reply
functions.doc: Appends new header into the reply at the request time processing. The AVP name is the name of the header field. If you need to append header with name which differs from the AVP name use attr_to_reply(header_name, $avp_name) instead.

functions.name: attr_to_reply
functions.doc: Appends new header into the reply at the request time processing.

functions.name: attr_destination
functions.doc: Sets the destination of the forwarded request to the value of AVP, which must be either a SIP URI or a string in nameaddr format (e.g. "Foo Bar" ).

functions.name: xlset_destination
functions.doc: Sets the destination of the forwarded request to the value of result of xprint formatted string. Either SIP URI or nameaddr format is allowed.

functions.name: subst_attr
functions.doc: The value of the AVP identified by $avp_name name is matched and substitued according to the subst_re sed like expression. Result of the substitution is then stored in the original AVP.

functions.name: del_attr
functions.doc: The AVP identified by $avp_name name is deleted.

functions.name: hdr_body2attrs
functions.doc: Function parses a header body content scans for fld1=val1,fld2=val2,... and creates bunch of avps prefixfld1:= val1, prefixfld2:= val2, .... If possible stores values as integers.

functions.name: hdr_body2attrs2
functions.doc: Function parses a header body content scans for fld1=val1,val2;fld2=val3,... and creates bunch of avps prefixfld1#1:= val1, prefixfld1#2:= val2, prefixfld2:=val3 .... If possible stores values as integers.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: DB URL for database connection.

params.name: avp_table
params.doc: DB table to be used.

params.name: use_domain
params.doc: If the domain part of the URI should be used for identifying an AVP in DB operations.

params.name: uuid_column
params.doc: Name of column containing the uuid (unique user id).

params.name: username_column
params.doc: Name of column containing the username.

params.name: domain_column
params.doc: Name of column containing the domain name.

params.name: attribute_column
params.doc: Name of column containing the attribute name (AVP name).

params.name: value_column
params.doc: Name of column containing the AVP value.

params.name: type_column
params.doc: Name of integer column containing the AVP type.

params.name: db_scheme
params.doc: Definition of a DB scheme to be used for non-standard access to Database information.

functions.name: avp_db_load
functions.doc: Loads from DB into memory the AVPs corresponding to the given source. If given, it sets the script flags for loaded AVPs. It returns true if it loaded some values in AVPs, false otherwise (db error, no avp loaded ...).

functions.name: avp_db_store
functions.doc: Stores to DB the AVPs corresponding to the given source.

functions.name: avp_db_delete
functions.doc: Deletes from DB the AVPs corresponding to the given source.

functions.name: avp_db_query
functions.doc: Make a database query and store the result in AVPs. This command is deprecated, please use the more flexible and advanced sqlops module instead.

functions.name: avp_delete
functions.doc: Deletes from memory the AVPs with name or, if empty, all AVPs.

functions.name: avp_pushto
functions.doc: Pushes the value of AVP(s) into the SIP message.

functions.name: avp_check
functions.doc: Checks the value of the AVP(s) against an operator and value.

functions.name: avp_copy
functions.doc: Copy / move an avp under a new name.

functions.name: avp_printf
functions.doc: NOTE: since Kamailio 1.3.0 the function has been moved to core and it is an alias to pv_printf().

functions.name: avp_subst
functions.doc: Perl/sed-like subst applied to AVPs having string value.

functions.name: avp_subst_pv
functions.doc: Same functionality than avp_subst() but seccond parameter will be evaluated first.

functions.name: avp_op
functions.doc: Different integer operations with avps.

functions.name: is_avp_set
functions.doc: Check if any AVP with name is set.

functions.name: avp_print
functions.doc: Prints the list with all the AVPs from memory. This is only a helper/debug function.

params.name: enable
params.doc: Even when the module is loaded, benchmarking is not enabled per default. This variable may have three different values: * -1 - Globally disable benchmarking * 0 - Enable per-timer enabling. Single timers are inactive by default and can be activated through the RPC interface as soon as that feature is implemented. * 1 - Globally enable benchmarking

params.name: granularity
params.doc: Logging normally is not done for every reference to the log_timer() function, but only every n'th call. n is defined through this variable. A sensible granularity seems to be 100.

params.name: loglevel
params.doc: Set the log level for the benchmark logs. These levels should be used: * -5 - L_ALERT * -4 - L_BUG * -3 - L_CRIT * -2 - L_CRIT (no prefix) * -1 - L_ERR * 0 - L_WARN * 1 - L_NOTICE * 2 - L_INFO * 3 - L_DBG

params.name: register
params.doc: Register a timer id at startup. Required when using the start/log functions via Kemi framework. This parameter can be set many times to register several timer ids.

functions.name: bm_start_timer
functions.doc: Start timer “name”. A later call to “bm_log_timer()” logs this timer..

functions.name: bm_log_timer
functions.doc: This function logs the timer with the given ID. The following data are logged: * Last msgs is the number of calls in the last logging interval. This equals the granularity variable.

functions.name: blst_add
functions.doc: Adds the source of the current message to the blocklist for timeout seconds. If timeout is missing or 0 it uses the default blocklist timeout (dst_blocklist_expire).

functions.name: blst_add_retry_after
functions.doc: Adds the source of the current message to the blocklist for the time interval specified in the Retry-After header. If the Retry-After header is missing, it will fail (returns false). If the Retry-After value is less than min, then min seconds will be used instead. If the Retry-After value is greater than max, then max seconds will be used instead.

functions.name: blst_del
functions.doc: Removes the source of the current message from the blocklist. If the address is not present in the blocklist at the time of the call it returns false.

functions.name: blst_is_blocklisted
functions.doc: Returns true if the source of the current message is blocklisted.

functions.name: blst_set_ignore
functions.doc: Set errors that will not be taken into account when deciding whether to blocklist a destination for the current message or a local reply to the current message.

functions.name: blst_rpl_set_ignore
functions.doc: See function blst_set_ignore([flags]).

functions.name: blst_clear_ignore
functions.doc: Clears blocklist ignore flags previously set by the corresponding blst_set_ignore(...) or blst_rpl_set_ignore(...) functions.

functions.name: blst_rpl_clear_ignore
functions.doc: See function blst_clear_ignore([flags]).

params.name: disable
params.doc: Boolean flag that specifies if callcontrol should be disabled. This is useful when you want to use the same Kamailio configuration in two different contexts, one using callcontrol, the other not. In the case callcontrol is disabled, calls to the call_control() function will return a code indicating that there is no limit associated with the call, allowing the use of the same configuration without changes.

params.name: socket_name
params.doc: The path to the filesystem socket where the callcontrol application listens for commands from the module.

params.name: socket_timeout
params.doc: How long time (in milliseconds) to wait for an answer from the callcontrol application.

params.name: signaling_ip_avp
params.doc: Specification of the AVP which holds the IP address from where the SIP signaling originated. If this AVP is set it will be used to get the signaling IP address, else the source IP address from where the SIP message was received will be used. This AVP is meant to be used in cases where there are more than one proxy in the call setup path and the proxy that actually starts callcontrol doesn't receive the SIP messages directly from the UA and it cannot determine the NAT IP address from where the signaling originated. In such a case attaching a SIP header at the first proxy and then copying that header's value into the signaling_ip_avp on the proxy that starts callcontrol will allow it to get the correct NAT IP address from where the SIP signaling originated.

params.name: canonical_uri_avp
params.doc: Specification of the AVP which holds an optional application defined canonical request URI. When this is set, it will be used as the destination when computing the call price, otherwise the request URI will be used. This is useful when the username of the ruri needs to have a different, canonical form in the rating engine computation than it has in the ruri.

params.name: diverter_avp_id
params.doc: Specification of the id of an integer AVP which holds an optional application defined diverter SIP URI. When this is set, it will be used by the rating engine as the billing party when finding the rates to apply to a given call, otherwise, the caller's URI taken from the From field will be used. When set, this AVP should contain a value in the form “user@domain” (no sip: prefix should be used).

functions.name: call_control
functions.doc: Trigger the use of callcontrol for the dialog started by the INVITE for which this function is called (the function should only be called for the first INVITE of a call). Further in-dialog requests will be processed automatically using internal bindings into the dialog state machine, allowing callcontrol to update its internal state as the dialog progresses, without any other intervention from the script.

params.name: start
params.doc: First number to assign when no number has been assigned yet.

params.name: end
params.doc: Last number to assign when all other numbers have been already assigned.

functions.name: call_obj_get
functions.doc: Get next free number. reply_number parameter is a variable where function will store result in string format.

functions.name: call_obj_free
functions.doc: Mark an object_number as free, so it can be assigned again. This number will not be readily assigned until a loop in the ring has completed. object_number shall be provided in string format.

params.name: subscriber_table
params.doc: The name of the table containing the subscribers

params.name: subscriber_user_col
params.doc: The name of the column in the subscriber table containing the usernames.

params.name: subscriber_domain_col
params.doc: The name of the column in the subscriber table containing the domain of the subscriber.

params.name: subscriber_carrier_col
params.doc: The name of the column in the subscriber table containing the carrier id of the subscriber.

params.name: config_source
params.doc: Specifies whether the module loads its config data from a file or from a database. Possible values are “file” and “db”.

params.name: config_file
params.doc: Specifies the path to the config file. The file has to be owned by the user and group used to run Kamailio.

params.name: default_tree
params.doc: The name of the carrier tree used per default (if the current subscriber has no preferred tree)

params.name: use_domain
params.doc: When using tree lookup per user, this parameter specifies whether to use the domain part for user matching or not. This parameter is tunable via the ser cfg framework.

params.name: fallback_default
params.doc: This parameter defines the behaviour when using user-based tree lookup. If the user has a non-existing tree set and fallback_default is set to 1, the default tree is used. Otherwise, cr_user_rewrite_uri returns an error. This parameter is tunable via the ser cfg framework.

params.name: fetch_rows
params.doc: The number of the rows to be fetched at once from database when loading the routing data. This value can be used to tune the load time at startup. For 1MB of private memory (default) it should be below 3750. The database driver must support the fetch_result() capability. This parameter is tunable via the ser cfg framework.

params.name: db_load_description
params.doc: Toggle on/off loading in memory the description column in the carrierroute/carrierfailureroute database tables. This reduces the shared memory used by the module.

params.name: match_mode
params.doc: The number of individual characters that are used for matching. Valid values are 10 or 128. When you specify 10, only digits will be used for matching, this operation mode is equivalent to the old behaviour. When configured with 128, all standard ascii chars are available for matching. Please be aware that memory requirements for storing the routing tree in shared memory will also increase by a factor of 12.8.

params.name: avoid_failed_destinations
params.doc: Integer parameter to toggle on/off the possibility that in the failurerouting cases destinations that previously failed are avoided. Possible values are 0 (off), 1 (on). Also see cr_route section.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: URL to the database containing the data.

params.name: carrierroute_table
params.doc: Name of the carrierroute table for the carrierroute module.

params.name: carrierroute_id_col
params.doc: Name of the column contains the unique identifier of a route.

params.name: carrierroute_carrier_col
params.doc: This column contains the carrier id.

params.name: carrierroute_domain_col
params.doc: This column contains the routing domain id. You can define several routing domains to have different routing rules. Maybe you use domain 0 for normal routing and domain 1 if domain 0 failed.

params.name: carrierroute_scan_prefix_col
params.doc: Name of column contains the scan prefixes. Scan prefixes define the matching portion of a phone number, e.g. when we have the scan prefixes 49721 and 49, the called number is 49721913740, it matches 49721, because the longest match is taken. If no prefix matches, the number is not routed. To prevent this, an empty prefix value of could be added.

params.name: carrierroute_flags_col
params.doc: This column contains the flags used for rule matching.

params.name: carrierroute_mask_col
params.doc: This column contains the mask that is applied to the message flags before rule matching.

params.name: carrierroute_prob_col
params.doc: Name of column contains the probability. The probability value is used to distribute the traffic between several gateways. Let's say 70 % of the traffic shall be routed to gateway A, the other 30 % shall be routed to gateway B, we define a rule for gateway A with a prob value of 0.7 and a rule for gateway B with a prob value of 0.3. If all probabilities for a given prefix, tree and domain don't add to 100%, the prefix values will be adjusted according the given prob values. E.g. if three hosts with prob values of 0.5, 0.5 and 0.4 are defined, the resulting probabilities are 35.714, 35.714 and 28.571%. But it is better to choose meaningful values in the first place because of clarity.

params.name: carrierroute_strip_col
params.doc: Name of the column contains the number of digits to be stripped of the userpart of an URI before prepending rewrite_prefix.

params.name: carrierroute_rewrite_host_col
params.doc: Name of column contains the rewrite prefixes. Here you can define a rewrite prefix for the localpart of the SIP URI. An empty field represents a blocklist entry, anything else is put as domain part into the Request URI of the SIP message.

params.name: carrierroute_rewrite_prefix_col
params.doc: Name of column contains the rewrite prefixes. Here you can define a rewrite prefix for the localpart of the SIP URI.

params.name: carrierroute_rewrite_suffix_col
params.doc: Name of column contains the rewrite suffixes. Here you can define a rewrite suffix for the localpart of the SIP URI.

params.name: carrierroute_description_col
params.doc: A comment for the route entry, useful for larger routing tables. The comment is also displayed by the rpc cmd "cr.dump_routes".

params.name: carrierfailureroute_table
params.doc: Name of the carrierfailureroute table for the carrierroute module.

params.name: carrierfailureroute_id_col
params.doc: This column contains the unique identifier of a failure route.

params.name: carrierfailureroute_carrier_col
params.doc: This column contains the carrier id.

params.name: carrierfailureroute_domain_col
params.doc: This column contains the routing domain id. You can define several routing domains to have different routing rules. Maybe you use domain 0 for normal routing and domain 1 if domain 0 failed.

params.name: carrierfailureroute_scan_prefix_col
params.doc: Name of column contains the scan prefixes. Scan prefixes define the matching portion of a phone number, e.g. we have the scan prefixes 49721 and 49, the called number is 49721913740, it matches 49721, because the longest match is taken. If no prefix matches, the number is not failure routed. To prevent this, an empty prefix value of could be added.

params.name: carrierfailureroute_host_name_col
params.doc: Name of the column containing the host name of the last routing destination, using for rules matching.

params.name: carrierfailureroute_reply_code_col
params.doc: This column contains the reply code used for rule matching.

params.name: carrierfailureroute_flags_col
params.doc: This column contains the flags used for rule matching.

params.name: carrierfailureroute_mask_col
params.doc: This column contains the mask that is applied to the message flags before rule matching.

params.name: carrierfailureroute_next_domain_col
params.doc: This column contains the route domain id that should be used for the next routing attempt.

params.name: carrierfailureroute_description_col
params.doc: A comment for the route entry, useful for larger routing tables.

params.name: carrier_name_table
params.doc: Name of the carrier_name table for the carrierroute module.

params.name: carrier_name_id_col
params.doc: Name of the column containing the unique identifier of a carrier.

params.name: carrier_name_carrier_col
params.doc: This column contains the carrier name.

params.name: domain_name_table
params.doc: Name of the domain_name table for the carrierroute module.

params.name: domain_name_id_col
params.doc: Name of the column containing the unique identifier of a domain.

params.name: domain_name_domain_col
params.doc: This column contains the domain name.

functions.name: cr_user_carrier
functions.doc: This function loads the carrier and stores it in a config variable. It cannot be used in the config file mode, as it needs a mapping of the given user to a certain carrier. The is drived from a database entry belonging to the user parameter. This mapping must be available in the table that is specified in the “subscriber_table” variable. This data is not cached in memory, that means for every execution of this function a database query will be done.

params.name: config_file
params.doc: This is the location of the XML configuration file.

params.name: latency_threshold
params.doc: The time in ms above which a log error is written to log file for long CDP transactions.

params.name: workerq_latency_threshold
params.doc: The time in ms above which a log error is written to log file for putting tasks into task queue.

params.name: workerq_length_threshold_percentage
params.doc: The threshold of the length of the worker queue as a percentage of the maximum queue size - when exceeded a warning is written to the log file. 0 means disabled

params.name: debug_heavy
params.doc: Flag to enable a more verbose log, which tells you more details about peers. This is disabled by default because it brings to a log too much verbose in DBG mode Can be enabled upon needs

params.name: enable_tls
params.doc: Flag to enable TLS for communication with all the peers.

params.name: tls_method
params.doc: Sets the TLS protocol method. Possible values are: * TLSv1.3+ - TLSv1.3 or newer connections are accepted (available starting with openssl/libssl v1.1.1) * TLSv1.3 - only TLSv1.3 connections are accepted (available starting with openssl/libssl v1.1.1) * TLSv1.2+ - TLSv1.2 or newer (TLSv1.3, ...) connections are accepted (available starting with openssl/libssl v1.1.1) * TLSv1.2 - only TLSv1.2 connections are accepted (available starting with openssl/libssl v1.0.1e) * TLSv1.1+ - TLSv1.1 or newer (TLSv1.2, ...) connections are accepted (available starting with openssl/libssl v1.0.1) * TLSv1.1 - only TLSv1.1 connections are accepted (available starting with openssl/libssl v1.0.1) * TLSv1+ - TLSv1.0 or newer (TLSv1.1, TLSv1.2, ...) connections are accepted. * TLSv1 - only TLSv1 (TLSv1.0) connections are accepted. This is the default value.

params.name: private_key
params.doc: Sets the private key file name.

params.name: certificate
params.doc: Sets the certificate file name. Must be in PEM format.

params.name: ca_list
params.doc: Sets the CA list file name. This file contains a list of all the trusted CAs certificates used when connecting to other SIP implementations. If a signature in a certificate chain belongs to one of the listed CAs, the verification of that certificate will succeed. If not set, the PCRF sent certificate is not checked.

functions.name: cdp_check_peer
functions.doc: The method checks, if a specific peer is connected and ready.

functions.name: cdp_has_app
functions.doc: The method checks, if any peer with this specific application has connected.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: Default database URL.

params.name: transl_tbl
params.doc: Name of table used for pointing group_name+name into configuration table. If empty/null field values are found then default values will be used. The default values are declared in record having group_name called . The C-code "absolutely" default values ("cfg_var", "group_name", "name", "value"). The other keyword is asterisk * which matches all parameters and will be used if parameter is not explicitly mentioned.

params.name: custom_tbl
params.doc: Name of table used for extra param declaration (group_name, name, type, min/max value, description).

params.name: basedir
params.doc: Control where the config reports should be stored. The dir must exist and Kamailio SIP Server Platform must have permissions to write on it.

params.name: mask
params.doc: mask - Control the type of vars it should display in the report: * 1 - dump null values * 2 - dump avp vars * 4 - dump script vars * 8 - dump xavp vars * 16 - dump DP_OTHER vars * 32 - dump ALL vars

params.name: callid_prefix
params.doc: Prefix used to identify test scenario messages. Last char of the string will be used as delimiter for the scenario ID. With parameter set to “NGCP%” and Call-ID “NGCP%123%456” the scenario identified will be “123”.

params.name: skip_unknown
params.doc: If enabled, value different from 0, cfgt will not generate the report of any message that doesn't match the callid_prefix.

params.name: route_log
params.doc: If enabled, value different from 0, cfgt will log (WARN) the execution time of routes.

params.name: initial_probability
params.doc: The initial value of the probability.

params.name: hash_file
params.doc: The config file name for that a hash value should be calculated on startup.

params.name: initial_gflags
params.doc: The initial value of global flags bitmap.

params.name: lock_set_size
params.doc: Size of lock set - the value is used as power of two to compute the size of lock array.

functions.name: rand_event
functions.doc: Return true or false, depending on a random value and a probability value.

functions.name: rand_set_prob
functions.doc: Set the “probability” of the decision.

functions.name: rand_reset_prob
functions.doc: Reset the probability back to the initial value.

functions.name: rand_get_prob
functions.doc: Return the current probability setting, e.g. for logging purposes.

functions.name: sleep
functions.doc: Waits "time" seconds.

functions.name: usleep
functions.doc: Waits "time" micro-seconds.

functions.name: abort
functions.doc: Debugging function that aborts the server. Depending on the configuration of the server a core dump will be created.

functions.name: pkg_status
functions.doc: Debugging function that dumps the status for the private (PKG) memory. This information is logged to the default log facility, depending on the general log level and the memlog setting. You need to compile the server with activated memory debugging to get detailed informations.

functions.name: pkg_summary
functions.doc: Debugging function that dumps the summary for the private (PKG) memory usage. This information is logged to the default log facility, depending on the general log level and the memlog setting. You need to compile the server with activated memory debugging to get detailed informations.

functions.name: shm_status
functions.doc: Debugging function that dumps the status for the shared (SHM) memory. This information is logged to the default log facility, depending on the general log level and the memlog setting. You need to compile the server with activated memory debugging to get detailed informations.

functions.name: shm_summary
functions.doc: Debugging function that dumps the summary for the shared (SHM) memory usage. This information is logged to the default log facility, depending on the general log level and the memlog setting. You need to compile the server with activated memory debugging to get detailed informations.

functions.name: set_gflag
functions.doc: Set the bit at the position “flag” in global flags.

functions.name: reset_gflag
functions.doc: Reset the bit at the position “flag” in global flags.

functions.name: is_gflag
functions.doc: Check if bit at the position “flag” in global flags is set.

functions.name: lock
functions.doc: Lock the key. Can be used to synchronize operations in config file, a hash id is computed over the keys and appropriate lock is set in the lock array controlled by parameter "lock_set_size". Do not use lock() after another lock() unless you are sure the keys hit different array entries.

functions.name: trylock
functions.doc: Try to lock the key. If the lock can not be obtained (possibly already locked), the function returns an error and script execution continues.

functions.name: unlock
functions.doc: Unlock the key.

functions.name: check_route_exists
functions.doc: Check if a route block exists. It returns true (1) on found and false on not found or error.

functions.name: route_if_exists
functions.doc: Execute a routing block only if it is defined. If it's not defined, silently move to the next action in the configuration script.

functions.name: core_hash
functions.doc: Exported function that enables the core_hash() function to be used from the configuration file.

params.name: redis
params.doc: Redis datasource connection information

params.name: credit_check_period
params.doc: Indicates how often the credit checking function should be called. It is directly related to the precision of the module. The maximum precision is 1, which means that every call is checked every one second.

functions.name: cnxcc_set_max_credit
functions.detail: cnxcc_set_max_credit(customer, maxcredit, connect, cps, ipulse, fpulse)

functions.name: cnxcc_terminate_all
functions.doc: Terminates all calls of the specified customer/profile.

params.name: alias_subdomains
params.doc: Register a domain and all its sub-domains to match the “myself” condition. It can be set many times. Its full format is: 'proto:domain:port', allowing to set restrictions on protocol and port as well. Protocol and port are optional.

params.name: dns_cache
params.doc: Add A or AAAA records to internal DNS cache at startup. It can be set many times to add more than one record.

params.name: dns_file
params.doc: Path to the file from where to load dns_cache records. It can be set many times to add more than one file.

params.name: evcb_reply_out
params.doc: Name of KEMI callback function to be executed instead of event_route[corex:reply-out].

params.name: nio_intercept
params.doc: If set to non-zero then raw data received from a remote host or about to be sent to a remote host is made available in event_route[network:msg]. The script writer may modify this and save to msg_avp, which will then be processed by SIP worker as normal.

params.name: nio_min_msg_len
params.doc: Minimum content length of the packet to execute the event_route[network:msg]. This only works if nio_intercept parameter is set to non-zero.

params.name: nio_msg_avp
