params.doc: AVP name to store modified content to be set in the packet. If not set in event_route[network:msg], then all changes are lost and original contents are used. This only works if nio_intercept parameter is to set non-zero.

functions.name: append_branch
functions.doc: Append a new branch to the destination set, useful to build the set of destination addresses for parallel forking or redirect replies.

functions.name: send_udp
functions.doc: Send the original SIP message to a specific destination in stateless mode. No changes are applied to received message, no Via header is added. Host can be an IP address or hostname. Port is optional and defaults to 5060. Used protocol: UDP.

functions.name: send_tcp
functions.doc: This function is identical to send_udp() described above, except that it sends the SIP message using the TCP protocol instead of UDP.

functions.name: send_data
functions.doc: Send the data to address specified by uri. Both parameters can contain pseudo-variables. The uri parameter has to be a valid SIP URI. The data parameter can by any arbitrary content.

functions.name: sendx
functions.doc: Send the data to address specified by uri using a specific local socket. All parameters can contain pseudo-variables. The uri parameter has to be a valid SIP URI. The sock parameter has to be a valid socket specifier (like values assigned to $fs). The data parameter can by any arbitrary content.

functions.name: is_incoming
functions.doc: Returns true if contents of message buffer $mb are the data received from remote host, otherwise false indicating that the contents of $mb are data that is about to be sent out to remote host. This only works if nio_intercept parameter is set to non-zero.

functions.name: msg_iflag_set
functions.doc: Set internal SIP message flag. The parameter flagname can be: USE_UAC_FROM, USE_UAC_TO, UAC_AUTH, MSG_APPLY_CHANGES or a number from 0 to 64 (the meaning of each value can be found in source code).

functions.name: msg_iflag_reset
functions.doc: Reset the internal flag given as parameter.

functions.name: msg_iflag_is_set
functions.doc: Test if the internal flag given as parameter is set.

functions.name: file_read
functions.doc: Read content of a text file into a variable.

functions.name: file_write
functions.doc: Write content of parameter to a text file.

functions.name: setxflag
functions.doc: Set the extended message (transaction) flag.

functions.name: isxflagset
functions.doc: Return true if the extended message (transaction) flag is set.

functions.name: resetxflag
functions.doc: Reset the extended message (transaction) flag.

functions.name: set_send_socket
functions.doc: Set the socket for sending out.

functions.name: set_send_socket_name
functions.doc: Set the socket for sending out.

functions.name: set_recv_socket
functions.doc: Switch local socket used for receiving the message.

functions.name: set_recv_socket_name
functions.doc: Switch local socket used for receiving the message.

functions.name: set_source_address
functions.doc: Set the source address for the message.

functions.name: via_add_srvid
functions.doc: Control if srvid parameter is added or not to local Via. If yes, the value is server_id, added only if it is different than 0.

functions.name: via_add_xavp_params
functions.doc: Control if fields of the xavp with the name specified by xavp_via_params global parameter are added or not to local Via.

functions.name: via_use_xavp_fields
functions.doc: Control if fields of the xavp with the name specified by xavp_via_fields global parameter are used or not to build local Via.

functions.name: via_reply_add_xavp_params
functions.doc: Control if fields of the xavp with the name specified by xavp_via_reply_params global parameter are added or not to the top Via of replies.

functions.name: is_faked_msg
functions.doc: Returns 1 (native config true) if the SIP message under processing is the internal faked msg structure. Returns -1 (native config false) if the SIP message under processing is received from the network.

functions.name: is_socket_name
functions.doc: Returns 1 (native config true) if the parameter matches a local socket name, otherwise -1 (native config false). The parameter can contain variables.

functions.name: forward_uac
functions.doc: Forward received request with a single Via header, the one added by Kamailio, the other ones being removed. Useful in cases when its reply should not be sent back (e.g., the reply was already sent out from Kamailio).

functions.name: forward_uac_uri
functions.doc: Similar to forward_uac() with the posibility to provide the target address as a SIP URI via the parameter vuri. The parameter vuri can contain variables.

functions.name: forward_reply
functions.doc: Forward received reply on demand.

functions.name: msg_vbflag_set
functions.doc: Set the via-body flag.

functions.name: msg_vbflag_is_set
functions.doc: Return true if the via-body flag is set.

functions.name: msg_vbflag_reset
functions.doc: Reset the via-body flag.

functions.name: add_tcp_alias
functions.doc: Add an alias to the TCP connection with the port parameter. If the port is 0, then the port of the first Via-header is used. The parameter can also be a variable holding an integer port value.

params.name: script_counter
params.doc: Define a new counter that can be used from the script. The declaration might include a group in front of the counter name, separated with '.'. It might also include a counter description string (help message), separated from the name with a ' ' or ':'. If the group is missing, the group defined in the script_cnt_grp_name module parameter will be used (the default is "script"). If the description is missing, the default is "custom script counter". The format of the declaration is: [group.]name[( |:)description].

params.name: script_cnt_grp_name
params.doc: Group name that will be used for the counters defined via the script_counter module parameter which do not have a specified group.

functions.name: cnt_inc
functions.doc: Increments the counter group.name. The counter must be defined using the script_counter module parameter. If the group name is missing, the group specified by the script_cnt_grp_name modparam will be used.

functions.name: cnt_add
functions.doc: Adds number the counter group.name. The counter must be defined using the script_counter module parameter. If the group name is missing, the group specified by the script_cnt_grp_name modparam will be used.

functions.name: cnt_reset
functions.doc: Resets the counter group.name. The counter must be defined using the script_counter module parameter. If the group name is missing, the group specified by the script_cnt_grp_name modparam will be used.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: A SQL URL have to be given to the module for knowing where the database containing the table with CPL scripts is locates. If required a user name and password can be specified for allowing the module to connect to the database server.

params.name: db_table
params.doc: Indicates the name of the table that store the CPL scripts. This table must be locate into the database specified by “db_url” parameter. For more about the format of the CPL table please see the modules/cplc/init.mysql file.

params.name: username_column
params.doc: Indicates the name of the column used for storing the username.

params.name: domain_column
params.doc: Indicates the name of the column used for storing the domain.

params.name: cpl_xml_column
params.doc: Indicates the name of the column used for storing the XML version of the cpl script.

params.name: cpl_bin_column
params.doc: Indicates the name of the column used for storing the binary version of the cpl script (compiled version).

params.name: cpl_dtd_file
params.doc: Points to the DTD file describing the CPL grammar. The file name may include also the path to the file. This path can be absolute or relative (be careful the path will be relative to the starting directory of Kamailio).

params.name: log_dir
params.doc: Points to a directory where should be created all the log file generated by the LOG CPL node. A log file per user will be created (on demand) having the name username.log.

params.name: proxy_recurse
params.doc: Tells for how many time is allow to have recurse for PROXY CPL node If it has value 2, when doing proxy, only twice the proxy action will be re-triggered by a redirect response; the third time, the proxy execution will end by going on REDIRECTION branch. The recurse feature can be disable by setting this parameter to 0

params.name: proxy_route
params.doc: Before doing proxy (forward), a script route can be executed. This parameter indicates the name of the route called. All modifications made by that route will be reflected only for the current branch.

params.name: case_sensitive
params.doc: Tells if the username matching should be perform case sensitive or not. Set it to a non zero value to force a case sensitive handling of usernames.

params.name: realm_prefix
params.doc: Defines a prefix for the domain part which should be ignored in handling users and scripts.

params.name: timer_avp
params.doc: Full specification (ID, NAME, ALIAS) of the AVP to be used to set the value of the Final Response INVITE timeout - it's used by the TIMEOUT attribute from the PROXY tag.

params.name: lookup_domain
params.doc: Used by lookup tag to indicate where to perform user location. Basically this is the name of the usrloc domain (table) where the user registrations are kept.

params.name: lookup_append_branches
params.doc: Tells if the lookup tag should append branches (to do parallel forking) if user_location lookup returns more than one contact. Set it to a non zero value to enable parallel forking for location lookup tag.

params.name: use_domain
params.doc: Indicates if the domain part of the URI should be used in user identification (otherwise only username part will be used).

params.name: redirect_route
params.doc: Before doing redirect (deflection), a script route can be executed. This parameter indicates the name of the route called. All modifications made by that route will be reflected only for the current branch.

params.name: ignore3xx
params.doc: Indicates if 3xx SIP response must be ignored.

functions.name: cpl_run_script
functions.doc: Starts the execution of the CPL script. The user name is fetched from new_uri or requested uri or from To header -in this order- (for incoming execution) or from FROM header (for outgoing execution). Regarding the stateful/stateless message processing, the function is very flexible, being able to run in different modes (see below the"mode" parameter). Normally this function will end script execution. There is no guaranty that the CPL script interpretation ended when Kamailio script ended also (for the same INVITE ;-)) - this can happen when the CPL script does a PROXY and the script interpretation pause after proxying and it will be resumed when some reply is received (this can happen in a different process of SER). If the function returns to script, the SIP server should continue with the normal behavior as if no script existed. When some error is returned, the function itself haven't sent any SIP error reply (this can be done from script).

functions.name: cpl_process_register
functions.doc: This function MUST be called only for REGISTER requests. It checks if the current REGISTER request is related or not with CPL script upload/download/ remove. If it is, all the needed operation will be done. For checking if the REGISTER is CPL related, the function looks first to "Content-Type" header. If it exists and has a the mime type set to "application/cpl+xml" means this is a CPL script upload/remove operation. The distinction between to case is made by looking at "Content-Disposition" header; id its value is "script;action=store", means it's an upload; if it's "script;action=remove", means it's a remove operation; other values are considered to be errors. If no "Content-Type" header is present, the function looks for "Accept" header and if it contains "*" or "application/cpl-xml" the request will be considered for downloading CPL scripts. The functions returns to script only if the REGISTER is not related to CPL. In other case, the function will send by itself the necessary replies (stateless - using sl), including for errors.

functions.name: cpl_process_register_norpl
functions.doc: Same as “cpl_process_register” without internally generating the reply. All information (script) is appended to the reply but without sending it out.

params.name: salt
params.doc: A keyword to generate salt for encryption. It must be at least 8 chars long. If set to empty, no salt is used for encryption.

params.name: register_callid
params.doc: Set it to 1 in order to register a callback to core for generation of callid values for requests generated by Kamailio tm module.

params.name: register_evcb
params.doc: Set it to 1 in order to register the event route callbacks, in case AES encryption/decryption of SIP traffic is wanted. The event_route[crypto:netio] or corresponding KEMI callback are executed.

params.name: kevcb_netio
params.doc: Name of the KEMI callback function for netio events. It receives a string parameter with event route name.

params.name: netio_key
params.doc: The shared secret used to encrypt/decrypt network traffic.

params.name: key_derivation
params.doc: Specify if the module should use an internal derivation function to generate the initialization vector for encryption operations. This is the default mode. If set to 0 the initialization vector will be generated randomly or read from the configuration file.

params.name: init_vector
params.doc: The initialization vector used for the cryptographic operations. This needs to be a Base64 encoded value with 16 bytes lengths.

functions.name: crypto_aes_encrypt
functions.doc: Encrypts the text with the key using AES encryption algorithm. The result is encoded in base64 format and stored in res. The parameter res must be a read-write variables. The parameters text and key can be static strings or strings with variables (dynamic strings).

functions.name: crypto_aes_decrypt
functions.doc: Decrypts the text with the key using AES encryption algorithm. The text has to be encoded in base64 format. The parameter res must be a read-write variables. The parameters text and key can be static strings or strings with variables (dynamic strings).

functions.name: crypto_hmac_sha256
functions.doc: Calculates HMAC (keyed-hash message authentication code) with SHA256 as a cryptographic hash function. The result is encoded in base64 url encoded format and stored in res. The parameter res must be a read-write variable. The parameters text and key can be static strings or strings with variables (dynamic strings).

functions.name: crypto_netio_in)
functions.doc: Return 1 (true) if it is an incoming net message, or -1 (false) otherwise.

functions.name: crypto_netio_out
functions.doc: Return 1 (true) if it is an outgoing net message, or -1 (false) otherwise.

functions.name: crypto_netio_encrypt
functions.doc: Mark the network message for encryption.

functions.name: crypto_netio_decrypt
functions.doc: Mark the network message for decryption.

params.name: binrpc
params.doc: Specifies the transport used for the binrpc protocol. The following transport protocol are supported: Unix datagram sockets, Unix stream sockets, UDP and TCP.

params.name: binrpc_buffer_size
params.doc: The size of the internal buffer used for printing elements of the RPC response (e.g., internal RPC printf()). The value is given in bytes.

params.name: mode
params.doc: Permissions used for the created Unix sockets or for the fifo.

params.name: user
params.doc: Username or uid used for the created Unix sockets or for the fifo.

params.name: group
params.doc: Group name or gid used for the created Unix sockets or for the fifo.

params.name: fifo
params.doc: fifo used for the obsolete fifo protocol. The fifo protocol can be run over a real fifo, over UDP or over TCP. Format: [protocol:]path|address. If no protocol is specified the default is "fifo". Examples: "fifo:/tmp/kamailio_fifo", "/tmp/kamailio_fifo2", "udp:*:2050", "tcp:localhost:2050". For more details on the UDP and TCP formats see binrpc. Multiple fifos or fifo transports can be used in the same time (just by setting the fifo parameter multiple times in the config).

params.name: autoconversion
params.doc: Enable or disable automatic type conversion globally, for all the methods parameters. If on, a type mismatch in a method parameter will not cause a fault if it is possible to automatically convert it to the expected type.

params.name: binrpc_max_body_size
params.doc: Set the size of binrpc buffer for RPC reply. Value represents kilobytes.

params.name: binrpc_struct_max_body_size
params.doc: Set the size of binrpc structure buffer for RPC reply. Value represents kilobytes.

params.name: config
params.doc: Default value is ldap.cfg.

params.name: reconnect_attempt
params.doc: Default value is 3.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: Default database URL.

params.name: declare_query
params.doc: Declare query_id for @db.query_id (see select syntax) or for reference from db_query(query_id). Queries are pre-compiled therefore volatile stuff must be passed via parameters (AVP or so).

params.name: declare_handle
params.doc: Declare handle for fetching.

functions.name: db_query
functions.doc: Executes query and in case of SELECT returns result via handle, seeks the first record and returns TRUE if table is not empty. The result is accessible using @db.fetch select. See also declare_handle. Query_id references to query declared using declare_query, handle references to query declared using declare_handle.

functions.name: db_close
functions.doc: Close table that has been opened using db_query. Note all close after script processing automatically.

functions.name: db_first
functions.doc: Returns TRUE if table is not empty. Note that rewind might not be supported by particular db driver.

functions.name: db_next
functions.doc: Moves to the next record and returns TRUE if not EOF.

functions.name: db_seek
functions.doc: Seeks at the row no (origin is zero) and Returns TRUE in case of success. Backward seek might not be supported by db driver.

functions.name: db_foreach
functions.doc: Call specific route for each row, loop is interrupted if route returns code <= 0. Return code of the last route call is returned as result of db_foreach (or -1 when no select is empty).

functions.name: db_proper
functions.doc: Hack which enables using db_ops queries in failure route. Call it at the beginning of FAILURE_ROUTE block.

functions.name: @db.query.query_id
functions.doc: Returns value of the first row and the first field.

functions.name: @db.query.query_id.count
functions.doc: Returns number of rows in select query.

functions.name: @db.query.query_id.is_empty
functions.doc: Returns 1 if select query is empty.

functions.name: @db.query.query_id.field[m]
functions.doc: Returns value of the first row and the m-th field. @*.field supports select_any_uri and select_any_nameaddr.

functions.name: @db.query.query_id.row[n]
functions.doc: Returns value of the n-th row and the first field, negative values count from the end (-1 == last row).

functions.name: @db.query.query_id.row[n].field[m]
functions.doc: Returns value of the n-th row and the m-th field. @*.field supports select_any_uri and select_any_nameaddr.

functions.name: @db.fetch.handle
functions.doc: Similar functionality as @db.query selects with exception that operation is performed at query has been opened by db_query.

functions.name: @db.fetch.handle.row_no
functions.doc: Returns current row number (origin is zero).

params.name: connection
params.doc: Specify the connection to a real database system. The format is 'conid=>DBURL' - providing a connection id and the database URL used by the database driver used.

params.name: cluster
params.doc: Specify the cluster definition. The format is 'clsid=>conid1=def1;conid2=def2' - providing a cluster id and the list of database connections to be used. For each connection you have to provide a usage definition. The usage definition is a 4-char long string, specifying priority and command mode for read and write operations to be performed on that connection.

params.name: inactive_interval
params.doc: How long (seconds) a connection is considered inactive after a DB operations failed on it.

params.name: max_query_length
params.doc: How long (seconds) a failed db operation needs to last before deactivating the connection for inactive_interval seconds. This prevents disabling of connections that reply fast with error codes, thus being active (e.g., due to primary key insert errors). In such cases, the database server is active.

params.name: flush
params.doc: Enable or disable flushing after each write.

params.name: encode_delimiter
params.doc: Enable or disable encoding of the escaped character using ""%" HEX HEX" mechanism for escaping from RFC 2396

params.name: ping_interval
params.doc: Time interval in seconds to send ping messages to MySQL server in order to keep the connection open.

params.name: server_timezone
params.doc: Control if kamailio converts a time to string using the local timezone or if MySQL will convert it using FROM_UNIXTIME. This option is useful if kamailio and the database are configured for different timezones.

params.name: timeout_interval
params.doc: Time interval (in seconds) after that a connection attempt, read or write request is aborted. The value counts three times, as several retries are done from the driver before it gives up.

params.name: auto_reconnect
params.doc: Configure whether the module should automatically reconnect to MySQL server if the connection was lost.

params.name: insert_delayed
params.doc: If set to 1, all INSERT SQL queries will be sent to MySQL server as INSERT DELAYED.

params.name: update_affected_found
params.doc: If set to 1, all UPDATE SQL queries will return the number of matched rows instead of the number of "updated" rows.

params.name: opt_ssl_mode
params.doc: Control how the connection to MySQL server is done in regards to SSL/TLS. If set to 1, SSL/TLS mode is disabled.

params.name: opt_ssl_ca
params.doc: Configures the CA certs used to verify the MySQL server cert when SSL is enabled.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Timeout value for any operation with BD.

params.name: reconnect
params.doc: Timeout value for connect (create session) operation.

params.name: retries
params.doc: How many retries to attempt to reconnect if connection to Postgres server becomes broken.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Setting this variable to any value larger than zero (which is the default value) enables mainly query timeout. For backward compatibility it also enables connection timeout if connect_timeout param is not set using the con_param below. If a connection attempt or a query takes longer than this many seconds, the operation will be aborted and an error will be returned.

params.name: tcp_keepalive
params.doc: Enable the TCP keepalive timer and set the number of seconds the connection must be idle before to start sending keepalive packets. Defaults to zero, which disables TCP keepalive packets.

params.name: lockset
params.doc: The value is used as power of two to compute the size of the lock set needed to implement the equivalent of REPLACE SQL statement.

params.name: bytea_output_escape
params.doc: Control if the module should request escaping the output for bytea fields.

params.name: con_param
params.doc: Specifies the connection string parameters. Parameter definition must be in the format param1=value1;param2=value2. Many parameters can be set.

params.name: schema_path
params.doc: The path to the table schemas.

params.name: keys
params.doc: The entry and mapping keys of tables.

params.name: verbosity
params.doc: Control the verbosity of debug messages printed by the module. If set to 1, the module prints schema details for all tables on each connect operation to Redis server.

params.name: opt_tls
params.doc: Controls TLS usage while connecting to a remote DB. If set to 1, TLS is used to connect to the DB.

params.name: max_key_length
params.doc: Controls the max possible key length to be used when adding/prepending strings into the redis key. If used will be always compared against the given string key length.

params.name: mapping_struct_type
params.doc: Controls the type of mapping structures to be used. Beforehand, only sets were used. For the rationale behind mapping structures, see the discussion about mapping structures in the overview section. Currently supported values: 0 - sets (default), 1 - hashes.

params.name: hash_value
params.doc: Only has sense if mapping_struct_type is set to hash (1). Defines the value to be used for the hash entries in the hashes that now replace mapping sets.

params.name: hash_expires
params.doc: Set an expiration time in seconds for the keys in the hash data structures in the database. This is useful for the usrloc module for example, for automatic contact expiry. A value of 0 is interpreted as no expiration. This is only supported with mapping_struct_type set to hash (1).

params.name: db_pass
params.doc: Sets the password to connect to the DB.

params.name: ca_path
params.doc: Sets the path where Certificates Authorities certs for the Redis server certificate are stored.

params.name: with_sentinels
params.doc: Enables the use of Redis sentinels for high availability. If set to 1, the module will connect to the Redis server using the sentinels defined in the "sentinels_config" modparam.

params.name: sentinels_config
params.doc: Sets the sentinels to connect to the Redis server. The format is semi-colon separated list of key-value pairs: password, sentinels. Sentinels is a pipe separated list of host:port pairs. Password applies to all sentinels.

params.name: redis_master_name
params.doc: Sets the name of the Redis master. This is needed when building the SENTINEL get-master-addr-by-name command. The name should match the name used in the Redis Sentinel configuration.

params.name: use_replicas
params.doc: Enables connecting to Redis replicas instead of the master when using sentinels. Replicas are selected randomly. This helps distribute load across the Redis setup (i.e.: read from replicas instead of master). If for whatever reason no replicas are available, the module will fall back to connecting to the master (this cannot be toggled off).

params.name: recheck_replicas_interval
params.doc: The parameter sets the interval in seconds to recheck for available replicas so that we don't remain connected to the master. Because of implementation details, the first check can exceptionally happen after half of this interval. If set to 0, no rechecks will be performed and the module will remain connected to the master until a new connection is established (i.e.: Redis server goes down and comes back up).

params.name: db_set_readonly
params.doc: This will set the db connection to "SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY", useful if another program is writing to the DB. The value is the full path to the sqlite file used for example in any db_url or sqlops/sqlcon This parameter may be set multiple times to set many DB connections to readonly in the same configuration file.

params.name: db_set_journal_mode
params.doc: This will set the db connection journal mode, for the given connection. The value is the full path to the sqlite file used for example in any db_url or sqlops/sqlcon Other journal mode are : DELETE | TRUNCATE | PERSIST | MEMORY | WAL | OFF When setting this option, you must also set db_set_busy_timeout, because all kamailio sub-processes will set this option individually and simultaneously, causing "database locked" errors on startup if no busy timeout is set. This parameter may be set multiple times to set many DB connections to readonly in the same configuration file.

params.name: db_set_busy_timeout
params.doc: This will set the db connection busy timeout to let it wait for the given milliseconds for database locks to be released by other processes before giving up. Use this with the WAL journaling mode if you run into "database locked" errors. The value is the full path to the sqlite file used for example in any db_url or sqlops/sqlcon This parameter may be set multiple times to set the busy-timeout for different DB connections in the same configuration file.

params.name: db_mode
params.doc: Set caching mode (0) or non-caching mode (1). In caching mode, data is loaded at startup. In non-caching mode, the module checks every time a table is requested whether the corresponding file on disk has changed, and if yes, will re-load the table from file.

params.name: db_delim
params.doc: Set the delimiter inside the db_text file.

params.name: default_connection
params.doc: connection for use with rpc query command.

params.name: emptystring
params.doc: db_text by default handles an empty string as a NULL value. Some modules, like the dialplan module, does not accept NULL strings. If you enable emptystring an empty string will not be NULL, but an empty string.

params.name: file_buffer_size
params.doc: size of the buffer used to read the text file. Some presence tables have columns with large content.

params.name: max_result_rows
params.doc: number of rows to read from the text file.

params.name: ping_interval
params.doc: Sets the ping time interval.

params.name: auto_reconnect
params.doc: Turns on or off the auto_reconnect mode.

params.name: use_escape_common
params.doc: Escape values in query using internal escape_common() function. It escapes single quote ''', double quote '"', backslash '\', and NULL characters.

params.name: replace_query
params.doc: Tells if the ODBC replace query is supported by the DB odbc driver.

params.name: quote_char
params.doc: The character to be used for quoting the table and column names in database queries.

params.name: cfgtrace
params.doc: Control whether the config script trace is enabled or disabled at startup. You can change the value at runtime without restart, globally or per process.

params.name: cfgtrace_format
params.doc: Control what is printer in the cfgtrace log message. If it is set to 1, then the configuration file path is not printed, making the log messages shorter when not including other configuration files in the main one.

params.name: breakpoint
params.doc: Control whether every line (global) breakpoint is enabled or disabled at startup.

params.name: log_level
params.doc: What log level is to be used to print module-specific messages.

params.name: log_level_name
params.doc: What log level name is to be used to print cfg trace messages.

params.name: log_facility
params.doc: Which log facility is to be used to print module-specific messages. By using this setting, you can configure syslog to send debug messages to a separate log channel, like a specific kamailio-debug log file.

params.name: log_prefix
params.doc: String to print before any module-specific messages.

params.name: step_usleep
params.doc: Microseconds to sleep before checking for new commands when waiting at a breakpoint.

params.name: step_loops
params.doc: How many sleeps of 'step_usleep' the RPC process performs when waiting for a reply from a worker process before responding to RPC. This avoids blocking RPC process forever in case the worker process 'forgets' to write back a reply.

params.name: mod_hash_size
params.doc: Used to compute power of two as size of internal hash table to store levels per module (e.g., if it is set to 4, internal hash table has 16 slots). One must set its value grater than 0 such that memory to be allocated to save the module specific debug levels or facility configured by mod_level or mod_facility. This parameter is accessible readonly via the Kamailio config framework.

params.name: mod_level_mode
params.doc: Enable or disable per module log level (0 - disabled, 1 - enabled). This parameter is tunable via the Kamailio config framework. To use per module log level you also have to set mod_hash_size.

params.name: mod_level
params.doc: Specify module log level - the value must be in the format: modulename=level. The parameter can be set many times. For core log level, use module name 'core'. You also must enable mod_level_mode and mod_hash_size.

params.name: mod_facility_mode
params.doc: Enable or disable per module log facility (0 - disabled, 1 - enabled). This parameter is tunable via the Kamailio config framework. To use per module log facility you also have to set mod_hash_size.

params.name: mod_facility
params.doc: Specify module log facility - the value must be in the format: modulename=facility. The parameter can be set many times. For core log facility, use module name 'core'. You also must enable mod_facility_mode and mod_hash_size.

params.name: log_assign
params.doc: Enable or disable log assign actions on config (0 - disabled, 1 - enabled).

params.name: cfgpkgcheck
params.doc: If set, before each config action is done pkg memory check, useful to detect buffer overflows.

params.name: reset_msgid
params.doc: Used to enable or disable the ability to reset the msgid ($mi) through the dbg.reset_msgid RPC command. (0 - disabled, 1 - enabled).

params.name: cfgtest
params.doc: Control whether the cfgt module is enabled or disabled at startup. Module cfgt needs to be loaded before.

functions.name: dbg_breakpoint
functions.doc: Anchor a breakpoint at the current line of the config (the one on which this function is called). The 'mode' specifies whether the breakpoint is enabled (1) or disabled (0) at startup.

functions.name: dbg_pv_dump
functions.doc: Prints the content of pv_cache on json format. Defaults are mask=31 and level = "L_DBG"

functions.name: dbg_sip_msg
functions.doc: Prints how the sip message would look like if it would be sent out at that point in the config(i.e. if the current lump lists would have been applied at that point in the config). It also prints a diff list for both header and body of sip msg which contain the lump lists content. The lumps deleted are printed with "-" sign whereas the lumps added have no sign. The config line where the function has been called is also printed.

params.name: enable_stats
params.doc: If statistics support should be enabled or not. Via statistics variables, the module provides information about the dialog processing. Set it to zero to disable or to non-zero to enable it.

params.name: hash_size
params.doc: The size of the hash table internally used to keep the dialogs. A larger table is much faster but consumes more memory. The hash size must be a power of two.

params.name: rr_param
params.doc: Name of the Record-Route parameter used to store the dialog cookie. It is used for the fast matching of sequential requests to tracked dialogs.

params.name: timeout_avp
params.doc: The specification of an AVP that contains a custom timeout value (in seconds) for the dialog. It may be used only in a request (initial or sequential) context.

params.name: default_timeout
params.doc: The default dialog timeout (in seconds), in the absence of a custom value provided in an AVP.

params.name: early_timeout
params.doc: The timeout (in seconds) after which the dialogs in unconfirmed or early state (no final response received) are destroyed.

params.name: noack_timeout
params.doc: The timeout (in seconds) after which the dialogs which were answered with 200 OK but didn't receive the ACK are marked for termination (the lifetime is set to 10 more seconds).

params.name: end_timeout
params.doc: The timeout (in seconds) after which the dialogs in terminated state are destroyed.

params.name: dlg_extra_hdrs
params.doc: A string containing the extra headers (full format, with EOH) to be added to requests generated locally by the module (like BYEs).

params.name: dlg_match_mode
params.doc: How the sequential requests should be matched against the known dialogs. The modes are a combination of matching based on a cookie (DID) stored as cookie in Record-Route header and matching based on SIP elements (as in RFC 3261).

params.name: detect_spirals
params.doc: Whether spirals (i.e., messages routed through the proxy multiple times) should be detected.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: In order to store information about dialogs in a database, a database URL must be specified.

params.name: db_mode
params.doc: Mode of synchronisation of dialog information from memory to an underlying database (if desired):

params.name: db_update_period
params.doc: The interval (seconds) at which to update dialogs' information, if the server is configured to store the dialog information at a given interval. A too short interval will generate intensive database operations, while an excessively long one will miss dialogs with a short lifetime.

params.name: db_fetch_rows
params.doc: The number of the rows to be fetched at once from database when loading the dialog records at startup from the database. This value can be used to tune the load time at startup. For 1MB of private memory (default), it should be below 400. The database driver must support the fetch_result() capability. A value of 0 means the database fetch is not limited.

params.name: db_skip_load
params.doc: Set db_skip_load to 1, to skip the loading of dialog data from the database.

params.name: table_name
params.doc: Database table name used for storing dialog information.

params.name: call_id_column
params.doc: The column name in the database to store the dialog call-id.

params.name: from_uri_column
params.doc: The column name in the database to store the caller's SIP address (URI).

params.name: from_tag_column
params.doc: The column name in the database to store the From header tag from the INVITE request.

params.name: to_uri_column
params.doc: The column name in the database to store the callee's SIP address (URI).

params.name: to_tag_column
params.doc: The column name in the database to store the To header tag from the 200 OK response to the INVITE request, if present.

params.name: from_cseq_column
params.doc: The column name in the database to store the Cseq from caller side.

params.name: to_cseq_column
params.doc: The column name in the database to store the cseq from callee side.

params.name: from_route_column
params.doc: The column name in the database to store the route records from caller side (proxy to caller).

params.name: to_route_column
params.doc: The column name in the database to store the route records from callee side (proxy to callee).

params.name: from_contact_column
params.doc: The column name in the database to store the caller's contact uri.

params.name: to_contact_column
params.doc: The column name in the database to store the callee's contact uri.

params.name: from_sock_column
params.doc: The column name in the database to store the information about the local interface receiving the traffic from caller.

params.name: to_sock_column
params.doc: The column name in the database to store information about the local interface receiving the traffic from callee.

params.name: h_id_column
params.doc: The column name in the database to store the dialogs' hash id information.

params.name: h_entry_column
params.doc: The column name in the database to store the dialog's hash entry information.

params.name: state_column
params.doc: The column name in the database to store the dialog's state information.

params.name: start_time_column
params.doc: The column name in the database to store the dialog's start time information.

params.name: timeout_column
params.doc: The column name in the database to store the dialog's timeout.

params.name: sflags_column
params.doc: The column name in the database to store the dialog script flags.

params.name: toroute_name_column
params.doc: The column name in the database to store the index of the route to be executed at timeout.

params.name: vars_table_name
params.doc: If you want to store the dialog variables (“$dlg_var(name)”) for a dialog in a database a table name must be specified.

params.name: vars_h_id_column
params.doc: The column name in the database to store the dialog's hash id information (as a reference to the dialog table).

params.name: vars_h_entry_column
params.doc: The column name in the database to store the dialog's hash entry information (as a reference to the dialog table).

params.name: vars_key_column
params.doc: The column name in the database to store the names (keys) of a dialog variable.

params.name: vars_value_column
params.doc: The column name in the database to store the values of a dialog variable.

params.name: profiles_with_value
params.doc: List of names for profiles with values, separated with semi-colon ";".

params.name: profiles_no_value
params.doc: List of names for profiles without values, separated with semi-colon ";".

params.name: bridge_controller
params.doc: SIP address to be used in From header when initiating a call bridge.

params.name: bridge_contact
params.doc: SIP address to be used in Contact header when doing a call bridge.

params.name: initial_cbs_inscript
params.doc: If the initial dialog callbacks (i.e., DLGCB_CREATED and DLGCB_SPIRALED) should be executed in-script or post-script. If dlg_manage() is not used, the setting of this parameter does not matter; otherwise, initial callbacks will be executed directly after dlg_manage() is called if this parameter is enabled. If it is disabled, initial callback execution will be postponed until configuration script execution completes.

params.name: send_bye
params.doc: If set to 1, BYE requests will be sent out for each dialog that timed out. It is an alternative to $dlg_ctx(timeout_bye)=1 for all dialogs.

params.name: dlg_filter_mode
params.doc: Set dialog fitering mode, which can specify what dialogs are processed. Its value can be a combination (the sum) of following flags: * 1 - do not send keepalives and do not execute timeout function if dialog is not local (if the associated bind address is not a local socket).

params.name: wait_ack
params.doc: If set to 1, dialog will be kept a bit longer in memory in order to absorb the ACK negative replies of initial INVITE. If not, the dialog is destroyed when negative reply is sent out (less internal complexity).

params.name: ka_timer
params.doc: Keep-alive timer step - how often to execute the callback to send dialog keep alives (SIP OPTIONS requests within dialog). The value represents the number of seconds.

params.name: ka_interval
params.doc: The interval between keep alives within dialog (SIP OPTIONS requests), sent to caller or callee. The keep alive request will be sent by the first callback fired by KA timer after the ka_interval elapsed from dialog setup or previous keep-alive. The value represents the number of seconds.

params.name: ka_failed_limit
params.doc: The number of failed keep-alive requests that is accepted before generating a dialog timeout.

params.name: timeout_noreset
params.doc: If set to 1, the dialog timeout won't be reset each time a sequential request is processed. It is an alternative to dlg_set_property("timeout-noreset") for all dialogs.

params.name: timer_procs
params.doc: If set to 1, the dialog module will start a separate dialog timer process to execute dialog timeout tasks. The default is to use the core timer process.

params.name: enable_dmq
params.doc: If set to 1, the dialog will be synced via dmq. For now, only very basic dialog info is shared, just enough to have synced profiles. Notably, it is not possible to send in-dialog requests on any but the original proxy instance.

params.name: track_cseq_updates
params.doc: Enable the callbacks for tracking if CSeq number needs to be updated. It is the case when the INVITE has to be authenticated to downstream provider using uac_auth() from uac module.

params.name: lreq_callee_headers
params.doc: SIP headers to be added when sending local generated requests (e.g., BYE) to callee. It can be useful when you use topoh module with call-id masking (see the docs of topoh module).

params.name: event_callback
params.doc: The name of the function in the kemi configuration file (embedded scripting language such as Lua, Python, ...) to be executed instead of event_route[...] blocks.

params.name: h_id_start
params.doc: Set the offset to be used for generating dialog internal hash id. If set to -1, the h_id_start is set to the value of the server_id global parameter.

params.name: h_id_step
params.doc: Set the step to increment the dialog internal hash id.

params.name: keep_proxy_rr
params.doc: Whether to keep the record-route header added by the proxy. When enabled, it will keep this proxy's record-route header from the reply. The result is that generated requests like the BYE from the dlg_end_dlg mi function will pass through the proxy (looped).

params.name: bye_early_code
params.doc: This parameter defines the reply-code being used for dialogs being terminated in early stage (e.g. before 200 OK/ACK). Default value is “480”.

params.name: bye_early_reason
params.doc: This parameter defines the reply-reason being used for dialogs being terminated in early stage (e.g. before 200 OK/ACK). Default value is “Temporarily Unavailable”.

params.name: dlg_ctxiuid_mode
params.doc: Set dialog context iuid mode, which can specify additional cases when the internal unique id should be set: * 1 - set it when processing CANCEL requests.

params.name: debug_variables
params.doc: Activate additional debugging for printing internal lists for dialog variables. This output is only visible at debug log level and should only be used for debugging. By default it is deactivated.

params.name: dlg_mode
params.doc: Control how dialog state management is done. If set to 0, the the management is done with tm module callbacks; if set to 1, tm callbacks are not used, states have to be set from config.

functions.name: set_dlg_profile
functions.doc: Inserts the current dialog into a profile. Note that if the profile does not support values, they will be silently discarded. Also, there is no check for inserting the same dialog into the same profile multiple times.

functions.name: unset_dlg_profile
functions.doc: Removes the current dialog from a profile.

functions.name: is_in_profile
functions.doc: Checks if the current dialog belongs to a profile. If the profile is defined with values, then the check is also matching with the specific value provided as parameter.

functions.name: get_profile_size
functions.doc: Returns the number of dialogs belonging to a profile. If the profile supports values, the check can be reinforced to take into account a specific value, i.e. how many dialogs were inserted into the profile with a specific value. If no value is passed, only the membership of the dialog in the profile per se is checked. Note that if the profile does not support values, the value parameter will be silently discarded.

functions.name: dlg_isflagset
functions.doc: Check if the dialog flag is set or not.

functions.name: dlg_setflag
functions.doc: Set a dialog flag.

functions.name: dlg_resetflag
functions.doc: Reset the dialog flag.

functions.name: dlg_bye
functions.doc: Send BYE to parties of a dialog or - if in early stage - a CANCEL to the B-Party and a SIP response to the A-Party (as defined in bye_early_code / bye_early_reason).

functions.name: dlg_refer
functions.doc: Refer the 'side' to a new SIP 'address'.

functions.name: dlg_refer_did
functions.doc: Refer the 'side' of the identified dialog to a new SIP 'address'.

functions.name: dlg_refer_dcid
functions.doc: Refer the 'side' of the first matching dialog by call-id to a new SIP 'address'.

functions.name: dlg_manage
functions.doc: Process current SIP request with dialog module.

functions.name: dlg_bridge
functions.doc: Bridge 'from' SIP address to 'to' SIP address via outbound proxy 'op'.

functions.name: dlg_get
functions.doc: Search and set current dialog based on Call-ID, From-Tag and To-Tag parameters.

functions.name: dlg_get_var
functions.doc: Get dlg_var of another dialog value based on Call-ID, From-Tag and To-Tag parameters.

functions.name: dlg_set_var
functions.doc: Set dlg_var of another dialog value based on Call-ID, From-Tag and To-Tag parameters.

functions.name: is_known_dlg
functions.doc: This function checks if the current SIP message being processed belongs to any transaction within an active dialog that the dialog module is currently tracking. This is a check for tracking of any kind, without regard to profiles.

functions.name: dlg_set_timeout
functions.doc: Set the dialog timeout. Dialog timeout will be updated if it was already set. If h_entry and h_id parameters are not provided, the dialog will be searched based on (callid, fromtag, totag) of currently processed SIP message.

functions.name: dlg_set_timeout_by_profile
functions.doc: Like dlg_set_timeout(), but simultaneously sets the timeout of all dialogs in a given profile. Can be constrained by profile value.

functions.name: dlg_set_property
functions.doc: Set a dialog property - an attribute that enable/disable various behaviours (e.g., sending keep alive requests).

functions.name: dlg_remote_profile
functions.doc: Manage remote profile via config file. A remote profile item is considered when the dialog is not managed by this server instance. The notification to add/remove can be received via SIP or a RPC command, the operation can be then triggered from configuration file. This should allow counting active dialogs in a profile that are managed by multiple SIP server instances.

functions.name: dlg_set_ruri
functions.doc: This function sets the R-URI with the corresponding endpoint address stored in dialog structure (i.e., its Contact field).

functions.name: dlg_db_load_callid
functions.doc: Load dialog record from database matching on Call-Id provided as parameter.

functions.name: dlg_db_load_extra
functions.doc: Load all dialog records from database that are not in memory of the current Kamailio instance.

functions.name: dlg_reset_property
functions.doc: Reset a dialog property - an attribute that enable/disable various behaviours (e.g., sending keep alive requests).

functions.name: dlg_req_within
functions.doc: Sends an in-dialog SIP Request with method to a party of a dialog indicated by the side parameter.

functions.name: dlg_set_state
functions.doc: Set the state for dialog matching current message.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: The translation rules will be loaded using this database URL.

params.name: table_name
params.doc: The name of the database table used to load the translation rules.

params.name: dpid_col
params.doc: The column name used to store the dialplan group ID.

params.name: pr_col
params.doc: The column name used to store the priority of the corresponding rule from the database row.

params.name: match_op_col
params.doc: The column name used to store the type of matching of the rule.

params.name: match_exp_col
params.doc: The column name to store the rule match expression.

params.name: match_len_col
params.doc: The column name to store the length of a string matching the match expression.

params.name: subst_exp_col
params.doc: The column name to store the rule's substitution expression.

params.name: repl_exp_col
params.doc: The column name to store the rule's replacement expression.

params.name: attrs_col
params.doc: The column name to store the rule's attributes to be set after match (see attrs_pvar )

params.name: attrs_pvar
params.doc: The pseudovariable used to store the rule's attributes, after translation (when dp_translate() succeeds). This parameter can be an “AVP” or a script variable (“$var()”)..

params.name: fetch_rows
params.doc: The number of rows to be fetched at once from database

params.name: match_dynamic
params.doc: If set to 1, the match and substitution expressions can include script variables and their values are evaluated at runtime.

params.name: append_branch
params.doc: If set to 1, the module appends a new outgoing branch when request URI (r-uri) or its user part are changed by dp_translate() or dp_replace() inside a failure_route block. Set it to 0 if the branch should not be added.

params.name: reload_delta
params.doc: The number of seconds that have to be waited before executing a new reload of dialplan rules. By default there is a rate limiting of maximum one reload in five seconds.

functions.name: dp_replace
functions.doc: The function translates the input value 'inval' using the rules with dialplan id 'dpid', storing the value in the variable 'outvar'. If the rule that was applied has attributes, they are stored in the variable provided via the module parameter 'attrs_pvar'.

functions.name: dp_match
functions.doc: The function matches the input value 'inval' using the rules with dialplan id 'dpid'. If the rule that was applied has attributes, they are stored in the variable provided via the module parameter 'attrs_pvar'.

functions.name: dp_translate
functions.doc: Will try to translate “src” into “dest” according to the translation rules in the dialplan identified by “id” . If src/dest is missing the default parameter “ruri.user/ruri.user” will be used, thus translating the request URI user part. If only “dest” is missing, only matching and storing of the matching rule's attributes is done.

functions.name: dp_reload
functions.doc: Reload the translation rules from the database. Note that there is a rate limiting defined by 'reload_delta' parameter. By default is allowed maximum one reload in five seconds.

params.name: list_file
params.doc: Path to the file with destination sets (destination groups).

params.name: db_url
params.doc: If you want to load the list of gateways from the database you must set this parameter.

params.name: table_name
params.doc: If you want to load the list of gateways from the database you must set this parameter as the database name.

params.name: setid_col
params.doc: The column's name in the database storing the gateway's set (group) id.

params.name: destination_col
params.doc: The column's name in the database storing the destination sip URI.

params.name: flags_col
params.doc: The column's name in the database storing the flags for the destination URI.

params.name: priority_col
params.doc: The column's name in the database storing the priority for destination URI.

params.name: attrs_col
params.doc: The column's name in the database storing the attributes for destination URI.

params.name: force_dst
params.doc: If set to 1, force overwriting of destination address (outbound proxy) when that is already set. If set to 0, will return error when the destination address is already set.

params.name: flags
params.doc: Various flags that affect dispatcher's behaviour. The flags are defined as a bitmask on an integer value. If flag 1 is set only the username part of the URI will be used when computing an URI based hash. If no flags are set the username, hostname and port will be used. The port is used only if different from 5060 (normal sip URI) or 5061 (in the sips: case).

params.name: use_default
params.doc: If the parameter is set to 1, the last address in destination set is used as a final option to send the request to. For example, it is useful when wanting to send the call to an announcement server saying: "the gateways are full, try later".

params.name: xavp_dst
params.doc: The name of the XAVP which will hold the list with addresses and associated properties, in the order they have been selected by the chosen algorithm. If use_default is 1, the values of last XAVP correspond to the last address in destination set. In case of using dispatcher.list file, you have to set the priority field for each destination to ensure a particular order there. The first XAVP is the current selected destination. All the other addresses from the destination set will be added in the XAVP list to be able to implement serial forking.

params.name: xavp_dst_mode
params.doc: Control what fields are added to the XAVP specified by xavp_dst parameter.

params.name: xavp_ctx
params.doc: The name of the XAVP which will hold some attributes specific to dispatcher routing context. The XAVP can hold the next fields: cnt - the number of addresses selected for routing.

params.name: xavp_ctx_mode
params.doc: Control what fields are added to the XAVP specified by xavp_ctx parameter. The cnt field is added if xavp_cnt_mode does not have the bit 1 set.

params.name: hash_pvar
params.doc: String with PVs used for the hashing algorithm 7.

params.name: setid_pvname
params.doc: The name of the PV where to store the set ID (group ID) when calling ds_is_from_list() with no parameter.

params.name: attrs_pvname
params.doc: The name of the PV where to store the attributes of matching address when calling ds_is_from_list().

params.name: ds_ping_method
params.doc: With this method you can define, with which method you want to probe the gateways. Pinging gateways feature depends on ds_ping_interval parameter.

params.name: ds_ping_from
params.doc: With this Method you can define the "From:"-Line for the request, sent to the failed gateways. This method is only available, if compiled with the probing of failed gateways enabled.

params.name: ds_ping_interval
params.doc: With this parameter you can define the interval for sending a request to a gateway marked as inactive upon a failed request routing to it. This parameter is only used, when the TM-Module is loaded. If set to “0”, the pinging of inactive gateway is disabled.

params.name: ds_ping_fr_timer
params.doc: If greater than 0, its value is used to set the "fr_timer" value for the local transactions created to send out the OPTIONS pings.

params.name: ds_probing_threshold
params.doc: If you want to set a gateway into inactive mode, there can be a specific number of failed requests until it will change from "active" to "inactive". It is using the state "trying", that allows selection of gateway but indicates there was a failure previously with the gateway. The number of attempts can be set with this parameter. This parameter can be modified via ser config framework.

params.name: ds_inactive_threshold
params.doc: If you want to set a gateway into active mode (after being inactive), there can be a specific number of successful requests until it will change from "inactive" to "active". The number of attempts can be set with this parameter. This parameter can be modified via ser config framework.

params.name: ds_ping_reply_codes
params.doc: This parameter defines the valid response codes, which are accepted as a valid reply to the PING-Method. It is a list separated by colons, where you may define either a single code (e.g. "code=202" would accept 202 as an additional, valid response) or a class of responses, you want to accept (e.g. "class=2" would accept everything from 200 to 299 as valid response). This parameter can be modified via config framework.

params.name: ds_probing_mode
params.doc: Controls what gateways are tested to see if they are reachable. * Value 0: If set to 0, only the gateways with state PROBING are tested. After a gateway is probed, the PROBING state is cleared in this mode. This means that no probing will be executed at all only if flag in config file is set to 8/PROBING (please check destination list file syntaxis for more details), it will probe only one time at startup or after dispatcher reload. * Value 1: If set to 1, all gateways are tested. If set to 1 and there is a failure of keepalive to an active gateway, then it is set to TRYING state. This means that probing will be executed all the time, but you can skip some servers with flag 4 in destination list file, for example. * Value 2: if set to 2, only gateways in INACTIVE state with PROBING mode set are tested. * Value 3: If set to 3, any gateway with state PROBING is continually probed without modifying/removing the PROBING state. This allows selected gateways to be probed continually, regardless of state changes.

params.name: ds_ping_latency_stats
params.doc: Enable latency measurement when pinging nodes The estimator can be initialized at startup and reload using the attribute latency. * If set to 0, disable latency measurement. * If set to 1, enable latency measurement.

params.name: ds_retain_latency_stats
params.doc: Retain latency stats for existing destinations when reloading from file or database. * If set to 0, stats for all destinations will be reset on reload. * If set to 1, stats for existing destinations will persist across reloads.

params.name: ds_latency_estimator_alpha
params.doc: The parameter decides how important each latency ping observation is in the calculation of the EWMA. The higher the value of alpha, the more closely the EWMA tracks the original time series. Because Kamailio doesn't support float parameter types, the value in the parameter is divided by 1000 and stored as float. For example, if you want to set the alpha to be 0.25, use value 250 here.

params.name: ds_hash_size
params.doc: The value to be used as power of two to set the number of slots to hash table storing data for call load dispatching (e.g., value 8 will create a hash table with 256 slots). It must be greater than 0 to enable call load dispatching feature (alg 10).

params.name: ds_hash_expire
params.doc: Expiration time in seconds to remove the load on a destination if no BYE was received meanwhile.

params.name: ds_hash_initexpire
params.doc: Expiration time in seconds to remove the load on a destination if no 200 for INVITE was received meanwhile and state updated with ds_load_update().

params.name: ds_hash_check_interval
params.doc: Time interval in seconds to scan internal hash table with call load dispatching data for expired items.

params.name: outbound_proxy
params.doc: SIP URI of outbound proxy to be used when sending pings.

params.name: ds_default_socket
params.doc: Default socket to be used for sending pings and dispatching requests when a gateway has no send socket configured.

params.name: ds_default_sockname
params.doc: Default socket name to be used for sending pings and dispatching requests when a gateway has no send socket configured.

params.name: ds_ping_socket
params.doc: Default socket to be used for sending ping requests when a gateway has no "ping_socket" configured.

params.name: ds_timer_mode
params.doc: Specify the timer process to be used by the module for keepalives and active dialogs tracking.

params.name: event_callback
params.doc: The name of the function in the kemi configuration file (embedded scripting language such as Lua, Python, ...) to be executed instead of event_route[...] blocks.

params.name: event_callback_mode
params.doc: Controls when the event_route or the KEMI event callback function are executed. If set to 0, they are executed when the destination state changes based on OPTIONS keepalives or the use of config functions to set the state (e.g., ds_mark_dst(...)). If set to 1, they are executed only on state change due to OPTIONS keepalives. If set to 2, the event routes will always be executed when a state change occurs, even if no previous state exists (for example, on startup or reload).

params.name: ds_attrs_none
params.doc: If set to 1, "none=yes" is set in the attrs for those records that have no attrs value, to ensure that corresponding XAVP fields for records do not get mixed up.

params.name: ds_db_extra_attrs
params.doc: Set a list of column names to be loaded from database dispatcher table and be concatenated to 'attrs' field. The format is: 'aname1=cname1;aname2=cname2;...;anameN=cnameN'.

params.name: ds_load_mode
params.doc: If set to 1, the module throws error when failing to add a destination address (e.g., invalid URI). If set to 0, it skips the failing address and continues with the next ones.

params.name: reload_delta
params.doc: The number of seconds that have to be waited before executing a new reload of dispatcher records. By default there is a rate limiting of maximum one reload in five seconds.

params.name: ds_dns_mode
params.doc: Specify the how DNS resolving is done for destination addresses.

params.name: ds_dns_interval
params.doc: The interval in seconds to periodically refresh the DNS queries for destination addresses if ds_dns_mode has value 4 set.

params.name: ds_dns_ttl
params.doc: The interval in seconds to set TTL for DNS results received for queries dones inside this module. If 0, this TTL is not set, result and core values are used.

functions.name: ds_select_dst
functions.doc: The method selects a destination from addresses set. It returns true if a new destination is set. The selected address is set to dst_uri field (aka the outbound proxy address or the $du variable), not being visible in the SIP request.

functions.name: ds_select_domain
functions.doc: The method selects a destination from addresses set and rewrites the host and port from R-URI. The parameters have same meaning as for ds_select_dst().

functions.name: ds_select
functions.doc: The method selects a destination from addresses set and adds it in the XAVP specified for this module. It is not updating R-URI nor the destination URI. The parameters have same meaning as for ds_select_dst().

functions.name: ds_select_routes
functions.doc: The method selects destinations following the rules combining groups add algorithms, controlling where the first destination address is pushed, and optionally setting a limit of selected addresses.

functions.name: ds_next_dst
functions.doc: Takes the next destination address from the corresponding XAVPs and sets the dst_uri (outbound proxy address).

functions.name: ds_next_domain
functions.doc: Takes the next destination address from the corresponding XAVPs and sets the domain part of the request URI.

functions.name: ds_set_dst
functions.doc: Takes the current destination address from the corresponding XAVPs and sets the dst_uri (outbound proxy address).

functions.name: ds_set_domain
functions.doc: Takes the current destination address from the corresponding XAVPs and sets the domain part of the request URI.

functions.name: ds_mark_dst
functions.doc: Mark the last used address from destination set as inactive ("i"/"I"), active ("a"/"A"), disabled ("d"/"D") or trying ("t"/"T"). Apart of disabled state, a destination can be set in probing mode by adding ("p"/"P") flag. With this function, an automatic detection of failed gateways can be implemented. When an address is marked as inactive or disabled, it will be ignored by 'ds_select_dst' and 'ds_select_domain'.

functions.name: ds_mark_addr
functions.doc: Set the state to the target specified by setid and uri. The parameter state can have same value as for ds_mark_dst(). All parameters can contain variables.

functions.name: ds_list_exists
functions.doc: Function alias: ds_list_exist(groupid)

functions.name: ds_is_from_list
functions.doc: This function returns true, if there is a match of source address or uri with an address in the given group of the dispatcher-list; otherwise false.

functions.name: ds_is_active
functions.doc: This function returns true, if there is an active URI in the destination group; otherwise false. If the uri parameter is provided, then the corresponding destination has to be active.

functions.name: ds_load_update
functions.doc: Updates the load state: * if it is a BYE or CANCEL - remove the load from destination address used to forward the INVITE * if it is a reply to INVITE - set internal state to confirmed for call load structure when reply code is 2xx.

functions.name: ds_load_unset
functions.doc: Remove the call load for the destination that routed the call.

functions.name: ds_reload
functions.doc: Reloads the groups and included destinations.

functions.name: ds_dsg_fetch
functions.doc: Sets the destination group id to setid for fetching $dsg(key) attributes.

functions.name: ds_dsg_fetch_uri
functions.doc: Sets the destination group id to setid for fetching $dsg(key) attributes and the overload-control attributes to the corresponding uri record from that group.

functions.name: ds_oc_set_attrs
functions.doc: Sets the overload control rate, time interval limit and sequence number for the destination record (setid, uri) following RFC7339 specifications.

params.name: suffix
params.doc: The suffix to be appended to the end of the header field. You can use the parameter to specify additional parameters to be added to the header field, see the example.

functions.name: add_diversion
functions.doc: The function adds a new diversion header field before any other existing Diversion header field in the message (the newly added Diversion header field will become the topmost Diversion header field). If 'uri' parameter is missing, the inbound (without any modifications done by the proxy server) Request-URI will be used as the Diversion URI.

params.name: active_lifetime
params.doc: The lifetime in seconds of an active dialog in memory. A dialog is considered active after the ACK of 200 OK for INVITE.

params.name: init_lifetime
params.doc: The lifetime in seconds of an initial dialog in memory. A dialog is in initial state from the moment of creation until it gets to active state. If the dialog stays longer in the initial state, then it is destroyed by the next timer cleanup.

params.name: finish_lifetime
params.doc: The lifetime in seconds of a finished dialog in memory. A dialog is finished if the initial INVITE was not answered or the BYE was received. Once this lifetime passes, the dialog record is removed from memory by the next timer cleanup.

params.name: timer_interval
params.doc: The value in seconds to run the timer callback function for cleaning up dialogs past the lifetime limit.

params.name: hash_size
params.doc: The size of the hash table internally used to keep the dialogs. A larger table is much faster but consumes more memory. The hash size must be a power of two.

functions.name: dlgs_init
functions.doc: Start track the dialog corresponding to the current SIP message. It has to be used for INVITE messages.

functions.name: dlgs_update
functions.doc: Update dialog state. It has to be used for SIP requests only, the SIP responses are handled automatically.

functions.name: dlgs_count
functions.doc: Return the number of dialogs matching the filter specified by the parameters. It does not count the dialogs that are finished (not answered or terminated with BYE).

functions.name: dlgs_tags_add
functions.doc: Add a tag to current dialog.

functions.name: dlgs_tags_rm
functions.doc: Remove a tag from current dialog.

functions.name: dlgs_tags_count
functions.doc: Count all tags for ongoing dialogs matching the parameter.

params.name: server_address
params.doc: The local server address. This is the address with which the local DMQ node joins the servers group to send/receive messages.

params.name: server_socket
params.doc: The local listen address. This is the interface over which the DMQ engine will send/receive messages.

params.name: notification_address
params.doc: The address of another DMQ node from which the local node should retrieve initial information about all other nodes. This parameter can be specified multiple times in the configuration, to configure multiple notification servers. If you configure multiple notification servers, the multi_notify parameter needs to be disabled.

params.name: notification_channel
params.doc: The name of the channel for notifications about peers availability.

params.name: multi_notify
params.doc: Enables the ability to resolve multiple IPv4/IPv6 addresses for a single notification address. Please note that this mode is not supported if you specify multiple notification address parameter.

params.name: num_workers
params.doc: The number of worker threads for sending/receiving messages.

params.name: worker_usleep
params.doc: The default locking/synchronisation mechanism between producer/consumer threads is the optimum for most environments. On some systems (e.g. FreeBSD) it can cause high CPU load and in such cases, it can be useful to disable locking and switch to polling for tasks at set intervals instead - putting the thread to sleep in-between and taking it out of process during that time.

params.name: ping_interval
params.doc: The number of seconds between node pings (for checking status of other nodes).

params.name: remove_inactive
params.doc: A value of zero disable removing dmq nodes. Node status will be changed to not_active. A non-zero value (default is 1) enable removing nodes. For node that is defined as notification address status will be changed to not_active. Otherwise it will be marked as disabled and then will be removed.

params.name: fail_count_enabled
params.doc: Enable per node counting of failed responses.

params.name: fail_count_threshold_not_active
params.doc: DMQ node status change from "active" to "not_active" if 408 fail counts are greater than this threshold value: This threshold can be reached both via internal DMQ notification ping mechanism, and other modules that use dmq to broadcast messages: * Fail counts reset every time a node responds with response code 200 OK, on response callback of notification ping. * Fail counts increase every time a node responds with response code 408, on response callback of notification ping. * Fail counts increase every time a node responds with response code 408, on response callback of other modules that use dmq, only if node is in "active" state.

params.name: fail_count_threshold_disabled
params.doc: DMQ node status change from "not_active" to "disabled" if 408 fail counts are greater than this threshold value. This threshold can be reached only via internal DMQ notification ping mechanism: * Fail counts reset every time a node responds with response code 200 OK, on response callback of notification ping. * Fail counts increase every time a node responds with response code 408, on response callback of notification ping.

functions.name: dmq_handle_message
functions.doc: Handles a DMQ message by passing it to the appropriate local peer (module). The peer is identified by the user part of the To header.

functions.name: dmq_process_message
functions.doc: Similar to dmq_handle_message, but the processing is happening immediately, no longer cloning the request in shared memory to be passed to a DMQ worker process.

functions.name: dmq_send_message
functions.doc: Sends a DMQ message directly from config file to a single node.

functions.name: dmq_bcast_message
functions.doc: Broadcasts a DMQ message from config file to all active nodes (except self) on the specific channel.

functions.name: dmq_t_replicate
functions.doc: Replicates the current SIP message to all active nodes (except self). Useful for replicating REGISTER, PUBLISH etc. in a clustered environment.

functions.name: dmq_is_from_node
functions.doc: Checks whether the current message has been sent by another active DMQ node in the cluster.

params.name: enable
params.doc: The parameter controls whether the replication is active or not. The value can be: * 0 - replication is disabled * 1 - replication is enabled

params.name: sync
params.doc: The parameter controls whether to request synchronization of all usrloc records at startup. The value can be: * 0 - disabled * 1 - enabled

params.name: batch_size
params.doc: The parameter controls whether to throttle synchronization of all contacts in batches. Once a batch of SIP requests is sent out, then sleep for 'batch_usleep' microseconds. The value can be: * <=0 - disabled (no batching) * >0 - how many records to be sent in a batch

params.name: batch_usleep
params.doc: The parameter controls whether to throttle synchronization of all contacts in batches. Once a batch of SIP requests is sent out, then sleep for 'batch_usleep' microseconds. The value can be: * <=0 - no sleep (it disables the batching) * >0 - how many microseconds to sleep before sending out another batch of usrloc records.

params.name: batch_msg_size
params.doc: The parameter controls the size of the messages during a sync. This is to make sure the messages are never larger than 65536 (the maximum datagram size).

params.name: batch_msg_contacts
params.doc: The parameter controls the amount of contact per message/transaction during a sync.

params.name: usrloc_domain
params.doc: The usrloc domain to synchronize.

params.name: replicate_socket_info
params.doc: The parameter controls whether the socket replication is active or not. This is important for anycast scenarios. The value can be: * 0 - disabled * 1 - enabled, replicate socket by proto:host:port * 2 - enabled, replicate socket by socket name * 3 - enabled, use local socket from dmq server_socket modparam

params.name: replicate_cflags
params.doc: The parameter controls whether the cflags replication is active or not. This is important for anycast scenarios. The value can be: * 0 - disabled * 1 - enabled, replicate cflags * > 1 - enabled, set cflags corresponding to this value, on replicated peers

params.name: usrloc_delete
params.doc: Enable (1) or disable (0) synchronizing usrloc delete actions. Disabling delete actions can be useful when user location data is ephemeral.

params.name: usrloc_delete_expired
params.doc: Enable (1) or disable (0) synchronizing usrloc expire actions using delete actions. In other words, sync delete of (UL_CONTACT_EXPIRE) expired contacts.

params.name: general_query_flags
params.doc: Set this parameter to an integer value containing of an ORed result of one or more of the following values (constant present only for documentation process, as they are mostly mapped to libval flags). Setting this parameter will cause the libval defaults to be completely overwritten

params.name: db_url
params.doc: This is URL of the database to be used.

params.name: domain_table
params.doc: Name of table containing names of local domains that the proxy is responsible for.

params.name: domain_attrs_table
params.doc: Name of table containing attributes of local domains.

params.name: did_col
params.doc: Name of column containing domain id (did) of domain in domain and domain_attrs tables. In domain table, a did column value may be NULL, which means that it has same value as domain column.

params.name: domain_col
params.doc: Name of column containing domain name in domain table.

params.name: name_col
params.doc: Name of column containing attribute name in domain_attrs table.

params.name: type_col
params.doc: Name of column containing attribute type in domain_attrs table. Type value 0 is integer and type value 2 is string.

params.name: value_col
params.doc: Name of column containing attribute value in domain_attrs table.

params.name: register_myself
params.doc: Register the list of domains to match 'myself' check: 0 means no myself registration, 1 means enable myself registration.

functions.name: is_from_local
functions.doc: Checks based on domain table if host part of From header uri is one of the local domains that the proxy is responsible for

functions.name: is_uri_host_local
functions.doc: If called from route or failure route block, checks based on domain table if host part of Request-URI is one of the local domains that the proxy is responsible for. If called from branch route, the test is made on host part of URI of first branch, which thus must have been appended to the transaction before is_uri_host_local() is called.

functions.name: is_domain_local
functions.doc: This function checks if the domain contained in the parameter is local. The parameter can be a static string or contain pseudo-variables.

functions.name: lookup_domain
functions.doc: This function checks if domain given in domain argument is local and, if so, adds attributes associated with domain's id (did) to AVPs.
