If prefix argument (string) is given, names of attributes are prefixes by it. In addition to attributes given in domain_attrs table, AVP named did containing the did of domain is added.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: This is URL of the database to be used.

params.name: dp_table
params.doc: Name of table containing the local support domain policy setup.

params.name: dp_col_rule
params.doc: Name of column containing the domain policy rule name which is equal to the URI as published in the domain policy NAPTRs.

params.name: dp_col_type
params.doc: Name of column containing the domain policy rule type. In the case of federation names, this is "fed". For standard referrals according to draft-lendl-speermint-technical-policy-00, this is "std". For direct domain lookups, this is "dom".

params.name: dp_col_att
params.doc: Name of column containing the AVP's name. If the rule stored in this row triggers, than dp_can_connect() will add an AVP with that name.

params.name: dp_col_val
params.doc: Name of column containing the value for AVPs created by dp_can_connect().

params.name: port_override_avp
params.doc: This parameter defines the name of the AVP where dp_apply_policy() will look for an override port number.

params.name: transport_override_avp
params.doc: Name of the AVP which contains the override transport setting.

params.name: domain_replacement_avp
params.doc: Name of the AVP which contains a domain replacement.

params.name: domain_prefix_avp
params.doc: Name of the AVP which contains a domain prefix.

params.name: domain_suffix_avp
params.doc: Name of the AVP which contains a domain suffix.

params.name: send_socket_avp
params.doc: Name of the AVP which contains a send_socket. The format of the send socket (the payload of this AVP) must be in the format [proto:]ip_address[:port]. The function dp_apply_policy will look for this AVP and if defined, it will force the send socket to its value (similar to the force_send_socket core function).

functions.name: dp_can_connect
functions.doc: Checks the interconnection policy of the caller. It uses the domain in the request URI to perform the DP-DDDS algorithm according to draft-lendl-domain-policy-ddds-02 to retrieve the domain's policy announcements. As of this version, only records conforming to draft-lendl-speermint-federations-02 and draft-lendl-speermint-technical-policy-00 are supported.

functions.name: dp_apply_policy
functions.doc: This function sets the destination URI according to the policy returned from the dp_can_connect() function. Parameter exchange between dp_can_connect() and dp_apply_policy() is done via AVPs. The AVPs can be configured in the module's parameter section.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: The database url.

params.name: drd_table
params.doc: The name of the db table storing gateway addresses.

params.name: drr_table
params.doc: The name of the db table storing routing rules.

params.name: drg_table
params.doc: The name of the db table storing groups.

params.name: drl_table
params.doc: The name of the db table storing definitions of destination lists (to be used directly by the routing rules). You will have an identifier to a group of gateways instead of having all the members of the group as individual elements. Very useful to reuse a list of gateways in different places.

params.name: sort_order
params.doc: Defines how the destination list should be processed (ordering of the elements). Possible modes are * 0 - destination groups are ignored and all the destinations are tried in the given order; Ex: list 1,2;3,4,5;6 will lead to usage as 1,2,3,4,5,6 * 1 - the destinations from each group are randomly arranged (only the two first elements are randomly selected); groups do maintain their order (as given); the resulting list is used (with all the defined destinations). Ex: 1,2;3,4,5;6 -> randomizer -> (A) 2,1;4,3,5;6 -> usage 2,1,4,3,5,6 (B) 1,2;3,5,4;6 -> usage 1,2,3,5,4,6 * 2 - from each destination group, only a single destination is randomly selected; groups do maintain their order (as given); Ex: 1,2;3,4,5;6 -> randomizer -> (A) 2;4;6 -> usage 2,4,6 (B) 1;5;6 -> usage 1,5,6 It is ok to have repeating gateways in different groups. The module will take care internally in case of failure not to choose a gateway that was tried already. Ex: 1,2,3; 1,2,3; 1,2,3 -> no gateway will be chosen twice. So in case there are 2 failures, all the three gateways (1,2,3) will be tried in a random order.

params.name: ruri_avp
params.doc: The name of the avp for storing Request URIs to be later used (alternative destinations for the current one).

params.name: attrs_avp
params.doc: The name of the avp for storing the attribute of the current selected destination - once a new destination is selected (via the use_next_gw() function), the AVP will be updated with the attrs of the new used destination.

params.name: use_domain
params.doc: Flag to configure whether to use domain match when querying database for user's routing group.

params.name: drg_user_col
params.doc: The name of the column in group db table where the username is stored.

params.name: drg_domain_col
params.doc: The name of the column in group db table where the domain is stored.

params.name: drg_grpid_col
params.doc: The name of the column in group db table where the group id is stored.

params.name: fetch_rows
params.doc: The number of rows that should be fetched from the result of a query in rules db table.

params.name: force_dns
params.doc: Force DNS resolving of GW/destination names (if not IPs) during startup. If not enabled, the GW name will be blindly used during routing.

params.name: enable_keepalive
params.doc: Enable monitoring of GW/destinations using keepalive module. Destinations found unavailable will not be used on do_routing() call.

functions.name: do_routing
functions.doc: Function to trigger routing of the message according to the rules in the database table and the configured parameters.

functions.name: next_routing
functions.doc: The function takes the next available destination (set by do_routing, as alternative destinations) and push it into RURI. Note that the function just sets the RURI (nothing more).

functions.name: use_next_gw
functions.doc: Same as next_routing().

functions.name: goes_to_gw
functions.doc: Function returns true if the destination of the current request (destination URI or Request URI) points (as IP) to one of the gateways. There is no DNS lookups done if the domain part of the URI is not an IP.

functions.name: is_from_gw
functions.doc: The function checks if the sender of the message is a gateway from a group in drouting rules.

params.name: domain_suffix
params.doc: The domain suffix to be added to the domain name obtained from the digits of an E164 number. Can be overridden by a parameter to enum_query.

params.name: tel_uri_params
params.doc: A string whose contents is appended to each new tel URI in the request as tel URI parameters.

params.name: i_enum_suffix
params.doc: The domain suffix to be used for i_enum_query() lookups. Can be overridden by a parameter to i_enum_query.

params.name: branchlabel
params.doc: This parameter determines which label i_enum_query() will use to branch off to the infrastructure ENUM tree.

params.name: bl_algorithm
params.doc: This parameter determines which algorithm the i_enum_query() function will use to select the position in the DNS tree where the infrastructure tree branches off the user ENUM tree.

functions.name: enum_query
functions.doc: The function performs an enum query and rewrites the Request-URI with the result of the query. See Section 1, “Overview” for more information.

functions.name: enum_pv_query
functions.doc: The function performs an enum query on E.164 number stored in its first argument and rewrites the Request-URI with the result of the query. See Section 1, “Overview” for more information.

functions.name: i_enum_query
functions.doc: The function performs an enum query and rewrites the Request-URI with the result of the query. This is the Infrastructure-ENUM version of enum_query(). The only difference to enum_query() is in the calculation of the FQDN where NAPTR records are looked for.

functions.name: is_from_user_enum
functions.doc: Checks if the user part of from URI is found in an enum lookup. Returns 1 if yes and -1 if not.

params.name: no_cnodes
params.doc: Number of erlang C node processes to be started to handle the communication tasks. A C node is a C program written to act as a hidden node in a distributed Erlang system.

params.name: cnode_alivename
params.doc: alivename is the registered name of the Kamailio process.

params.name: cnode_host
params.doc: C node host is the name of the machine we're running on. If long names are to be used, it should be fully qualified.

params.name: erlang_nodename
params.doc: The format of the node name is a name@host where name is the name given by the user and host is the full host name if long names are used, or the first part of the host name if short names are used.

params.name: cookie
params.doc: Each node has its own magic cookie. When a nodes tries to connect to another node, the magic cookies are compared If they do not match, the connected node rejects the connection.

params.name: trace_level
params.doc: Used to set tracing on the distribution. The parameter is different verbosity level. A higher level means more information. Useful in development, but in production should be disabled.

params.name: rpc_reply_with_struct
params.doc: Prepend Erlang atom struct in RPC Kamailio reply where RPC struct is generated. Some libraries for converting erlang term in JSON require atom struct as first element in tuple to convert list of properties into javscript object. Default value is 0 (disabled).

functions.name: erl_rpc
functions.doc: This function supports calling Erlang functions on remote nodes.

functions.name: erl_reg_send
functions.doc: This function sends an Erlang term to a registered process.

functions.name: erl_send
functions.doc: This function sends an Erlang term to a process. This function can be used from ANY_ROUTE. The argument pid is the Erlang process id of the intended recipient process on remote node. The argument msg is containing the message to be sent.

functions.name: erl_reply
functions.doc: Function to send message from event route (pseudo process). Function sends reply message msg to the sender process.

params.name: workers
params.doc: Number of worker processes to be started to handle incoming messages from remote applications. If the value is 0, the handling of the incoming message is done by the evapi dispatcher process.

params.name: bind_addr
params.doc: Local IP and port to listen on for incoming TCP connections.

params.name: netstring_format
params.doc: Control if messages on the socket (to and from clients) are encapsulated in netstring format.

params.name: event_callback
params.doc: The name of the function in the kemi configuration file (embedded scripting language such as Lua, Python, ...) to be executed instead of event_route[...] blocks.

params.name: max_clients
params.doc: Maximum number of clients that can connect to evapi socket.

params.name: wait_idle
params.doc: How many micro-seconds to wait on idle, when no evapi messages are in the processing queue.

params.name: wait_increase
params.doc: Increase wait_idle by itself till its value becomes initial value multiplied with wait_increase. The increase is done only consecutive cycles without any evapi message. When a new evapi message is received, wait_idle is reset to initial value. If wait_increase is set to 1, then wait_idle is used with its initial value always.

functions.name: evapi_relay
functions.doc: Relay the event data given as parameter to connected applications.

functions.name: evapi_async_relay
functions.doc: Relay the event data given as parameter to connected applications. Before evaluating the parameter, the request processing is suspended using tm module (using the t_suspend()/t_continue() framework). The routing of the SIP request can be continued once event_route[evapi:message-received] is triggered. After evapi_async_relay() returns true, no relaying should happen in request_route(), it should be followed by exit;.

functions.name: evapi_multicast
functions.doc: Relay the event data given as parameter to connections that match the tag provided by etag value. The etag can be a variable. For more see evapi_relay() and evapi_set_tag().

functions.name: evapi_async_multicast
functions.doc: Async relay the event data given as parameter to connections that match the tag provided by etag value. The etag can be a variable. For more see evapi_async_relay() and evapi_set_tag().

functions.name: evapi_unicast
functions.doc: Relay the event data given as parameter to the first connection that match the tag provided by etag value. The etag can be a variable. For more see evapi_relay() and evapi_set_tag().

functions.name: evapi_async_unicast
functions.doc: Async relay the event data given as parameter to the first connection that match the tag provided by etag value. The etag can be a variable. For more see evapi_async_relay() and evapi_set_tag().

functions.name: evapi_close
functions.doc: Close evapi current client connection.

functions.name: evapi_set_tag
functions.doc: Set tag name for current client connection. The parameters has to be a string up to 64 characters. It can also be a variable holding such string.

params.name: exec
params.doc: The definition of an exec task. The value of the parameter must have the following format: * "name=_string_;wait=_number_;workers=_number_;sockaddr=_udp_socket_ "

params.name: setvars
params.doc: Turn off to disable setting environment variables for executed commands.

params.name: time_to_kill
params.doc: Specifies the longest time a program is allowed to execute. If the time is exceeded, the program is killed.

functions.name: exec_dset
functions.doc: Executes an external command. Current URI is passed to the command as parameter. Output of the command is considered URI set (separated by lines).

functions.name: exec_msg
functions.doc: Executes an external command. The whole message is passed to it in input, no command-line parameters are added, output of the command is not processed.

functions.name: exec_avp
functions.doc: Executes an external command. Each line from output of the command is saved in an AVP from 'avplist'. If 'avplist' is missing, the AVPs are named 1, 2, 3, ...

functions.name: exec_cmd
functions.doc: Executes an external command. It is a lightweight version, which does not pass the SIP message as parameter, does not set the environment variables and it does not use the output of the command.

params.name: base_folder
params.doc: Absolute path to the folder where log files should be saved.

params.name: file
params.doc: The definition of a file and its properties. The value of the parameter may have the following format: * "name=accounting;extension=.out;interval=20;prefix=accounting:"

params.name: worker_usleep
params.doc: The time in microseconds which worker will sleep for until next iteration.

params.name: timer_interval
params.doc: The time in seconds which timer will trigger for rotating the files. Make sure that this value is lower than the interval of the files.

functions.name: file_out
functions.doc: This function is used to write a string to a file. The file is determined by the filename parameter. The string parameter is the string to be written to the file. Filename is the name of the file defined in the configuration file as name=filename.

params.name: init_vector
params.doc: The initialization vector used for the cryptographic operations. This needs to be a string value with 16 bytes lengths.

params.name: aes_mode
params.doc: Set it to 1 in order to do AES CBC encryption mode. By default, it does AES ECB mode.

params.name: register_callid
params.doc: Set it to 1 in order to register a callback to core for generation of callid values for requests generated by Kamailio tm module.

functions.name: gcrypt_aes_encrypt
functions.doc: Encrypts the text with the key using AES256 ECB encryption algorithm. The result is encoded in base64 format and stored in res. The parameter res must be a read-write variables. The parameters text and key can be static strings or strings with variables (dynamic strings).

functions.name: gcrypt_aes_decrypt
functions.doc: Decrypts the text with the key using AES256 ECB encryption algorithm. The text has to be encoded in base64 format. The parameter res must be a read-write variables. The parameters text and key can be static strings or strings with variables (dynamic strings).

params.name: path
params.doc: Path to the GeoIP database file.

functions.name: geoip_match
functions.doc: Match ipaddr against the GeoIP database and set the pvc container. The function has to be called before accessing a key via: $gip(pvc=>key).

params.name: path
params.doc: Path to the GeoIP2 database file.

params.name: resid
params.doc: Preregister result container id during initialization, enabling the use of the module in KEMI scripts. In native kamailio.cfg file, registration is done when parsing config and finding variables.

functions.name: geoip2_match
functions.doc: Match ipaddr against the GeoIP database and set the pvc container. The function has to be called before accessing a key via: $gip2(pvc=>key). At least one function needs to be present that access the pvc container, otherwise this function will not work.

functions.name: geoip2_distance
functions.doc: The function calculates the distance in miles between the geocoordinates of the IP address passed as parameter (the coordinates are calculated inside the function) and the geocoordinates latitude and longitude

params.name: db_url
params.doc: URL of the database table to be used.

params.name: table
params.doc: Name of the table holding strict definitions of groups and their members.

params.name: user_column
params.doc: Name of the “table” column holding usernames.

params.name: domain_column
params.doc: Name of the “table” column holding domains.

params.name: group_column
params.doc: Name of the “table” column holding group names.

params.name: use_domain
params.doc: If enabled (set to a non zero value) then the domain will be used also used for strict group matching; otherwise only the username part will be used.

params.name: re_table
params.doc: Name of the table holding definitions for regular-expression based groups. If no table is defined, the regular-expression support is disabled.

params.name: re_exp_column
params.doc: Name of the “re_table” column holding the regular expression used for user matching.

params.name: re_gid_column
params.doc: Name of the “re_table” column holding the group IDs.

params.name: multiple_gid
params.doc: If enabled (non zero value) the regular-expression matching will return all group IDs that match the user; otherwise only the first will be returned.

functions.name: is_user_in
functions.doc: This function is to be used for script group membership. The function returns true if username in the given URI is a member of the given group and false if not.

functions.name: get_user_group
functions.doc: This function is to be used for regular expression based group membership. The function returns true if username in the given URI belongs to at least one group; the group ID(s) are returned as AVPs.

params.name: header_name
params.doc: Name of the header that indicates compression or decompression has to be done.

params.name: header_value
params.doc: Value of the header that indicates compression or decompression has to be done.

params.name: sanity_checks
params.doc: If set to 1, gzcompress module will bind to sanity module in order to perform sanity checks over received SIP request. Default sanity checks are done. It is useful to check if received request is well formatted before proceeding to encoding/decoding.

params.name: ldap_session
params.doc: Name of the LDAP session to be used for H.350 queries, as defined in the LDAP module configuration file.

params.name: base_dn
params.doc: Base LDAP DN to start LDAP search for H.350 entries. For best performance, this should be set to the direct ancestor of the H.350 objects.

params.name: search_scope
params.doc: LDAP search scope for H.350 queries, one of "one", "base", or "sub".

functions.name: h350_sipuri_lookup
functions.doc: This function performs an LDAP search query for an H.350 commObject with a SIPIdentitySIPURI of sip_uri. The sip_uri parameter first gets escaped according the rules for LDAP filter strings. The result of the LDAP search is stored internally and can be accessed either by one of the h350_result* or one of the ldap_result* functions from the Kamailio LDAP module.

functions.name: h350_auth_lookup
functions.doc: This function performs an LDAP search query for SIP digest authentication credentials in an H.350 directory. The H.350 directory is searched for a commObject with SIPIdentityUserName of auth_username. If such a commObject is found, the SIP digest authentication username and password are stored in AVPs username_avp_spec and pwd_avp_spec, respectively. pv_*_authorize functions from AUTH module can then be used to perform SIP digest authentication.

functions.name: h350_result_call_preferences
functions.doc: This function parses the callPreferenceURI attribute of an H.350 commObject, which must have been fetched through h350_*_lookup or ldap_search. callPreferenceURI is a multi-valued attribute that stores call preference rules like e.g. forward-on-busy or forward-unconditionally. Directory services architecture for call forwarding and preferences [H.350.6] defines a format for simple call forwarding rules:

functions.name: h350_result_service_level
functions.doc: Directory services architecture for SIP [H.350.4] defines a multi-valued LDAP attribute named SIPIdentityServiceLevel, which can be used to store SIP account service level values in an LDAP directory. This function parses the SIPIdentityServiceLevel attribute and stores all service level values as AVPs for later retrieval in the Kamailio routing script. The function accesses the H.350 commObject fetched by a call to h350_*_lookup or ldap_search.

params.name: htable
params.doc: The definition of a hash table. The value of the parameter may have the following format: * "htname=>size=_number_;autoexpire=_number_;dbtable=_string_"

params.name: db_url
params.doc: The URL to connect to database for loading values in hash table at start up.

params.name: key_name_column
params.doc: The name of the column containing the hash table key name.

params.name: key_type_column
params.doc: The name of the column containing the hash table key type.

params.name: value_type_column
params.doc: The name of the column containing the hash table value type.

params.name: key_value_column
params.doc: The name of the column containing hash table key value.

params.name: expires_column
params.doc: The name of the column containing the expires value.

params.name: array_size_suffix
params.doc: The suffix to be added to store the number of items in an array (see key type).

params.name: fetch_rows
params.doc: How many rows to fetch at once from database.

params.name: timer_interval
params.doc: Interval in seconds to check for expired htable values.

params.name: db_expires
params.doc: If set to 1, the module loads/saves the value for expire of the items in hash table from/to database. It applies only to hash tables that have the auto-expires attribute defined. If set to 0, only the key name and the value are loaded, the expires for each item being set to 0.

params.name: enable_dmq
params.doc: If set to 1, will enable DMQ replication of actions performed upon entries in all tables having "dmqreplicate" parameter set. Any update action performed via pseudo-variables and RPC commands will be repeated on all other nodes. Therefore, it is important to ensure the table definition (size, autoexpire etc.) is identical across all instances.

params.name: dmq_init_sync
params.doc: If set to 1, will request synchronization from other nodes at startup. It applies to all tables having the "dmqreplicate" parameter set. As above, it is important to ensure the definition (size, autoexpire etc.) of replicated tables is identical across all instances.

params.name: timer_procs
params.doc: If set to 1 or greater, the module will create its own timer processes to scan for expired items in hash tables. If set to zero, it will use the core timer for this task. Set it to 1 if you store a lot of items with autoexpire property.

params.name: event_callback
params.doc: The name of the function in the kemi configuration file (embedded scripting language such as Lua, Python, ...) to be executed instead of event_route[...] blocks.

params.name: event_callback_mode
params.doc: Control when event_route[htable:init] is executed: 0 - after all modules were initialized; 1 - in first worker process.

functions.name: sht_print
functions.doc: Dump content of hash table to L_ERR log level. Intended for debug purposes.

functions.name: sht_rm
functions.doc: Delete the item with the name 'itname' from hash table 'htname'. This API function is equivalent to '$sht(htname=>itname) = $null'.

functions.name: sht_rm_name_re
functions.doc: Delete all entries in the htable that match the name against regular expression.

functions.name: sht_rm_value_re
functions.doc: Delete all entries in the htable that match the value against regular expression.

functions.name: sht_rm_name
functions.doc: Delete all entries in the htable that match the name against the val parameter.

functions.name: sht_rm_value
functions.doc: Delete all entries in the htable that match the value against the val parameter.

functions.name: sht_setxs
functions.doc: Set the item with the name 'itname' from hash table 'htname' to string value 'itval' and expire property to 'exval'.

functions.name: sht_setxi
functions.doc: Set the item with the name 'itname' from hash table 'htname' to integer value 'itval' and expire property to 'exval'.

functions.name: sht_reset
functions.doc: Delete all entries in the htable. The name of the hash table can be a dynamic string with variables.

functions.name: sht_lock
functions.doc: Lock the slot in htable corresponding to the key item. Note that the locking is re-entrant for the process, therefore the lock and unlock should be done by the same process.

functions.name: sht_unlock
functions.doc: Unlock the slot in htable corresponding to the key item. Note that the locking is re-entrant for the process, therefore the lock and unlock should be done by the same process.

functions.name: sht_iterator_start
functions.doc: Start an iterator for hash table named by the value of parameter hname. The parameter iname is used to identify the iterator. There can be up to 4 iterators at the same time, with different name.

functions.name: sht_iterator_end
functions.doc: Close the iterator identified by iname parameter and release the hash table slot acquired by the iterator. The iname value must be the same used for sht_iterator_start().

functions.name: sht_iterator_next
functions.doc: Move the iterator to the next item in hash table. It must be called also after sht_iterator_start() to get the first item in the hash table. Items are returned as they are found in the hash table slot, starting with the first slot.

functions.name: sht_iterator_rm
functions.doc: Remove the current item in the iterator and move the iterator to the next one.

functions.name: sht_iterator_sets
functions.doc: Set the value of the current item to the string in the sval.

functions.name: sht_iterator_seti
functions.doc: Set the value of the current item to the integer in the ival.

functions.name: sht_iterator_setex
functions.doc: Set the expire of the current item to the integer in the exval.

functions.name: sht_match_name
functions.doc: Return greater than 0 (true) if the htable has an item that matches the name against the mval parameter.

functions.name: sht_has_name
functions.doc: Alias for sht_match_name().

functions.name: sht_match_str_value
functions.doc: Return greater than 0 (true) if the htable has an item that matches the string value against the mval parameter.

functions.name: sht_has_str_value
functions.doc: Alias for sht_match_str_value().

functions.name: sht_is_null
functions.doc: Check if the item with the name 'itname' from hash table 'htname' exists. This API function is equivalent to '($sht(htname=>itname) == $null)'.

functions.name: sht_inc
functions.doc: Atomically increment the value of 'itname' in hash table 'htname'. This API function is similar to '$shtinc(htname=>itname)', without returning the value.

functions.name: sht_dec
functions.doc: Atomically decrement the value of 'itname' in hash table 'htname'. This API function is similar to '$sht_dec(htname=>itname)', without returning the value.

params.name: workers
params.doc: Number of worker processes to be started to send HTTP requests and asynchronously handle responses.

params.name: connection_timeout
params.doc: Defines in milliseconds how long Kamailio waits for a response from HTTP server.

params.name: hash_size
params.doc: The size of the hash table internally used to keep the requests. A larger table is much faster but consumes more memory. The hash size must be a power of two, otherwise it will be rounded down to the nearest power of two.

params.name: tls_version
params.doc: For HTTPS connections, what's the preferred SSL version. http://curl.haxx.se/libcurl/c/CURLOPT_SSLVERSION.html

params.name: tls_verify_host
params.doc: For HTTPS connections, whether the client should verify the server host. http://curl.haxx.se/libcurl/c/CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST.html

params.name: tls_verify_peer
params.doc: For HTTPS connections, whether the client should verify the server identity. http://curl.haxx.se/libcurl/c/CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER.html

params.name: curl_verbose
params.doc: If defined to a non-zero value, extra information from cURL (request and response headers) will be included in the kamailio logs, with LM_INFO priority.

params.name: curl_follow_redirect
params.doc: If defined to a non-zero value, will tell curl to follow HTTP 3xx redirects.

params.name: memory_manager
params.doc: Choose the memory manager used by curl: * shm: curl will use kamailio's SHM pool and memory manager * sys: curl will use the system memory and memory manager (malloc, free, ...)

params.name: tls_client_cert
params.doc: For HTTPS connections, the file path of the TLS client certificate to be used. http://curl.haxx.se/libcurl/c/CURLOPT_SSLCERT.html

params.name: tls_client_key
params.doc: For HTTPS connections, the file path of the TLS client certificate key. http://curl.haxx.se/libcurl/c/CURLOPT_SSLKEY.html

params.name: tls_ca_path
params.doc: The path of the directory holding the CA certificates. http://curl.haxx.se/libcurl/c/CURLOPT_CAPATH.html

params.name: tcp_keepalive
params.doc: If defined to a non-zero value, TCP keepalive will be enabled on cURL connections.

params.name: tcp_ka_idle
params.doc: TCP keep-alive idle time wait value (in seconds).

params.name: tcp_ka_interval
params.doc: TCP keep-alive interval (in seconds).

functions.name: http_async_query
functions.doc: Sends HTTP(S) request asynchronously to the URL given in “url” parameter, which is a string that may contain pseudo variables.

params.name: httpredirect
params.doc: If set to 1, enabled, http_client will follow HTTP 302 Redirects. If set to 0, http_client will not follow redirects. Default is 1, enabled.

params.name: httpproxy
params.doc: URL for a HTTP proxy to use as a default proxy for all connections.

params.name: httpproxyport
params.doc: Port number for a HTTP proxy to use as a default proxy port for all connections.

params.name: useragent
params.doc: Useragent to use in the HTTP protocol for requests. Defaults to the Kamailio SIP useragent string - including software version and platform.

params.name: maxdatasize
params.doc: Defines the maximum size in bytes for a response. Note that this is allocated from pkg memory (process memory) dynamically.

params.name: connection_timeout
params.doc: Defines how long Kamailio waits for response from servers. Value is expressed in seconds or milliseconds, depending on parameter timeout_mode.

params.name: timeout_mode
params.doc: Defines if timeouts are enabled, and in which unit timeout values are expressed.

params.name: client_cert
params.doc: File name for a TLS client certificate. The certificate needs to be encoded in PEM format.

params.name: client_key
params.doc: File name for a TLS client key. The key needs to be encoded in PEM format.

params.name: cacert
params.doc: File name for the trusted TLS CA cert used to verify servers. The certificates need to be encoded in PEM format.

params.name: cipher_suites
params.doc: List of allowed cipher suites. See http://curl.haxx.se/libcurl/c/CURLOPT_SSL_CIPHER_LIST.html for details of the cipher list curl option.

params.name: verify_peer
params.doc: If set to 0, TLS verification of the server certificate is disabled. This means that the connection will get encrypted, but there's no authentication. There's no proof that the transmission of data is to the host that is meant to receive data.

params.name: verify_host
params.doc: If set to 0, domain verification of the server certificate is disabled. This means that the connection will get encrypted but there is no check that data will be sent to the host that is meant to receive it. Disable with caution.

params.name: tlsversion
params.doc: Sets the preferred TLS/SSL version.

params.name: authmethod
params.doc: Sets the preferred authentication mode for HTTP/HTTPS requests. The value is a bitmap and multiple methods can be used. Note that in this case, the CURL library will make an extra request to discover server-supported authentication methods. You may want to use a specific value.

params.name: keep_connections
params.doc: If an HTTP server is accessed multiple times keeping the connection open for reuse saves a significant amount of time, especially if TLS is used. If this function is enabled, the Curl library will try to reuse existing open connections. The HTTP server will have to support this feature and keep connections open for it to work properly.

params.name: query_result
params.doc: Control what is returned by the http_client_query(...) in the result variable.

params.name: query_maxdatasize
params.doc: Control the size in bytes of the data to be returned by the http_client_query(...) in the result variable.

params.name: httpcon
params.doc: Defines a connection and credentials for the connection for use in a connection-oriented function call in this module.

params.name: config_file
params.doc: The file name of a configuration file containing definitions of http connections. This is an alternative to the "httpcon" module parameter - especially when the number of options per line gets too big.

params.name: netinterface
params.doc: Set local network interface to be used for HTTP queries. It can be interface name or IP address. For more details see: https://curl.haxx.se/libcurl/c/CURLOPT_INTERFACE.html .

params.name: response_headers
params.doc: Set to 1 in order to store HTTP response headers. A header value can be retrieved with $httprhdr(name).

functions.name: http_connect
functions.doc: Sends HTTP GET or POST request to a given connection. For a POST request, content-type can be specified. * connection - the name of an existing HTTP connection, defined by a httpcon modparam. url - the part of the URL to add to the predefined URL in the connection definition. content_type - Used only when posting data with HTTP POST. An Internet Media type, like "application/json" or "text/plain". Will be added to the HTTP request as a header. data - Data or a pseudo variable holding data to be posted. (may contain pseudo variable) result - The name of a pseudo variable that will have the data of the response from the HTTP server.

functions.name: http_connect_raw
functions.doc: Sends HTTP POST request to a given connection. Similar to http_connect. The only difference is that the data parameter will not be parsed for pseudo variables, therefore it can safely be used for content that may contain "$" character like JSON. * connection - the name of an existing HTTP connection, defined by a httpcon modparam. url - the part of the URL to add to the predefined URL in the connection definition. content_type - Used only when posting data with HTTP POST. An Internet Media type, like "application/json" or "text/plain". Will be added to the HTTP request as a header. data - Data or a pseudo variable holding data to be posted. (will not be parsed for pseudo variable) result - The name of a pseudo variable that will have the data of the response from the HTTP server.

functions.name: http_get_redirect
functions.doc: When a http connection gets a redirect and the connection is configured to follow redirects (301,302) then the target URL, the result of the redirects can be retrieved with this function after a successful connection. * connection - the name of an existing HTTP connection, defined by a httpcon modparam. result - The name of a pseudo variable that will contain the last used URL.

functions.name: http_client_query
functions.doc: Sends HTTP GET or POST request according to URL given in “url” parameter, which is a string that may contain pseudo variables.

functions.name: http_client_get
functions.doc: Perform a HTTP GET request to "url", storing the response body in the "respv" variable. The "body" and "hdrs" can be empty strings to skip setting them. The first three parameters can contain variables that are evaluated at runtime. The "respv" has to be the name of a writable variable.

functions.name: http_client_request
functions.doc: Perform a HTTP request to "url", storing the response body in the "respv" variable. The method of the request is set by "met". The "body" and "hdrs" can be empty strings to skip setting them. The first four parameters can contain variables that are evaluated at runtime. The "respv" has to be the name of a writable variable.

functions.name: http_client_request_v2pk
functions.doc: Similar to http_client_request(), but using HTTP/2 prior-knowledge that the server does not need HTTP/1.1-Upgrade (direct HTTP/2 by seting libcurl option CURL_HTTP_VERSION_2_PRIOR_KNOWLEDGE).

functions.name: http_client_response_headers_set
functions.doc: Set if the HTTP response header should be stored (when mode is 1) or not (when mode is 0). If mode is 0, then it also clears previously stored response headers.

functions.name: http_client_response_headers_clear
functions.doc: Clear stored response headers, if not explicitely done, it happens when the next HTTP request is performed.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: The database url.

params.name: db_mode
params.doc: The module supports 2 modes of operation, high speed memory based storage (mode 0), and database only (mode 2) where all data is stored in a database, allowing scalability at the expense of speed. Mode 1 is reserved.

params.name: rooms_table
params.doc: The name of the table storing IMC rooms.

params.name: members_table
params.doc: The name of the table storing IMC members.

params.name: hash_size
params.doc: The power of 2 to get the size of the hash table used for storing members and rooms.

params.name: imc_cmd_start_char
params.doc: The character which indicates that the body of the message is a command.

params.name: outbound_proxy
params.doc: The SIP address used as next hop when sending the message. Very useful when using Kamailio with a domain name not in DNS, or when using a separate Kamailio instance for imc processing. If not set, the message will be sent to the address in destination URI.

params.name: extra_hdrs
params.doc: Extra headers (each ending with \r\n) to be added in messages sent out from imc server.

params.name: create_on_join
params.doc: If set to 1 and user requests to join a non-existing room, the room will be automatically created. If set to 0, joining a non-existing room returns an error.

params.name: check_on_create
params.doc: If set to 1, the chat server will report an error if the user attempts to create a room that already exists.

functions.name: imc_manager
functions.doc: THis function handles incoming MESSAGE requests. If detects if the body of the message is a conference command it executes it, otherwise it sends the message to all the members in the room.

functions.name: imc_room_active
functions.doc: Return 1 (true) if the room is active, -1 (false) if the room is not found. The parameter is the SIP URI to identify the room, it can contain variables.

functions.name: imc_room_member
functions.doc: Return 1 (true) if the user is member of the room, -1 (false) if the user is not member of the room. The parameters are the SIP URIs to identify the room and the user, they can contain variables.

params.name: name
params.doc: This is the name of the SCSCF as identified in communication with the HSS (Server-Name AVP of MAR).

params.name: auth_data_hash_size
params.doc: This is the size of the hash table used to store auth vectors (AV). Default value is fine for most people. Use the parameter if you really need to change it.

params.name: auth_vector_timeout
params.doc: This is the time, in seconds, that a SENTauth vector is valid for. If there is no response ...

params.name: auth_data_timeout
params.doc: Time, in seconds, a used auth vector is valid for.

params.name: av_request_at_once
params.doc: How many auth vectors to request in MAR.

params.name: av_request_at_sync
params.doc: How many auth vectors to request at sync. Default value is 1.

params.name: registration_default_algorithm
params.doc: The default authentication algorithm to use for registration if one is not specified.

params.name: registration_qop
params.doc: The QOP options to put in the authorisation challenges.

params.name: cxdx_forced_peer
params.doc: FQDN of Diameter Peer (HSS) to use for communication (MAR). If you use this, the routing defined in your diameter xml configuration file (CDP) will be ignored and as a result you will lose the benefits of load balancing and failover.

params.name: cxdx_dest_realm
params.doc: Destination realm to be used in Diameter messages to HSS

params.name: cxdx_dest_host
params.doc: Destination Host to be used in Diameter-MAR messages to HSS

params.name: max_nonce_reuse
params.doc: Defines, how many times a nonce can be reused (provided nc is incremented)

params.name: add_authinfo_hdr
params.doc: Should an Authentication-Info header be added on 200 OK responses?

params.name: ignore_failed_auth
params.doc: Ignore invalid passwords (only IMPI/IMPU is checked).

params.name: av_check_only_impu
params.doc: When storing the authentication vectors for an account, use either IMPI/IMPU (=0, default) or IMPU (=1).

params.name: av_mode
params.doc: Control how authentication vector is generated: 0 - get it from HSS via DIAMETER; 1 - generate it locally. Default is 0.

functions.name: ims_www_authorize
functions.doc: The function verifies credentials according to RFC2617. If the credentials are verified successfully then the function will succeed and mark the credentials as authorized (marked credentials can be later used by some other functions). If the function was unable to verify the credentials for some reason then it will fail and the script should call www_challenge which will challenge the user again.

functions.name: ims_www_authenticate
functions.doc: It is the same function as www_authenticate(realm, table). This name is kept for backward compatibility, since it was named this way first time by it actually does user authentication.

functions.name: ims_www_challenge
functions.doc: Name alias: proxy_authorize(realm, table)

functions.name: ims_www_challenge
functions.doc: Same as 4.3 except here there is the additional option to specify the authorisation algorithm * algorithm - The algorithm to be used when challenging the client. Can be AKAv1-MD5, AKAv2-MD5, MD5, or HSS-Selected. If left as an empty string, the default algorithm will be chosen according to the parameter registration_default_algorithm (see section 3.7)

functions.name: ims_proxy_challenge
functions.doc: Name alias: proxy_authorize(realm, table)

functions.name: ims_proxy_authenticate
functions.doc: It is same function as proxy_authenticate(realm, table). This name is kept for backward compatibility, since it was named this way first time but it actually does user authentication.

functions.name: ims_auth_data_set
functions.doc: Set the key, op, op_c and amf to be used for AKAv1-MD5 authentication when av_mode parameter is set to 1 (authentication vector generated locally). It has to be used before the function for doing authentication.

functions.name: ims_auth_data_reset
functions.doc: Reset the authentication attributes when av_mode parameter is set to 1.

params.name: hash_size
params.doc: The size of the hash table internally used to keep the Diameter-Ro-Session. A larger table is much faster but consumes more memory. The hash size must be a power of two number.

params.name: db_mode
params.doc: Should a database be used to store dialog information.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: Default value is “mysql://kamailio:kamailiorw@localhost/kamailio”

params.name: interim_update_credits
params.doc: How much credit should be requested interim request? At the start of the call, we request the amount of seconds as per Command. For each interim request, we would request credit for "interim_update_credits".

params.name: timer_buffer
params.doc: How many seconds before expiry of our credit should we request more credit?

params.name: ro_forced_peer
params.doc: FQDN of Diameter Peer (OCS) to use for communication (CCR). If you use this, the routing defined in your diameter xml configuration file (CDP) will be ignored and as a result you will lose the benefits of load balancing and failover.

params.name: ro_auth_expiry
params.doc: This is the expiry length in seconds of the initiated Diameter sessions.

params.name: cdp_event_latency
params.doc: This is a flag to determine whether or slow CDP responses should be reported in the log file. 1 is enabled and 0 is disabled.

params.name: cdp_event_threshold
params.doc: This time in milliseconds is the limit we should report a CDP response as slow. i.e. if a CDP response exceeds this limit it will be reported in the log file. This is only relevant is cdp_event_latency is enabled (set to 0).

params.name: cdp_event_latency_log
params.doc: This time log level at which we should report slow CDP responses. 0 is ERROR, 1 is WARN, 2 is INFO and 3 is DEBUG. This is only relevant is cdp_event_latency is enabled (set to 0)

params.name: single_ro_session_per_dialog
params.doc: This tells the module whether it should do a single ro session per dialog no matter how many times Ro_send_CCR is called from the config file or initiate an ro session each time Ro_send_CCR is called. It is useful for IMS charging where you might want to charge for on-net originating and off-net originating calls but always have only a single ro session.

params.name: origin_host
params.doc: Origin host to be used in Diameter messages to charging-server.

params.name: origin_realm
params.doc: Origin Realm to be used in Diameter messages to charging-server.

params.name: destination_host
params.doc: Destination host to be used in Diameter messages to charging-server.

params.name: destination_realm
params.doc: Destination realm to be used in Diameter messages to charging-server.

params.name: service_context_id_root
params.doc: This defines a root-element of the Service-Context-Id AVP used in the diameter-message

params.name: service_context_id_ext
params.doc: This defines the extension of the Service-Context-Id AVP used in the diameter-message.

params.name: service_context_id_mnc
params.doc: This defines Mobile-Network-Code (MNC) of the Service-Context-Id AVP used in the diameter-message.

params.name: voice_service_identifier
params.doc: This defines the service identifier to be used for charging voice.

params.name: voice_rating_group
params.doc: This defines the rating group to be used for charging voice.

params.name: video_service_identifier
params.doc: This defines the service identifier to be used for charging video.

params.name: video_rating_group
params.doc: This defines the rating group to be used for charging video.

params.name: service_context_id_mcc
params.doc: This defines Mobile-Country-Code (MCC) of the Service-Context-Id AVP used in the diameter-message.

params.name: service_context_id_release
params.doc: This defines Release of the Service-Context-Id AVP used in the diameter-message.

params.name: custom_user_avp
params.doc: When this parameter is set and the contents of the AVP is not empty, the User-AVP in the Ro-Charging-Request will be based on the this parameter rather than on the P-Asserted or From-Header.

params.name: app_provided_party_avp
params.doc: When this parameter is set and the contents of the AVP is not empty, an Application-Provided-Called Party-Address AVP will be addedd to charging related requests. This is required for special cases e.g. related to roaming for some diameter server.

params.name: vendor_specific_chargeinfo
params.doc: This parameter can be used to activate or deactivate the addition of Vendor-Specific-Termination-Clause and Vendor-Specific-Termination-Reason AVPs to the requests. To activate set this parameter to 1.

params.name: vendor_specific_id
params.doc: To set the ID of the Vendor-Specific information, not implemented right now.

params.name: strip_plus_from_e164
params.doc: Strip + from subscription id when E.164 format is used. This is according to spec, but this parameter is to keep existing behavior as the default.

params.name: use_pani_from_term_invite
params.doc: P-Access-Network-Info is normally relevant for the "orig" scenario where it's extracted from INVITE. This setting instruct Kamailio to include it in "term" scenario too, where it might have been added to the INVITE based on info from a REGISTER. Normally used to start a charging session when the user is roaming.

params.name: node_func
params.doc: Defines what should be sent as Node-Functionality (862) in the Diameter Ro request. Possible values are: 0 (S-CSCF), 1 (P-CSCF), 2 (I-CSCF), 3 (MRFC), 4 (MGCF), 5 (BFCF) or 6 (AS)

functions.name: Ro_set_session_id_avp
functions.doc: Sets the Ro session ID to an AVP for use in the config file

params.name: enable_stats
params.doc: This function is currently not supported by the ims_dialog module. To be incorporated in the future.

params.name: hash_size
params.doc: The size of the hash table internally used to keep the dialogs. A larger table is much faster but consumes more memory. The hash size must be a power of two number.

params.name: rr_param
params.doc: Name of the Record-Route parameter to be added with the dialog cookie. It is used for the fast dialog matching of sequential requests.

params.name: dlg_flag
params.doc: Flag to be used for marking if a dialog should be constructed for the current request (this makes sense only for initial requests).

params.name: timeout_avp
params.doc: The specification of an AVP that contain a custom timeout (in seconds) for the dialog. It may be used only in a request (initial or sequential) context

params.name: default_timeout
params.doc: The default dialog timeout (in seconds) if no custom one is set.

params.name: dlg_extra_hdrs
params.doc: A string containing the extra headers (full format, with EOH) to be added in the requests generated by the module (like BYEs).

params.name: dlg_match_mode
params.doc: Deprecated - in the new dialog module we always match using DID ONLY

params.name: detect_spirals
params.doc: Whether spirals (i.e., messages routed through the proxy multiple times) should be detected or not.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: In order to store information about dialogs in a database, a database URL must be specified.

params.name: db_mode
params.doc: This is the database mode to be used for dialog persistent storage. * 0 - NO_DB - the memory content is not flushed into DB; * 1 - REALTIME - any dialog information changes will be reflected into the database immediately. * 2 - DELAYED - the dialog information changes will be flushed into DB periodically, based on a timer routine. * 3 - SHUTDOWN - the dialog information will be flushed into DB only at shutdown - no runtime updates.

params.name: db_update_period
params.doc: The interval (seconds) at which to update dialogs' information, if the server is configured to store the dialog information at a given interval. A too short interval will generate intensive database operations, while an excessively long one will miss dialogs with a short lifetime.

params.name: db_fetch_rows
params.doc: The number of the rows to be fetched at once from database when loading the dialog records at startup from the database. This value can be used to tune the load time at startup. For 1MB of private memory (default), it should be below 400. The database driver must support the fetch_result() capability. A value of 0 means the database fetch is not limited.

params.name: profiles_with_value
params.doc: List of names for profiles with values.

params.name: profiles_no_value
params.doc: List of names for profiles without values.

params.name: bridge_controller
params.doc: SIP address to be used in From header when initiating a call bridge.

params.name: initial_cbs_inscript
params.doc: This has been deprecated since dlg_manage has been removed.

functions.name: set_dlg_profile
functions.doc: Inserts the current dialog into a profile. Note that if the profile does not supports values, this will be silently discarded. Also, there is no check for inserting the same dialog in the same profile for multiple times.

functions.name: unset_dlg_profile
functions.doc: Removes the current dialog from a profile.

functions.name: is_in_profile
functions.doc: Checks if the current dialog belongs to a profile. If the profile supports values, the check can be reinforced to take into account a specific value - if the dialog was inserted into the profile for a specific value. If no value is passed, only the simply belonging of the dialog to the profile is checked. Note that if the profile does not supports values, this will be silently discarded.

functions.name: get_profile_size
functions.doc: Returns the number of dialogs belonging to a profile. If the profile supports values, the check can be reinforced to take into account a specific value - how many dialogs were inserted into the profile with a specific value. If no value is passed, only simply belonging of the dialog to the profile is checked. Note that if the profile does not supports values, this will be silently discarded.

functions.name: dlg_isflagset
functions.doc: Check if the dialog flag is set or not.

functions.name: dlg_setflag
functions.doc: Set the dialog flag.

functions.name: dlg_resetflag
functions.doc: Reset the dialog flag.

functions.name: dlg_terminate
functions.doc: Terminates a dialog. In ims_dialog module this function now includes support for early as well as confirmed dialogs.

functions.name: dlg_refer
functions.doc: This function is currently not supported by the ims_dialog module. To be incorporated in the future.

functions.name: dlg_manage
functions.doc: This has been deprecated in ims_dialog. Instead set dialog flag for initial INVITE and Route-parameter-callback execution for within-dialog requests.

functions.name: dlg_bridge
functions.doc: This function is currently not supported by the ims_dialog module. To be incorporated in the future.

functions.name: dlg_get
functions.doc: Search and set current dialog based on Call-ID, From-Tag and To-Tag parameters.

functions.name: is_known_dlg
functions.doc: This function is currently not supported by the ims_dialog module. To be incorporated in the future.

functions.name: diameter_request
functions.doc: This method will send a Diameter Request.

functions.name: diameter_request_async
functions.doc: This method will send a Diameter Request asynchronously. The Reply to this request will be visible in the event-route "diameter:response".

params.name: route_lir_user_unknown
params.doc: This is the route which is executed if HSS returns "user unknown" in LIR

params.name: route_uar_user_unknown
params.doc: This is the route which is executed if HSS returns "user unknown" in UAR.

params.name: scscf_entry_expiry
params.doc: This is the time in s after which S-CSCF entries in the I-CSCF's SCSCF list will expire.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: URL of the database to be used.

params.name: db_nds_table
params.doc: NDS (Network Domain Security) table name in database to be used.

params.name: db_scscf_table
params.doc: S-CSCF table name in database to be used.

params.name: db_capabilities_table
params.doc: S-CSCF capabilities table name in database to be used.

params.name: cxdx_forced_peer
params.doc: FQDN of Diameter Peer (HSS) to use for communication (UAR, LIR). If you use this, the routing defined in your diameter xml configuration file (CDP) will be ignored and as a result you will lose the benefits of load balancing and failover.

params.name: cxdx_dest_realm
params.doc: Destination realm to be used in Diameter messages to HSS

params.name: use_preferred_scscf_uri
params.doc: Whether or not this ICSCF has a preferred S-CSCF to use when the HSS returns a list of SCSCFs. 0 means this I-CSCF has no preferred SCSCF. 1 means it has a preferred S-CSCF.

params.name: preferred_scscf_uri
params.doc: If use_preferred_scscf_uri is set then this is the URI of the preferred SCSCF.

functions.name: I_scscf_select
functions.doc: This function is used to retrieve the next unused SCSCF from the list for this request (based on callid).

functions.name: I_scscf_drop
functions.doc: Drop the list of SCSCFs for this request (based on callid).

functions.name: I_perform_user_authorization_request
functions.doc: Perform a UAR on Diameter CXDX interface. This function will build a list of SCSCFs to be used and populate the SCSCF list for the request. On a successful return of this message you can get the next available SCSCF by using the I_scscf_select function in 4.1. * Route block to resume after async UAR Diameter reply. * capabilities - whether to request capabilities or not "1" - with capabilities, "0" - no capabilities.

functions.name: I_perform_location_information_request
functions.doc: Perform a LIR on Diameter CXDX interface. * Route block to resume after async LIR Diameter reply.

params.name: ipsec_listen_addr
params.doc: IP address which the Proxy-CSCF will use for incoming/outgoing SIP traffic over IPSec.

params.name: ipsec_listen_addr6
params.doc: IPv6 address which the Proxy-CSCF will use for incoming/outgoing SIP traffic over IPSec.

params.name: ipsec_client_port
params.doc: Port number which will be bound for incoming (server) IPSec traffic.

params.name: ipsec_server_port
params.doc: Port number which will be bound for incoming (server) IPSec traffic.

params.name: ipsec_listen_name
params.doc: Set a common prefix to build listen socket names. Default value: not set.

params.name: ipsec_listen_agname
params.doc: Set async (action) workers group name for udp sockets for multi-threaded reading. Default value: not set.

params.name: ipsec_max_connections
params.doc: Maximum simultaneous IPSec connections

params.name: ipsec_reuse_server_port
params.doc: Reuse (1) or not (0) the P-CSCF IPSec information for Re-registration for one UA. When set to 0 - During Re-registration P-CSCF will create new IPSec tunnels. When set to 1 - During Re-registration P-CSCF will reuse the old IPSec tunnels.

params.name: ipsec_spi_id_start
params.doc: Each IPSec tunnel has a unique system-wide identifier. This and the following option allows to tune the SPIs used by Kamailio in order to avoid collisions with other IPSec useres. If Kamailio is the only process on the system which uses IPSec, don't bother with this option.

params.name: ipsec_spi_id_range
params.doc: How many SPIs to be allocated for the process. E.g. if ipsec_spi_id_start = 100 and ipsec_spi_id_range = 1000, SPIs between 100 and 1100 will be used.

params.name: ipsec_preferred_alg
params.doc: A name of an authentication algorithm which the Proxy-CSCF will prefer when creating IPSec tunnels.

params.name: ipsec_preferred_ealg
params.doc: A name of an encrytion algorithm which the Proxy-CSCF will prefer when creating IPSec tunnels.

functions.name: ipsec_create
functions.doc: This function creates IPSec SA and Policy based on the parameters sent in Security-Client header in the REGISTER message. It's called when OK is received. The function also adds Security-Server header to the REGISTER.

functions.name: ipsec_forward
functions.doc: The function processes redirects outgoing message via the IPSec tunnel initiated with ipsec_create().

functions.name: ipsec_destroy
functions.doc: The function destroys IPSec tunnel, created with ipsec_create.

functions.name: ipsec_destroy_by_contact
functions.doc: The function destroys IPSec tunnel, created with ipsec_create.

params.name: my_uri
params.doc: This is the SIP URI of server on which the SCSCF is hosted.

params.name: expires_grace
params.doc: This is the expires value to add to the expires during 3rd party registration to prevent expiration in Application Server.

params.name: isc_fr_timeout
params.doc: This is the time in ms that we will wait for an AS response before we consider it dead. It has to be lower than the SIP transaction timeout to prevent downstream timeouts. But not too small as ASs tend to take a long time to respond.

params.name: isc_fr_inv_timeout
params.doc: This is the time in ms that we will wait for an AS INVITE response before we consider it dead. It has to be lower than the SIP transaction timeout to prevent downstream timeouts. But not too small as ASs tend to take a long time to respond.

params.name: add_p_served_user
params.doc: This boolean indicates if a P-Served-User should be added on the ISC interface, according to RFC 5502.

functions.name: isc_match_filter_reg
functions.doc: This function checks if a REGISTER messages matches Initial Filter Criteria - if so it inserts the necessary route headers and modifies the destination URI to forward to the relevant Application Server.

functions.name: isc_match_filter
functions.doc: This function checks if a non-REGISTER messages matches Initial Filter Criteria - if so it inserts the necessary route headers and modifies the destination URI to forward to the relevant Application Server.

functions.name: isc_from_as
functions.doc: This function checks if this message has come from an Application Server.

functions.name: ccr_result
functions.doc: This method sets the response code of the Diameter Request.

params.name: rx_dest_realm
params.doc: This is the name of the Diameter realm of the Diameter server (typically a PCRF).

params.name: rx_forced_peer
params.doc: FQDN of the Diameter server (typically a PCRF) to communicate with. If not set then realm routing is used. If you use this, the routing defined in your diameter xml configuration file (CDP) will be ignored and as a result you will lose the benefits of load balancing and failover.

params.name: rx_auth_expiry
params.doc: This is the expiry length in seconds of the initiated Diameter sessions.

params.name: cdp_event_latency
params.doc: This is a flag to determine whether or slow CDP responses should be reported in the log file. 1 is enabled and 0 is disabled.

params.name: cdp_event_threshold
params.doc: This time in milliseconds is the limit we should report a CDP response as slow. i.e. if a CDP response exceeds this limit it will be reported in the log file. This is only relevant is cdp_event_latency is enabled (set to 0).

params.name: cdp_event_latency_log
params.doc: This time log level at which we should report slow CDP responses. 0 is ERROR, 1 is WARN, 2 is INFO and 3 is DEBUG. This is only relevant is cdp_event_latency is enabled (set to 0)

params.name: authorize_video_flow
params.doc: This is a flag that specifies whether or not to authorize video flows. 1 means video flows will be authorized over Rx and 0 means video flows will not be authorized over Rx

params.name: cdp_event_list_size_threshold
params.doc: This is a threshold on the size of the cdp event list. Once the queue exceeds this length a warning is logged. 0 disables this feature

params.name: audio_default_bandwidth
params.doc: This parameters defines the default bandwidth for Audio, if no "b=AS"-Parameter is found in the SDP.

params.name: video_default_bandwidth
params.doc: This parameters defines the default bandwidth for Video, if no "b=AS"-Parameter is found in the SDP.

params.name: early_qosrelease_reason
params.doc: This sets the default Reason, when a call is terminated in early stage due to QoS-failure.

params.name: confirmed_qosrelease_headers
params.doc: These headers are added to the BYE-Message, when a confirmed call is terminated due to a QoS failure.

params.name: regex_sdp_ip_prefix_to_maintain_in_fd
params.doc: The flow-description AVP is typically populated using IP:port information present in the SDP. Certain (buggy) UEs can change ports midway during calls which causes the flow-description to no longer match the traffic. This parameter allows the flow-description AVP to use to the any keyword instead of certain IP:port combinations in the SDP. The parameter is a regex that if set adds an extra filter for all IPs that do not match the regex with the any keyword in the flow-description AVP

params.name: terminate_dialog_on_rx_failure
params.doc: If set then active dialogs associated with an Rx session are torn down in the Rx session fails

params.name: delete_contact_on_rx_failure
params.doc: If set then contacts associated with signalling Rx sessions are deleted if the Rx session fails

params.name: include_rtcp_fd
params.doc: If set then a flow description is added for media flows - next available odd port is used as the default for RTCP traffic

params.name: af_signaling_ip
params.doc: Set P-CSCF IPv4 address to generate the flows for the UE - PCSCF signaling path. Used only for AAR register, Flow-Description AVP (507)

params.name: af_signaling_ip6
params.doc: Set P-CSCF IPv6 address to generate the flows for the UE - PCSCF signaling path. Used only for AAR register, Flow-Description AVP (507)

params.name: media_type
params.doc: Describe Media Type AVP(520) for AAR register

params.name: flow_protocol
params.doc: Describe Flow protocol for Flow-Description AVP (507). Used only for AAR register

params.name: omit_flow_ports
params.doc: If set to 1 ommit ports for Flow-Description AVP (507). Used only for AAR register

params.name: rs_default_bandwidth
params.doc: Describe default RS-Bandwidth AVP(522) for AAR

params.name: rr_default_bandwidth
params.doc: Describe default RR-Bandwidth AVP(521) for AAR

params.name: suspend_transaction
params.doc: If enabled, suspends the tm transaction while doing the AAR.

params.name: recv_mode
params.doc: If set to 0, rx_aar_register() takes the received-from address values (IP, port, proto) from the IP frame. If set to 1, it takes them from Via header.

params.name: dialog_direction
params.doc: If set to 1, DLG_MOBILE_ORIGINATING is set to rx_add_media_component_description_avp() instead of DLG_MOBILE_REGISTER (which corresponds to value 3).

params.name: trust_bottom_via
params.doc: If set to 1 it will trust the bottom Via as the UE IP/port/transport when doing client identification.

functions.name: Rx_AAR_Register
functions.doc: Perform an AAR on Diameter RX interface to subscribe to signalling status. The purpose of this is tell a Diameter server (typically a PCRF) to inform the requesting Diameter client (us) on changes to the status of signalling bearer for the same framed IP address. For more details see 3GGP TS 29.214.

functions.name: Rx_STR
functions.doc: Perform an STR on Diameter RX interface to terminate an authorization session. For more details see 3GGP TS 29.214.

params.name: pcscf_uri
params.doc: URI of this Proxy-CSCF.

params.name: pending_reg_expires
params.doc: How long (in seconds), until pending (uncomplete) Registrations expire

params.name: received_avp
params.doc: AVP, holding the received information (optional)

params.name: is_registered_fallback2ip
params.doc: Defines, whether a contact should be searched by its Contact: only or alternatively by the received IP-Address.

params.name: publish_reginfo
params.doc: If set to "1", the module will send PUBLISH regarding changes of the registration (e.g. due to Rx-Information) towards the network core.

params.name: subscribe_to_reginfo
params.doc: If set to "1", the module will send a SUBSCRIBE for the registration status towards the network core.

params.name: subscription_expires
params.doc: How long should the subscription of reg-info towards the packet-core be valid?

params.name: ignore_contact_rxport_check
params.doc: Validate, if the port, from which the request was received, is the same as used during registration.

params.name: ignore_contact_rxproto_check
params.doc: Validate, if the protocol, from which the request was received, is the same as used during registration. Note: with IMS, the UE opens IPsec Security Associations between IPs and ports with the P-CSCF. These are for both UDP and TCP, with a single negotiation, which does not need to specify the protocol.

params.name: ignore_reg_state
params.doc: Validate, if the found contact is really and completely registered.

params.name: force_icscf_uri
params.doc: Instead of doing a DNS-Lookup on the domain, always send the requests to a specific I-CSCF.

params.name: reginfo_queue_size_threshold
params.doc: As reginfo operations are processed asynchronously, this parameter defines at what length of the queue, the length should be logged (in order to determine overload)

params.name: delete_delay
params.doc: If set greater than 0, the delete of a pcontact record is delayed with its value instead of being done immediately.

params.name: trust_bottom_via
params.doc: If set to 1 it will trust the bottom Via as the UE IP/port/transport when doing client identification.

functions.name: pcscf_save
functions.doc: The function processes a reply to a REGISTER message. It can add, remove or modify location records (in usrloc) depending on Contact and Expires HFs in the REGISTER message.

functions.name: pcscf_save_pending
functions.doc: Same as pcscf_save(), but it will store the registration in a "Pending" state.

functions.name: pcscf_follows_service_routes
functions.doc: Returns true, if the request is following the "learned" service-routes during registration.

functions.name: pcscf_force_service_routes
functions.doc: Remove existing route-headers and force the Service-Routes, that were learned during registration.

functions.name: pcscf_is_registered
functions.doc: Returns true, if the request is coming from a "registered" endpoint.

params.name: default_expires
params.doc: If the processed message contains neither Expires HFs nor expires contact parameters, this value will be used for newly created S-CSCF usrloc records. The parameter contains number of second to expire (for example use 3600 for one hour). If it is set to a lower value than the min_expires parameter then it will be ignored. This parameter can be modified via ser config framework. A random value in a specific interval can be selected by using the default_expires_range parameter

params.name: default_expires_range
params.doc: This parameter specifies that the expiry used for newly created S-CSCF usrloc records are not fixed(when default_expires applies), but a random value in the intervalrdq [default_expires-default_expires_range%, default_expires+default_expires_range%]. The value is between 0 and 100 and represent the maximum percentage from default_expires that will be subtracted or added when computing the value. Default in 0, meaning default_expires is left unmodified. This parameter can be modified via ser config framework.

params.name: min_expires
params.doc: The minimum expires value of a Contact, values lower than this minimum will be automatically set to the minimum. Value 0 disables the checking. This parameter can be modified via ser config framework.

params.name: max_expires
params.doc: The maximum expires value of a Contact, values higher than this maximum will be automatically set to the maximum. Value 0 disables the checking. This parameter can be modified via ser config framework.

params.name: subscription_default_expires
params.doc: If the processed message contains neither Expires HFs nor expires contact parameters, this value will be used for newly created subscriptions. The parameter contains number of second to expire (for example use 3600 for one hour). If it is set to a lower value than the subscription_min_expires parameter then it will be ignored. A random value in a specific interval can be selected by using the subscription_expires_range parameter

params.name: subscription_expires_range
params.doc: This parameter specifies that the expiry used for newly created subscriptions are not fixed(when subscription_default_expires applies), but a random value in the interval [subscription_default_expires-subscription_expires_range%, subscription_default_expires+subscription_expires_range%]. The value is between 0 and 100 and represent the maximum percentage from subscription_default_expires that will be subtracted or added when computing the value. Default in 0, meaning subscription_default_expires is left unmodified.

params.name: subscription_min_expires
params.doc: The minimum expires value of a subscription, values lower than this minimum will be automatically set to the minimum. Value 0 disables the checking.

params.name: subscription_max_expires
params.doc: The maximum expires value of a subscription, values higher than this maximum will be automatically set to the maximum. Value 0 disables the checking.

params.name: ue_unsubscribe_on_dereg
params.doc: Many UEs do not unsubscribe on de-register, therefor if the parameter is set to 0, the default, any subscription of that subscriber will be removed and NOTIFY will be not sent. To disable this behaviour set this parameter to 1.

params.name: user_data_dtd
params.doc: DTD to check the user data received in SAA (Server Assignment Answer).

params.name: user_data_xsd
params.doc: XSD to check the user data received in SAA (Server Assignment Answer).

params.name: support_wildcardPSI
params.doc: indicate support for wildcard PSI is subscription profile (SAA)

params.name: scscf_name
params.doc: The name of the S-CSCF

params.name: store_profile_dereg
params.doc: Should the subscription profile be stored on de-registration

params.name: cxdx_dest_realm
params.doc: Destination realm to be used in Diameter messages

params.name: cxdx_forced_peer
params.doc: FQDN of Diameter Peer (HSS) to use for communication (SAR). If you use this, the routing defined in your diameter xml configuration file (CDP) will be ignored and as a result you will lose the benefits of load balancing and failover.

params.name: append_branches
params.doc: The parameter controls how lookup function processes multiple contacts. If there are multiple contacts for the given username in usrloc and this parameter is set to 1, Request-URI will be overwritten with the highest-q rated contact and the rest will be appended to sip_msg structure and can be later used by tm for forking. If the parameter is set to 0, only Request-URI will be overwritten with the highest-q rated contact and the rest will be left unprocessed. This parameter can be modified via Kamailio config framework.

params.name: method_filtering
params.doc: Tells if the contact filtering based on supported methods should be performed during lookup. It's enabled only if it has a non zero value.

params.name: user_data_always
params.doc: If specified this will make the S-CSCF always request user data from HSS.

params.name: error_reply_code
params.doc: In certain error conditions, the S-CSCF may not be able to process the request (e.g. in case of database failures). Per default and according to the Specs, the S-CSCF would return a 500 error in this case. However, according to the SIP-Specs for DNS-SRV, this won't trigger a failover, which may be desired.

params.name: skip_multiple_bindings_on_reg_resp
params.doc: If set to 1 - on Re-Registration registrar sends in 200 OK reply only current contact in case of multiple bindings. If set to 0 - on Re-Registration registrar sends in 200 OK reply all contacts in case of multiple bindings according to RFC3261.

functions.name: save
functions.doc: The function processes a REGISTER message. It can add, remove or modify usrloc records depending on Contact and Expires HFs in the REGISTER message. On success and when called from the REQUEST_ROUTE, 200 OK will be returned listing all contacts that are currently in usrloc. On an error, error message will be sent with a short description in reason phrase. In case of internal errors the function will return FALSE, otherwise a force to exit the cfg is file is actioned by returning 0 (asynchronous processing)

functions.name: lookup
functions.doc: This function extract the IMPU from the Request-URI and tries to find all registered contacts in usrloc. If there are no such contacts, -1 is returned. If there are, Request-URI will be rewritten with the contact that has the highest q value. The rest of the contacts will be appended to the sip msg structure (if append_branches is set) and can be later used by TM module for forking for example...

functions.name: lookup_path_to_contact
functions.doc: This function take a URI and tries to find the contact in usrloc. If the contact is found and has a path set, then a path header is added to the SIP message so it can be loose routed.

functions.name: unregister
functions.doc: This function will remove all bindings for the IMPU found in the Request-URI.

functions.name: assign_server_unreg
functions.doc: TBD

functions.name: impu_registered
functions.doc: This function checks if the IMPU in the To header is registered in usrloc.

functions.name: term_impu_registered
functions.doc: This function checks if the IMPU in the Request-URI is registered in usrloc.

functions.name: reg_fetch_contacts
functions.doc: The function fetches the contacts for 'uri' from table 'domain' to pseudo-variable $ulc(profile) [ulc = ims scscf ulc].

functions.name: reg_free_contacts
functions.doc: The function frees the contacts from pseudo-variable $ulc(profile). Should be called to release the content of a profile. Anyhow, fetching a new contact addresses set over a profile will release any existing data in that profile.

functions.name: can_subscribe_to_reg
functions.doc: This function checks to see that a SUBSCRIBE request is authorised to subscribe to the particular identity. Only 3 entities can subscribe: * The user agent to its own state * The P-CSCF specified in the path header for that user * Application Server (AS) not yet implemented

functions.name: subscribe_to_reg
functions.doc: Save the subscription to the REG event for the UAC or the appropriate P-CSCF (in the path to the UAC).

functions.name: can_publish_reg
