functions.doc: This function checks to see that a PUBLISH request is authorised to publish for a particular identity. Only 3 entities can publish: * The user agent to its own state * The P-CSCF specified in the path header for that user * Application Server (AS) not yet implemented

functions.name: publish_reg
functions.doc: Save the publish to the REG event for the UAC or the appropriate P-CSCF (in the path to the UAC).

params.name: hash_size
params.doc: The number of entries of the hash table used by to store the contact records is 2^hash_size. For hash_size=4, the number of entries of the hash table is 16.

params.name: timer_interval
params.doc: Number of seconds between two timer runs. The module uses timer to delete expired contacts.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: Database URL.

params.name: db_mode
params.doc: This is the database mode to be used for the PCSCF usrloc data persistent storage. Currently this module supports the Write-Through scheme only. * 0 - This disables DB mode. Only memory will be used for usrloc and data will not survive a restart. * 1 - Write-Through Scheme. All changes to usrloc are immediately reflected in the database. This is slow but very reliable. This mode will ensure that no registration data is lost as a result of a restart or crash. * 3 - DB_ONLY Scheme. All changes to usrloc are immediately reflected in the database and additionally PCSCF usrloc data are downloaded from db and inserted into PCSCF usrloc cache if required - i.e. If contact data cannot be found in cache a db query for the contact is done in table location and when contact is found there its respective data are inserted in PCSCF usrloc cache. Also an audit had been added for removal of long expired PCSCF usrloc data in table location. This mode will ensure that no registration data is lost as a result of a restart or crash.

params.name: match_contact_host_port
params.doc: If set to 1 (default), the contact is matched using only host and port in the contact URI. * 0 - When matching contact do full contact match procedure. * 1 - When matching contact compare only host and port of the contact URI.

params.name: expires_grace
params.doc: Specify a grace time for keeping the contacts until they are finally deleted. The value of the parameter is defined in seconds.

params.name: audit_expired_pcontacts_interval
params.doc: Number of seconds between two audit runs. Note: audit is used for db_mode DB_ONLY (3) only. The module uses this audit to delete expired contacts found in db table location which are expired at least as the audit_expired_pcontacts_timeout value. Such expired contacts in location may appear when these contacts are not present in usrloc cache because PCSCF crashed before contact expiry.

params.name: audit_expired_pcontacts_timeout
params.doc: Number of seconds the contacts must be already expired before the audit starts working on them. It is recommended to set only values greater than the Default value 40. The module uses this audit to delete expired contacts found in db table location which are expired at least as many seconds as the sum of this timeout parameter value plus the value of the expires_grace parameter.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: database URL for storing impu/contacts records

params.name: db_mode
params.doc: This is the database mode to be used for the SCSCF usrloc data persistent storage. Currently this module supports the Write-Back scheme only. * 0 - This disables database completely. Only memory will be used. Contacts will not survive restart. * 1 - Write-Backend scheme. All changes are made to memory and database synchronization is done in the timer

params.name: maxcontact
params.doc: The parameter can be used to limit the number of contact for each impu

params.name: maxcontact_3gpp
params.doc: The parameter can be used to limit the number of 3GPP contact for each impu

params.name: maxcontact_behaviour
params.doc: Behaviour of usrloc , after impu reach max contacts limit. * 0 - Disabled * 1 - Reject after reaching limit. * 2 - Overwrite

params.name: max_subscribes
params.doc: Max number of subscribes allowed per watcher for each IMPU

params.name: sub_dialog_hash_size
params.doc: Subscriber dialog hash table size

params.name: timer_procs
params.doc: process number of handling registeration

params.name: timer_interval
params.doc: Number of seconds between two timer runs. The module uses a timer to delete expired contacts, synchronize with database and other tasks, that need to be run periodically

params.name: desc_time_order
params.doc: If the user's contacts should be kept timestamp ordered; otherwise the contact will be ordered based on q value. Non 0 value means true.

params.name: matching_mode
params.doc: What contact matching algorithm to be used. * 0 - Contact Only matching * 1 - Contact and Callid Matching * 2 - Contact and Path header matching * 3 - Only contact IP and Port Matching

params.name: cseq_delay
params.doc: Delay (in seconds) for accepting as retransmissions register requests with same Call-ID and Cseq.

params.name: fetch_rows
params.doc: The number of the rows to be fetched at once from database when loading the location records.

params.name: hash_size
params.doc: The number of entries of the hash table used by usrloc

params.name: subs_hash_size
params.doc: The number of entries of the hash table used by usrloc to store the ims subscribe records

params.name: contacts_hash_size
params.doc: The number of entries of the hash table used by usrloc to store the contact records

params.name: nat_bflag
params.doc: NAT marker to handle natted registration

params.name: contact_delete_delay
params.doc: If contact is put into delay delete state, this is how long we delay before deleting

params.name: support_wildcardPSI
params.doc: Wildcard Public-Service-Identity (RFC5002). it will be actived by setting 1

params.name: unreg_validity
params.doc: Default validity time in seconds for unregister assignment to SCSCF

params.name: user_data_xsd
params.doc: Default value is 1800

params.name: realm
params.doc: Default value is NULL

params.name: skip_realm
params.doc: Skipping defined network name in the realm for NOTIFY's Message body reginfo tag.

params.name: server
params.doc: Address of InfluxDB server.

params.name: port
params.doc: Address of InfluxDB server.

params.name: database
params.doc: Database of InfluxDB server.

functions.name: influxdbc_measure
functions.doc: Start a measure group with the given name.

functions.name: influxdbc_measureend
functions.doc: End the current measure group.

functions.name: influxdbc_sub
functions.doc: Start a measure subgroup with the given name.

functions.name: influxdbc_subend
functions.doc: End the current measure subgroup.

functions.name: influxdbc_push
functions.doc: Push accumulated values to the server.

functions.name: influxdbc_long
functions.doc: Save the pair with provided name and value. Both parameters can have variables.

functions.name: is_ip
functions.doc: Returns TRUE if the argument is a valid IPv4, IPv6 or IPv6 reference. FALSE otherwise.

functions.name: is_pure_ip
functions.doc: Returns TRUE if the argument is a valid IPv4 or IPv6. FALSE otherwise.

functions.name: is_ipv4
functions.doc: Returns TRUE if the argument is a valid IPv4. FALSE otherwise.

functions.name: is_ipv6
functions.doc: Returns TRUE if the argument is a valid IPv6. FALSE otherwise.

functions.name: is_ipv6_reference
functions.doc: Returns TRUE if the argument is a valid IPv6 reference. FALSE otherwise.

functions.name: ip_type
functions.doc: Returns the type of the given IP.

functions.name: detailed_ip_type
functions.doc: Returns the detailed type of the given IP () (see http://www.iana.org/assignments/ipv6-address-space/ipv6-address-space.t xt, http://www.iana.org/assignments/iana-ipv6-special-registry/iana-ipv6-sp ecial-registry.txt, RFC 5735 and RFC 6598: PRIVATE, SHARED, LOOPBACK, IPV4MAP, DISCARD etc).

functions.name: detailed_ipv4_type
functions.doc: Returns the detailed type of the given IP () (see RFC 5735 and RFC 6598).

functions.name: detailed_ipv6_type
functions.doc: Returns the detailed type of the given IP () (see http://www.iana.org/assignments/ipv6-address-space/ipv6-address-space.t xt, http://www.iana.org/assignments/iana-ipv6-special-registry/iana-ipv6-sp ecial-registry.txt).

functions.name: compare_ips
functions.doc: Returns TRUE if both IP addresses are the same. FALSE otherwise. This function also allows comparing an IPv6 address against an IPv6 reference.

functions.name: compare_pure_ips
functions.doc: Returns TRUE if both IP's are the same. FALSE otherwise. This function does NOT allow comparing an IPv6 against an IPv6 reference.

functions.name: is_ip_rfc1918
functions.doc: Returns TRUE if the argument is a private IPv4 according to RFC 1918. FALSE otherwise.

functions.name: is_in_subnet
functions.doc: Returns TRUE if the first argument is an IP address within the (CIDR notation) subnets list in the second argument. FALSE otherwise.

functions.name: dns_sys_match_ip
functions.doc: Returns TRUE if ipaddr is associated by DNS to hostname. FALSE otherwise. It does not use the internal DNS resolver, but directly getaddrinfo(...). All addresses returned for the hostname are checked. Note that some hosts may return different lists of IP addresses for each query, if the DNS server is configured in that way (e.g., for providing load balancing through DNS).

functions.name: dns_int_match_ip
functions.doc: Returns TRUE if ipaddr is associated by DNS to hostname. FALSE otherwise. It uses internal DNS resolver. At this moment, the function might not check all the IP addresses as returned by dns_sys_match_ip(), because the internal resolver targets to discover the first address to be used for relaying SIP traffic. Thus is better to use dns_sys_match_ip() if the host you want to check has many IP addresses, in different address families (IPv4/6).

functions.name: dns_query
functions.doc: Store the IP addresses and their type that correspond to hostname in a config variable $dns(pvid=>key).

functions.name: ptr_query
functions.doc: Store the hostname that correspond to an IP address (IPv4 or IPv6) in a pseudo-variable variable $ptrquery(pvid=>hostname).

functions.name: srv_query
functions.doc: Queries DNS SRV records to resolve a service/protocol name into a list of priorities, weights, ports, and targets sorted by priority and weight as outlined in RFC 2782.

functions.name: naptr_query
functions.doc: Queries DNS NAPTR records to resolve a domain name into a list of orders, preferences, flags, services, regex, replaces sorted by orders and preferences as outlined in RFC 2915.

functions.name: dns_set_local_ttl
functions.doc: Set local ttl for DNS query results. If vttl is 0, then the value of the result and the core parameters are used.

functions.name: jansson_get
functions.doc: Copy the value at the location 'path' from the json object 'src' and store it in variable 'dst'. The path can also be a simple field name (a key), if it does not include any path separator. To retrieve the value of a field that includes path separators in the name, use jansson_get_field().

functions.name: jansson_pv_get
functions.doc: Similar to jansson_get(), but the 'srcvar' parameter can be only a variable name.

functions.name: jansson_set
functions.doc: Insert 'value' as 'type' at location 'path' into 'result'.

functions.name: jansson_append
functions.doc: Like jansson_set but can be used to append to arrays. It can also be used to combine two json objects.

functions.name: jansson_array_size
functions.doc: Puts the size of the array in 'src' at location 'path' into the pvar 'dst'.

functions.name: jansson_xdecode
functions.doc: Parse a JSON string in 'json' and store the elements in xapv 'xavp'. Top-level JSON must be an object or an array of objects. Nested arrays and objects are not decoded but stored as string.

functions.name: jansson_xencode
functions.doc: Encode the items in the xavp 'xavp' as JSON and store the result in a pv. Nested xavp's are not supported.

functions.name: jansson_get_field
functions.doc: Copy the value of the field 'field_name' from json object 'src' and store it in pvar 'dst'. The field name is not evaluated as JSON path, therefore it has a different behaviour than jansson_get() and can be used when the field name contains path delimiters.

params.name: min_srv_ttl
params.doc: The minimum acceptable TTL in seconds for SRV DNS entries. This means that TTLs from the DNS will be ignored if they are lower than this value. It cannot be set lower than 1 second.

params.name: result_pv
params.doc: The PV spec where to store the result of a call to janssonrpc_request(). It can be any writable PV.

params.name: server
params.doc: The server providing the remote jsonrpc service. Format can be "conn=example;addr=localhost;port=9999;priority=10;weight=20" or "conn=bar;srv=_sip._tcp.example.net".

params.name: retry_codes
params.doc: A comma delimited list of error codes or error code ranges to automatically schedule a request retry if received.

params.name: keep_alive
params.doc: number of seconds to send a tcp keep-alive to the server connection

functions.name: janssonrpc_notification
functions.doc: * conn - name for a collection of servers (required) * method - jsonrpc method (required) * params - jsonrpc request params (required) Use $null or empty string to not send any parameters in the jsonrpc notification.

functions.name: janssonrpc_request
functions.doc: The conn, method, params, and options can be a static string or a dynamic string value with config variables.

functions.name: json_get_field
functions.doc: Copy field 'field_name' from json object 'json_string' and store it in pvar 'destination'.

functions.name: json_get_string
functions.doc: Copy field 'field_name' from json object 'json_string' and store it in pvar 'destination'.

params.name: servers
params.doc: The servers providing the remote jsonrpc service. Format is "host1:port1,priority1 host2:port2,priority2". Requests to servers of the same priority will be distributed evenly (round robin). Server groups with higher priority are used first.

params.name: max_conn_attempts
params.doc: Max number of connection attempts for a server. -1 will keep reconnecting forever, 0 will skip any attempt to reconnect.

functions.name: jsonrpc_notification
functions.doc: Invokes the remote 'method' with the given 'parameters' as a notification. Unlike jsonrpc_request (below), notifications do not receive a response. Script processing continues in the usual fashion as soon as the notification has been sent.

params.name: pretty_format
params.doc: Pretty format for JSON-RPC response document if set to 1. To disable, set to 0.

params.name: transport
params.doc: Control what transports are enabled. The value can be: * 0 - all transports that can be enabled. For http, the xhttp module must be loaded. For FIFO, the fifo_name parameter must be set. For DATAGRAM, the dgram_socket parameter must be set. For TCP, the tcp_socket parameter must be set. * 1 - only HTTP transport * 2 - only FIFO transport * 4 - only DATAGRAM transport * 8 - only TCP transport

params.name: fifo_name
params.doc: The name of the FIFO file to be created for listening and reading external commands. If the given path is not absolute, the fifo file is created relative to run_dir (global parameter).

params.name: fifo_mode
params.doc: Permission to be used for creating the listening FIFO file. It follows the UNIX conventions.

params.name: fifo_group
params.doc: System Group to be used for creating the listening FIFO file.

params.name: fifo_user
params.doc: System User to be used for creating the listening FIFO file.

params.name: fifo_reply_dir
params.doc: Directory to be used for creating the reply FIFO files.

params.name: dgram_socket
params.doc: The name of a Unix socket file or an IP address. The Unix datagram or UDP socket will be created using this parameter in order to read the external commands. Both IPv4 and IPv6 are supported. If the given path for Unix socket is not absolute, then it is created relative to run_dir (global parameter).

params.name: dgram_workers
params.doc: The number of worker processes to be created. Each worker process will be a datagram server.

params.name: dgram_mode
params.doc: Permission to be used for creating the listening UNIX datagram socket. Not necessary for a UDP socket. It follows the UNIX conventions.

params.name: dgram_group
params.doc: Group to be used for creating the listening UNIX socket.

params.name: dgram_user
params.doc: User to be used for creating the listening UNIX socket.

params.name: dgram_timeout
params.doc: The reply will expire after trying to send it for socket_timeout milliseconds.

params.name: tcp_socket
params.doc: The name of tcp socket to listen on for RPC commands. Only IPv4/IPv6 sockets are supported, unix file stream socket not yet.

functions.name: jsonrpc_dispatch
functions.doc: Handle the JSONRPC request and generate a response.

functions.name: jsonrpc_exec
functions.doc: Execute a JSON-RPC command given as a parameter.

params.name: key_mode
params.doc: Mode to use the private and public keys. If set to 0, they are read always from the disk. If set to 1, they are cached in memory with the first use (no reload support yet).

functions.name: jwt_generate
functions.doc: Generate the JWT, its value can be retrieved in the variable $jwt(val).

functions.name: jwt_verify
functions.doc: Verify the JWT.

functions.name: jwt_verify_key
functions.doc: Verify the JWT.

params.name: brokers
params.doc: Specifies a list of brokers separated by commas.

params.name: configuration
params.doc: Specifies a set of general properties.

params.name: topic
params.doc: Specifies a topic name and a set of topic properties.

params.name: init_without_kafka
params.doc: Set to anything but 0, specifies if kamailio starts even when kafka brokers are not available at startup time.

params.name: metadata_timeout
params.doc: Specifies, in milliseconds, how much time kamailio waits to get topic metadata info at startup time.

params.name: log_without_overflow
params.doc: Set to anything but 0, will skip logging most of the error messages that may happen to each kafka message sent to the broker. This is useful when e.g. kafka broker goes down, not to overflow syslog with error messages.

functions.name: kafka_send
functions.doc: Send a message to a specific topic via Kafka server.

functions.name: kafka_send_key
functions.doc: Send a message with an associated key to a specific topic via Kafka server.

params.name: node_hostname
params.doc: The name of this host to register in rabbitmq.

params.name: amqp_consumer_processes
params.doc: The number of worker processes to handle messages consumption.

params.name: amqp_consumer_event_key
params.doc: The default name of the field in json payload to compose the event name 1st part

params.name: amqp_consumer_event_subkey
params.doc: The default name of the field in json payload to compose the event name 2nd part

params.name: amqp_max_channels
params.doc: The number of pre allocated channels for the connection.

params.name: amqp_connection
params.doc: The connection url to rabbitmq. can be set multiple times for failover.

params.name: event_callback
params.doc: The name of the function in the kemi configuration file (embedded scripting language such as Lua, Python, ...) to be executed instead of event_route[...] blocks.

params.name: amqp_consumer_loop_count
params.doc: The consumer loop count.

params.name: amqp_internal_loop_count
params.doc: The internal listen for commands loop count.

params.name: amqp_consumer_ack_loop_count
params.doc: The work ack loop count.

params.name: consume_messages_on_reconnect
params.doc: This parameter indicates if the module ignores the loop counters on reconnect and consumes all the pending messages ready to be consumed.

params.name: single_consumer_on_reconnect
params.doc: When the main loop receives a message from rabbitmq it will defer the execution to a worker in a round-robin manner. This parameter allows to use the same worker when kazoo reconnects to rabbitmq.

params.name: amqp_consumer_ack_timeout
params.doc: Timeout when checking for acknowledge from workers.

params.name: amqp_interprocess_timeout
params.doc: Timeout when checking for commands (publish/query) for sending to rabbitmq.

params.name: amqp_waitframe_timeout
params.doc: Timeout when checking for messages from rabbitmq.

params.name: amqp_query_timeout
params.doc: Timeout when checking for reply messages from rabbitmq for kazoo_query commands.

params.name: amqp_query_timeout_avp
params.doc: avp holding the value in seconds for Timeout when checking for reply messages from rabbitmq for kazoo_query commands.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: The database for the presentity table.

params.name: presentity_table
params.doc: The name of the presentity table in the database.

params.name: pua_mode
params.doc: Control if the module has to connect to presence database tables. Set it to 0 to not connect to database.

functions.name: kazoo_publish
functions.doc: The function publishes a json payload to rabbitmq. The routing_key parameter should be encoded. Optional AMQP-Headers are specified in the format key1=value1;key2=value2

functions.name: kazoo_subscribe
functions.doc: The function subscribes to exchange/type on queue with routing_key. The routing_key parameter should be encoded.

functions.name: kazoo_subscribe
functions.doc: The function takes additional parameters to the subscribe function.

functions.name: kazoo_pua_publish
functions.doc: The function build presentity state from json_payload and updates presentity table.

functions.name: kazoo_encode
functions.doc: The function encodes the 1st parameter for amqp and puts the result in the 2nd parameter.

functions.name: kazoo_json
functions.doc: The function extracts the value from a json payload and puts the result in the 3rd parameter. It can use nested values for the query part.

params.name: ping_interval
params.doc: Define the interval (in seconds) ping requests are sent to destinations

params.name: destination
params.doc: Allows to statically define destinations you want to monitor

params.name: delete_counter
params.doc: Unsuccessful attempts increase delete_counter. After passing it, keepalive module doesn't try to send options requests. Ignored if it's set to 0.

params.name: ping_from
params.doc: Sets from header's uri.

functions.name: ka_is_alive
functions.doc: Get destination status.

functions.name: ka_add_destination
functions.doc: Adds SIP URI in the memory destinations list to perform keep alive to it.

functions.name: ka_del_destination
functions.doc: Deletes the SIP URI from the memory destinations list used for monitoring.

functions.name: setsflag
functions.doc: Set the script flag.

functions.name: issflagset
functions.doc: Return true if the script flag is set.

functions.name: resetsflag
functions.doc: Reset the script flag.

functions.name: setbflag
functions.doc: Set the branch flag.

functions.name: isbflagset
functions.doc: Return true if the branch flag is set.

functions.name: resetbflag
functions.doc: Reset the branch flag.

functions.name: setdsturi
functions.doc: Set the destination address URI (outbound proxy address).

functions.name: resetdsturi
functions.doc: Reset the destination address URI (outbound proxy address).

functions.name: isdsturiset
functions.doc: Check if the destination address URI (outbound proxy address) is set.

functions.name: pv_printf
functions.doc: Evaluates the str and sets the resulting value to variable var. For backward compatibility reasons, the same function can be executed via 'avp_printf(var, str)'.

functions.name: is_myself
functions.doc: Check if the parameter matches the 'myself' condition (i.e., is a local IP or domain). Note that if the port is missing in the URI, then no port matching is done (in other words, port matching is skipped -- it does not use default SIP ports 5060 or 5061 for matching).

functions.name: is_myhost
functions.doc: Check if the host part of the parameter matches a local domain or IP address.

functions.name: setdebug
functions.doc: Set the debug log level per process.

functions.name: resetdebug
functions.doc: Reset the local debug log level back to the value of core parameter 'debug'.

functions.name: km_append_branch
functions.doc: This function was replaced by append_branch() from corex module, starting with version 4.0.0.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: URL of the database table to be used.

params.name: lcr_gw_table
params.doc: Name of the table holding gateways definitions.

params.name: id_column
params.doc: Name of the auto-increment, primary key column. Common to all lcr module tables.

params.name: lcr_id_column
params.doc: Name of the column holding the identifier of an LCR instance. Common to all lcr module tables. In lcr_rule and lcr_rule_target tables, value of the column is integer from 1 to lcr_count. In lcr_gw table, value of the column is from 0 to lcr_count.

params.name: gw_name_column
params.doc: Name of the column holding gateway's name for documentation purpose.

params.name: ip_addr_column
params.doc: Name of the column holding the IPv4 or IPv6 address of the gateway.

params.name: hostname_column
params.doc: Name of the column holding gateway's hostname that is used in Request-URI hostpart, when request is sent to the gateway.

params.name: port_column
params.doc: Name of the column holding the port number of the gateway.

params.name: params_column
params.doc: Name of the column holding gateway's parameters that is used in Request-URI, when request is sent to the gateway.

params.name: uri_scheme_column
params.doc: Name of the column holding the uri scheme of the gateway.

params.name: transport_column
params.doc: Name of the column holding the transport protocol to be used for the gateway.

params.name: strip_column
params.doc: Name of the column holding the number of characters to be stripped from the front of Request-URI user part before inserting tag.

params.name: tag_column
params.doc: Name of the column holding gateway specific tag string that is added to Request URI userpart after stripping.

params.name: flags_column
params.doc: Name of the column holding gateway specific flag values.

params.name: defunct_column
params.doc: Name of the column holding UNIX timestamp telling the time until which the gw is considered as defunct. If timestamp value is 4294967295 (= max UNIX timestamp value) or greater, gw is considered currently unused and is not loaded into memory at all.

params.name: lcr_rule_table
params.doc: Name of the table holding the LCR rules.

params.name: prefix_column
params.doc: Name of the column in lcr_rule and lcr_gw tables holding prefix of Request-URI user part and prefix of gateway, respectively.

params.name: from_uri_column
params.doc: Name of the column holding the From (caller's) URI.

params.name: mt_tvalue_column
params.doc: Name of the column holding mtree tvalue.

params.name: request_uri_column
params.doc: Name of the column holding the regular expression to match against the complete request URI (including the "sip:" prefix).

params.name: stopper_column
params.doc: Name of the column holding rule's stopper attribute.

params.name: enabled_column
params.doc: Name of the column telling is the rule is currently enabled or disabled.

params.name: lcr_rule_target_table
params.doc: Name of the table holding information about the LCR rule targets (gateways).

params.name: rule_id_column
params.doc: Name of lcr_rule_target_table column containing an id of lcr_rule table.

params.name: gw_id_column
params.doc: Name of lcr_rule_target_table column containing an id of lcr_gw table.

params.name: priority_column
params.doc: Name of the column holding the priority of the rule target.

params.name: weight_column
params.doc: Name of the column holding weight of rule target.

params.name: lcr_count
params.doc: Maximum value of lcr_id.

params.name: gw_uri_avp
params.doc: Internal AVP that load_gws() function uses to store information of matching gateways.

params.name: ruri_user_avp
params.doc: Internal AVP that next_gw function uses to store Request-URI user for subsequent next_gw calls.

params.name: tag_avp
params.doc: If defined, an AVP where successful next_gw and from_gw functions store gateway's tag.

params.name: flags_avp
params.doc: If defined, an AVP where successful next_gw and from_gw functions store gateway's flags.

params.name: rule_id_avp
params.doc: If defined, an AVP where successful next_gw and from_gw functions store matching rule's id.

params.name: mt_pv_values
params.doc: If defined and mt_value is given for a rule, load_gws() matches caller URI userpart to a mtree given as mtree parameter.

params.name: mtree
params.doc: Name of mtree to which load_gws() matches caller URI userpart.

params.name: defunct_capability
params.doc: Tells if defunct capability of (non-responsive) gateways is supported. Non-zero value turns on defunct capability.

params.name: lcr_id_avp
params.doc: Internal AVP that load_gws() function uses to store LCR instance identifier of loaded gateways. Only needed if gateway defunct capability has been activated.

params.name: defunct_gw_avp
params.doc: Internal AVP that next_gw() function uses to store internal index of the selected gateway for later use by defunct_gw() function. Only needed if gateway defunct capability has been activated.

params.name: lcr_rule_hash_size
params.doc: Defines the size of hash table used to store LCR rules. Hashing is done based on rule's prefix. Larger value means less collisions with other prefixes. Hash size value should be a power of 2.

params.name: lcr_gw_count
params.doc: Defines the maximum number of gateways in lcr_gw table.

params.name: dont_strip_or_prefix_flag
params.doc: Defines the flag number used to tell if stripping and tagging is done for the selected gateway.

params.name: priority_ordering
params.doc: Defines how matching gateways are ordered (see Overview section).

params.name: fetch_rows
params.doc: The number of the rows to be fetched at once from database when loading data from lcr_rule table. This value can be used to tune the load time at startup. For 1MB of private memory (default) it should be below 3750. In order for this parameter to have effect, the database driver must support fetch_result() capability.

params.name: ping_interval
params.doc: Interval in seconds for sending OPTIONS ping requests to gateways that, due to failures, have been marked as inactive by inactivate_gw() function call. If an inactive gateway later gives a valid response (see ping_valid_reply_codes) to a ping request, it is marked again as active.

params.name: ping_inactivate_threshold
params.doc: Tells after how many failures (= inactivate_gw() function calls) a gateway is marked as inactive.

params.name: ping_valid_reply_codes
params.doc: A comma separated list of SIP reply codes, which are accepted as valid replies to OPTIONS ping requests. Reply codes 2xx are by default accepted as valid replies and they don't need to be listed here.

params.name: ping_from
params.doc: From URI used in OPTIONS ping requests.

params.name: ping_socket
params.doc: Socket to be used for sending OPTIONS ping request. If not set or set to “”, default socket is used.

functions.name: load_gws
functions.doc: Loads attributes of matching gateways to gw_uri_avp (see Overview section). Argument lcr_id specifies the used LCR instance. It can be a positive integer or a pseudo variable containing an integer value. If uri_user is given, it is used, instead of Request-URI user part, to look for matching gateways. Caller's URI may be given by caller_uri argument. If caller_uri argument is omitted, it defaults to empty string. Both uri_user and caller_uri argument may be a string or a pseudo variable containing a string value.

functions.name: next_gw
functions.doc: Upon first call, fetches attribute values stored in first gw_uri_avp, destroys that AVP, and rewrites Request-URI and possibly also destination URI as described in the Overview section. Saves user part of Request-URI into ruri_user_avp for use in subsequent next_gw() calls.

functions.name: inactivate_gw
functions.doc: Inactivates the gateway denoted by lcr_id_avp and defunct_gw_avp (which were set by previous next_gw() call). Use of this function requires that ping_interval module parameter has been set to a positive value allowing an inactivated gateway to be automatically activated by a positive response to OPTIONS ping request.

functions.name: defunct_gw
functions.doc: Defuncts gateway denoted by lcr_id_avp and defunct_gw_avp (which were set by previuos next_gw() call) for a period of seconds given as argument. Argument must be a positive integer constant or a pseudo variable with positive integer value. Value of defunct column in database is not updated.

functions.name: from_gw
functions.doc: Checks if request comes from IP address, transport protocol and source port specified for a gateway in LCR instance lcr_id. Fails if the LCR instance includes one or more gateways without IP address. IP address, transport protocol and source port to be checked are either taken from source IP address and port of the request or (if present) from ip_addr, proto and src_port arguments.

functions.name: from_any_gw
functions.doc: Checks if request comes from IP address, transport protocol and source port specified for any gateway. Only LCR instances, where all gateways have IP address, are included in the test. IP address, transport protocol and source port to be checked are either taken from source IP address, transport protocol and source port of the request or (if present) from ip_addr, proto and src_port arguments. See from_gw() function for more info about the arguments.

functions.name: to_gw
functions.doc: Checks if in-dialog request goes to IP address and transport protocol specified for a gateway in LCR instance lcr_id. Fails if LCR instance includes one or more gateways without IP address. IP address and transport protocol to be checked are either taken from Request-URI or (if present) from ip_addr and proto arguments. See from_gw() for more info regarding the arguments.

functions.name: to_any_gw
functions.doc: Checks if in-dialog request goes to IP address and transport protocol of any gateway. Only LCR instances, where all gateways have IP address, are included in the test. IP address and transport protocol to be checked are either taken from Request-URI or (if present) from ip_addr and proto arguments. See from_gw() for more info regarding the arguments.

params.name: config_file
params.doc: Full path to LDAP configuration file.

params.name: connect_mode
params.doc: Control if the module must stop loading when connecting to server fails during start up. Values: 0 - stop loading; 1 - continue even if connecting to database server fails..

functions.name: ldap_search
functions.doc: Performs an LDAP search operation using given LDAP URL and stores result internally for later retrieval by ldap_result* functions. If one or more LDAP entries are found the function returns the number of found entries which evaluates to TRUE in the Kamailio configuration script. It returns -1 (FALSE) in case no LDAP entry was found, and -2 (FALSE) if an internal error like e.g. an LDAP error occurred.

functions.name: ldap_result
functions.doc: This function converts LDAP attribute values into AVPs for later use in the message routing script. It accesses the LDAP result set fetched by the last ldap_search call. ldap_attr_name specifies the LDAP attribute name who's value will be stored in AVP avp_spec. Multi valued LDAP attributes generate an indexed AVP. The optional regex_subst parameter allows to further define what part of an attribute value should be stored as AVP.

functions.name: ldap_result_check
functions.doc: This function compares ldap_attr_name's value with string_to_match for equality. It accesses the LDAP result set fetched by the last ldap_search call. The optional regex_subst parameter allows to further define what part of the attribute value should be used for the equality match. If ldap_attr_name is multi valued, each value is checked against string_to_match. If one or more of the values do match the function returns 1 (TRUE).

functions.name: ldap_result_next
functions.doc: An LDAP search operation can return multiple LDAP entries. This function can be used to cycle through all returned LDAP entries. It returns 1 (TRUE) if there is another LDAP entry present in the LDAP result set and causes ldap_result* functions to work on the next LDAP entry. The function returns -1 (FALSE) if there are no more LDAP entries in the LDAP result set.

functions.name: ldap_filter_url_encode
functions.doc: This function applies the following escaping rules to string and stores the result in AVP avp_spec:

functions.name: log_udp
functions.doc: Send the text to the address specified in core parameter log_engine_data. It is provided as sample function mainly for testing, because all logs messages printed by kamailio should be diverted as described in the section 'Core Logging', so you can use xlog functions in config file.

functions.name: sd_journal_print
functions.doc: Print the text in the systemd journal at the provided level parameter.

functions.name: sd_journal_send_xavp
functions.doc: Creates a structured log event in journald.

params.name: exact_type
params.doc: Indicates to the location server that the contents of the "location_type" parameter must be strictly followed. Values are 0 (false) or 1 (true).

params.name: response_time
params.doc: A time value informs the location server how long the client is prepared to wait for a response.

params.name: location_type
params.doc: The "locationType" element contains a list of types that are requested. Values are "any", "geodetic", "civic" or "locationURI" and combinations. * any - returns location information in all forms available * geodetic - returns a location by value in the form of a geodetic location * civic - returns a location by value in the form of a civic address * locationURI - returns a set of location URIs (location by reference)

params.name: post_request
params.doc: Dereferencing the location can be done using either the HTTP GET or POST method. This parameter globally defines whether only HTTP POST method should be used. Values are 0 (GET) or 1 (POST).

params.name: location_profile
params.doc: A Presence Information Data Format Location Object (PIDF-LO) may contain geodetic or civic location profile or combinations. A LoST findService contains only one location, which is selected via this parameter as follows: * 0 - takes the first location of any type * 1 - takes the last location of any type * 2 - takes the first geodetic location * 3 - takes the first civic location

params.name: location_3d
params.doc: A Presence Information Data Format Location Object (PIDF-LO) may contain one of the shape types as listed in RFC5491 (https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5491). A LoST findService request currently contains only a profile for two-dimensional geodetic location information, which is the default setting for this parameter. The parameter can be set to 1 if a LoST server supports 3d, otherwise a 3d location is reduced to 2d by the module. * 0 - two-dimensional (2d) shape representations only * 1 - three-dimensional (3d) volume representations allowed

params.name: geoheader_type
params.doc: A Geolocation header may include a list of locationValues pointing to either a Presence Information Data Format Location Object (PIDF-LO) in the SIP body using a content-indirection (cid:) URI per RFC4483 (https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4483), or an http(s) URI pointing to an external source. This parameter supports filtering of the following types: * 0 (any) - any URI (first or last) * 1 (cid) - cid URI (aka Location-by-Value) * 2 (http) - http URI (aka Location-by-Reference) * 3 (https) - https URI (aka Location-by-Reference)

params.name: geoheader_order
params.doc: A Geolocation header may include a list of locationValues. This parameter sets the order of the URI used to retrieve the location information, either the first element of a certain type or the last. Values are 0 (first) or 1 (last).

params.name: recursion
params.doc: A Geolocation header may include a list of locationValues. This parameter sets the order of the URI used to retrieve the location information, either the first element of a certain type or the last. Values are 0 (first) or 1 (last).

params.name: verbose
params.doc: Detailed output of LoST findService, redirect or error response as shown below. Values are 0 (disabled) or 1 (enabled). ### LOST expires: [2031-01-27T14:54:21+00:00] ### LOST lastUpdated: [2021-01-29T14:54:21+00:00] ### LOST source: [ecrf.demo.gridgears.xx] ### LOST sourceId: [06ac5b1c-d6c8-42bd-a667-5d1b90bb3d95] ### LOST displayName: [Polizeinotruf (de)] ### LOST serviceNumber: [112] ### LOST service: [urn:service:sos] ### LOST uri: [sip:112@demo.dec112.xx] ### LOST via: [ecrf.demo.gridgears.xx]

functions.name: lost_held_query
functions.doc: Sends a HELD locationRequest to a given connection. The device identity is either specified, or the P-A-I header value, or the From header value. * con - the name of an existing HTTP connection, defined by a httpcon modparam * id - the device id used in the HELD locationRequest * pidf-lo - the PIDF-LO returned in the HELD locationRequest response * url - the location reference returned in the HELD locationRequest response - this reference may be added as Geolocation header value and forwarded downstream. Note: to work properly, it is required to include "locationURI" in the location_type parameter. * error - any error code returned in the HELD response

functions.name: lost_held_dereference
functions.doc: Sends a HELD POST locationRequest to a given URL. Attributes are responseTime and responseType. The locationType property "exact" is set to "false". * url - a URL received via Geolocation header to dereference location * rtime - the response time as defined in Section 3.2, “response_time (int)” * rtype - the response type (location) as defined in Section 3.3, “location_type (string)” * pidf-lo - the PIDF-LO returned in the HELD locationRequest response * error - any error code returned in the HELD response

functions.name: lost_query
functions.doc: Sends a LOST findService request to a given connection. PIDF-LO and URN are either specified, or, if omitted, parsed from the message body (PIDF-LO) and request line (URN). Either "pidf-lo" or "urn" can be set to an empty string to be ignored. * con - the name of an existing HTTP connection defined by a httpcon modparam * pidf-lo - the PIDF-LO used to create the LOST findService request * urn - the URN used to create the LOST findService request * uri - the SIP uri returned in the LOST findServiceResponse * name - the display name returned in the LOST findServiceResponse * error - any error code returned in the LOST findServiceResponse

params.name: lrkproxy_sock
params.doc: Used to define the list of LRKP_TSL instances to connect to. These can be UNIX sockets or IPv4/IPv6 UDP sockets. Each modparam entry will insert sockets into a single set with default value set ID '0'. To define multiple LRKP_TSL, just add the instances in each modparam.

params.name: lrkproxy_disable_tout
params.doc: Once LRKP_TSL was found unreachable and marked as disabled, the LRKP_CL module will not attempt to establish communication to LRKP_TSL for lrkproxy_disable_tout seconds.

params.name: lrkproxy_tout
params.doc: Timeout value in waiting for reply from LRKP_TSL.

params.name: lrkproxy_retr
params.doc: How many times the LRKP_CL should retry to send and receive after timeout was generated.

params.name: lrkp_alg
params.doc: This parameter set the algorithm of LRKP_TSL selection. lrk_LINER=0, lrk_RR=1

params.name: hash_table_tout
params.doc: Number of seconds after an lrkproxy hash table entry is marked for deletion. By default, this parameter is set to 3600 (seconds).

params.name: hash_table_size
params.doc: Size of the hash table. Default value is 128.

params.name: custom_sdp_ip_avp
params.doc: This option useful for solving STUN and help UDP packets make it across NAT devices safe and sound. In this way, it should be set by clients' IP public manually.

params.name: gt
params.doc: This option useful for optimization in allocation port resource in lrkproxy service.

params.name: behind_nat
params.doc: The behind_nat is used when the LRKProxy is behind NAT firewall and the external IP should be as Advertised IP. It could be set 0:disable or 1:enable. If you use AWS for LRKProxy, you might should set behind_nat option.

params.name: start_port
params.doc: This option use for local rang port for working with LRKProxy engine. Default value is based on LRKProxy engine option. For example if the range of ports in LRKProxy is set from 20000 to 30000, You could use this option to set a subset of the LRKProxy range.

params.name: end_port
params.doc: This option use for local rang port for working with LRKProxy engine. Default value is based on LRKProxy engine option. For example if the range of ports in LRKProxy is set from 20000 to 30000, You could use this option to set a subset of the LRKProxy range.

functions.name: set_lrkproxy_set
functions.doc: Sets the Id of the lrkproxy set to be used for the next lrkproxy_manage() command. The parameter can be an integer or a config variable holding an integer.

functions.name: lrkproxy_manage
functions.doc: Manage the LRKProxy session - it combines the functionality of lrkproxy_offer(), lrkproxy_answer() and unforce_lrkproxy(), detecting internally based on message type and method which one to execute.

params.name: protocol
params.doc: The websocket sub-protocol.

params.name: timeout_init
params.doc: The interval in microseconds to wait for websocket connection to be initialized.

params.name: timeout_read
params.doc: The interval in microseconds to wait for the response of the lwsc_request() group of functions.

params.name: verbosity
params.doc: Control the verbosity of debug messages on libwebsockets events, higher value means more debug messages. It has to be a positive number, currently 2 or higher results in maximum verbosity.

functions.name: lwsc_notify
functions.doc: Send data via websockets to the address specified by wsurl. No response is expected. Transmission is not guaranteed (e.g., cannot connect to target).

functions.name: lwsc_notify_proto
functions.doc: Send data via websockets to the address specified by wsurl, providing websocket protocol. No response is expected. Transmission is not guaranteed (e.g., cannot connect to target).

functions.name: lwsc_request
functions.doc: Send data via websockets to the address specified by wsurl, a response is expected and made available in $lwsc(rdata).

functions.name: lwsc_request_proto
functions.doc: Send data via websockets to the address specified by wsurl, providing websocket protocol. A response is expected and made available in $lwsc(rdata).

params.name: contact_flds_separator
params.doc: First char of this parameter is used as a separator for encoding/decoding Contact headers. If you set this parameter to "-", then an encoded URI will look like "sip:user-password-ip-port-protocol@PublicIP"

functions.name: sdp_mangle_ip
functions.doc: Changes IP addresses inside SDP document in lines describing connections like c=IN IP4 . Currently this function only changes IP4 addresses since IP6 probably will not need to traverse NAT :)

functions.name: sdp_mangle_port
functions.doc: Changes ports in SDP document in lines starting a media section like "m=audio 13451".

functions.name: encode_contact
functions.doc: This function will encode URIs inside the "Contact" header in the following manner "sip:username:password@ip:port;transport=protocol" goes sip:enc_pref*username*ip*port*protocol@public_ip. "*" (asterisk) is the default separator.

functions.name: decode_contact
functions.doc: This function will decode the URI in first line in packets which come with encoded URI in the following manner sip:enc_pref*username*ip*port*protocol*src_ip*src_port*src_proto@public _ip;parameters is converted to sip:username:password@ip:port;parameters and will set destination URI to sip:src_ip:src_port;transport=src_proto (so that the next forward() or t_relay() will send the message back to src_ip:src_port using src_proto). It uses the default set parameter for contact encoding separator.

functions.name: decode_contact_header
functions.doc: This function will decode URIs inside the "Contact" header in the same manner as decode_contact(). The difference is that no dst_uri is set (src_ip, src_port and src_proto are ignored) and instead of changing the request URI, the Contact header URI is modified. It uses the default set parameter for contact encoding separator.

functions.name: pow
functions.doc: The exponentiation function, computing the base raised to power, storing in res.

functions.name: math_logN
functions.doc: The function computes the natural logarithm of x and stores the result in res.

functions.name: math_log2
functions.doc: The function computes the base-2 logarithm of x and stores the result in res.

functions.name: math_log10
functions.doc: The function computes the base-10 logarithm of x and stores the result in res.

functions.name: math_sqrt
functions.doc: The function computes the square root of x and stores the result in res.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: The URL for the database connection.

params.name: matrix_table
params.doc: The name of the table containing the matrix data.

params.name: matrix_first_col
params.doc: The name of the column containing the first row in the matrix.

params.name: matrix_second_col
params.doc: The name of the column containing the second row in the matrix.

params.name: matrix_res_col
params.doc: The name of the column containing the result ID to be used.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: URL to the database containing the data.

params.name: matrix_table
params.doc: Name of the matrix table for the matrix module.

params.name: matrix_first_col
params.doc: The row index in the matrix

params.name: matrix_second_col
params.doc: The column index in the matrix

params.name: matrix_res_col
params.doc: The resource contained in the matrix

functions.name: matrix
functions.detail: matrix (string first, string second, string dstavp)
functions.doc: Looks up the desired result ID in the matrix for the given column and value and saves the result in dstavp. Returns false if the cell is not defined or when an error occurred. Pseudo-variables or AVPs can be used for first and second.

params.name: max_limit
params.doc: Set an upper limit for the max-forward value in the outgoing requests. If the header is present, the decremented value is not allowed to exceed this max_limits - if it does, the header value will by decreased to “max_limit”.

functions.name: maxfwd_process
functions.doc: If no Max-Forward header is present in the received request, a header will be added having the original value equal with “max_value”. If a Max-Forward header is already present, its value will be decremented (if not 0). The parameter can be a variable.

functions.name: mf_process_maxfwd_header
functions.doc: Same as maxfwd_process(max_value).

functions.name: process_maxfwd
functions.doc: Same as maxfwd_process(max_value).

functions.name: is_maxfwd_lt
functions.doc: Checks if the Max-Forward header value is less than the “max_value” parameter value. It considers also the value of the new inserted header (if locally added). The parameter can be a variable.

functions.name: maxfwd_at_least
functions.doc: Same as is_maxfwd_lt(max_value).

functions.name: mf_lowlimit
functions.doc: Same as is_maxfwd_lt(max_value).

params.name: disable
params.doc: Boolean flag that specifies if mediaproxy should be disabled. This is useful when you want to use the same kamailio configuration in two different context, one using mediaproxy, the other not. In the case mediaproxy is disabled, calls to its functions will have no effect, allowing you to use the same configuration without changes.

params.name: mediaproxy_socket
params.doc: It is the path to the filesystem socket where the mediaproxy dispatcher listens for commands from the module.

params.name: mediaproxy_timeout
params.doc: How much time (in milliseconds) to wait for an answer from the mediaproxy dispatcher.

params.name: signaling_ip_avp
params.doc: Specification of the AVP which holds the IP address from where the SIP signaling originated. If this AVP is set it will be used to get the signaling IP address, else the source IP address from where the SIP message was received will be used. This AVP is meant to be used in cases where there are more than one proxy in the call setup path and the proxy that actually starts mediaproxy doesn't receive the SIP messages directly from the UA and it cannot determine the NAT IP address from where the signaling originated. In such a case attaching a SIP header at the first proxy and then copying that header's value into the signaling_ip_avp on the proxy that starts mediaproxy will allow it to get the correct NAT IP address from where the SIP signaling originated.

params.name: media_relay_avp
params.doc: Specification of the AVP which holds an optional application defined media relay IP address of a particular media relay that is preferred to be used for the current call. If an IP address is written to this AVP before calling use_media_proxy(), it will be preferred by the dispatcher over the normal selection algorithm.

params.name: ice_candidate
params.doc: Indicates the type of ICE candidate that will be added to the SDP. It can take 3 values: 'none', 'low-priority' or 'high-priority'. If 'none' is selected no candidate will be added to the SDP. If 'low-priority' is selected then a low priority candidate will be added and if 'high-priority' is selected a high priority one.

params.name: ice_candidate_avp
params.doc: Specification of the AVP which holds the ICE candidate that will be inserted in the SDP. The value specified in this AVP will override the value in ice_candidate module parameter. If the AVP is not set, the default value will be used.

functions.name: engage_media_proxy
functions.doc: Trigger the use of MediaProxy for all the dialog requests and replies that have an SDP body. This needs to be called only once for the first INVITE in a dialog. After that it will use the dialog module to trace the dialog and automatically call use_media_proxy() on every request and reply that belongs to the dialog and has an SDP body. When the dialog ends it will also call automatically end_media_session(). All of these are called internally on dialog callbacks, so for this function to work, the dialog module must be loaded and configured.

functions.name: use_media_proxy
functions.doc: Will make a call to the dispatcher and replace the IPs and ports in the SDP body with the ones returned by the media relay for each supported media stream in the SDP body. This will force the media streams to be routed through the media relay. If a mix of supported and unsupported streams are present in the SDP, only the supported streams will be modified, while the unsupported streams will be left alone.

functions.name: end_media_session
functions.doc: Will call on the dispatcher to inform the media relay to end the media session. This is done when a call ends, to instruct the media relay to release the resources allocated to that call as well as to save logging information about the media session. Called on BYE, CANCEL or failures.

params.name: servers
params.doc: The servers to connect to. At the moment only one server is supported.

params.name: expire
params.doc: The default expire value of entries in memcached in seconds. The maximal value is 2592000 (about 30 days). A value of zero means that no automatic expiration is done, memcached will then delete the least used items when the cache gets full.

params.name: mode
params.doc: The used storage mode for the memcached module for write access to the hash table. A value of “0” means to set (overwrite) the old value, with a value of “1” the module will not overwrite it. Here every entry to the hash table could be written only once, subsequent inserts will fail.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: The timeout for the memcache servers access in milliseconds.

params.name: memory
params.doc: The memory mode for the memcached client library. The library can use the system memory manager or the internal memory manager from Kamailio. The system memory manager configuration is the default, most implementations (like other projects) probably use this approach as well. The internal memory configuration should be faster and protects better against memory leaks that could bring down your server, as the available memory pool is limited by the Kamailio configuration.

params.name: stringify
params.doc: The string mode for the memcached module. By default the module checks the flags for each returned value from the memcached library to decide to evaluate it as string or numerical value. If you need interoperability with existing applications that are not able to set this flag, you can force the module to evaluate all values as strings.

params.name: listen_addr
params.doc: IPv4 address to listen for HTTP connection. If not set, then it listens on all local addresses (port has to be specified by listen_port parameter).

params.name: listen_port
params.doc: Port to listen for HTTP connection.

params.name: event_callback
params.doc: The name of the function in the kemi configuration file (embedded scripting language such as Lua, Python, ...) to be executed instead of event_route[microhttpd:request] block.

functions.name: mhttpd_reply
functions.doc: Send back a reply with content-type and body.

params.name: radius_config
params.doc: This is the location of the configuration file of radius client libraries.

params.name: caller_service_type
params.doc: This is the value of the Service-Type radius attribute to be used, when caller's attributes are loaded.

params.name: callee_service_type
params.doc: This is the value of the Service-Type radius attribute to be used, when callee's attributes are loaded.

params.name: group_service_type
params.doc: This is the value of Service-Type RADIUS attribute to be used, when radius_is_user_in() function is called.

params.name: uri_service_type
params.doc: This is the value of Service-Type RADIUS attribute to be used, when radius_does_uri[_user]_exist() function is called.

params.name: caller_extra
params.doc: Semi-colon separated list of extra RADIUS attribute name=pseudo variable pairs. When radius_load_caller_avps() is called, the listed extra attributes are included RADIUS request with current values of corresponding pseudo variables.

params.name: callee_extra
params.doc: Semi-colon separated list of extra RADIUS attribute name=pseudo variable pairs. When radius_load_callee_avps() is called, the listed extra attributes are included RADIUS request with current values of corresponding pseudo variables.

params.name: group_extra
params.doc: Semi-colon separated list of extra RADIUS attribute name=pseudo variable pairs. When radius_is_user_in() is called, the listed extra attributes are included RADIUS request with current values of corresponding pseudo variables.

params.name: uri_extra
params.doc: Semi-colon separated list of extra RADIUS attribute name=pseudo variable pairs. When radius_does_uri[_user]_exist() function is called, the listed extra attributes are included in RADIUS request with current values of corresponding pseudo variables.

params.name: use_sip_uri_host
params.doc: If zero, radius_does_uri_exist() function sends to RADIUS server userpart@hostpart in UserName attribute. If non-zero, radius_does_uri_exist() function sends to RADIUS server userpart in UserName attribute and hostpart in SIP-URI-Host attribute.

params.name: common_response
params.doc: Set it to 1 if you need common radius response attributes to be added as AVPs in radius_load_caller_avps and radius_load_callee_avps with name as radius attribute name and value as radius attribute value.

functions.name: radius_load_caller_avps
functions.doc: The functions loads caller's attributes from radius and stores them into AVPs. Parameter “caller” is a string that may contain pseudo variables. It indicates the user, whose attributes are loaded.

functions.name: radius_load_callee_avps
functions.doc: The functions loads callee's attributes from radius and stores them into AVPs. Parameter “callee” is a string that may contain pseudo variables. It indicates the user, whose attributes are loaded.

functions.name: radius_is_user_in
functions.doc: The functions checks from RADIUS, if user given in first argument belongs to group given in second argument. Both arguments are strings, but user string may also contain pseudo variables. In case of positive result, loads AVPs from SIP-AVP reply items, if any.

functions.name: radius_does_uri_exist
functions.doc: Checks from RADIUS if userpart@hostpart of Request-URI or of an URI stored in optional pseudo variable argument belongs to a local user. In case of positive result, loads AVPs from SIP-AVP reply items, if any.

functions.name: radius_does_uri_user_exist
functions.doc: Similar to radius_does_uri_exist, but check is done based only on Request-URI userpart or userpart stored in optional pseudo variable argument. Userpart should thus be unique among all user URIs, such as an E.164 number. In case of positive result, loads AVPs from SIP-AVP reply items, if any.

params.name: memory
params.doc: Initialize for memory testing. Set it to 1 to prepare the memory testing.

params.name: mem_check_content
params.doc: When doing the tests, check also for the possibility of the memory being overwritten. When activated, the allocated memory will be filled with a special pattern, that will be checked on free.

params.name: message
params.doc: Initialize and perform message testing.

params.name: message_data
params.doc: Set SIP message data for testing.

params.name: message_file
params.doc: Set path to file from where to read SIP message data for testing.

params.name: lock_threads_mode
params.doc: Initialize (1) or not (0) the internal lock for pthreads testing.

functions.name: mt_mem_alloc
functions.doc: Allocates size bytes.

functions.name: mt_mem_free
functions.doc: Frees all the memory allocated with mem_alloc() up to this point.

functions.name: mt_tcp_thread_exec
functions.doc: Print the text via the tcp main process threads.

functions.name: mt_lock_test
functions.doc: Lock and unlock the global lock count times.

functions.name: mt_lock_threads
functions.doc: Creates a set of threads that try to use the internal lock (see also lock_threads_mode parameter).

functions.name: mt_unlock_threads
functions.doc: Unlock the internal global lock used by mt_lock_threads(). It is done nrops-times.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: The URL to connect to the database for the mohqueue tables.

params.name: db_qtable and db_ctable
params.doc: db_qtable is the name of the table that defines the queues and db_ctable is the table that maintains the call status.

params.name: mohdir
params.doc: Path to the directory where the audio files are stored. Audio files are usually relative to this directory although the value can be overridden by a directory specified in the queues table.

params.name: moh_maxcalls
params.doc: Defines the maximum number of calls that can be placed in queue. It is the sum of all calls in all queues. It must be in the range of 1 to 5000. NOTE: it may be limited by the processing power of the server or the number of available rtpproxy ports.

functions.name: mohq_process
functions.doc: Checks to see if the current SIP message involves a queue. If it does it will process the message and return a TRUE value.

functions.name: mohq_send
functions.doc: Normally calls enter the queue with an initial INVITE message that 1) has a RURI that matches a queue URI and 2) is passed through mohq_process (), which is the preferred method.

functions.name: mohq_retrieve
functions.doc: Retrieves the oldest call in a queue and redirects it to a URI. Although the function returns, the transfer of the call may not have completed since the new URI (operator) must answer the call.

functions.name: mohq_count
functions.doc: Finds the number of calls that are in a queue. It will not count calls that are in the process of entering or exiting the queue.

params.name: host
params.doc: MQTT Broker IP/Hostname.

params.name: port
params.doc: MQTT Broker port number.

params.name: keepalive
params.doc: The number of seconds after which the broker should send a PING message to the kamailio if no other messages have been exchanged in that time.

params.name: id
params.doc: String to use as the mqtt client id. If NULL, a random client id will be generated.

params.name: username
params.doc: The username to send as a string or NULL to disable authentication.

params.name: password
params.doc: The password to send as a string or NULL to disable authentication.

params.name: will_topic
params.doc: The topic on which to publish the mqtt will.

params.name: will
params.doc: The mqtt will payload to be published.

params.name: event_callback
params.doc: The name of the function in the kemi configuration file (embedded scripting language such as Lua, Python, ...) to be executed instead of event_route[...] blocks.

params.name: ca_file
params.doc: Path to a file containing the PEM encoded trusted CA certificate files.

params.name: ca_path
params.doc: Used to define a directory that contains PEM encoded CA certificates that are trusted. For ca_path to work correctly, the certificates files must have ".pem" as the file ending and you must run "openssl rehash /your/ca_path" each time you add/remove a certificate.

params.name: tls_method
params.doc: The version of the SSL/TLS protocol to use as a string. If NULL, the default value is used. The default value and the available values depend on the version of openssl that libmosquitto was compiled against.

params.name: tls_alpn
params.doc: Used to set the TLS ALPN option for cases where one TLS port is used to share multiple services. Prominent example is AWS IoT, where you have to set the tls_alpn to "mqtt" to be able to connect via MQTT.

params.name: certificate
params.doc: Path to a file containing the PEM encoded certificate file for a TLS client connection.

params.name: private_key
params.doc: Path to a file containing the PEM encoded private key for a TLS client connection.

params.name: cipher_list
params.doc: A string describing the ciphers available for use. See the cipher(1) OpenSSL man page. If NULL, the libssl default ciphers will be used.

params.name: verify_certificate
params.doc: Configure verification of the server certificate. If value is set to 0, it is impossible to guarantee that the host you are connecting to is not impersonating your server.

functions.name: mqtt_subscribe
functions.doc: Subscribe to the given topic. Mqtt qos levels 0, 1 and 2 can be used.

functions.name: mqtt_unsubscribe
functions.doc: Unsubscribe to a previously subscribed topic. The mqtt broker will stop forwarding messages for this topic.

functions.name: mqtt_publish
functions.doc: Send out a message to a topic with a specified mqtt qos level (0, 1, 2). Again the actual sending is done in a mqtt dispatcher process and will not block the SIP worker.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: The URL to connect to database for loading values in mqueue table at start up and/or saving values at shutdown.

params.name: mqueue
params.doc: Definition of a memory queue

params.name: mqueue_name
params.doc: Definition of a memory queue, just by name.

params.name: mqueue_size
params.doc: Definition of the size of all memory queues defined via "mqueue_name" parameter.

params.name: mqueue_addmode
params.doc: Sets the mode to be used when adding a new (key,value) pair in the mqueue. * 0 Add all new (key,value) at the end of mqueue * 1 Unique key, keep oldest (key,value) * 2 Unique key, keep newest(key,value)

functions.name: mq_add
functions.doc: Add a new item (key, value) in the queue. If max size of queue is exceeded, the oldest one is removed.

functions.name: mq_fetch
functions.doc: Take oldest item from queue and fill $mqk(queue) and $mqv(queue) pseudo variables.

functions.name: mq_pv_free
functions.doc: Free the item fetched in pseudo-variables. It is optional, a new fetch frees the previous values.

functions.name: mq_size
functions.doc: Returns the current number of elements in the mqueue.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: Database URL.

params.name: db_table
params.doc: The name of table where to store the messages.

params.name: sc_mid
params.doc: The name of the column in silo table used to store the message id.

params.name: sc_from
params.doc: The name of the column in silo table, storing the source address.

params.name: sc_to
params.doc: The name of the column in silo table, storing the destination address.

params.name: sc_uri_user
params.doc: The name of the column in silo table, storing the user name.

params.name: sc_uri_host
params.doc: The name of the column in silo table, storing the domain.

params.name: sc_body
params.doc: The name of the column storing the message body in silo table.

params.name: sc_ctype
params.doc: The name of the column in silo table, storing content type.

params.name: sc_exp_time
params.doc: The name of the column in silo table, storing the expire time of the message.

params.name: sc_inc_time
params.doc: The name of the column in silo table, storing the incoming time of the message.

params.name: sc_snd_time
params.doc: The name of the column in silo table, storing the send time for the reminder.

params.name: sc_stored_hdrs
params.doc: The name of the column in silo table, storing the extra headers.

params.name: sc_callid
params.doc: The name of the column in silo table, storing callid.

params.name: sc_callid
params.doc: The name of the column in silo table, storing status.

params.name: from_address
params.doc: The SIP address used to inform users that destination of their message is not online and the message will be delivered next time when that user goes online. If the parameter is not set, the module will not send any notification. This parameter may contain pseudo-variables.

params.name: contact_hdr
params.doc: The value of the “Contact” header (including header name and ending \r\n) to be added in notification messages. It can contain pseudo-variables.

params.name: extra_hdrs
params.doc: Extra headers (each ending with \r\n) to be added in messages sent from silo by m_dump. It can contain pseudo-variables.

params.name: offline_message
params.doc: The body of the notification message. It can contain pseudo-variables.

params.name: content_type_hdr
params.doc: The value of the Content-Type header (including header name and ending \r\n) to be added in notification messages. It must reflect what the 'offline_message' contains. It can contain pseudo-variables.

params.name: reminder
params.doc: The SIP address used to send reminder messages. If this value is not set, the reminder feature is disabled.

params.name: outbound_proxy
params.doc: The SIP address used as next hop when sending the message. Very useful when using Kamailio with a domain name not in DNS, or when using a separate Kamailio instance for msilo processing. If not set, the message will be sent to the address in destination URI.

params.name: expire_time
params.doc: Expire time of stored messages - seconds. When this time passed, the message is silently discarded from database.

params.name: check_time
params.doc: Timer interval to check if dumped messages are sent OK - seconds. The module keeps each request send by itself for a new online user and if the reply is 2xx then the message is deleted from database.

params.name: send_time
params.doc: Timer interval in seconds to check if there are reminder messages. The module takes all reminder messages that must be sent at that moment or before that moment.

params.name: clean_period
params.doc: Number of “check_time” cycles when to check if there are expired messages in database.

params.name: use_contact
params.doc: Turns on/off the usage of the “Contact” address to send notification back to sender whose message is stored by MSILO.

params.name: snd_time_avp
params.doc: The name of an AVP which may contain the time when to send the received message as reminder. The AVP is used only by m_store().

params.name: add_date
params.doc: Whether to add as prefix the date when the message was stored.

params.name: max_messages
params.doc: Maximum number of stored message for an AoR. Value 0 equals to no limit.

params.name: add_contact
params.doc: Whether to add contact header to generated messages. The contact address is the From URI.

params.name: extra_hdrs_avp
params.doc: Name of an AVP which may contain extra headers that are stored with the message when m_store() is called. These extra headers (if any) are then included in MESSAGE request generated by m_dump().

params.name: skip_notification_flag
params.doc: Flag to mark the message for which no notification should be sent back to sender when storing in msilo. Valid value is in between 0 and 31.

params.name: use_mode
params.doc: If set to 1, the call-id header of incoming MESSAGE is stored and reused later for delivery MESSAGE.

functions.name: m_store
functions.doc: The method stores certain parts of the current SIP request (it should be called when the request type is MESSAGE and the destination user is offline or his UA does not support MESSAGE requests). If the user is registered with a UA which does not support MESSAGE requests you should not use mode=“0” if you have changed the request uri with the contact address of user's UA.

functions.name: m_store_addrs
functions.doc: Similar to m_store(), but instead of getting source user address from From-URI and destination user address from To_URI, this function allows to give them via parameters.

functions.name: m_dump
functions.doc: The method sends stored messages for the SIP user that has registered to the contact address in the registration. The method should be called when a REGISTER request is received and the “Expire” header has a value greater than zero.

params.name: sipmsg
params.doc: If set to 1, the module will build a SIP message from MSRP frame headers, providing it to “event_route[msrp:frame-in]”. All the config file functions (apart from SIP request relay) that can be used in a request route block can be used in the MSRP event_route.

params.name: cmap_size
params.doc: The size of connection map table, to be computed as power of 2 (e.g., if the value is 4, then the number of slots in map table is 2^4 = 16).

params.name: timer_interval
params.doc: The timer interval in seconds to run the procedure for cleaning expired connections.

params.name: auth_min_expires
params.doc: The minimum value accepted for the “Expires” header in AUTH requests.

params.name: auth_max_expires
params.doc: The maximum value accepted for “Expires” header in AUTH requests.

params.name: use_path_addr
params.doc: The hostname:port to be used when building the Path header.

params.name: event_callback
params.doc: The name of the function in the kemi configuration file (embedded scripting language such as Lua, Python, ...) to be executed instead of event_route[...] blocks.

functions.name: msrp_forward
functions.doc: Forward MSRP frame to target destination. If tpath is provided then the original To-Path is replaced by it and the From-Path is replaced by fpath or the original To-Path. If the target destination is not set then tpath will be used to set it.

functions.name: msrp_relay
functions.doc: Relay MSRP frame according to the To-Path. This function has to be executed for each MSRP request or reply that has to be forwarded. Note that due to nature of the MSRP transport layer, which is reliable (TCP/TLS), there is no retransmission of MSRP frames.

functions.name: msrp_reply
functions.doc: Send a reply for the current MSRP request, adding optional headers.

functions.name: msrp_is_request
functions.doc: Return true if the MSRP frame is a request.

functions.name: msrp_is_reply
functions.doc: Return true if the MSRP frame is a reply.

functions.name: msrp_set_dst
functions.doc: Set destination attributes: addr - target address as MSRP URI; sock - local socket to be used (format 'proto:ip:port').

functions.name: msrp_relay_flags
functions.doc: Set transport layer sending flags for forwarding current MSRP frame; flags - a bitmask of flags - 1 (don't create a new connection), 2 (close connection after send).

functions.name: msrp_reply_flags
functions.doc: Set transport layer sending flags for replies to the current MSRP frame; flags - a bitmask of flags - 1 (don't create a new connection), 2 (close connection after send).

functions.name: msrp_cmap_save
functions.doc: Save details of a MSRP connection upon AUTH request inside the internal map table, indexed by session id.

functions.name: msrp_cmap_lookup
functions.doc: Lookup MSRP connection details for current session id.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: URL of the database server to be used.

params.name: db_table
params.doc: Name of database table where data for many trees is stored. It is ignored if a 'mtree' parameter is defined. The SQL scripts creates a table named 'mtrees' that can be used for this parameter.

params.name: mtree
params.doc: Definition of memory tree with using a parameters format string. The parameter names can be: * name - the name of the tree to be used for referencing inside configuration file. * mode - the mode of items management. If set to 0 (default), the items are (re)loaded from database. If set to 1, it is an in-memory only tree, the items can be added with modparam 'item'. * dbtable - the name of the database table from where to load the records stored in the tree. * cols - the column names of the database table. They must be enclosed in quotes in order to form a valid SIP parameter value and be separated by comma. The first column corresponds to tprefix. When specified, there must be at least two columns. If this attribute is not specified, then the global module parameters for tprefix and tvalue are used. If more than one value columns are specified, the tree will pack the column values in a comma separated string, which will be associated with the prefix (string transformation {s.select,...) can be used in configuration file to extract a specific column value). * type - the type of tree elements (0 = string, 1 = d:w, 2 = integer). None-zero is valid only when the (tprefix, tvalue) pairs are loaded (not for multi-column values). When the type is 1, the value in database has to be two integers separated by colon, the first one (d - dstid) will be stored in pv_dstid AVP and the second (w - weight) will be stored in pv_weight AVP. If in the matching records are many with the same dstid, it will keep only the one with the longest prefix. Then the records are ordered by the weight and stored in the specified AVPs. The number of stored records is saved in pv_count variable. * multi - tells if dbtable can contain more than one tree (0 = one tree, 1 = more than one tree identified by tname column). It is valid only when the (tprefix, tvalue) pairs are loaded (not for multi-column values).

params.name: tname_column
params.doc: Name of 'tname' column.

params.name: tprefix_column
params.doc: Name of 'tprefix' column.
