params.name: tvalue_column
params.doc: Name of 'tvalue' column.

params.name: fetch_rows
params.doc: Number of rows to be loaded in one step from database.

params.name: char_list
params.doc: The list with characters allowed in prefix.

params.name: item
params.doc: Add items to a mtree. The value has to contain the tree name, prefix and value, separated by the first character of the value. For example, if the wanted separator is ':', then the value format is ':tname:tprefix:tvalue'.

params.name: pv_value
params.doc: The PV spec where to store the matched value. It can be any writable PV.

params.name: pv_values
params.doc: The AVP where to store the matched values when mtree is of type 0 or 2 and mode of mt_match() call has value 2.

params.name: pv_dstid
params.doc: The AVP name where to store the first integer value when tree type is 1.

params.name: pv_weight
params.doc: The AVP name where to store the second integer value when tree type is 1.

params.name: pv_count
params.doc: The PV spec where to store the count of matched values when tree type is 1. It can be any writable PV.

params.name: mt_tree_type
params.doc: Default payload type for trees data stored in 'db_table'. Documented values are 0 for string payloads and 2 for integer payloads.

params.name: mt_ignore_duplicates
params.doc: Ignore duplicated prefixes when loading data.

params.name: mt_allow_duplicates
params.doc: Allow duplicate prefixes when loading data.

functions.name: mt_match
functions.doc: Match 'pv' value against 'mtree'. If 'mtree' type is 0 or 2 and value of 'mode' is NOT 2, sets associated value of the longest matching prefix to pseudo variable specified by pv_value parameter. If 'mtree' type is 0 or 2 and value of 'mode' is 2, sets values of all matching prefixes to avp specified by pv_values parameter so that a value of longest matching prefix is in avp index 0. Parameter 'mode' can be an integer constant or a pseudo variable with integer value.

params.name: keepalive_interval
params.doc: The time interval (in seconds) required to send a keepalive message to all the endpoints that need being kept alive. During this interval, each endpoint will receive exactly one keepalive message. A negative value or zero will disable the keepalive functionality.

params.name: keepalive_method
params.doc: What SIP method to use to send keepalive messages. Typical methods used for this purpose are NOTIFY and OPTIONS. NOTIFY generates smaller replies from user agents, but they are almost entirely negative replies. Apparently almost none of the user agents understand that the purpose of the NOTIFY with a “keep-alive” event is to keep NAT open, even though many user agents send such NOTIFY requests themselves. However this does not affect the result at all, since the purpose is to trigger a response from the user agent behind NAT, positive or negative replies having little relevance as they are discarded anyway. The OPTIONS method on the other hand has a much higher rate of positive replies, but at the same time those positive replies are much bigger, mostly because the OPTIONS method is used to inform about the user agent capabilities and thus it includes a lot of extra headers to indicate those capabilities. Many user agents also include a SDP body with a bogus media session, probably to indicate media capabilities. All of this makes that positive replies to OPTIONS requests are 2 to 3 times bigger than negative replies or replies to NOTIFY requests. For this reason the default value for the used method is NOTIFY.

params.name: keepalive_from
params.doc: Indicates what SIP URI to use in the From header of the keepalive requests. If not specified it will use sip:keepalive@proxy_ip, where proxy_ip is the IP address of the outgoing interface used to send the keepalive message, which is the same interface on which the request that triggered keepalive functionality arrived.

params.name: keepalive_extra_headers
params.doc: Specifies extra headers that should be added to the keepalive messages that are sent by the proxy. The header specification must also include the CRLF (\r\n) line separator. Multiple headers can be specified by concatenating them and each of them must include the \r\n separator.

params.name: keepalive_state_file
params.doc: Specifies a filename where information about the NAT endpoints and the conditions for which they are being kept alive is saved when Kamailio exits. The information in this file is then used when Kamailio starts to restore its internal state and continue to send keepalive messages to the NAT endpoints that have not expired in the meantime. This is useful when restarting Kamailio to avoid losing keepalive state information about the NAT endpoints. The internal keepalive state is guaranteed to be saved in this file on exit, even when Kamailio crashes.

params.name: contact_match
params.doc: Control how to match the contact URIs between requests and replies.

functions.name: client_nat_test
functions.doc: Check if the client is behind NAT. What tests are performed is specified by the type parameter which is an integer given by the sum of the numbers corresponding to the tests that one wishes to perform. The numbers corresponding to individual tests are shown below:

functions.name: fix_contact
functions.doc: Will replace the IP and port in the Contact header with the IP and port the SIP message was received from. Usually called after a successful call to client_nat_test(type)

functions.name: nat_keepalive
functions.doc: Trigger keepalive functionality for the source address of the request. When called it only sets some internal flags, which will trigger later the addition of the endpoint to the keepalive list if a positive reply is generated/received (for REGISTER and SUBSCRIBE) or when the dialog is started/replied (for INVITEs). For this reason, it can be called early or late in the script. The only condition is to call it before replying to the request or before sending it to another proxy. If the request needs to be sent to another proxy, t_relay() must be used to be able to intercept replies via TM or dialog callbacks. If stateless forwarding is used, the keepalive functionality will not work. Also for outgoing INVITEs, record_route() should also be used to make sure the proxy that keeps the caller endpoint alive stays in the path. For multi-proxy setups, this function should always be called on the border proxies (the ones that received the request directly from the user agent). For more details about this function, see the Implementation subsection from the Keepalive functionality section.

params.name: force_socket
params.doc: Socket to be used when sending NAT pings for UDP communication. If no one specified, the OS will choose a socket.

params.name: natping_interval
params.doc: Period of time in seconds between sending the NAT pings to all currently registered UAs to keep their NAT bindings alive. Value of 0 disables this functionality.

params.name: ping_nated_only
params.doc: If this parameter is set to 1 then only contacts that have the behind NAT “nat_bflag” flag set in user location records get the NAT ping (the “nat_bflag” is specified via modparam of usrloc module). By default the ping is done with 4-bytes UDP packet. If sipping_bflag is also set, then the ping is done with a stateless SIP request (by default: OPTIONS request).

params.name: natping_processes
params.doc: How many timer processes should be created by the module for the exclusive task of sending the NAT pings.

params.name: natping_socket
params.doc: Spoof the natping's source-ip to this address. Works only for IPv4.

params.name: received_avp
params.doc: The name of the Attribute-Value-Pair (AVP) used to store the URI containing the received IP, port, and protocol. The URI is created by fix_nated_register function of nathelper module and the attribute is then used by the registrar to store the received parameters. Do not forget to change the value of corresponding parameter in registrar module if you change the value of this parameter.

params.name: sipping_bflag
params.doc: Which branch flag should be used by the module to identify NATed contacts for which it should perform NAT ping via a SIP request instead of dummy UDP packet.

params.name: sipping_from
params.doc: The parameter sets the SIP URI to be used in generating the SIP requests for NAT ping purposes. To enable the SIP request pinging feature, you have to set this parameter. The SIP request pinging will be used only for requests marked so.

params.name: sipping_method
params.doc: The parameter sets the SIP method to be used in generating the SIP requests for NAT ping purposes.

params.name: natping_disable_bflag
params.doc: What branch flag should be used by the module to disable NAT pings on a per-registration basis. If the given flag is set for a particular registration, then no NAT pings will be sent at all, regardless of any other conditions.

params.name: nortpproxy_str
params.doc: The parameter sets the SDP attribute used by nathelper to mark the packet SDP that information have already been mangled.

params.name: keepalive_timeout
params.doc: The parameter sets the interval in seconds after which a natted contact is removed from location table if it does not reply to SIP keepalives (usually OPTIONS ping requests).

params.name: udpping_from_path
params.doc: Enable sending UDP pings (keepalives) using raw socket from Path address.

params.name: ignore_path
params.doc: Enable ignore of Path header address when sending UDP pings (keepalives).

params.name: append_sdp_oldmediaip
params.doc: The parameter controls if oldmediaip field should be appended to the SDP.

params.name: filter_server_id
params.doc: Filter contacts by “server_id” core parameter. Use this parameter to limit pinging. When set to “1”, only proxy instances which send packets are those where core server_id matches server_id saved in usrloc. Default value is “0” (disabled).

params.name: nat_addr_mode
params.doc: If set to 0, only default private net addresses are checked by nat_uac_test(). If set to 1, other reserved net addresses are checked by nat_uac_test() as well.

params.name: alias_name
params.doc: The parameter sets the name of the Contact URI parameter set by set_contact_alias() or add_contact_alias() and processed by handle_ruri_alias() in R-URI.

functions.name: fix_nated_contact
functions.doc: Rewrites the “Contact” header to contain the request's source address:port.

functions.name: fix_nated_sdp
functions.doc: Alters the SDP information in order to facilitate NAT traversal. What changes to be performed may be controlled via the “flags” parameter. Return value is -1 if error occurred, 1 if ip's were replaced, 2 if no ip's were replaced.

functions.name: add_rcv_param
functions.doc: Add a received parameter to the “Contact” header fields (available for all transports) or to the Contact URI (available only for UDP traffic).

functions.name: fix_nated_register
functions.doc: The function creates a URI consisting of the source IP, port, and protocol and stores the URI in an Attribute-Value-Pair. The URI will be appended as "received" parameter to Contact in 200 OK and registrar will store it in the received column in the location table.

functions.name: nat_uac_test
functions.doc: Tries to guess if client's request originated behind a nat. The parameter determines what heuristics is used.

functions.name: is_rfc1918
functions.doc: Determines if the address in the parameter is an rfc1918 or rfc6598 address. The parameter allows pseudo-variables usage.

functions.name: add_contact_alias
functions.doc: Adds an “;alias=ip~port~transport” parameter to the contact URI containing either received ip, port, and transport protocol or those given as parameters. If called without parameters, “;alias” parameter is only added if received ip, port, or transport protocol differs from that in contact URI.

functions.name: handle_ruri_alias
functions.doc: Checks if the Request URI has an “alias” parameter and if so, removes it and sets the “$du” based on its value. Note that this means that routing of request is based on “;alias” parameter value of the Request URI rather than the Request URI itself. If you call handle_ruri_alias() on a request, make sure that you screen the alias parameter value of Request URI the same way as you would screen the Request URI itself.

functions.name: set_contact_alias
functions.doc: Adds an “;alias=ip~port~transport” parameter to the contact URI containing the received ip, port, and transport protocol. The update of contact URI is signaled to a few other modules in the way the fix_nated_contact() does it by using the internal flags. The new value is not visible to pseudo-variables and it does not change the SIP message buffer.

functions.name: set_alias_to_pv
functions.doc: Reads “;alias=ip~port~transport” from Contact header then writes to target pseudo-variable as a sip uri.

params.name: nats_url
params.doc: The nats url.

params.name: num_publish_workers
params.doc: The number of worker threads for publishing messages.

params.name: subject_queue_group
params.doc: The NATS Subject and Queue Group. Separated by ":"

params.name: event_callback
params.doc: Name of the KEMI function to be executed instead of the event route.

functions.name: nats_publish
functions.doc: Publishes the payload to subject, with an optional reply subject.

params.name: host
params.doc: Host of Cassandra node.

functions.name: cass_insert
functions.doc: Inserts the value for the given key, column, column_family and keyspace. There must be an existing keyspace called 'keyspace' with a column_family called 'column_family' in the targeted Cassandra node.

functions.name: cass_retrieve
functions.doc: Retrieves the value for the given key, column, column_family and keyspace. There must be an existing keyspace called 'keyspace' with a column_family called 'column_family' in the targeted Cassandra node.

params.name: server
params.doc: Specify the details to connect to MongoDB server. It takes a list of attribute=value separated by semicolon, the attributes can be name and uri. Name is a generic identifier to be used with module functions. The uri parameter must be a valid MongoDB database connection string.

functions.name: mongodb_cmd
functions.doc: Send a valid command to MongoDB server identified by srvname. The reply will be stored in a local container identified by replyid. All the parameters can be strings with pseudo-variables that are evaluated at runtime.

functions.name: mongodb_cmd_simple
functions.doc: Send a valid command to MongoDB server identified by srvname. The reply will be stored in a local container identified by replyid. All the parameters can be strings with pseudo-variables that are evaluated at runtime.

functions.name: mongodb_find
functions.doc: Send a find command to MongoDB server identified by srvname. The reply will be stored in a local container identified by replyid. All the parameters can be strings with pseudo-variables that are evaluated at runtime.

functions.name: mongodb_find_one
functions.doc: Similar to mongodb_find(...), but it stops searching after first match, returning the result with one object - faster when expecting to have a single match. Parameters and behaviour are the same as for mongodb_find(...).

functions.name: mongodb_next
functions.doc: Moves to next document in a MongoDB reply. This function can be used after a successful mongodb_cmd() or mongodb_find(). It returns true if there is a shift to document. The current document becomes available via $mongodb(key) variable.

functions.name: mongodb_free
functions.doc: Frees data in a previous reply from memory. After this function call, accessing to a freed replyid returns null value.

params.name: server
params.doc: Specify the details to connect to REDIS server. It takes a list of attribute=value separated by semicolon, the attributes can be: * name - is a generic identifier to be used with module functions. * unix - is the path to the unix domain socket to connect to REDIS server. * addr - is the IP address to connect to REDIS server. * port - is the port to connect to REDIS server. * db - is the DB number to use (defaults to 0 if not specified). * pass - is the server password. * tls - is to enable TLS connectivity. * connect_timeout - is to set connect timeout to REDIS server. * command_timeout - is to set command timeout to REDIS server.

params.name: init_without_redis
params.doc: If set to 1, the module will correctly initialize even if redis is not available at start up.

params.name: connect_timeout
params.doc: The timeout when connecting to the redis server

params.name: cmd_timeout
params.doc: The timeout for each query to the redis server. If the redis server does not reply within the timeout value, the command will fail and kamailio will continue executing the cfg file.

params.name: cluster
params.doc: If set to 1, the module will connect to servers indicated in the "MOVED" reply.

params.name: allowed_timeouts
params.doc: If this is set to a non-negative value, it sets the number of consecutive REDIS commands that can fail before temporarily disabling the REDIS server. This is similar to rtpengine_disable_tout parameter from the rtpengine module.

params.name: disable_time
params.doc: If allowed_timeouts is set to a non negative value this determines the number of seconds the REDIS server will be disabled

params.name: flush_on_reconnect
params.doc: If this is set to a non zero value, a "FLUSHALL" command is issued after reconnecting to a REDIS server, to clear the entire database.

params.name: allow_dynamic_nodes
params.doc: If set to 1, the module will connect to servers indicated in the "MOVED" reply, even if they are not specified at startup.

params.name: debug
params.doc: Set the verbosity level for some of the log messages. It has to be a log level value.

params.name: ca_path
params.doc: Sets the path where Certificates Authorities certs for the REDIS server certificate are stored.

functions.name: redis_cmd
functions.doc: Send a command to REDIS server identified by srvname. The reply will be stored in a local container identified by replyid. All the parameters can be strings with pseudo-variables that are evaluated at runtime.

functions.name: redis_pipe_cmd
functions.doc: Add a command to be sent to REDIS server identified by srvname. All the commands will be stored in a buffer until a call to redis_execute is made. When calling redis_execute the stored commands are sent using the pipelining functionality of redis. The replies will be stored in local containers identified by the replyid of each added command. All the parameters can be strings with pseudo-variables that are evaluated at runtime.

functions.name: redis_execute
functions.doc: Sends commands to REDIS server identified by srvname. Commands are added with redis_pipe_cmd function, and will be stored for an existing REDIS server. When this function is called all the commands will be sent in a single message to the REDIS server.

functions.name: redis_free
functions.doc: Frees data in a previous reply from memory. After this function call, accessing to a freed replyid returns null value.

params.name: listen_addr
params.doc: IPv4 address to listen for HTTP2 connection. If not set, then it listens on all local addresses (port has to be specified by listen_port parameter).

params.name: listen_port
params.doc: Port or service name to listen for HTTP2 connection.

params.name: event_callback
params.doc: The name of the function in the kemi configuration file (embedded scripting language such as Lua, Python, ...) to be executed instead of event_route[nghttp2:request] block.

functions.name: nghttp2_reply
functions.doc: Send back a reply with body. The body can be empty string. Both parameters can contain variables.

functions.name: nghttp2_reply_header
functions.doc: Set a header to be added to reply. There can be up to 15 headers.

params.name: msg_match
params.doc: Regular expression to match against content of the packet in order to execute the event_route[nosip:msg].

params.name: msg_skip
params.doc: Regular expression to match against content of the packet in order to skip execution the event_route[nosip:msg].

params.name: lookupd_address
params.doc: The nsqlookupd address.

params.name: lookupd_port
params.doc: The nsqlookupd TCP port.

params.name: nsqd_address
params.doc: The nsqd address. You can specify connecting directly to nsqd instead of using nsqlookupd.

params.name: nsqd_port
params.doc: The nsqd TCP port.

params.name: consumer_use_nsqd
params.doc: Set to 1 if you'd like to connect to nsqd instead of nsqlookupd.

params.name: consumer_event_key
params.doc: The default name of the field in json payload to compose the event name 1st part

params.name: consumer_event_subkey
params.doc: The default name of the field in json payload to compose the event name 2nd part

params.name: max_in_flight
params.doc: The number of messages the consumer can receive before nsqd expects a response.

params.name: consumer_workers
params.doc: Number of consumer connections to NSQ per topic_channel.

params.name: topic_channel
params.doc: The NSQ Topic and Channel. Delimiter-separated by “:”. It be set multiple times to subscribe to multiple topics and channels. The value of consumer_workers is allocated per topic_channel.

params.name: force_outbound_flag
params.doc: A flag which, if set for a request, will force path and rr to add flow tokens to Path: and Record-Route: headers regardless of the request contents.

params.name: force_no_outbound_flag
params.doc: A flag which, if set for a request, will force path and rr not to add flow tokens to Path: and Record-Route: headers regardless of the request contents.

params.name: flow_token_secret
params.doc: Secret phrase used to calculate the outbound key value used for flow tokens validation. Allows to set persistent outbound key.

functions.name: check_flow_token
functions.doc: This function search flow token for the current message and make checks: 1. headers can be parsed; 2. Route header can be parsed; 3. top route header is myself; 4. flow token present in the Route header; 5. flow token can be decoded; 6. TCP/TLS or WS/WSS connection present; 7. flow token is not expired;

params.name: write_db_url
params.doc: The url to the master database where errors are written to.

params.name: read_db_url
params.doc: The url to the master database where the distribution data is read from. It is separated from write access, so for better performance, a local replicate can be used for read access.

params.name: reg_db_table
params.doc: Specifies the table where the information about the distributed databases is stored.

params.name: id_column
params.doc: Specifies the column where the id of a distributed database is stored.

params.name: num_column
params.doc: Specifies the column where the associated number of the distributed database is stored. For each distributed database ID there must be at least two databases available, the databases above the second are ignored.

params.name: url_column
params.doc: Specifies the column where the url of the distributed database is stored.

params.name: status_column
params.doc: Specifies the column where the status of the distributed database is stored.

params.name: failover_time_column
params.doc: Specifies the column where the failover time of the location databases is stored. This field is set to the current time when a databases is turned off or turned on.

params.name: spare_flag_column
params.doc: Specifies the column where the spare flag of the location databases is stored. It is possible to declare an entry in the p_usrloc table as spare which is used in a failover. Due to the fact that the data is stored in two databases and it takes the spare the complete expire time to be up to date, it is not very useful.

params.name: error_column
params.doc: Specifies the column where the errors of the distributed databases are stored. Each call to db_handle_error increases the error counter. After exceeding the error threshold, the database's status is set to off.

params.name: risk_group_column
params.doc: Specifies the column where the risk group of the distributed databases is stored. All databases on one host are in the same risk group. This is only useful when using spares and prevents the module from taking a spare which shares the same risk as the broken database.

params.name: expire_time
params.doc: Specifies the time (in seconds) when a contact expires, used for resetting the failover time of a reactivated database. It should be equal or greater than the contact expiration time of the registrar module.

params.name: db_err_threshold
params.doc: Specifies the error value on which a database shall be turned of.

params.name: failover_level
params.doc: Specifies the manner a failover is done. Following modes are supported: * 1 - Just turn off the broken database * 2 - Try to find a spare, if none found, just turn off the broken database

params.name: db_retry_interval
params.doc: Specifies the interval (in seconds) in which a timer process shall check the availability of the databases and try to reconnect to broken ones. It doesn't make sense to choose a lower value as 10. It's necessary to provide a writeable master database, otherwise this check stays disabled.

params.name: db_use_transactions
params.doc: Specifies if transactions should be used (set to 1) to reach a higher data consistency. Keep in mind that this will probably decrease performance.

params.name: db_transaction_level
params.doc: Specifies the isolation level on which transactions are performed. Possible values: Modes supported by the database backend. In order to activate transaction the db_use_transactions parameter must be also set.

params.name: write_on_master_db
params.doc: Sets the write access to the master database. If set to 0, no write operations are permitted on the master database.

params.name: mdb_availability_control
params.doc: Checks the master database in certain time intervals specified by the “retry_interval” parameter. Overwrites the “write_on_master_db” parameter based on the reachability of master database. If the master db is unavailable then the aforementioned parameter will be deactivated.

params.name: write_on_db
params.doc: Sets the write access to the distributed databases. If set to 0, no write operations are permitted on the databases.

params.name: connection_expires
params.doc: Specifies the period (in seconds) after a database connection expires. Usage of a too small value will probably decrease the performance.

params.name: alg_location
params.doc: Specify the way the distribution of the subscriptions are computed. At the moment the only way is to use the CRC32 algorithm to compute the location ID. Any integer value is fine.

params.name: domain_db
params.doc: Specify the way the lookup is made. In can be either partitioned or single. For example, if you have a location table that is large and needs to be partitioned, and a smaller table cfa that is ok to be on only the master db(so there is no need to have it distributed), you can set this parameter to “location=cluster,cfa=single”. This means that a call to

params.name: default_db_type
params.doc: In case a domain (like location,cfa) is not matched by a domain_db definition, the type is configured by using this parameter. Accepted values are single and cluster.

params.name: db_ops_ruid
params.doc: Defines how database queries are done: * 0 uses the old style using aor, contact and call-id * 1 uses ruid value * 2 uses the new style using aor, contact and call-id * 3 uses contact uniq value + ruid value

params.name: db_update_as_insert
params.doc: Set this parameter if you want to do INSERT DB operations instead of UPDATE DB operations. It is recommended to set this parameter if you use Cassandra as a DB backend.

params.name: default_db_url
params.doc: The URL of the default database for Location domains (for domains that are single). This must be configured if they are use.

params.name: matching_mode
params.doc: Defines the matching algorithm. Possible values are: * 0 (CONTACT_ONLY) * 1 (CONTACT_CALLID) * 2 (CONTACT_PATH)

params.name: UTC_timestamps
params.doc: Enables UTC timestamps for expires and last_modified columns. It can be changed at runtime via rpc command.

params.name: use_domain_crc32
params.doc: Enables or disables the crc32 of domain part for user@domain. If disabled, will calculate crc32 only for user part.

params.name: use_received
params.doc: If set to 1, the “received” parameter of the first Route URI is evaluated and used as destination-URI if present.

params.name: received_format
params.doc: If set to 0, the “received” parameter value will be in the escaped SIP URI format.

params.name: received_name
params.doc: Set the name of the header parameter to add the “received” value.

params.name: enable_r2
params.doc: If set to 1, the module will add two Path headers, similar to the double Record-Route done by rr module. One Path headers corresponds to incoming network socket and the other to outgoing network socket. The URIs in the Path headers will have the 'r2=on' parameter as well.

params.name: sockname_mode
params.doc: If set to 1, the Path URI is built to contain socket name in 'sn' parameter.

functions.name: add_path
functions.doc: This function is used to insert a Path header in the form “Path: ”, where “1.2.3.4” is the address of the outgoing interface.

functions.name: add_path
functions.doc: This function adds a Path header in the form “Path: ”.

functions.name: add_path
functions.doc: This function adds a Path header in the form “Path: ” and appends the given parameters as additional URI parameters.

functions.name: add_path_received
functions.doc: This function adds a Path header in the form “Path: ”, setting its own outgoing address as domain-part, and the address the request has been received from as received-parameter.

functions.name: add_path_received
functions.doc: This function adds a Path header in the form “Path: ”, setting 'user' as username part of address, its own outgoing address as domain-part, and the address the request has been received from as received-parameter.

functions.name: add_path_received
functions.doc: This function adds a Path header in the form “Path: ”, setting 'user' as username part of address, its own outgoing address as domain-part, and the address the request has been received from as received-parameter.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: This is the timeout in milliseconds for the pdb_query function.

params.name: server
params.doc: This is the list of servers to be used by the pdb_query function. Queries will be sent in parallel to all servers configured in this list. This parameter is mandatory.

params.name: ll_info
params.doc: Local log level (per module) for specific INFO messages. It has to be a valid log level value (see xlog() function from xlog module for more details).

functions.name: pdb_query
functions.doc: Sends the query string to all configured servers and stores the answer in dstvp. If it takes more than the configured timeout, false is returned. In addition to a string, any pseudo-variable can be used as query. The answer must consist of the null terminated query string followed by a two byte integer value in network byte order. The integer value will be stored in the given pseudo-variable dstvp.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: URL of the database table to be used.

params.name: db_table
params.doc: Table name.

params.name: sdomain_column
params.doc: Name of 'sdomain' column.

params.name: prefix_column
params.doc: Name of 'prefix' column.

params.name: domain_column
params.doc: Name of 'domain' column.

params.name: prefix
params.doc: Default leading prefix who denotes what URI needs to be translated - if it is NULL the module will not check the R-URI against it and the PDT prefix is considered starting from the first digit. Otherwise, the module will check first if the R-URI starts with it and will skip it to look up the domain.

params.name: fetch_rows
params.doc: Number of rows to be loaded in one step from database.

params.name: char_list
params.doc: The list with characters allowed in prefix.

params.name: check_domain
params.doc: Module will check if destination domain is duplicated for same source domain (1 - check; 0 - don't check).

params.name: mode
params.doc: If set to 1, duplicated prefixes are ingnored and starting continues, if 0, then starting or loading fails.

functions.name: prefix2domain
functions.doc: Build a new URI if it is necessary. Returns 1 when the translation was made or there was nothing to translate (user part of the URI is empty, it does not match the prefix parameter or there is no domain associated with a possible prefix from user part). Returns -1 in error cases.

functions.name: prefix2domain
functions.doc: The same as prefix2domain(rewrite_mode, "0"), that is without multidomain support, translation of URI being done regardless of the source domain.

functions.name: prefix2domain
functions.doc: The same as prefix2domain("0", "0").

functions.name: pd_translate
functions.doc: Translate R-URI based on source domain and longest prefix matching. Returns 1 when the translation was made or there was nothing to translate. Returns -1 in error cases.

params.name: radius_config
params.doc: This is the location of the configuration file of Radius client libraries.

params.name: verify_destination_service_type
params.doc: This is the value of the Service-Type Radius attribute to be used, when sender of SIP Request verifies the request's destination using verify_destination() function.

params.name: verify_source_service_type
params.doc: This is the value of the Service-Type Radius attribute to be used, when receiver of SIP Request verifies the request's source using verify_source() function.

functions.name: verify_destination
functions.doc: Function verify_destination() queries from broker's Radius server if domain (host part) of Request URI is served by a trusted peer. Radius request contains the following attributes/values: * User-Name - Request-URI host * SIP-URI-User - Request-URI user * SIP-From-Tag - From tag * SIP-Call-Id - Call id * Service-Type - verify_destination_service_type

functions.name: verify_source
functions.doc: Function verify_source() queries the broker's Radius server whether the SIP request was received from a trusted peer. The Radius request contains the following attributes/values: * User-Name - Request-URI host * SIP-URI-User - Request-URI user * SIP-From-Tag - From tag * SIP-Call-Id - Call id * SIP-Request-Hash - body of P-Request-Hash header * Service-Type - verify_source_service_type

params.name: cache_hash_size
params.doc: The size of the hash table internally used to keep the peer state information. A larger table is much faster but consumes more memory. The hash size must be a power of two.

params.name: cache_expire
params.doc: The time in seconds after which inactive peer entries are removed from the cache. Set to 0 to disable automatic expiration. This helps conserve memory by removing stale peer information. Minimum allowed value is 60 seconds (when enabled).

params.name: cache_cleanup_interval
params.doc: The interval in seconds between automatic cache cleanup runs. Must be less than or equal to cache_expire. Set to 0 to disable automatic cleanup. During cleanup, expired entries are removed from the cache. Minimum allowed value is 10 seconds (when enabled).

params.name: use_avps
params.doc: Enable or disable the use of AVPs for peer identification instead of extracting peer information from SIP headers. When enabled, the module will use the AVPs specified by caller_avp, callee_avp, and reg_avp parameters to identify peers.

params.name: caller_avp
params.doc: The specification of an AVP that contains the caller's peer identifier. Only used when use_avps is set to 1. The AVP should contain the peer identifier in the format "peer@domain".

params.name: callee_avp
params.doc: The specification of an AVP that contains the callee's peer identifier. Only used when use_avps is set to 1. The AVP should contain the peer identifier in the format "peer@domain".

params.name: reg_avp
params.doc: The specification of an AVP that contains the registered peer identifier for usrloc events. Only used when use_avps is set to 1.

params.name: enable_notify_on_trying
params.doc: Enable state change notifications for dialog TRYING state. By default, only EARLY, CONFIRMED, and TERMINATED states trigger notifications. When enabled, TRYING state will also trigger notifications.

params.name: disable_caller_notify_flag
params.doc: Message flag to disable caller state change notifications for specific calls. When this flag is set on a message, state changes for the caller will not trigger notifications. Set to -1 to disable this feature.

params.name: disable_callee_notify_flag
params.doc: Message flag to disable callee state change notifications for specific calls. When this flag is set on a message, state changes for the callee will not trigger notifications. Set to -1 to disable this feature.

params.name: disable_reg_notify
params.doc: Globally disable registration event processing. When set to 1, the module will not register callbacks with the usrloc module and will not process registration events.

params.name: disable_dlg_notify
params.doc: Globally disable dialog event processing. When set to 1, the module will not register callbacks with the dialog module and will not process dialog events.

params.name: default_allow_file
params.doc: Default allow file used by the functions with no parameters. If you don't specify a full pathname then the directory in which the main config file is located will be used.

params.name: default_deny_file
params.doc: Default file containing deny rules. The file is used by functions with no parameters. If you don't specify a full pathname then the directory in which the main config file is located will be used.

params.name: check_all_branches
params.doc: If set then allow_routing functions will check Request-URI of all branches (default). If disabled then only Request-URI of the first branch will be checked.

params.name: allow_suffix
params.doc: Suffix to be appended to basename to create filename of the allow file when version with one parameter of either allow_routing or allow_register_include_port or allow_register is used.

params.name: deny_suffix
params.doc: Suffix to be appended to basename to create filename of the deny file when version with one parameter of either allow_routing or allow_register_include_port or allow_register is used.

params.name: address_file
params.doc: This is the name of full path to the file that store rules used by allow_address function (and its variants). If it is only the file name, it is expected to be in the same folder as kamailio.cfg file.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: This is URL of the database to be used to store rules used by allow_trusted or allow_address functions.

params.name: address_table
params.doc: The name of the database table containing IP subnets and DNS domain names used by allow_address and allow_source_address functions.

params.name: grp_col
params.doc: Name of address table column containing the group identifier of the address.

params.name: ip_addr_col
params.doc: Name of address table column containing the IP address part of the address.

params.name: mask_col
params.doc: Name of address table column containing the network mask of the address. Possible values are 0-32 for IPv4 and 0-128 for IPv6 addresses. If the value is 0, the network mask is set to 32 for IPv4 addresses and to 128 for IPv6 addresses.

params.name: port_col
params.doc: Name of address table column containing the port part of the address.

params.name: db_mode
params.doc: Database mode. 0 means non-caching, 1 means caching. Valid only for the allow_trusted function.

params.name: trusted_table
params.doc: Name of database table containing the matching rules used by the allow_trusted function.

params.name: source_col
params.doc: Name of column in the “trusted” table containing the source IP address that is matched against source IP address of received request.

params.name: proto_col
params.doc: Name of column in the “trusted” table containing the transport protocol that is matched against transport protocol of the received request. Possible values that can be stored in proto_col are “any”, “udp”, “tcp”, “tls”, “sctp”, “ws”, “wss”, and “none”. Value “any” matches always and value “none” never.

params.name: from_col
params.doc: Name of the column trusted table containing a regular expression that is matched against the From URI.

params.name: ruri_col
params.doc: Name of the column trusted table containing a regular expression that is matched against the Request URI.

params.name: tag_col
params.doc: Name of the column in the “address” or “trusted” table containing a string that is added as value to peer_tag AVP if peer_tag AVP has been defined and if the address or peer matches.

params.name: priority_col
params.doc: The column name used to store the priority of the corresponding rule from the database row. Priority values should be integer. When db_mode is set to 1 (caching), priorities are ordered from highest to lowest. In non-caching mode, priority order (ASC vs DESC) is determined by database.

params.name: peer_tag_avp
params.doc: If defined, the AVP will be set as a side effect of allow_trusted call to not NULL tag column value of the matching peer.

params.name: peer_tag_mode
params.doc: Tag mode for allow_trusted. “0” sets only the tag of the first match. “1” adds the tags of all matches to the avp. In addition the return value of allow_trusted is the number of matches. This parameter is not used for address table matching functions.

params.name: max_subnets
params.doc: The maximum number of subnet addresses to be loaded from address table.

params.name: subnet_match_mode
params.doc: Control how subnet addresses are matched: 0 - return on the first prefix match; 1 - return on the longest prefix match. It impacts functions like allow_source_address(), allow_address(), allow_source_address_group() or allow_address_group().

params.name: load_backends
params.doc: Control what backends should be loaded: 1 - address table; 2 - trusted table; 4 - allow file; 8 - deny file.

params.name: reload_delta
params.doc: The number of seconds that have to be waited before executing a new RPC reload. By default there is a rate limiting of maximum one reload in five seconds.

params.name: trusted_cleanup_interval
params.doc: If module parameter db_mode is set to 1 a cleanup timer is set to the trusted_cleanup_interval value in seconds. This process will cleanup the previous values from memory after a RPC reload.

functions.name: allow_routing
functions.doc: Returns true if all pairs constructed as described in Section 1.1, “Call Routing” have appropriate permissions according to the configuration files. This function uses default configuration files specified in default_allow_file and default_deny_file.

functions.name: allow_routing
functions.doc: Returns true if all pairs constructed as described in Section 1.1, “Call Routing” have appropriate permissions according to the configuration files given as parameters.

functions.name: allow_routing
functions.doc: Returns true if all pairs constructed as described in Section 1.1, “Call Routing” have appropriate permissions according to the configuration files given as parameters.

functions.name: allow_register
functions.doc: The function returns true if all pairs constructed as described in Section 1.2, “Registration Permissions” have appropriate permissions according to the configuration files given as parameters.

functions.name: allow_register
functions.doc: The function returns true if all pairs constructed as described in Section 1.2, “Registration Permissions” have appropriate permissions according to the configuration files given as parameters.

functions.name: allow_register_include_port
functions.doc: The function does exacty the same thing as allow_register(basename) apart that it tells the module to include the port value of Contact into the check. No additional function parameters required.

functions.name: allow_register_include_port
functions.doc: The function does exacty the same thing as allow_register(allow_file, deny_file) apart that it tells the module to include the port value of Contact into the check. No additional function parameters required.

functions.name: allow_uri
functions.doc: Returns true if the pair constructed as described in Section 1.3, “URI Permissions” have appropriate permissions according to the configuration files specified by the parameter.

functions.name: allow_address
functions.doc: Returns true if the address and port given as values of pvar arguments belonging to a group given as group_id argument matches an IP subnet or a DNS domain name found in cached address table.

functions.name: allow_source_address
functions.doc: Equal to “allow_address(group_id, "$si", "$sp")”. If 'group_id' is missing, the function is equal to allow_address("1", "$si", "$sp").

functions.name: allow_source_address_group
functions.doc: Checks if source address/port is found in cached address or subnet table in any group. If yes, returns that group. If not returns -1. Port value 0 in cached address and group table matches any port.

functions.name: allow_address_group
functions.doc: Checks if address/port is found in cached address or subnet table in any group. If yes, returns that group. If not returns -1. Port value 0 in cached address and group table matches any port. The parameters can be pseudo-variables.

functions.name: allow_trusted
functions.doc: Checks based either on request's source address and transport protocol or source address and transport protocol given in pvar arguments, and From URI of request (or furi_pvar if provided) if request can be trusted without authentication. Returns “1” if a match is found as described in Section 1.5, “Trusted Requests” and “-1” otherwise. If a match is found and peer_tag_avp has been defined, adds a non-NULL tag column value of the matching peer to AVP peer_tag_avp.

params.name: smode
params.doc: Phone number search mode (not in use yet).

params.name: resid
params.doc: Preregister result container id during initialization, enabling the use of the module in KEMI scripts. In native kamailio.cfg file, registration is done when parsing config and finding variables.

functions.name: phonenum_match
functions.doc: Match num against the libphonenumber and set the attributes inside the pvc result container. The function has to be called before accessing a key via: $phn(pvc=>key).

functions.name: phonenum_match_cn
functions.doc: Match num against the libphonenumber and set the attributes inside the pvc container, restricting the rules with a country name code (two letter, e.g: "DE", "US", "ES"). The function has to be called before accessing a key via: $phn(pvc=>key).

params.name: sampling_time_unit
params.doc: Time period in seconds used for sampling (or the sampling accuracy). The smaller the better, but slower. If you want to detect peeks, use a small one. To limit the access (like total number of requests on a long period of time) to a proxy resource (a gateway for example), use a bigger value of this parameter.

params.name: reqs_density_per_unit
params.doc: How many requests should be allowed per sampling_time_unit before blocking all the incoming request from that IP. Practically, the blocking limit is between ( let's have x=reqs_density_per_unit) x and 3*x for IPv4 addresses and between x and 8*x for IPv6 addresses.

params.name: remove_latency
params.doc: Specifies for how long the IP address will be kept in memory after the last request from that IP address. It's a sort of timeout value, in seconds. Note that it is not the duration to keep the IP in state 'blocked'. An IP is unblocked next occurrence of 'sampling_time_unit' that does not exceed 'reqs_density_per_unit'. Keeping an IP in memory results in faster reaching of blocked state -- see the notes about the limits of getting to state 'blocked'.

params.name: pike_log_level
params.doc: Syslog log level to be used by module to auto report the blocking (only first time) and unblocking of IPs detected as source of floods.

functions.name: pike_check_req
functions.doc: Process the source IP of the current request and return false if the IP was exceeding the blocking limit.

functions.name: pike_check_ip
functions.doc: Process the IP address parameter and return false if it was exceeding the blocking limit. The return codes are the same from pike_check_req().

params.name: hash_size
params.doc: Used to compute the number of slots for the internal hash table, as power of 2 (number of slots = 2^hash_size, aka 1<<hash_size). If you have many pipes, increase this value for proper performances, but don't go too high (hash_size=10 means 1024 slots).

params.name: db_url
params.doc: URL of the database server to be used.

params.name: plp_table_name
params.doc: Name of DB table where data definition for pipes is stored.

params.name: plp_pipeid_column
params.doc: Name of 'pipeid' column.

params.name: plp_limit_column
params.doc: Name of 'limit' column.

params.name: plp_algorithm_column
params.doc: Name of 'algorithm' column.

params.name: timer_interval
params.doc: The length of the timer interval in seconds. Counted messages are reset each timer_interval, therefore the amounts of messages have to be divided by this timer_interval value to get the messages per second value. For example, if you want to allow an average of 10 messages per second with a timer interval of 10 seconds, then the limit value has to be 100.

params.name: timer_mode
params.doc: Control what timer process to be used: 0 - use main fast timer; 1 - use secondary wheel timer.

params.name: load_fetch
params.doc: Control if the module should fetch the load for CPU and network traffic. If set to 0, no load is fetched; if set to 1, the load is fetched every timer interval.

params.name: reply_code
params.doc: The code of the reply sent by Kamailio while limiting.

params.name: reply_reason
params.doc: The reason of the reply sent by Kamailio while limiting.

params.name: clean_unused
params.doc: Clean unused pipes after this number of timer intervals.

functions.name: pl_check
functions.doc: Check the current request against the 'name' pipe.

functions.name: pl_active
functions.doc: Check the pipe 'name' was already created. Return 1 (true) if the pipe is found, -1 (false) if the pipe is not found.

functions.name: pl_drop
functions.doc: For the current request, a "503 - Server Unavailable" reply is sent back. The reply may or may not have a "Retry-After" header. If no parameter is given, there will be no "Retry-After" header. If only the max parameter is given, the reply will contain a "Retry-After: max" header. If both min and max params are given, the reply will contain a "Retry-After: random" header with random being a random value between the given min and max.

params.name: idx0
params.doc: The value to return by functions seeking a position when the index is 0 (note: returning 0 is stopping the execution of configuration file like 'exit', but for KEMI usage it is ok).

functions.name: pos_append
functions.doc: Append the value val after the position idx in the SIP message buffer.

functions.name: pos_insert
functions.doc: Insert the value val at the position idx in the SIP message buffer.

functions.name: pos_rm
functions.doc: Remove len characters starting at the position idx in the SIP message buffer.

functions.name: pos_set_char
functions.doc: Set the char at position index to first character in val.

functions.name: pos_headers_start
functions.doc: Return the position in the message buffer where headers start.

functions.name: pos_headers_end
functions.doc: Return the position in the message buffer where headers end.

functions.name: pos_body_start
functions.doc: Return the position in the message buffer where body starts.

functions.name: pos_body_end
functions.doc: Return the position in the message buffer where body ends.

functions.name: pos_find_str
functions.doc: Return the position of the val in message buffer starting at idx. In case of not finding it or error, the return code is negative. If val is at index 0, it returns the value specified by modparam idx0.

functions.name: pos_findi_str
functions.doc: Return the position of the val (matching case insensitive) in message buffer starting at idx. In case of not finding it or error, the return code is negative. If val is at index 0, it returns the value specified by modparam idx0.

functions.name: pos_rfind_str
functions.doc: Return the last position of the val in message buffer starting at idx (reverse search). In case of not finding it or error, the return code is negative. If val is at index 0, it returns the value specified by modparam idx0.

functions.name: pos_rfindi_str
functions.doc: Return the last position of the val (matching case insensitive) in message buffer starting at idx (reverse search). In case of not finding it or error, the return code is negative. If val is at index 0, it returns the value specified by modparam idx0.

functions.name: pos_search
functions.doc: Return the position that starts matching the regular expression re in message buffer starting at idx. In case of not finding it or error, the return code is negative. If val is at index 0, it returns the value specified by modparam idx0.

functions.name: pos_rsearch
functions.doc: Return the position of last match that starts matching the regular expression re in message buffer starting at idx. In case of not finding it or error, the return code is negative. If val is at index 0, it returns the value specified by modparam idx0.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: This is URL of the database to be used.

params.name: db_table
params.doc: The name of table where to read prefix route set.

params.name: exit
params.doc: If set, exit the execution of the configuration file when a route block is executed upon matching a prefix. Otherwise return 1 (true).

functions.name: prefix_route
functions.doc: This function tries to find a route from the user part of the request URI (if no parameter is provided), or from the value of the parameter. The parameter can contain config variables.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: The database url.

params.name: presentity_table
params.doc: The name of the db table where PUBLISH presence information is stored.

params.name: active_watchers_table
params.doc: The name of the db table where active subscription information is stored.

params.name: watchers_table
params.doc: The name of the db table where subscription states are stored.

params.name: clean_period
params.doc: The period in seconds between checks if there are expired messages stored in the database.

params.name: cseq_offset
params.doc: The allowed offset between server and client cseq.

params.name: db_update_period
params.doc: The period at which to synchronize cached subscriber info with the database.

params.name: waitn_time
params.doc: The maximum time period that NOTIFY requests will be buffered for. The server will attempt to send NOTIFY requests within many seconds of a change occurring.

params.name: notifier_poll_rate
params.doc: The number of times per second that the notifier processes should check for work. Approximately 1/(waitn_time * notifier_poll_rate * notifier_processes) of the pending updates will be sent each time a notifier process runs.

params.name: notifier_processes
params.doc: The number of notifier processes that should be started.

params.name: force_delete
params.doc: Enabling this parameter will delete expired presentity records without updating watchers.

params.name: startup_mode
params.doc: Setting this parameter to 0 will provide startup related backward compatibility for some modules. Setting to 0 fixes presentity requests with low expires (e.g. time() + 1)

params.name: expires_offset
params.doc: The value in seconds that should be subtracted from the expires value when sending a 200OK for a publish. It is used for forcing the client to send an update before the old publish expires.

params.name: max_expires
params.doc: The maximum admissible expires value for PUBLISH/SUBSCRIBE message (in seconds).

params.name: min_expires
params.doc: The minimum admissible expires value for PUBLISH/SUBSCRIBE message (in seconds).

params.name: min_expires_action
params.doc: The action to take when UA sends an expires value less than min_expires.

params.name: server_address
params.doc: The presence server address which will become the value of Contact header filed for 200 OK replies to SUBSCRIBE and PUBLISH and in NOTIFY messages.

params.name: subs_db_mode
params.doc: The presence module can utilize database for persistent subscription storage. If you use database, your subscriptions will survive machine restarts or SW crashes. The disadvantage is that accessing the database can be time consuming. Therefore, presence module implements four database accessing modes: * 0 - This disables database completely. Only memory will be used. Subscriptions will not survive restart. Use this value if you need a really fast presence module and subscription persistence is not necessary or is provided by other means. * 1 - Write-Through scheme. Subscriptions are updated synchronously in database and in memory(used for read operations). Use this scheme if speed is not top priority, but it's important that no subscriptions will be lost during crash or reboot or if you have an external application that reads the state of the subscriptions from database and they need to be updated synchronously. * 2 - Write-Back scheme. This is a combination of previous two schemes. All changes are made to memory and database synchronization is done in the timer. The timer deletes all expired contacts and flushes all modified or new subscriptions to database. Use this scheme if you encounter high-load peaks and want them to process as fast as possible. Latency of this mode is much lower than latency of mode 1, but slightly higher than latency of mode 0. To control the interval at which data is flushed to database, set the db_update_period parameter. * 3 - DB-Only scheme. No memory cache is kept, all operations being directly performed with the database. The timer deletes all expired subscriptions from database. The mode is useful if you configure more servers sharing the same DB without any replication at SIP level. The mode may be slower due the high number of DB operation.

params.name: publ_cache
params.doc: To improve performance, the presence module can operate in a couple of modes related to how PUBLISH data is stored. If publ_cache is 0, then no information is stored in memory.

params.name: subs_htable_size
params.doc: The size of the in-memory hash table to store subscription dialogs. This parameter will be used as the power of 2 when computing table size.

params.name: pres_htable_size
params.doc: The size of the in-memory hash table to store publish records. This parameter will be used as the power of 2 when computing table size.

params.name: send_fast_notify
params.doc: This parameter enables or disables the sending of an initial empty NOTIFY after a SUBSCRIBE/reSUBSCRIBE. This caused problems for MWI application, because some CPEs (like Samsung) fail to understand an empty NOTIFY to a message-summary event. This parameter is enabled by default, thus adhering to the standard.

params.name: enable_sphere_check
params.doc: This parameter is a flag that should be set if permission rules include sphere checking. The sphere information is expected to be present in the RPID body published by the presentity. The flag is introduced as this check requires extra processing that should be avoided if this feature is not supported by the clients.

params.name: timeout_rm_subs
params.doc: This parameter is a flag that should be set if subscriptions should be removed from the active_watchers when a NOTIFY times out. RFC3265 section 3.2.2 defines this behaviour as a SHOULD, so by default it is on. Disabling this will keep subscriptions active on unreliable networks.

params.name: fetch_rows
params.doc: Number of rows to be loaded in one step from database.

params.name: db_table_lock_type
params.doc: Enable (=1) or disable (=0) the Locks for table during a transaction. Locking only the "current" table causes problems with a MySQL-Databases in "DB-Only" mode.

params.name: local_log_level
params.doc: Control log level for some debug messages inside the module.

params.name: local_log_facility
params.doc: Control syslog facility for some debug messages inside the module.

params.name: subs_remove_match
params.doc: Control how to match the subscriptions to remove from memory. If set to 0, then the match is done on To-Tag (local generated), if set to 1, then the match is done on all dialog attributes (Call-Id, From-Tag, To-Tag).

params.name: xavp_cfg
params.doc: The name of the xavp to be used to specify attributes for internal processing of presence module.

params.name: retrieve_order
params.doc: If set to 0, presentity records are retrieved by received_time order. If set to 1, presentity records are retrieved by the value of retrieve_order_by parameter.

params.name: retrieve_order_by
params.doc: Used to set the order-by of the db query for fetching the presence records when retrieve_order is set to 1.

params.name: sip_uri_match
params.doc: The mode used when comparing uris.

params.name: enable_dmq
params.doc: If set to 1, will enable DMQ replication of presence data between nodes. Use this instead of a shared DB to share state across a cluster and update local watchers in realtime (subs_db_mode < 3) or on next notifier run (subs_db_mode = 3).

params.name: enable_pres_dmq
params.doc: If set to 1, will enable DMQ replication of presentities.

params.name: enable_pres_sync_dmq
params.doc: If set to 1, will enable initial synchronization of presentities state.

params.name: enable_subs_dmq
params.doc: If set to 1, will enable DMQ replication of subscriptions.

params.name: enable_subs_sync_dmq
params.doc: If set to 1, will enable initial synchronization of subscriptions state.

params.name: skip_notify_dmq
params.doc: Skip sending Notify messages if presentity was received by DMQ.

params.name: default_socket
params.doc: Default socket name to rewrite socket info in subcription that was received by DMQ.

params.name: pres_subs_mode
params.doc: Allow disabling cloning subscription structure for pv $subs(...), saving the pkg memory and copy operations for all its fields. If 1 the cloning is done; if 0, no cloning and $subs(...) returns $null.

params.name: delete_same_subs
params.doc: Enable deleting of subscriptions with the same presence uri and callid.

params.name: timer_mode
params.doc: Specify what timer process to be used. If set to 0, the core main timer is used. If set to 1, the core secondary timer is used.

params.name: subs_respond_200
params.doc: Specify the response code for accepted SUBSCRIBE requests. If set to 0, "202 Accepted" will be returned (default behaviour till version 5.5). If set to 1, "200 OK" will be returned instead, in conformance to RFC6665, which prohibits 202 responses.

functions.name: handle_publish
functions.doc: Handles PUBLISH requests by storing and updating published information in memory cache and database, then calls functions to send NOTIFY messages when changes in the published information occur. It takes one argument -> sender_uri. The parameter was added for enabling BLA implementation. If present, notification of a change in published state is not sent to the respective uri even though a subscription exists. It should be taken from the Sender header. It was left at the decision of the administrator whether or not to transmit the content of this header as parameter for handle_publish, to prevent security problems.

functions.name: handle_subscribe
functions.doc: The function which handles SUBSCRIBE requests. It stores or updates information in memory and database and calls functions to send NOTIFY messages when a SUBSCRIBE which initiate a dialog is received.

functions.name: pres_auth_status
functions.doc: The function checks if watcher URI is authorized to subscribe event 'presence' of presentity URI. Both watcher_uri and presentity_uri can be static strings or contain pseudo variables.

functions.name: pres_has_subscribers
functions.doc: Allows to check if presentity has any subscribers of event.

functions.name: pres_refresh_watchers
functions.doc: The function can be used in configuration to trigger notifies to watchers if a change in watchers authorization or in published state occurred (i.e., updates of xcap documents).

functions.name: pres_update_watchers
functions.doc: The function can be used in configuration to trigger updates to watchers status if a change in watchers authorization state occurred (i.e., updates of xcap documents change state from pending to active).

params.name: use_partial_states
params.doc: Control usage of partial state notifications.

params.name: default_expires
params.doc: The default expires value used when missing from SUBSCRIBE message (in seconds).

params.name: force_single_dialog
params.doc: By default the module aggregates all available dialog info into a single dialog-info document containing multiple "dialog" elements. If the phone does not support this, you can activate this parameter.

params.name: force_dummy_dialog
params.doc: By default the module returns null body if there are no bodies to aggregate. some sip clients like Bria expect at least one dialog. you can activate this parameter to send a dummy dialog.

params.name: default_expires
params.doc: The default expires value used when missing from SUBSCRIBE message (in seconds).

params.name: default_expires
params.doc: The default expires value used when missing from SUBSCRIBE message (in seconds).

params.name: default_expires
params.doc: The default expires value used when missing from SUBSCRIBE message (in seconds).

params.name: default_expires
params.doc: The default expires value used when missing from SUBSCRIBE message (in seconds).

params.name: aggregate_presentities
params.doc: Whether to aggregate in a single notify body all registration presentities. Useful to have all registrations on first NOTIFY following initial SUBSCRIBE.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: The database URL.

params.name: xcap_table
params.doc: The name of the database table where XCAP documents are stored.

params.name: disable_presence
params.doc: Set this parameter to disable the handling of the "presence" event.

params.name: disable_winfo
params.doc: Set this parameter to disable the handling of the "presence.winfo" event.

params.name: disable_bla
params.doc: Set this parameter to disable the handling of the "dialog;sla" event.

params.name: disable_xcapdiff
params.doc: Set this parameter to disable the handling of the "xcap-diff" event.

params.name: force_active
params.doc: This parameter is used for permissions when handling Subscribe messages. If set to 1, subscription state is considered active and the presentity is not queried for permissions (should be set to 1 if not using an XCAP server). Otherwise, the XCAP server is queried and the subscription states is according to user defined permission rules. If no rules are defined for a certain watcher, the subscriptions remains in pending state and the Notify sent will have no body.

params.name: integrated_xcap_server
params.doc: This parameter is a flag for the type of XCAP servers used. If the XCAP server is integrated with Kamailio presence_xml module and access the same database tables directly, like the embedded XCAP server implemented in xcap_server module, the parameter has to be set to 1. Apart from updating in xcap table, if the integrated server is not running on the same Kamailio instance, it must send an RPC command presence.refreshWatchers [pres_uri] [event] when a user modifies a rules document, to instruct the presence_xml module to update states from the database and, if needed, send NOTIFY updates.

params.name: xcap_server
params.doc: The address of the xcap servers used for storage. This parameter is compulsory if the integrated_xcap_server parameter is not set. It can be set more than once, to construct an address list of trusted XCAP servers.

params.name: passive_mode
params.doc: If set to 1, module acts in passive mode - no bind to presence module, no connection to database. Useful when needing only to use $xml(...) pseudo-variable.

params.name: xcapauth_userdel_reason
params.doc: This parameter represents the reason that will be included in the Subscription-State header of the Notify when a rule is no longer found in the XCAP pres-auth document for a user that was previously allowed. The Subscription state in this case switches to "terminated". Because it is not clear which reason is most appropriate in this case from the ones defined by the RFC 3265, this parameter offers the possibility for the admin to decide which one he wishes to use.

params.name: force_dummy_presence
params.doc: Set this parameter to enable simple body notify with status 'open' when presentity info is not available.

params.name: force_presence_single_body
params.doc: Set this parameter to enable single body notify. One presentity can have multiple dialogs and will by default notify all the dialogs and this can be a problem when dealing with large ring-groups or attendants, use this parameter to only send one body. Look at presence_single_body_priorities and presence_single_body_lookup_element to customize the behaviour.

params.name: presence_single_body_priorities
params.doc: Change this parameter to set the priorities when choosing the dialog that will be the final.

params.name: presence_single_body_lookup_element
params.doc: Set the name of the element that should be used to get the priority. If the value obtained is not in the list of presence_single_body_priorities the priority is 0.

params.name: default_expires
params.doc: The default expires value used when missing from SUBSCRIBE message (in seconds).

functions.name: pres_check_basic
functions.doc: Checks the /presence/tuple/status/basic nodes in the presentity for presentity_uri against the value in status.

functions.name: pres_check_activities
functions.doc: Checks whether a /presence/person/activities/activity node exists in the presentity for presentity_uri.

params.name: default_type
params.doc: The default timer type (if not present on the "timer" parameter).

params.name: default_interval
params.doc: The default interval to execute loop route for timers (if not present on the "timer" parameter). Suffix with "s", "ms", or "us" for an interval in seconds, milliseconds, or microseconds. If a number is given without a suffix, the number will be treated as seconds. Defaults to default_interval.

params.name: default_nworkers
params.doc: The default number of workers to run per timer (if not present on the "timer" parameter).

params.name: timer
params.doc: The definition of a timer. The value of the parameter must have the following format: * "name=_str_;type=_int_;interval=_str_;nworkers=_int_;ntasks=_int_;n slices=_int_"

params.name: start
params.doc: Route to be executed when timer stars. The value of the parameter must have the following format: * "timer=_str_;route=_str_"

params.name: loop
params.doc: Route to be executed on timer interval. The value of the parameter must have the following format: * "timer=_str_;route=_str_"

params.name: end
params.doc: Route to be executed when timer ends. The value of the parameter must have the following format: * "timer=_str_;route=_str_"

params.name: hash_size
params.doc: The size of the hash table used for storing SUBSCRIBE and PUBLISH information. This parameter will be used as the power of 2 when computing table size.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: Database url.

params.name: db_table
params.doc: The name of the database table.

params.name: min_expires
params.doc: The inferior expires limit for both Publish and Subscribe.

params.name: default_expires
params.doc: The default expires value used in case this information is not provisioned.

params.name: update_period
params.doc: The interval at which the information in database and hash table should be updated. In the case of the hash table updating means deleting expired messages. Setting a value less than or equal to zero, disables updates.

params.name: outbound_proxy
params.doc: SIP URI of outbound proxy to be used when sending PUBLISH requests if no outbound proxy is given in outbound_proxy field of struct publ_info.

params.name: dlginfo_increase_version
params.doc: When sending PUBLISH messages for Event: dialog, the body contains an XML document according to RFC 4235. This XML document contains a version attribute to easily detect changes in the dialog state. By setting this parameter, the pua module parses the XML document and sets the version attribute to the proper value. If the receiver of the PUBLISH does not care about the version parameter (e.g. like Kamailio presence_dialoginfo module) it makes no sense to waste CPU resources for parsing the XML body and the parameter should be set to 0.

params.name: reginfo_increase_version
params.doc: When sending PUBLISH messages for Event: reg, the body contains an XML document according to RFC 4235(?). This XML document contains a version attribute to easily detect changes in the registration state. By setting this parameter, the pua module parses the XML document and sets the version attribute to the proper value. If the receiver of the PUBLISH does not care about the version parameter (e.g. like Kamailio presence_reginfo module) it makes no sense to waste CPU resources for parsing the XML body and the parameter should be set to 0.

params.name: db_mode
params.doc: The module supports 2 modes of operation, high speed memory based storage (mode 0), and database only (mode 2) where all data is stored in a database, allowing scalability at the expense of speed. Mode 1 is reserved.

params.name: db_table_lock_write
params.doc: Enable (=1) or disable (=0) the Locks for table during a transaction. Locking only the "current" table causes problems with a MySQL-Databases in "DB-Only" mode.

params.name: check_remote_contact
params.doc: When sending a SUBSCRIBE check that the remote contact matches the one in the stored dialog or not. If the remote contact is checked and does not match the one in the stored dialog then the dialog is not matched. Checking the remote contact can cause problems when using modules like RLS and should not be required in order to properly match the dialog anyway. Set this parameter to 0 to disable checking of remote contact for SUBSCRIBE dialog matching.

params.name: fetch_rows
params.doc: Number of rows to be loaded in one step from database.

functions.name: pua_update_contact
functions.doc: The remote target can be updated by the Contact of a subsequent in dialog request. In the PUA watcher case (sending a SUBSCRIBE messages), this means that the remote target for the following Subscribe messages can be updated at any time by the contact of a Notify message. If this function is called on request route on receiving a Notify message, it will try to update the stored remote target.

params.name: default_domain
params.doc: The default domain for the registered users to be used when constructing the uri for the registrar callback.

params.name: header_name
params.doc: The name of the header to be added to Publish requests. It will contain the uri of the user agent that sent the Notify that is transformed into Publish. It stops sending a Notification with the same information to the sender.

params.name: outbound_proxy
params.doc: The outbound_proxy uri to be used when sending Subscribe requests.

params.name: server_address
params.doc: The IP address of the server.

functions.name: bla_set_flag
functions.doc: The function is used to mark REGISTER requests made to a BLA AOR. The module subscribes to the registered contacts for dialog;sla event.

functions.name: bla_handle_notify
functions.doc: The function handles Notify requests sent from phones on the same BLA to the server. The message is transformed in Publish request and passed to presence module for further handling. in case of a successful processing a 2xx reply should be sent.

params.name: use_uuid
params.doc: If this parameter is set, the pres_id will be generated using libuuid via uuid module. uuid module has to be loaded before pua_dialoginfo in this case.

params.name: include_callid
params.doc: If this parameter is set, the optional call-id will be put into the dialog element. This is needed for call-pickup features.

params.name: include_tags
params.doc: If this parameter is set, the local and remote tag will be put into the dialog element. This is needed for call-pickup features.

params.name: include_localremote
params.doc: If this parameter is set, the optional local and remote elements will be put into the dialog element. This is needed for call-pickup features.

params.name: override_lifetime
params.doc: The PUBLISH requests used to send the dialog-info contain an Expires header. The value of the expires is usually taken from the lifetime of the dialog (see README of dialog module). If the override_lifetime is set, the value specified here is used instead of the lifetime of the dialog module. If used, the value should at least be a few seconds more than the fr_inv_timer of the tm module.

params.name: include_req_uri
params.doc: controls if R-URI is going to be used instead of To header value in the PUBLISH as "identity" on "remote" node.

params.name: caller_confirmed
params.doc: Usually the dialog-info of the caller will be "trying -> early -> confirmed" and the dialog-info of the callee will be "early -> confirmed". On some phones the function LED will start blinking if the state is early, regardless if is is the caller or the callee (indicated with the "direction" parameter). To avoid blinking LEDs for the caller, you can enable this parameter. Then the state of the caller will be signaled as "confirmed" even in "early" state. This is a workaround for the buggy Linksys SPA962 phones. SNOM phones work well with the default setting.

params.name: send_publish_flag
params.doc: This message flag indicates whether to send PUBLISH requests or not. If not set, PUBLISH requests are sent out only if their R-URI is local (according to myself).

params.name: disable_caller_publish_flag
params.doc: This message flag indicates whether to send caller (initiator) PUBLISH requests or not. If set, PUBLISH requests are not sent for the caller (initiator).

params.name: disable_callee_publish_flag
params.doc: This message flag indicates whether to send callee (recipient) PUBLISH requests or not. If set, PUBLISH requests are not sent for the callee (recipient).

params.name: use_pubruri_avps
params.doc: Get Publish R-Uri from avps (see corresponding avp params), not from request to/from uri.

params.name: refresh_pubruri_avps_flag
params.doc: If use_pubruri_avps is enabled, this message flag indicates whether to refresh R-Uri from avps before sending the PUBLISH requests.

params.name: pubruri_caller_avp
params.doc: If use_pubruri_avps is enabled, PUBLISH-requests reporting dialog-information about the caller (entity=caller) are sent using the value of the specified avp as R-Uri.
