If multiple AVPs with the same name (but different indexes) are present, for each value a corresponding PUBLISH-request is generated. If no AVP with the specified name exists, no caller-related PUBLISH requests are sent.

params.name: pubruri_callee_avp
params.doc: If use_pubruri_avps is enabled, PUBLISH-requests reporting dialog-information about the callee (entity=callee) are sent using the value of the specified avp as R-Uri. If multiple AVPs with the same name (but different indexes) are present, for each value a corresponding PUBLISH-request is generated. If no AVP with the specified name exists, no callee-related PUBLISH requests are sent.

params.name: pubruri_caller_dlg_var
params.doc: Must be set to the name of dialog variable where to store the URI for caller, used to send the notifications. This is needed to restored the value after Kamailio restart. If not set, loaded dialogs at restart are no longer sending notifications. New dialogs are working fine.

params.name: pubruri_callee_dlg_var
params.doc: Must be set to the name of dialog variable where to store the URI for callee, used to send the notifications. This is needed to restored the value after Kamailio restart. If not set, loaded dialogs at restart are no longer sending notifications. New dialogs are working fine.

params.name: callee_trying
params.doc: If this parameter is set, a "Trying" state will be sent for both the caller and callee, rather than just the caller.

params.name: caller_entity_when_publish_disabled
params.doc: Must be a valid sip uri. If this parameter is set, this uri is used as caller entity in publish xml body if associated dialog has the flag disable_caller_publish_flag set. Note only the flag received on dialog creation is used to activate this feature.

params.name: callee_entity_when_publish_disabled
params.doc: Must be a valid sip uri. If this parameter is set, this uri is used as callee entity in publish xml body if associated dialog has the flag disable_callee_publish_flag set. Note only the flag received on dialog creation is used to activate this feature.

params.name: publish_dialog_req_within
params.doc: If this parameter is set to 1, subsequents requests received in dialog generate corresponding publish request.

params.name: local_identity_dlg_var
params.doc: PUBLISH-requests reporting dialog-information will use the value of the dialog variable if exists

params.name: attribute_display
params.doc: If set to 1, the display name attribute is added with user part of the URI for local and remote targets.

functions.name: pua_json_publish
functions.doc: The function build presentity state from json_payload and updates presentity table.

params.name: default_domain
params.doc: The default domain for the registered users to be used when constructing the uri for the registrar callback.

params.name: publish_reginfo
params.doc: Whether or not to generate PUBLISH requests.

params.name: outbound_proxy
params.doc: The outbound_proxy uri to be used when sending Subscribe and Publish requests.

params.name: server_address
params.doc: The IP address of the server.

functions.name: reginfo_handle_notify
functions.doc: This function processes received "NOTIFY"-requests and updates the local registry accordingly.

functions.name: reginfo_subscribe
functions.doc: This function will subscribe for reginfo-information at the given server URI.

functions.name: reginfo_disable_publish
functions.doc: This function disables sending the PUBLISH request in the registrar callback invocation, for the current message only.

params.name: default_domain
params.doc: The default domain to use when constructing the presentity URI if it is missing from stored AOR in the usrloc table (in memory or database).

params.name: entity_prefix
params.doc: The prefix used when constructing the entity attribute to be added to a presence node in the XML PIDF document. (ex: pres:user@domain ).

params.name: branch_flag
params.doc: Which branch flag to be used to select the contact addresses for which to generate PUBLISH. Valid values are 0 to 31.

functions.name: pua_set_publish
functions.doc: The function is used to mark REGISTER requests that have to issue a PUBLISH. The PUBLISH is issued when REGISTER is saved in location table.

params.name: server_address
params.doc: The SIP URI specifying the address of the SIP server.

functions.name: pua_xmpp_notify
functions.doc: Function that handles Notify messages addressed to a user from an xmpp domain. It requires filtering after method and domain in configuration file. If the function is successful, a 2xx reply must be sent.

functions.name: pua_xmpp_req_winfo
functions.doc: Function called when a Subscribe addressed to a user from an xmpp domain is received. It calls sending a Subscribe for winfo for the user, and the following Notify with dialog-info is translated into a subscription in xmpp. It also requires filtering in configuration file, after method, domain and event(only for presence).

params.name: shvset
params.doc: Set the initial value of a shared variable ($shv(name)). The parameter can be set many times.

params.name: varset
params.doc: Set the value of a script variable ($var(name)). The parameter can be set many times.

params.name: avp_aliases
params.doc: Define aliases for PV AVP names.

functions.name: pv_isset
functions.doc: Return true if a PV value is different than 'null'.

functions.name: pv_unset
functions.doc: Unset the value of the PV (e.g., delete AVP, set to null).

functions.name: is_int
functions.doc: Function checks if pvar argument contains integer value and returns 1 if it does and -1 otherwise.

functions.name: typeof
functions.doc: Returns true if the type of pseudo-variable matches the second parameter. The second parameter can be: 'int' - type is integer; 'str' - type is string; 'null' - type is null.

functions.name: not_empty
functions.doc: Returns true if the pseudo-variables has the type string and is not empty value.

functions.name: xavp_copy
functions.doc: Copy and append one XAVP.

functions.name: xavp_params_explode
functions.doc: Convert a parameters string in xavp attributes.

functions.name: xavp_xparams_explode
functions.doc: Convert a parameters string in xavp attributes.

functions.name: xavp_params_implode
functions.doc: Serialize the subfields in an XAVP to a parameters string format.

functions.name: xavp_params_implode_qval
functions.doc: Serialize the subfields in an XAVP to a parameters string format, enclosing string values in double quotes.

functions.name: xavu_params_explode
functions.doc: Convert a parameters string in xavu attributes.

functions.name: xavu_params_implode
functions.doc: Serialize the subfields in an XAUP to a parameters string format.

functions.name: xavp_slist_explode
functions.doc: Breaks a string list in tokens by separators and stores them in XAVPs. Note that is not storing empty values.

functions.name: xavp_child_seti
functions.doc: Set the value of $xavp(rname=>cname) to integer value ival.

functions.name: xavi_child_seti
functions.doc: Set the value of $xavi(rname=>cname) to integer value ival.

functions.name: xavp_child_sets
functions.doc: Set the value of $xavp(rname=>cname) to string value sval.

functions.name: xavi_child_sets
functions.doc: Set the value of $xavi(rname=>cname) to string value sval.

functions.name: xavp_rm
functions.doc: Remove the value of $xavp(rname).

functions.name: xavp_rm_all
functions.doc: Remove all the values of $xavp(rname).

functions.name: xavi_rm
functions.doc: Remove the value of $xavi(rname).

functions.name: xavi_rm_all
functions.doc: Remove all the values of $xavi(rname).

functions.name: xavp_child_rm
functions.doc: Remove the value of $xavp(rname=>cname).

functions.name: xavi_child_rm
functions.doc: Remove the value of $xavi(rname=>cname).

functions.name: xavp_lshift
functions.doc: Left shift with rotation of the xavps with name xname so that the one at the index idx becomes the first and the ones before it are at the end of the list.

functions.name: xavp_push_dst
functions.doc: Set destination fields from XAVP attributes.

functions.name: sbranch_set_ruri
functions.doc: Use the attributes from static branch ($sbranch(key) variable) to set request URI and the other fields of the branch associated with request URI (destination URI, path, ...).

functions.name: sbranch_append
functions.doc: Use the attributes from static branch ($sbranch(key) variable) to append a new branch to destination set. It is an alternative to append_branch() that allows setting each attribute specific to the branch.

functions.name: sbranch_reset
functions.doc: Reset the content of static branch ($sbranch(key) variable.

functions.name: pv_xavp_print
functions.doc: Print all XAVPs to the syslog using INFO log level.

functions.name: pv_xavu_print
functions.doc: Print all XAVUs to the syslog using INFO log level.

functions.name: pv_xavi_print
functions.doc: Print all XAVIs to the syslog using INFO log level.

functions.name: pv_var_to_xavp
functions.doc: Copy the script variable value into an xavp.

functions.name: pv_xavp_to_var
functions.doc: Copy xavp values into vars. Reverse of pv_var_to_xavp().

functions.name: pv_evalx
functions.doc: The fmt string is evaluated twice for exiting variables, the result is stored in dst variable. The dst must be the name of a writable variable. The fmt can contain variables that have a value containing other variables.

params.name: xavi_name
params.doc: Name of the XAVI where the collected headers are stored.

params.name: header_value_size
params.doc: Defines an internal maximum SIP header value size. Header values longer than this setting will be stripped down when collected or applied.

params.name: header_collect_flag
params.doc: Used to mark that headers are collected for the SIP message, leading to subsequent headers collection on this message to be declined with an error. Should be used only in branches and replies.

params.name: header_apply_flag
params.doc: Used to mark that headers are applied for the SIP message, leading to subsequent headers applies on this message to be declined with an error. Should be used only in branches and replies.

params.name: skip_headers
params.doc: A comma separated headers list that must be excluded from processing (they are skipped when pvh_apply_headers() changes the SIP message headers).

params.name: split_headers
params.doc: A comma separated headers list that must be split into multi headers if their value is a comma separated list.

params.name: auto_msg
params.doc: Defines whether the headers are automatically collected for incoming messages, as well as automatically applied for forwarded messages.

functions.name: pvh_collect_headers
functions.doc: Collects all headers from the message into the XAVP. It should be used preferably just when the SIP message is received by Kamailio.

functions.name: pvh_apply_headers
functions.doc: Applies the current XAVP headers state to the real headers. Should be called only once per branch when the message is about to leave Kamailio.

functions.name: pvh_reset_headers
functions.doc: Collects all headers from the message into the XAVP. It should be used preferably just when the SIP message is received by >Kamailio.

functions.name: pvh_check_header
functions.doc: Checks if the header “hname” already exists in the XAVP.

functions.name: pvh_append_header
functions.doc: Appends a new header “hname” with the value “hvalue” into the XAVP. Please note that subsequent "pv_append_header" calls will result in multiple headers.

functions.name: pvh_modify_header
functions.doc: Modifies an existing header in the XAVP “hname” with the value “hvalue” into the XAVP. Index order is top to bottom. Please note that subsequent pvh_append_header calls will result in multiple headers.

functions.name: pvh_remove_header
functions.doc: Removes an existing header “hname” from the XAVP. Index order is top to bottom.

functions.name: pvh_remove_all_headers
functions.doc: Removes all sip message headers.

functions.name: pvh_header_param_exists
functions.doc: Checks if the parameter “hparameter” is present in the header “hname” from XAVP.

functions.name: pvh_remove_header_param
functions.doc: Removes an existing parameter “hparameter” in the header “hname” from the XAVP.

params.name: tpl
params.doc: The definition of a template file: * "name=_string_;fpath=_number_;bsize=_number_"

functions.name: pvtpl_render
functions.doc: Render the template 'tplname' using config variables, setting the result in the variable specified by 'res'.

params.name: qos_flag
params.doc: The module will not do anything to any message unless instructed to do so via the config script. You must set the qos_flag value in the setflag() call of the INVITE you want the qos module to process. But before you can do that, you need to tell the qos module which flag value you are assigning to qos.

params.name: url
params.doc: The amqp connection url.

params.name: timeout_sec
params.doc: The timeout in seconds. The timeout_sec + timeout_usec combination gives the time to wait for an amqp reply, when rabbitmq_publish_consume() is used.

params.name: timeout_usec
params.doc: The timeout in micro seconds. The timeout_sec + timeout_usec combination gives the time to wait for an amqp reply, when rabbitmq_publish_consume() is used.

params.name: direct_reply_to
params.doc: Setting this parameter to 1, enables rabbitmq direct reply-to feature. More info about this, can be found at https://www.rabbitmq.com/direct-reply-to.html.

functions.name: rabbitmq_publish
functions.doc: The function publishes messagebody without waiting for a reply.

params.name: timer_interval
params.doc: The initial length of a timer interval in seconds. All amounts of messages have to be divided by this timer to get a messages per second value.

params.name: queue
params.doc: The format of the queue parameter is "pipe_no:method". For each defined method, the algorithm defined by pipe number "pipe_no" will be used.

params.name: pipe
params.doc: The format of the pipe param is "pipe_no:algorithm:limit". For each defined pipe, the given algorithm with the given limit will be used.

functions.name: rl_check
functions.doc: Check the current request against the matched ratelimit algorithm. If no parameter is provided, the queue will be matched based on method type, and then the pipe will be identified based on the matched queue. If a pipe number is provided as a parameter, then the given pipe number will be used for identifying the ratelimit algorithm. The pipe number must be provided as number or via a pseudovariable.

functions.name: rl_check_pipe
functions.doc: Check the current request against the matched ratelimit algorithm of the pipe provided as parameter. The parameter can be provided as number or variable.

params.name: file
params.doc: Text file containing the regular expression groups. It must be set in order to enable the group matching function.

params.name: max_groups
params.doc: Max number of regular expression groups in the text file.

params.name: group_max_size
params.doc: Max content size of a group in the text file.

params.name: pcre_caseless
params.doc: If this options is set, matching is done caseless. It is equivalent to Perl's /i option, and it can be changed within a pattern by a (?i) or (?-i) option setting.

params.name: pcre_multiline
params.doc: By default, PCRE treats the subject string as consisting of a single line of characters (even if it actually contains newlines). The "start of line" metacharacter (^) matches only at the start of the string, while the "end of line" metacharacter ($) matches only at the end of the string, or before a terminating newline.

params.name: pcre_dotall
params.doc: If this option is set, a dot metacharacter in the pattern matches all characters, including those that indicate newline. Without it, a dot does not match when the current position is at a newline. This option is equivalent to Perl's /s option, and it can be changed within a pattern by a (?s) or (?-s) option setting.

params.name: pcre_extended
params.doc: If this option is set, whitespace data characters in the pattern are totally ignored except when escaped or inside a character class. Whitespace does not include the VT character (code 11). In addition, characters between an unescaped # outside a character class and the next newline, inclusive, are also ignored. This is equivalent to Perl's /x option, and it can be changed within a pattern by a (?x) or (?-x) option setting.

functions.name: pcre_match
functions.doc: Matches the given string parameter against the regular expression pcre_regex, which is compiled in runtime into a PCRE object. Returns TRUE if it matches, FALSE otherwise.

functions.name: pcre_match_group
functions.doc: Tries to match the given string against a specific group in the text file (see Section 6.1, “File format”). Returns TRUE if it matches, FALSE otherwise.

params.name: default_expires
params.doc: If the processed message contains neither Expires header fields nor expires contact parameters, this value will be used for newly created usrloc records. The parameter contains number of second to expire (for example use 3600 for one hour). If it is set to a lower value than the “min_expires” parameter then it will be ignored. This parameter can be modified via ser config framework. A random value in a specific interval can be selected by using the default_expires_range parameter

params.name: default_expires_range
params.doc: This parameter specifies that the expiry used for newly created usrloc records are not fixed, but a random value in the interval “[default_expires-default_expires_range%, default_expires]”. The value is between 0 and 100 and represent the maximum percentage from expires that will be subtracted when computing the value. Default is 0, meaning default_expires is left unmodified. This parameter can be modified via the Kamailio config framework.

params.name: expires_range
params.doc: Similar to default_expires_range, but it applies to the incoming expires value. Default in 0, meaning the expires is left unmodified. This parameter can be modified via the Kamailio config framework.

params.name: min_expires
params.doc: The minimum expires value of a “Contact”. Values lower than this minimum will be either set to the minimum or 423 response is sent back. Value 0 disables the checking. This parameter can be modified via the Kamailio config framework.

params.name: min_expires_mode
params.doc: Control what to do when expires value in REGISTER request is lower than min_expires parameter. If set to 0, expires is set to min_expires. If set to 1, then 423 Interval Too Brief is sent back.

params.name: max_expires
params.doc: The maximum accepted expires value of a “Contact”, values higher than this maximum will be automatically set to the maximum. Value 0 disables the checking. This parameter can be modified via the Kamailio config framework.

params.name: default_q
params.doc: The parameter represents default “q” value for new contacts. Because Kamailio doesn't support float parameter types, the value in the parameter is divided by 1000 and stored as float. For example, if you want default_q to be 0.38, use value 380 here. This parameter can be modified via the Kamailio config framework.

params.name: realm_prefix
params.doc: Prefix to be automatically stripped from realm. As an alternative to SRV records (not all SIP clients support SRV lookup), a subdomain of the master domain can be defined for SIP purposes (like sip.mydomain.net pointing to same IP address as the SRV record for mydomain.net). By ignoring the realm_prefix "sip.", at registration, sip.mydomain.net will be equivalent to mydomain.net. This parameter can be modified via the Kamailio config framework.

params.name: append_branches
params.doc: The parameter controls how lookup function processes multiple contacts. If there are multiple contacts for the given username in usrloc and this parameter is set to 1, Request-URI will be overwritten with the highest-q rated contact. The rest will be appended to sip_msg structure and can be later used by tm for forking. If the parameter is set to 0, only Request-URI will be overwritten with the highest-q rated contact and the rest will be left unprocessed. This parameter can be modified via Kamailio config framework.

params.name: aor_avp
params.doc: This module parameter has been removed. Use the 'uri' parameter from functions (e.g., save, lookup, registered).

params.name: case_sensitive
params.doc: If set to 1 then AOR comparison and also storing will be case sensitive, if set to 0 then AOR comparison and storing will be case insensitive. This is recommended. This parameter can be modified via Kamailio config framework.

params.name: received_avp
params.doc: Registrar will store the value of the AVP configured by this parameter in the received column in the user location database. It will leave the column empty if the AVP is empty. The AVP should contain a SIP URI consisting of the source IP, port, and transport protocol of the REGISTER message being processed.

params.name: received_param
params.doc: The name of the parameter that will be appended to Contact URI's of 200 OK when the received URI was set by the “nathelper” module. If the value is an empty string, then the parameter is not appended anymore.

params.name: max_contacts
params.doc: The parameter can be used to limit the number of contacts per AOR (Address of Record) in the user location database. If the maximum number of contacts is exceeded, Kamailio will not accept the registration and send an error response. Value 0 disables the check. This parameter can be modified via the Kamailio config framework. (Please also check the flag for save() if you only want only one active registration).

params.name: retry_after
params.doc: The registrar can generate a 5xx reply to REGISTER requests in various situations. It can, for example, happen when the max_contacts parameter is set and the processing of REGISTER request would exceed the limit. In this case the registrar would generate "503 Service Unavailable" response. This parameter can be modified via the Kamailio config framework.

params.name: sock_flag
params.doc: Message flag to signal to the registrar module to look into REGISTER request for a header which contains a socket description (IP:port). This socket info will be stored by registrar instead of the received socket info.

params.name: sock_hdr_name
params.doc: Header which contains a socket description (proto:IP:port) to override the received socket info. The header will be read only if the flag sock_flag is set.

params.name: sock_mode
params.doc: If set to 1, the server stores the advertised address in socket field, instead of bind address.

params.name: method_filtering
params.doc: Tells if the contact filtering based on supported methods should be performed during lookup on initial requests without to-tag. It's enabled only if it has a non zero value. Supported methods are listed in the “Allow:” header in the REGISTER message and stored in the location database.

params.name: use_path
params.doc: If set to 1, the “Path:” header is handled according to the parameter. This parameter can be modified via Kamailio config framework. “path_mode”.

params.name: path_mode
params.doc: The registrar module implements three different modes regarding the response to a registration which includes one or more Path headers: * 0 - The Path header is saved into usrloc, but is not included in the reply. * 1 - The Path header is saved into usrloc, but is only included in the reply if path support is indicated in the registration request by the “path” option in the “Supported:” header. * 2 - The path header is only saved into usrloc, if path support is indicated in the registration request by the “path” option of the “Supported” header. If no path support is indicated, the request is rejected with “420 - Bad Extension” and the header “Unsupported: path” is included in the reply along with the received “Path” header. This mode is the one recommended by RFC-3327.

params.name: path_use_received
params.doc: If set to 1, the “received” parameter of the first Path URI of a registration is set as received-uri and the NAT branch flag is set for this contact. This is useful if the registrar is placed behind a SIP loadbalancer, which passes the nat'ed UAC address as “received” parameter in its Path uri.

params.name: path_check_local
params.doc: If set to 1, when performing a lookup the Path (if present) is evaluated and if the first hop is local (according to “myself” test), we skip it to avoid unnecessary looping.

params.name: reg_callid_avp
params.doc: obsolete. use match_option in registered function

params.name: xavp_cfg
params.doc: Defines the name of XAVP class to store runtime module config values. The values are stored as inner XAVPs, like $xavp(class=>attribute). Valid inner XAVP names: * match_callid - filter contacts by callid. Used in registered(). * match_contact - filter contacts by contact. Used in registered(). * match_received - filter contacts by received. Used in registered(). * rlf_bflags - filter contacts by branch flags. Used in lookup(). * q - q value of contact (integer 0-1000). It overrides q value given in contact header and default_q parameter. Used in save(). * expires - the expires value, to overwrite the value from SIP headers. Used in save(). * max_contacts - the number of maximum contacts to be stored for the current registration AoR. It overwrites the 'max_contacts' module parameter value. Used in save(). * socket - the string representing the socket on which the register request was received, as alternative to using the sock_hdr. Used in save(). * tcpconn_id This can be set with $conid, the TCP connection ID of the connection the current message. This is useful when calling save() on a reply route to set the connecion of the original request. Used in save().

params.name: xavp_rcd
params.doc: Defines the name of XAVP class to store details from the location records. The values are stored as inner XAVPs, like $xavp(class[0]=>attribute). Valid inner XAVP names: * ruid - the record's internal unique id. * contact - the record's contact value. * expires - the record's expires value. * received - the record's received value. * path - the record's path value.

params.name: xavp_rcd_mask
params.doc: Defines what values to skip when xavp_rcd is stored. * 1 - ruid * 2 - contact * 4 - expires * 8 - received * 16 - path

params.name: gruu_enabled
params.doc: If set to 1 and the “+sip.instance” parameter to Contact header of REGISTER is present, then the value of the parameter is saved to location and pub-gruu and temp-gruu addresses are generated.

params.name: outbound_mode
params.doc: If set to 0 this module will accept REGISTER requests that do not contain a “Supported:” header with the outbound options-tag. The 200 OK response to REGISTER requests that this module generates will not contain “Require:” or “Supported:” headers with the outbound options-tag. If the client has a “Require:” header with the outbound options tag the REGISTER will be rejected with a “420 Bad Extension” response.

params.name: regid_mode
params.doc: If set to 0 this module will ignore the “regid” contact param when saving REGISTER request if the request does not indicate support for outbound.

params.name: flow_timer
params.doc: If set to 0 then this module will not add a “Flow-Timer:” header to 200 OK responses to REGISTER requests.

params.name: contact_max_size
params.doc: Max size of URIs in “Contact:” header.

params.name: event_callback
params.doc: The name of the function in the KEMI configuration file (embedded scripting language such as Lua, Python, ...) to be executed instead of event_route[...] blocks.

params.name: lookup_filter_mode
params.doc: Control what filters should be applied to lookup(...) operations. It can be a combination (sum) of the next values: * 1 - apply the branch flags filter - return only contact records with branch flags matching at least one set inside xavp specified by xavp_cfg parameter with inner name rlf_bflags - e.g., $xavp(reg=>rlf_bflags). * 2 - apply the active tcp connection filter - return only contact records that have the associated TCP/TLS/WSS connection active. UDP and SCTP contacts are not filtered, all are returned.

params.name: use_expired_contacts
params.doc: Allow/Disallow the usage of the expired contacts. * 0 Disallow the usage of the expired contacts. * 1 Allow the usage of the expired contacts.

functions.name: save
functions.doc: The function processes a REGISTER message. It can add, remove or modify location records (in usrloc) depending on Contact and Expires header fields in the REGISTER message. On success and when called from the REQUEST_ROUTE, “200 OK” will be returned listing all contacts that are currently in the location database. As a side effect, also branch flags are stored in usrloc. On an error, an error message will be sent with a short description in reason phrase.

functions.name: lookup
functions.doc: The lookup function extracts username and/or domain from Request-URI and tries to find all contacts for the username in usrloc. If there are no such contacts, -1 will be returned. If there are such contacts, Request-URI will be overwritten with the contact that has the highest q value and optionally the rest will be appended to the message (depending on append_branches parameter value). As a side effect, also branch flags are restored from usrloc.

functions.name: lookup_to_dset
functions.doc: Similar to lookup(...), but push the location contacts to destination set, without changing the R-URI (first branch not changed, it creates additional branches). For the meaning of the parameters and the return codes, see the documentation for lookup(...) function.

functions.name: lookup_branches
functions.doc: The function performs lookup(domain) on r-uri and additional branches (only branches that have no other attributes set than uri).

functions.name: lookup_xavp
functions.doc: Similar to lookup(...), but store the location record attributes in XAVPs. Note that not all contact record fields are stored

functions.name: registered
functions.doc: The function returns true if the AOR in the URI is registered, false otherwise. The function does not modify the message being processed, it neither rewrites the Request-URI if a contact is found nor append branches. If uri parameter is not provided, then it considered to be the Request-URI for SIP requests and To-URI for SIP replies.

functions.name: add_sock_hdr
functions.doc: Adds a new header to the current REGISTER request with “hdr_name” which contains the description of the received socket (proto:ip:port)

functions.name: unregister
functions.doc: The function removes contacts associated with 'uri' from the location database. If 'ruid' is provided a specific contact is removed, if 'ruid' is not provided all the current contacts are removed. If 'ruid' is provided and the “usrloc” module is using “db_mode=3”, 'uri' does not need to be given and can be empty string.

functions.name: reg_fetch_contacts
functions.doc: The function fetches the contacts for 'uri' from table 'domain' to pseudo-variable $ulc(profile).

functions.name: reg_free_contacts
functions.doc: The function frees the contacts from pseudo-variable $ulc(profile). Should be called to release the content of a profile. Anyhow, fetching a new contact addresses set over a profile will release any existing data in that profile.

functions.name: reg_send_reply
functions.doc: The function sends the SIP reply that is normally sent by save(...), but that was skipped due to flag 0x2. It must be used after save(..., "0x2"). Practically it allows saving registration to location table, do other operations and then send the reply.

functions.name: reg_from_user
functions.doc: The function returns true if the SIP message comes from the user identified by 'uri' parameter by matching the associated location records. The matching is done with the field 'received' if it is set, otherwise with the contact address.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: The database url.

params.name: rlpres_db_url
params.doc: The rlpres (rls_presentity table) database url. This parameter only needs to be specified if the rls_watchers table and rls_presentity tables are in different databases. rls_presentity is used to cache the bodies of back-end NOTIFY requests until an RLS NOTIFY can be sent. On a multi-server system having a single cache for all active servers can cause issues if both servers try to send RLS NOTIFY requests at the same time. This parameter enables each server to have its own (possibly local) rls_presentity table.

params.name: xcap_db_url
params.doc: The xcap database url. This parameter only needs to be specified if the rls db and integrated xcap server db have different urls.

params.name: db_mode
params.doc: The module supports 2 modes of operation, high speed memory based storage (mode 0), and database only (mode 2) where all data is stored in a database, allowing scalability at the expense of speed. Mode 1 is reserved.

params.name: xcap_table
params.doc: The name of the xcap table in which the integrated server or the xcap_client module writes. If integrated_xcap_server parameter not set, the name of the table must be the same as the one set for the xcap_client module.

params.name: rlsubs_table
params.doc: The name of the db table where resource lists subscription information is stored.

params.name: rlpres_table
params.doc: The name of the db table where notified event specific information is stored.

params.name: clean_period
params.doc: The period at which to check for expired information. 0 means do not check.

params.name: rlpres_clean_period
params.doc: The period at which to check for expired rls_presentity information. -1 means do not use (clean_period) is used instead. 0 means do not check. This option can be used when you want to check rls_presentity and rls_watchers on different timeouts. This is useful when they are in different databases.

params.name: waitn_time
params.doc: The maximum time period that RLS NOTIFY requests will be buffered for. The server will attempt to send NOTIFY requests with the updated presence state of the subscribed list or watcher information within this many seconds of a change occurring.

params.name: notifier_poll_rate
params.doc: The number of times per second that the notifier processes should check for work. Approximately 1/(waitn_time * notifier_poll_rate * notifier_processes) of the pending updates will be sent each time a notifier process runs.

params.name: notifier_processes
params.doc: The number of notifier processes that should be started.

params.name: max_expires
params.doc: The maximum accepted expires for a subscription to a list.

params.name: expires_offset
params.doc: This parameter only has an effect when the db_mode is DB_ONLY (mode 2). When expired subscribers are checked for deletion from the database, those that have a value in the expires column which is less than current_time - expires_offset are matched. Hence when an offset of zero is used, all those that expire prior the current time will be deleted. If an offset of 't' is used, only those that expired more than t seconds ago are deleted from the database. Negative offsets are treated as though an offset of zero was specified.

params.name: hash_size
params.doc: The dimension of the hash table used to store subscription to a list. This parameter will be used as the power of 2 when computing table size.

params.name: xcap_root
params.doc: The address of the xcap server.

params.name: integrated_xcap_server
params.doc: This parameter should be set if only integrated xcap servers are used to store resource lists.

params.name: to_presence_code
params.doc: The code to be returned by rls_handle_subscribe function if the processed Subscribe is not a resource list Subscribe. This code can be used in an architecture with presence and rls servers collocated on the same machine, to call handle_subscribe on the message causing this code.

params.name: rls_event
params.doc: The default event that RLS handles is presence. If some other events should also be handled by RLS they should be added using this parameter. It can be set more than once.

params.name: outbound_proxy
params.doc: The SIP address where to send RLS subscriptions (outbound proxy address as SIP URI).

params.name: server_address
params.doc: The address of the server that will be used as a contact in sent Subscribe requests and 200 OK replies for Subscribe requests for RLS. It is a mandatory parameter.

params.name: max_notify_body_length
params.doc: The maximum size that the body of a NOTIFY message may be. If set to 0 (the default), no size limit is applied. Note that this refers only to the body, not the complete NOTIFY message.

params.name: reload_db_subs
params.doc: Reload subscriptions on module initialization (requires db_mode 0 (memory only mode)).

params.name: fetch_rows
params.doc: Number of rows to be loaded in one step from database.

params.name: disable_remote_presence
params.doc: When set to a non-zero value RLS will not perform back-end SUBSCRIBEs to non-local presentities. When people have large contact lists RLS will make lots of back-end subscriptions for each local subscriber. This can be a lot of traffic, and if the contact lists contain non-local (as in not on this Kamailio server or cluster) contacts this can result in a lot of Internet traffic. Setting this option to a non-zero value prevents RLS from performing back-end SUBSCRIBEs for remote presentities.

params.name: max_backend_subs
params.doc: When set to a non-zero value RLS will limit the number of back-end SUBSCRIBEs for each RLS SUBSCRIBE to this value. Leaving this at the default of zero means no limit. When people have large contact lists RLS will make lots of back-end subscriptions. This can easily overload a system. This option allows you to limit the number of back-end SUBSCRIBEs to help prevent overload.

functions.name: rls_handle_subscribe
functions.doc: This function detects if a Subscribe message should be handled by RLS. If not it replies with the configured to_presence_code. If it is, it extracts the dialog info and sends aggregate Notify requests with information for the list.

functions.name: rls_handle_notify
functions.doc: Handle NOTIFY requests.

functions.name: rls_update_subs
functions.doc: This function can be used in configuration to trigger updates to resource list subscriptions (for example, after the contents of a resource list has changes).

params.name: enable_full_lr
params.doc: If set to 1 then “;lr=on” instead of just “;lr” will be used. This is to overcome problems with broken UAs which strip “;lr” parameter when generating Route header fields from Record-Route (“;lr=on” seems to help).

params.name: append_fromtag
params.doc: If turned on, request's from-tag is appended to record-route; that's useful for understanding whether subsequent requests (such as BYE) come from caller (route's from-tag==BYE's from-tag) or callee (route's from-tag==BYE's to-tag)

params.name: enable_double_rr
params.doc: There are some situations when the server needs to insert two Record-Route header fields instead of one. For example when using two disconnected networks or doing cross-protocol forwarding from UDP->TCP. This parameter enables inserting of 2 Record-Routes. The server will later remove both of them.

params.name: add_username
params.doc: If set to a non 0 value (which means yes), the username part will be also added in the Record-Route URI.

params.name: enable_socket_mismatch_warning
params.doc: When a preset record-route header is forced in Kamailio config and the host from the record-route header is not the same as the host server, a warning will be printed out in the logs. The 'enable_socket_mismatch_warning' parameter enables or disables the warning. When Kamailio is behind a NATed firewall, we don't want this warning to be printed for every bridged call.

params.name: custom_user_avp
params.doc: When add_username is enabled, a call to record_route will add the username of the RequestURI to the Record-Route URI. This parameter allows you to set up an AVP with which you can customise the username to be added in the Record-Route URI.

params.name: force_send_socket
params.doc: If set to 1, local socket is forced even for single Record-Route, otherwise is done on double Record-Route (should that be enabled).

params.name: ignore_sips
params.doc: If set to 1, the Record-Route header are build with 'sip' schema always, ignoring the presence of 'sips' schema in request URI.

params.name: sockname_mode
params.doc: If set to 1, the Record-Route URI is built to contain socket name in 'sn' parameter and then it is used to lookup the local socket for Route header processing.

params.name: loose_route_mode
params.doc: Controls the behaviour of loose_route() in the same manner as the value of the parameter for for function loose_route_mode(val), in a global manner.

functions.name: loose_route
functions.doc: The function performs routing of SIP requests which contain a route set. The name is a little bit confusing, as this function also routes requests which are in the “strict router” format.

functions.name: loose_route_preloaded
functions.doc: The function is similar to `loose_route()`, but it returns 1 (true) when the Route header is preloaded (is in an initial request) and -1 (false) if processing of the Route header failed or it is for requests within dialog.

functions.name: loose_route_mode
functions.doc: The function is similar to `loose_route()`, but it accepts route mode bitmask as vmode parameter.

functions.name: record_route
functions.doc: The function adds a new Record-Route header field. The header field will be inserted in the message before any other Record-Route header fields.

functions.name: remove_record_route
functions.doc: The function removes the internal lumps added by record_route() functions.

functions.name: record_route_preset
functions.doc: This function will put the string params into Record-Route, avoid to use it unless you know what you are doing.

functions.name: record_route_advertised_address
functions.doc: The function adds a new Record-Route header field using the address given. The header field will be inserted in the message before any other Record-Route header fields.

functions.name: add_rr_param
functions.doc: Adds a parameter to the Record-Route URI (param must be in “;name=value” format. The function may be called also before or after the record_route(), record_route_advertised_address(), and record_route_preset() calls (see Section 5.4, “record_route([sparams])” or Section 5.7, “record_route_advertised_address(address)”)).

functions.name: check_route_param
functions.doc: The function checks if the URI parameters of the local Route header (corresponding to the local server) matches the given regular expression. It must be called after loose_route() (see Section 5.1, “loose_route()”).

functions.name: is_direction
functions.doc: The function checks the flow direction of in-dialog requests. This function uses the “ftag” parameter from the Route header, therefore the append_fromtag (see ??? module parameter must be enabled. Also this must be called only after loose_route() (see Section 5.1, “loose_route()”).

functions.name: rr_next_hop_route
functions.doc: The function returns 1 (true) if there is a Route header for the next hop address. It has to be used after loose_route(), when the local Route headers are processed.

params.name: default_interval
params.doc: The definition of the default interval of timers (if not present on the "timer" parameter)

params.name: timer
params.doc: The definition of a timer. The value of the parameter must have the following format: * "name=_string_;mode=_number_;interval=_number_"

params.name: exec
params.doc: Specify route to be executed on timer. The value of the parameter must have the following format: * "timer=_string_;route=_number_"

params.name: xavp_cfg
params.doc: The name of the xavp to be used internally by the module.

functions.name: rtjson_init_routes
functions.doc: Initialize routing based on JSON document stored in rtdoc parameter.

functions.name: rtjson_push_routes
functions.doc: Push the routes given in JSON document to rtjson_init_routes(rtdoc) to the internal fields used by Kamailio for routing.

functions.name: rtjson_next_route
functions.doc: To be used in failure_route for serial forking, to push the next route to the internal fields used by Kamailio for routing.

functions.name: rtjson_update_branch
functions.doc: To be used in branch_route if the JSON document had attributes that needs to be set for each branch.

params.name: log_file_name
params.doc: oRTP and MediaStreamer2 log file settings the log mask is not configurable : MESSAGE | WARNING | ERROR | FATAL levels are activated.

functions.name: rms_answer
functions.doc: Create a call leg with a SIP dialog and an RTP session call the event_route

functions.name: rms_hangup
functions.doc: Send a BYE, delete the RTP session and the media resources.

functions.name: rms_bridge
functions.doc: Bridge the incoming call, create a second call leg using a UAC in a B2BUA manner, this is needed in case we want to un-bridge later, a feature not currently implemented Call the specified event_route, defaulting to [rms:bridge].

functions.name: rms_dialog_check
functions.doc: Returns true if the current SIP message it handled/known by the RMS module, else it may be handled in any other way by Kamailio.

functions.name: rms_sip_request
functions.doc: This should be called for every in-dialog SIP request, it will be forwarded behaving as a B2BUA, the transaction will be suspended until the second leg replies.

functions.name: rms_play
functions.doc: Play a wav file, a resampler is automatically configured to resample and convert stereo to mono if needed.

params.name: rtpengine_sock
params.doc: Definition of socket(s) used to connect to (a set) RTP proxy. It may specify an IPv4/IPv6 UDP socket or a websocket URI.

params.name: rtpengine_disable_tout
params.doc: Once an RTP proxy was found unreachable and marked as disabled, the rtpengine module will not attempt to establish communication to that RTP proxy for rtpengine_disable_tout seconds.

params.name: aggressive_redetection
params.doc: This parameter determines what happens when all potential rtpengines are found to be unreachable. If enabled, the sip server will send pings to all rtpengines, else no rtpengine will be queried until its rtpengine_disable_tout timeout passes.

params.name: rtpengine_tout_ms
params.doc: Timeout value expressed in milliseconds in waiting for reply from RTP proxy.

params.name: rtpengine_allow_op
params.doc: Enable this setting to allow finishing the current sessions while denying new sessions for deactivated nodes.

params.name: queried_nodes_limit
params.doc: The total number of nodes inside a set (sets are configurable via rtpengine_sock function) to be queried before giving up establishing a session. This brings more flexibility in case checking all rtpengines would take too long. Max limit is 30.

params.name: rtpengine_retr
params.doc: How many times the module should retry to send and receive after timeout was generated.

params.name: extra_id_pv
params.doc: The parameter sets the PV definition to use when the “via-branch” parameter is used on rtpengine_delete(), rtpengine_offer(), rtpengine_answer() or rtpengine_manage() command.

params.name: setid_avp
params.doc: The parameter defines an AVP that, if set, determines which RTP proxy set rtpengine_offer(), rtpengine_answer(), rtpengine_delete(), and rtpengine_manage() functions use.

params.name: force_send_interface
params.doc: Forces all control messages between the SIP proxy and the RTP proxy to be sent from the specified local interface. Both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses are supported. If not specified, the default interface selected by the operating system will be used. Note: when rtpengine_sock is an IPv6 link-local address, one _must_ set this parameter in order to successfully connect to RTP engine. This is necessarily because OS needs additional scope_id hint to communicate over IPv6 link locals. The scope_id is resolved based on the given IPv6.

params.name: read_sdp_pv
params.doc: If this parameter is set to a valid AVP or script var specifier, rtpengine will take the input SDP from this pv instead of the message body.

params.name: write_sdp_pv
params.doc: If this parameter is set to a valid AVP or script var specifier, the SDP returned by rtpengine in the offer/answer operations is returned in the specified variable instead of the message body.

params.name: write_sdp_pv_mode
params.doc: If this parameter is set to 1, the returned SDP is written to pv and also set to message body.

params.name: rtp_inst_pvar
params.doc: A pseudo variable to store the chosen RTP Engine URI. If this parameter is set, the URI of the instance chosen will be stored in the given variable.

params.name: hash_table_size
params.doc: To maintain information about a selected rtp machine node for a given call, entries are added in a hashtable of (callid, node) pairs. This parameter sets the size of the hash table. Default value is 256.

params.name: hash_table_tout
params.doc: Number of seconds after an rtpengine hash table entry is marked for deletion. By default, this parameter is set to 3600 (seconds).

params.name: db_url
params.doc: The rtpengine database url. If present and valid, it activates database mode. In this mode the node information is read from database, not from configuration modparam parameters.

params.name: table_name
params.doc: The rtpengine table name. If database mode is activated (i.e. valid db_url), sets the name of the rtpengine table, on startup.

params.name: setid_col
params.doc: Column name for the "setid" in the rtpengine table. If database mode is activated (i.e. valid db_url), set the setid of rtp nodes according to this column, on startup. The MySQL value for this column should be INT UNSIGNED.

params.name: url_col
params.doc: Column name for the url in the rtpengine table. If database mode is activated (i.e. valid db_url), set the url of rtp nodes according to this column, on startup. The MySQL value for this column should be VARCHAR.

params.name: weight_col
params.doc: Column name for weight in the rtpengine table. If database mode is activated (i.e. valid db_url), set the weight of rtp nodes according to this column, on startup. The column value has priority over the URL weight. The MySQL value for this column should be INT UNSIGNED.

params.name: disabled_col
params.doc: Column name in the rtpengine table. If database mode is activated (i.e. valid db_url), set the state of rtp nodes according to this column, on startup. The MySQL value for this column should be INT.

params.name: setid_default
params.doc: The default set of nodes to be used.

params.name: media_duration
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to be filled in with the length of the media being played back after a call to “play_media”, expressed in milliseconds. It's set to -1 if the length of the media could not be determined.

params.name: mos_min_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the minimum encountered MOS (Mean Opinion Score) value for the call. The value typically has a range of 1.0 through 5.0.

params.name: mos_min_at_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the timestamp of when the minimum MOS value was encountered during the call, such as “0:30” for 30 seconds after the start of the call.

params.name: mos_min_packetloss_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the amount of packetloss in percent at the time the minimum MOS value was encountered;

params.name: mos_min_jitter_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the amount of jitter in milliseconds at the time the minimum MOS value was encountered;

params.name: mos_min_roundtrip_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the packet round-trip time in microseconds at the time the minimum MOS value was encountered;

params.name: mos_max_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the maximum encountered MOS value for the call. The value typically has a range of 1.0 through 5.0.

params.name: mos_max_at_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the timestamp of when the maximum MOS value was encountered during the call, such as “0:30” for 30 seconds after the start of the call.

params.name: mos_max_packetloss_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the amount of packetloss in percent at the time the maximum MOS value was encountered;

params.name: mos_max_jitter_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the amount of jitter in milliseconds at the time the maximum MOS value was encountered;

params.name: mos_max_roundtrip_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the packet round-trip time in microseconds at the time the maximum MOS value was encountered;

params.name: mos_average_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the average (median) MOS value for the call. The value typically has a range of 1.0 through 5.0.

params.name: mos_average_packetloss_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the average (median) amount of packetloss in percent present throughout the call.

params.name: mos_average_jitter_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the average (median) amount of jitter in milliseconds present throughout the call.

params.name: mos_average_roundtrip_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the average (median) packet round-trip time in milliseconds present throughout the call.

params.name: mos_average_samples_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the number of samples used to determine the other “average” MOS data points.

params.name: mos_A_label_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold a custom label used in rtpengine signalling. If set, all the statistics pseudovariables with the “_A” suffix will be filled in with statistics only from the call legs that match the label given in this variable. You need to fill this variable before invoking “rtpengine_delete”, “rtpengine_query”, or “rtpengine_manage”. Variable value should match the label= flag on “rtpengine_offer”, “rtpengine_answer”, or “rtpengine_manage”.

params.name: mos_min_A_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the minimum encountered MOS value for the call. The value typically has a range of 1.0 through 5.0.

params.name: mos_min_at_A_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the timestamp of when the minimum MOS value was encountered during the call, such as “0:30” for 30 seconds after the start of the call.

params.name: mos_min_packetloss_A_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the amount of packetloss in percent at the time the minimum MOS value was encountered;

params.name: mos_min_jitter_A_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the amount of jitter in milliseconds at the time the minimum MOS value was encountered;

params.name: mos_min_roundtrip_A_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the packet round-trip time in microseconds at the time the minimum MOS value was encountered;

params.name: mos_min_roundtrip_leg_A_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the packet round-trip time of the specific call leg in microseconds at the time the minimum MOS value was encountered;

params.name: mos_max_A_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the maximum encountered MOS value for the call. The value typically has a range of 1.0 through 5.0.

params.name: mos_max_at_A_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the timestamp of when the maximum MOS value was encountered during the call, such as “0:30” for 30 seconds after the start of the call.

params.name: mos_max_packetloss_A_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the amount of packetloss in percent at the time the maximum MOS value was encountered;

params.name: mos_max_jitter_A_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the amount of jitter in milliseconds at the time the maximum MOS value was encountered;

params.name: mos_max_roundtrip_A_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the packet round-trip time in microseconds at the time the maximum MOS value was encountered;

params.name: mos_max_roundtrip_leg_A_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the packet round-trip time of the specific call leg in microseconds at the time the maximum MOS value was encountered;

params.name: mos_average_A_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the average (median) MOS value for the call. The value typically has a range of 1.0 through 5.0.

params.name: mos_average_packetloss_A_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the average (median) amount of packetloss in percent present throughout the call.

params.name: mos_average_jitter_A_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the average (median) amount of jitter in milliseconds present throughout the call.

params.name: mos_average_roundtrip_A_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the average (median) packet round-trip time in microseconds present throughout the call.

params.name: mos_average_roundtrip_leg_A_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the average (median) packet round-trip time of the specific call leg in microseconds present throughout the call.

params.name: mos_average_samples_A_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the number of samples used to determine the other “average” MOS data points.

params.name: mos_B_label_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold a custom label used in rtpengine signalling. If set, all the statistics pseudovariables with the “_B” suffix will be filled in with statistics only from the call legs that match the label given in this variable. You need to fill this variable before invoking “rtpengine_delete”, “rtpengine_query”, or “rtpengine_manage”. Variable value should match the label= flag on “rtpengine_offer”, “rtpengine_answer”, or “rtpengine_manage”.

params.name: mos_min_B_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the minimum encountered MOS value for the call. The value typically has a range of 1.0 through 5.0.

params.name: mos_min_at_B_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the timestamp of when the minimum MOS value was encountered during the call, such as “0:30” for 30 seconds after the start of the call.

params.name: mos_min_packetloss_B_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the amount of packetloss in percent at the time the minimum MOS value was encountered;

params.name: mos_min_jitter_B_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the amount of jitter in milliseconds at the time the minimum MOS value was encountered;

params.name: mos_min_roundtrip_B_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the packet round-trip time in microseconds at the time the minimum MOS value was encountered;

params.name: mos_min_roundtrip_leg_B_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the packet round-trip time of the specific call leg in microseconds at the time the minimum MOS value was encountered;

params.name: mos_max_B_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the maximum encountered MOS value for the call. The value typically has a range of 1.0 through 5.0.

params.name: mos_max_at_B_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the timestamp of when the maximum MOS value was encountered during the call, such as “0:30” for 30 seconds after the start of the call.

params.name: mos_max_packetloss_B_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the amount of packetloss in percent at the time the maximum MOS value was encountered;

params.name: mos_max_jitter_B_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the amount of jitter in milliseconds at the time the maximum MOS value was encountered;

params.name: mos_max_roundtrip_B_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the packet round-trip time in microseconds at the time the maximum MOS value was encountered;

params.name: mos_max_roundtrip_leg_B_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the packet round-trip time of the specific call leg in microseconds at the time the maximum MOS value was encountered;

params.name: mos_average_B_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the average (median) MOS value for the call. The value typically has a range of 1.0 through 5.0.

params.name: mos_average_packetloss_B_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the average (median) amount of packetloss in percent present throughout the call.

params.name: mos_average_jitter_B_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the average (median) amount of jitter in milliseconds present throughout the call.

params.name: mos_average_roundtrip_B_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the average (median) packet round-trip time in microseconds present throughout the call.

params.name: mos_average_roundtrip_leg_B_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the average (median) packet round-trip time of the specific call leg in microseconds present throughout the call.

params.name: mos_average_samples_B_pv
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to hold the number of samples used to determine the other “average” MOS data points.

params.name: dtmf_event_callid
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to be filled in with the callid of the triggered dtmf event.

params.name: dtmf_event_source_tag
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to be filled in with the source tag that triggered the dtmf event.

params.name: dtmf_event_timestamp
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to be filled in with the timestamp when the dtmf event was triggered.

params.name: dtmf_event
params.doc: The name of a pseudovariable to be filled in with the triggered DTMF value.

params.name: control_cmd_tos
params.doc: The parameter is used to set the value of “type of service (tos)” for the control commands (such as rtpengine_offer(), rtpengine_answer() etc).

params.name: hash_algo
params.doc: The hashing algorithm to be used in node selection algorithm. There are two possibilities: SHA1 - 1 (calculate SHA1 hash over the Call-ID) or CRC32 - 2 (calculate crc32 sum over the callid). The legacy algorithm - 0 is not available anymore. If 0 is specified the default CRC32 will be used.

params.name: wsapi
params.doc: Configure a backend API for websocket usage. Currently the only supported setting is “lwsc” (libwebsockets). If unset, then the websocket protocol cannot be used.

params.name: dtmf_events_sock
params.doc: Definition of IPv4/IPv6 UDP socket used to receive dtmf events from RTPEngine.

params.name: ping_mode
params.doc: Specify if the RTPEngine instances have to be pinged at startup to detect if they are active. Set it to 0 to disable pinging and to 1 to activate pinging.

params.name: ping_interval
params.doc: Specify the interval in seconds between pings to all rtpengines registered.

params.name: enable_dmq
params.doc: If set to 1, will enable DMQ replication of hashtable of (callid, node) pairs.

functions.name: set_rtpengine_set
functions.doc: Sets the ID of the RTP proxy set to be used for the next rtpengine_delete(), rtpengine_offer(), rtpengine_answer() or rtpengine_manage() command. The parameter can be an integer or a config variable holding an integer.

functions.name: rtpengine_offer
functions.doc: Rewrites SDP body to ensure that media is passed through an RTP proxy. To be invoked on INVITE for the cases the SDP bodies are in INVITE and 200 OK and on 200 OK when SDP bodies are in 200 OK and ACK.

functions.name: rtpengine_answer
functions.doc: Rewrites SDP body to ensure that media is passed through an RTP proxy. To be invoked on 200 OK for the cases the SDP bodies are in INVITE and 200 OK and on ACK when SDP bodies are in 200 OK and ACK.

functions.name: rtpengine_info
functions.doc: Send an updated offer to rtpengine. This is meant to be used when processing Trickle ICE SDP Fragments that are carried in SIP INFO messages and are proxied to endpoints that do not support ICE. With a matching content type, the SDP fragment is used to update rtpengine's list of ICE candidates. No new SDP is returned and so the SIP INFO message should be consumed after calling this function.

functions.name: rtpengine_delete
functions.doc: Tears down the RTP proxy session for the current call. This populates the statistics pseudovariables (such “mos_min_pv” etc).

functions.name: rtpengine_destroy
functions.doc: Same as rtpengine_delete().

functions.name: rtpengine_query
functions.doc: Queries the RTP proxy about the current status and statistics of a running call. This populates the statistics pseudovariables (such “mos_min_pv” etc).

functions.name: rtpengine_query_v
functions.doc: Queries the RTP proxy about the current status and statistics of a running call, converts the response to JSON according to fmt and sets the variable var with the result.

functions.name: rtpengine_connect
functions.doc: Connects the media of two call parties directly without the need for a full offer/answer exchange. The media will be connected in the same way as it would through an offer/answer exchange. Transcoding will automatically be engaged if needed.

functions.name: rtpengine_manage
functions.doc: Manage the RTPEngine session - it combines the functionality of rtpengine_offer(), rtpengine_answer() and rtpengine_delete(), detecting internally based on message type and method which one to execute.

functions.name: rtpengine_subscribe_answer
functions.doc: Sends the SDP answer from the recording server to the rtpengine

functions.name: rtpengine_unsubscribe
functions.doc: Sends the SDP answer from the recording server to the rtpengine

functions.name: start_recording
functions.doc: This function will send a signal to the RTP relay to record the RTP stream flowing through it. See also the option “record-call=on” for rtpengine_manage()/rtpengine_offer(), which offers an alternative for call recording, saving also call metadata from SDP.

functions.name: stop_recording
functions.doc: This function will send a signal to the RTP relay to stop recording the RTP stream flowing through it. See also the option “record-call=off” for rtpengine_manage()/rtpengine_offer(), which offers an alternative for call recording.

functions.name: block_dtmf
functions.doc: This function will instruct the RTP proxy to start blocking DTMF event packets (RFC 4733). DTMF events will still be processed by the RTP proxy, but they won't be forwarded to the receiving peer.

functions.name: unblock_dtmf
functions.doc: Reverses the effects of a previously issued block_dtmf call. See above for a description of which flags can be used.

functions.name: block_media
functions.doc: Analogous to “block_dtmf”, but blocks media RTP packets instead of DTMF events. When media is blocked, DTMF events still pass through the RTP proxy.

functions.name: unblock_media
functions.doc: Analogous to “unblock_dtmf”, but applies to media RTP packets instead of DTMF events.

functions.name: silence_media
functions.doc: Identical to “block_media” except that media RTP packets are not simply blocked, but instead have their audio payload replaced by silence audio. This is only supported for certain trivial audio codecs (e.g. G.711, G.722).

functions.name: unsilence_media
functions.doc: Identical to “unblock_media” except that it's the counterpart to “silence_media”.

functions.name: start_forwarding
functions.doc: Controls the PCM forwarding feature of the recording daemon. Unlike the recording feature, PCM forwarding can be done directionally for individual call participants only, therefore this command takes the same flags as the media/DTMF blocking commands above.

functions.name: stop_forwarding
functions.doc: Analogous to “unblock_dtmf”, but controls the PCM forwarding feature instead of DTMF blocking.

functions.name: play_media
functions.doc: Instructs rtpengine to play a prerecorded announcement to the selected call participant, either from a local file or from a file stored in a database. The participant must be selected using the same flags as are described under the “block_dtmf” function. If none of these flags are given, then the “From” tag from the current SIP message context is used.

functions.name: stop_media
functions.doc: Stops the playback of media previously started by “play_media”. Media playback is automatically stopped when the end of the media file is reached, so this function is only useful to prematurely stop playback.

functions.name: play_dtmf
functions.doc: Injects a DTMF event into the media stream. Depending on which codecs were negotiated, this either injects an RFC 2833/4733 DTMF event, or an in-band PCM DTMF tone into the audio stream. The flag “inject DTMF” must have been present in both offer and answer messages when the call was established, which forces all audio to go through rtpengine's transcoding engine.

params.name: rtpproxy_sock
params.doc: Used to define the list of RTPProxy instances to connect to. These can be UNIX sockets or IPv4/IPv6 UDP sockets. Each modparam entry will insert sockets into a single set. If no set ID is given, the default set ID '0' will be used. To define multiple sets add the set number at the beginning of each parameter followed by '=='. Sockets can be weighted by adding '=#' to a socket where # is an integer. A socket with a weight of 2 will be chosen twice as often as one with a weight of 1.

params.name: rtpproxy_disable_tout
params.doc: Once RTPProxy was found unreachable and marked as disabled, the rtpproxy module will not attempt to establish communication to RTPProxy for rtpproxy_disable_tout seconds.

params.name: rtpproxy_tout
params.doc: Timeout value in waiting for reply from RTPProxy.

params.name: rtpproxy_retr
params.doc: How many times the module should retry to send and receive after timeout was generated.

params.name: nortpproxy_str
params.doc: This parameter sets the SDP attribute used by rtpproxy to mark the message's SDP attachment with information that it have already been changed.

params.name: timeout_socket
params.doc: The parameter sets the RTP timeout socket, which is transmitted to the RTP-Proxy. It will be used by the RTP proxy to signal back that a media stream timed out.

params.name: timeout_tag_pv
params.doc: The parameter devines the AVP of the string to be provided to the RTP-Proxy.

params.name: ice_candidate_priority_avp
params.doc: If specified and if value of the avp value is not 0, rtpproxy_manage function adds ICE relay candidate attributes to sdp stream(s) containing ICE candidate attributes.

params.name: extra_id_pv
params.doc: The parameter sets the PV definition to use when the “b” parameter is used on unforce_rtp_proxy(), rtpproxy_offer(), rtpproxy_answer() or rtpproxy_manage() command.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: The database URL to load rtp_proxy sets from. If this parameter is set, the module will attempt to load the rtpproxy sets from the specified database and will ignore any 'rtpproxy_sock' modparams.

params.name: table_name
params.doc: The name of the table containing the rtpproxy sets.

params.name: rtp_inst_pvar
params.doc: A pseudo variable to store the chosen RTPProxy address. If this parameter is set, the instance URL will be stored in the given variable.

functions.name: set_rtp_proxy_set
functions.doc: Sets the Id of the rtpproxy set to be used for the next unforce_rtp_proxy(), rtpproxy_offer(), rtpproxy_answer() or rtpproxy_manage() command. The parameter can be an integer or a config variable holding an integer.

functions.name: rtpproxy_offer
functions.doc: Rewrites SDP body to ensure that media is passed through an RTP proxy. To be invoked on INVITE for the cases the SDPs are in INVITE and 200 OK and on 200 OK when SDPs are in 200 OK and ACK.

functions.name: rtpproxy_answer
functions.doc: Rewrites SDP body to ensure that media is passed through an RTP proxy. To be invoked on 200 OK for the cases the SDPs are in INVITE and 200 OK and on ACK when SDPs are in 200 OK and ACK.

functions.name: rtpproxy_destroy
functions.doc: Tears down the RTPProxy session for the current call.

functions.name: unforce_rtp_proxy
functions.doc: Same as rtpproxy_destroy().

functions.name: rtpproxy_manage
functions.doc: Manage the RTPProxy session - it combines the functionality of rtpproxy_offer(), rtpproxy_answer() and unforce_rtpproxy(), detecting internally based on message type and method which one to execute.

functions.name: rtpproxy_stream2uac
functions.doc: Instruct the RTPproxy to stream prompt/announcement pre-encoded with the makeann command from the RTPproxy distribution. The uac/uas suffix selects who will hear the announcement relatively to the current transaction - UAC or UAS. For example invoking the rtpproxy_stream2uac in the request processing block on ACK transaction will play the prompt to the UA that has generated original INVITE and ACK while rtpproxy_stop_stream2uas on 183 in reply processing block will play the prompt to the UA that has generated 183.

functions.name: rtpproxy_stream2uas
functions.doc: See function rtpproxy_stream2uac(prompt_name, count).

functions.name: rtpproxy_stop_stream2uac
functions.doc: Stop streaming of announcement/prompt/MOH started previously by the respective rtpproxy_stream2xxx. The uac/uas suffix selects whose announcement relatively to tha current transaction should be stopped - UAC or UAS.

functions.name: rtpproxy_stop_stream2uas
functions.doc: See function rtpproxy_stop_stream2uac().

functions.name: start_recording
functions.doc: This function will send a signal to the RTP-Proxy to record the RTP stream on the RTP-Proxy. This function is only supported by Sippy RTPproxy at the moment!

params.name: http_timeout
params.doc: The interval in milliseconds after which the HTTP GET or POST query times out. It is the overall timeout, including DNS resolution, connecting time, redirects, and reading the response body. Slow DNS resolution may cause a request to exceed the timeout, because the DNS request cannot be interrupted with the available APIs. It takes precedence over http_timeout_read() and http_timeout_write(), but not http_timeout_connect. See also the comments in 'https://github.com/algesten/ureq/blob/main/src/agent.rs'.

params.name: http_timeout_connect
params.doc: The interval in milliseconds after which to give up on connecting to the HTTP/S server. If http_timeout is set, this one takes precedence. The library beneath has a default 30 seconds connect timeout.

params.name: http_timeout_read
params.doc: The interval in milliseconds after which the read on HTTP/S connection socket timeouts. If http_timeout is set, it takes precedence.

params.name: http_timeout_write
params.doc: The interval in milliseconds after which the write on HTTP/S connection socket timeouts. If http_timeout is set, it takes precedence.

params.name: http_tlsmode
params.doc: The mode to connect over TLS to HTTPS sites: 0 accept all certificates; 1 - accept trusted certificates.

params.name: http_reuse
params.doc: Set to 1 in order to reuse the connection for all requests (each Kamailio process has its own connection). Useful to avoid TCP connect (and TLS handshake) when all requests are performed against the same HTTP/S server.

params.name: http_retry
params.doc: How many times to retry if the HTTP request does not get a 200 OK response.

params.name: http_logtype
params.doc: Set the log type for libruxc http functions: 0 - stdout; 1 - syslog.

params.name: http_debug
params.doc: Set the debug mode for libruxc http functions: 0 - no debug; 1 - errors; 2 - debug.

functions.name: ruxc_http_get
functions.doc: Perform a HTTP GET request to "url", storing the response body in the "respv" variable. The "hdrs" can be empty string to skip setting them. The first two parameters can contain variables that are evaluated at runtime. The "respv" has to be the name of a writable variable.

functions.name: ruxc_http_post
functions.doc: Perform a HTTP POST request to "url", storing the response body in the "respv" variable. The "body" and "hdrs" can be empty strings to skip setting them. The first three parameters can contain variables that are evaluated at runtime. The "respv" has to be the name of a writable variable.

functions.name: ruxc_http_delete
functions.doc: Perform a HTTP DELETE request to "url", storing the response body in the "respv" variable. The "body" and "hdrs" can be empty strings to skip setting them. The first three parameters can contain variables that are evaluated at runtime. The "respv" has to be the name of a writable variable.

params.name: default_checks
params.doc: This parameter determines which of the checks from the sanity module are executed if no parameter was given to the sanity_check function call. By default all implemented checks are included in the execution of the sanity_check function. The integer value is the sum of the check numbers which should be executed by default.

params.name: uri_checks
params.doc: This parameter determines which URIs are going to be checked if the 'parse uri' will be executed.

params.name: proxy_require
params.doc: This parameter sets the list of supported SIP extensions for this Kamailio. The value is expected as a comma separated list (leading and trailing whitespaces are stripped from each token) of extensions. This list is separated into single tokens. Each token from a proxy require header will be compared with the tokens from this list.

params.name: autodrop
params.doc: This parameter controls whether the module drops the SIP message automatically if the sanity checks fail. Default value is 1 (auto drop). If set to 0, sanity_check() function will return -1 (false) to configuration file, allowing to write log messages for example - be sure you “exit” execution of config without sending a SIP reply because it is sent by module itself.

params.name: noreply
params.doc: If set to 1, then the module does not send a SIP reply internally in case there is an error detected when performing the sanity checks. There is the option to send the reply from config file with functions from sl or tm module as well as sanity_reply() from this module.

functions.name: sanity_check
functions.doc: This function makes a row of sanity checks over the given SIP request. The behavior of the function is also controlled by autodrop parameter. If autodrop=0, the function returns false (-1) if one of the checks failed. When autodrop=1, the function stops the execution of configuration file. In both cases, if one of the checks fails the module sends a precise error reply via SL send_reply(). Thus there is no need to reply with a generic error message.

functions.name: sanity_reply
functions.doc: Send a SIP reply using the code and reason text set internally by the module when detecting errors while performing the sanity checks. It is done only when parameter noreply is set to 1.

params.name: hash_table_size
params.doc: Size, as a power of two, of the shared memory hash table containing the call-info subscriptions and the appearance state. A larger power of two means better performance (fewer collisions, making for fewer subscriber URI comparisons) at the expense of increased shared memory use.

params.name: call_info_max_expires
params.doc: The maximum allowed call-info subscription time in seconds.

params.name: line_seize_max_expires
