params.doc: The maximum allowed line-seize subscription time in seconds.

params.name: purge_expired_interval
params.doc: The period of time in seconds between purges of expired call-info and line-seize subscriptions.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: URL of database to which subscribers will be written.

params.name: subs_table
params.doc: Name of the database table where call-info subscriptions are written.

params.name: db_update_interval
params.doc: Period in seconds between writes of call-info subscriber information to the database.

params.name: onhold_bflag
params.doc: When bflag is set the media will be treated as on-hold and sdp parse will be skipped. If the bflag is not set the sdp will be parsed to detect on-hold.

params.name: server_address
params.doc: The server address which will become the value of Contact header filed for reply messages.

params.name: contact_fallback
params.doc: contact used if defined when no contact is found in processed message.

params.name: from_uri_avp
params.doc: avp that will store the From URI used.

params.name: to_uri_avp
params.doc: avp that will store the To URI used.

functions.name: sca_handle_subscribe
functions.doc: The function handling call-info and line-seize SUBSCRIBE requests. It stores or updates the subscriptions in shared memory, and sends NOTIFYs to the subscriber and other members of the group as needed.

functions.name: sca_call_info_update
functions.doc: * mask - integer (optional) controls what to check as shared line (BOTH, CALLER, CALLEE) + 0 - SCA_CALL_INFO_SHARED_NONE (default) check both + 1 - SCA_CALL_INFO_SHARED_CALLER + 2 - SCA_CALL_INFO_SHARED_CALLEE * to - string (optional) string to use as To and skip parsing To header from the message. The parameter allows pseudo-variables usage * from - string (optional) string to use as From and skip parsing From header from the message. The parameter allows pseudo-variables usage

params.name: sctp_socket_rcvbuf
params.doc: Size for the sctp socket receive buffer.

params.name: sctp_socket_sndbuf
params.doc: Size for the sctp socket send buffer.

params.name: sctp_autoclose
params.doc: Number of seconds before autoclosing an idle association. Can be changed at runtime, but it will affect only new associations.

params.name: sctp_send_ttl
params.doc: Number of milliseconds before an unsent message/chunk is dropped. Can be changed at runtime.

params.name: sctp_send_retries
params.doc: How many times to attempt re-sending a message on a re-opened association, if the sctp stack did give up sending it (it's not related to sctp protocol level retransmission). Useful to improve reliability with peers that reboot/restart or fail over to another machine.

params.name: sctp_assoc_tracking
params.doc: Controls whether or not sctp associations are tracked inside Kamailio. Turning it off would result in less memory being used and slightly better performance, but it will also disable some other features that depend on it (e.g. sctp_assoc_reuse).

params.name: sctp_assoc_reuse
params.doc: Controls sctp association reuse. For now only association reuse for replies is affected by it. Default is on. Depends on sctp_assoc_tracking being on.

params.name: sctp_max_assocs
params.doc: Maximum number of allowed open sctp associations. -1 means maximum allowed by the OS. Default: -1. Can be changed at runtime (e.g.: kamctl rpc cfg.set_now_int sctp max_assocs 10). When the maximum associations number is exceeded and a new associations is opened by a remote host, the association will be immediately closed. However it is possible that some sip packets get through (especially if they are sent early, as part of the 4-way handshake).

params.name: sctp_srto_initial
params.doc: Initial value of the retransmission timeout (in milliseconds), used in RTO calculations.

params.name: sctp_srto_max
params.doc: Maximum value of the retransmission timeout (RTO) in milliseconds.

params.name: sctp_srto_min
params.doc: Minimum value of the retransmission timeout (RTO) in milliseconds.

params.name: sctp_asocmaxrxt
params.doc: Maximum retransmissions attempts per association. It should be set to sctp_pathmaxrxt * no. of expected paths.

params.name: sctp_init_max_attempts
params.doc: Maximum INIT retransmission attempts.

params.name: sctp_init_max_timeo
params.doc: Maximum INIT retransmission timeout (RTO max for INIT) in milliseconds.

params.name: sctp_hbinterval
params.doc: SCTP heartbeat interval. Setting it to -1 will disable the heartbeats.

params.name: sctp_pathmaxrxt
params.doc: Maximum retransmission attempts per path (see also sctp_asocmaxrxt).

params.name: sctp_sack_delay
params.doc: Delay until an ACK is generated after receiving a packet (in milliseconds).

params.name: sctp_sack_freq
params.doc: Number of packets received before an ACK is sent (without waiting for the sack_delay to expire). Default: OS specific.

params.name: sctp_max_burst
params.doc: Maximum burst of packets that can be emitted by an association.

functions.name: sdp_remove_codecs_by_id
functions.doc: Remove the codecs provided in the parameter 'list' from all media streams found in SDP payload. The parameter 'list' must be one item or a comma separated list of numeric codec IDs. The parameter can be a static string or a variable holding the list of numeric codec IDs.

functions.name: sdp_remove_codecs_by_name
functions.doc: Remove the codecs provided in the parameter 'list' from all media streams found in SDP payload. The parameter 'list' must be one item or a comma separated list of codec names. The parameter can be a static string or a variable holding the list of codec names.

functions.name: sdp_remove_line_by_prefix
functions.doc: Remove all SDP attribute lines beginning with 'string' in all media streams.

functions.name: sdp_keep_codecs_by_id
functions.doc: Keep only the codecs provided in the parameter 'list' from all media streams found in SDP payload. The parameter 'list' must be one item or a comma separated list of numeric codec IDs. The parameter can be a static string or a variable holding the list of numeric codec IDs.

functions.name: sdp_keep_codecs_by_name
functions.doc: Keep only the codecs provided in the parameter 'list' from all media streams found in SDP payload. The parameter 'list' must be one or a comma separated list of codec names. The parameter can be a static string or a variable holding the list of codec names.

functions.name: sdp_with_media
functions.doc: Return true if the SDP has 'media=type ...' line. Useful to check the content of the RTP sessions, such as 'audio' or 'video'. The parameter can be static string or variable holding the media type.

functions.name: sdp_with_active_media
functions.doc: Return true if the SDP has 'media=type ...' line and the media is active. Useful to check the content of the RTP sessions, such as 'audio' or 'video'. Active media means the port is non-zero and the direction is not "inactive" The parameter can be static string or variable holding the media type.

functions.name: sdp_remove_media
functions.doc: Remove the streams that match on 'm=type ...' line. The parameter can be static string or variable holding the media type.

functions.name: sdp_with_transport
functions.doc: Return true if the SDP has 'media=media port type ...' line. Useful to check the transport of the RTP sessions, such as 'RTP/AVP', 'RTP/SAVP', 'RTP/SAVPF' or 'UDP/TLS/RTP/SAVPF'. The parameter can be static string or variable holding the transport type. The function does an exact match of the strings.

functions.name: sdp_with_transport_like
functions.doc: Returns true if the SDP has 'media=media port type ...' line, where type contains the string in the parameter. The parameter can be static string or variable holding a string.

functions.name: sdp_transport
functions.doc: Assigns common media transport (if any) of 'm' lines to pv argument. Returns 1 if common media transport was found, -2 if there was no common media transport, and -1 in case of error.

functions.name: sdp_remove_transport
functions.doc: Remove the streams that match on 'm=media port type ...' line. The parameter can be static string or variable holding the transport type.

functions.name: sdp_with_codecs_by_id
functions.doc: Returns true if any of the codecs provided in the parameter 'list' from all media streams is found in SDP payload. The parameter 'list' must be one or a comma separated list of numeric codec IDs. The parameter can be a static string or a variable holding the list of numeric codec IDs.

functions.name: sdp_with_codecs_by_name
functions.doc: Returns true if any of the codecs provided in the parameter 'list' from all media streams is found in SDP payload. The parameter 'list' must be one item or a comma separated list of codec names. The parameter can be a static string or a variable holding the list of codec names.

functions.name: sdp_print
functions.doc: Print the SDP internal structure to log 'level'. The parameter can be static integer or variable holding the integer value of the log level.

functions.name: sdp_get
functions.doc: Store the SDP part of message body in an AVP. Return 1 if SDP is found, -1 on error and -2 if there is no SDP part in the message body.

functions.name: sdp_content
functions.doc: Return true if the SIP message has SDP body or a SDP part in body. If an argument is given, the function does not parse message body, but returns true if Content-Type is "application/sdp" or if that string exists in "multipart/mixed" body.

functions.name: sdp_with_ice
functions.doc: Return true if the SIP message has SDP body that contains ICE candidate attribute(s).

functions.name: sdp_get_line_startswith
functions.doc: Store the search part of SDP body message with line beginning with 'string' in an AVP. Return 1 if 'string' is found in SDP, -1 on error and -2 if there is no SDP part in the message body. The second parameter can contain pseudo-variables.

functions.name: sdp_get_address_family
functions.doc: It helps to get IP address family at c line from sdp body. It returns -1 on error, 4 for IP4 and 6 for IP6

functions.name: sdp_iterator_start
functions.doc: Start an iterator for lines in the body of the current SIP message. The parameter iname is used to identify the iterator. There can be up to 4 iterators at the same time, with different name.

functions.name: sdp_iterator_end
functions.doc: Close the iterator identified by iname parameter. The iname value must be the same used for sdp_iterator_start().

functions.name: sdp_iterator_next
functions.doc: Move the iterator to the next line in the body. It must be called also after sdp_iterator_start() to get the first header.

functions.name: sdp_iterator_rm
functions.doc: Remove the body line at the current iterator position.

functions.name: sdp_iterator_append
functions.doc: Add text after the line at the current iterator possition.

functions.name: sdp_iterator_insert
functions.doc: Add text before the line at the current iterator possition.

params.name: listen_sockets
params.doc: The listen_sockets string tells SEAS where to listen for incoming connections of Application Servers. It has the form: "ip:port". SEAS will open two server-sockets on that IP, at the specified port, and another at port+1. Application Servers must be configured to connect to that port.

functions.name: as_relay_t
functions.doc: Creates a new transaction (if it isn't already created) and sends the SIP Request and transaction information to the Application Server specified in the parameter. Every Application Server connected to Kamailio through the SEAS module, must be identified with a different name.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: Database URL.

params.name: table_name
params.doc: Name of the table used to store the blacklisted and whitelisted values.

params.name: action_col
params.doc: Name of database column containing the type of list. The possible values are:

params.name: type_col
params.doc: Name of database column containing the type of values. The possible values are:

params.name: data_col
params.doc: Name of database column containing blacklisted and whitelisted values.

params.name: dst_exact_match
params.doc: This value is used in the destinations blacklist and corresponds to the numbers that we want to prevent calling. If the value is 1, the call will appear as blacklisted if the destination is exactly the same. If the value is 0, every destination whose number begins with a number appearing on the destination blacklist will be rejected.

params.name: reload_delta
params.doc: The number of seconds that have to be waited before executing a new RPC reload. By default there is a rate limiting of maximum one reload in five seconds. If set to 0, no rate limit is configured.

params.name: cleanup_interval
params.doc: The number of seconds that have to be wait before cleanup the previous values from memory after a RPC reload.

functions.name: secf_check_ip
functions.doc: It checks if the source IP address is blacklisted. The search is approximate and data stored in the database will be compared as a prefix. For example, if we have blacklisted IP address 192.168.1. all messages from IPs like 192.168.1.% will be rejected.

functions.name: secf_check_ua
functions.doc: It checks if the user-agent is blacklisted. The search is approximate and the comparison will be made using the values of the database as a prefix. If we add to the user-agent blacklist the word sipcli, every message whose user-agent is named, for example, sipcli/1.6 or sipcli/1.8 will be blocked. It is very useful to block different versions of the same program.

functions.name: secf_check_country
functions.doc: Similar to secf_check_ua. It checks if the country (IP address) is blacklisted. Geoip module must be loaded to get the country code.

functions.name: secf_check_from_hdr
functions.doc: It checks if any value of from header is blacklisted. It checks if from name or from user are in the users blacklist or whitelist. It also checks if the from domain is in the domains blacklist or whitelist. The blacklisted value will be used as a prefix and if we block, for example, the user sipvicious, all users whose name starts with this word will be considered as blacklisted.

functions.name: secf_check_to_hdr
functions.doc: Do the same as secf_check_from_hdr function but with the to header.

functions.name: secf_check_contact_hdr
functions.doc: Do the same as secf_check_from_hdr function but with the contact header.

functions.name: secf_check_dst
functions.doc: It checks if the destination number is blacklisted. It must be user for INVITE messages. If the value of dst_exact_match is 1, the call will appear as blacklisted if the destination is exactly the same. If the value is 0, every destination whose number begins with a number appearing on the destination blacklist will be rejected.

functions.name: secf_check_sqli_hdr
functions.doc: Search for illegal characters in the given value.

functions.name: secf_check_sqli_all
functions.doc: Search for illegal characters in several headers (user-agent, from, to and contact). If illegal characters are found the message will be dropped.

params.name: expire
params.doc: The interval in seconds after which the Identity header JWT is considered to be expired.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: The interval in seconds after which the HTTP GET operation to download the public key times out.

params.name: cache_dir
params.doc: The path to the directory where to save cached public keys. If set, it activates the public key file caching in the libsecsipid library.

params.name: cache_expire
params.doc: The interval in seconds after which a cached public key is considered expired. This value is passed to the libsecsipid library.

params.name: modproc
params.doc: The name of or the path to the required per-process API module.

params.name: libopt
params.doc: Set a libsecsipid option. The value has to be name=value. The parameter can be set many times.

functions.name: secsipid_check_identity
functions.doc: Check the validity of the Identity header using the public keys stored in the file specified by "keyPath". If the parameter is empty, the function is downloading the public key using the URL from "info" parameter of the Identity header, using the value of "timeout" parameter to limit the download time. The validity of the JWT body in the Identity header is also checked against the "expire" parameter.

functions.name: secsipid_check_identity_pubkey
functions.doc: Similar to secsipid_check_identity() with the public key value provided in the parameter.

functions.name: secsipid_check
functions.doc: Check the validity of the "sIdentity" parameter using the public keys stored in the file specified by "keyPath". If the keyPath parameter is empty, the function is downloading the public key using the URL from "info" parameter of the sIdentity, using the value of "timeout" parameter to limit the download time. The validity of the JWT in the sIdentity value is also checked against the "expire" parameter.

functions.name: secsipid_verify
functions.doc: Check the validity of the "sIdentity" parameter using the key value given in the parameter "keyVal". The validity of the JWT in the sIdentity value is also checked against the "expire" parameter.

functions.name: secsipid_get_url
functions.doc: Get the content of a URL and store the result in a variable. The result is cached by libsecsipid, if caching is enabled.

functions.name: secsipid_add_identity
functions.detail: secsipid_add_identity(origTN, destTN, attest, origID, x5u, keyPath)
functions.doc: Add Identity header using the private key specified by "keyPath" to sign the JWT body. If origID is empty, a UUID string is generated to fill the field. The origTN represents the origination telephone number; destTN represents the destination telephone number; x5u is the HTTP URL referencing to the public key that should be used to verify the signature; attest represents the attestation level (should be "A", "B" or "C").

functions.name: secsipid_build_identity
functions.detail: secsipid_build_identity(origTN, destTN, attest, origID, x5u, keyPath)
functions.doc: Build Identity value using the key specified by private "keyPath" to sign the JWT body. If origID is empty, a UUID string is generated to fill the field. The origTN represents the origination telephone number; destTN represents the destination telephone number; x5u is the HTTP URL referencing to the public key that should be used to verify the signature; attest represents the attestation level (should be "A", "B" or "C"). On success, the Indentity value is stored in variable $secsipid(val). It also sets $secsipid(ret) to the return value of the libsecsipid functions.

functions.name: secsipid_sign
functions.doc: Build Identity value using the private key specified by "keyPath" to sign the JWT body. The sheaders and spayload have to be string representation of JSON headers and payload to be signed. On success, the Indentity value is stored in variable $secsipid(val). It also sets $secsipid(ret) to the return value of the libsecsipid functions.

functions.name: secsipid_sign_prvkey
functions.doc: Build Identity value using the private key given by "keyData" to sign the JWT body. The sheaders and spayload have to be string representation of JSON headers and payload to be signed. On success, the Indentity value is stored in variable $secsipid(val). It also sets $secsipid(ret) to the return value of the libsecsipid functions.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: Database URL.

params.name: table_name
params.doc: Name of the table's name used to store the SIP messages. Can contain multiple tables, separated by "|".

params.name: mt_mode
params.doc: Name of the mode used for storing data in multiple tables. Modes can be "rand" (random), "round_robin" (use a round_robin algorithm) or "hash" (use hashing to determine the table to store). These modes are only triggered if there is more than one table specified in table_name parameter, separated by "|".

params.name: hash_source
params.doc: The field of the SIP message used for hashing, when mt_mode is set to "hash". The value can be "call_id", "to_user" or "from_user".

params.name: db_insert_mode
params.doc: If set to 1, use INSERT DELAYED to store sip message into capture table when the DB driver has support for it. If no INSERT DELAYED support is offered by DB driver, then standard INSERT is used.

params.name: capture_on
params.doc: Parameter to enable/disable capture globally (on(1)/off(0))

params.name: capture_mode
params.doc: This parameter can be used for defining a capture mode which can be used in the sip_capture calls as a parameter. A capture mode has a name and some parameters. It must be defined in the format: name=>param1=val1;param2=val2;... The parameters are db_url, table_name, mt_mode and hash_source (optional). Multiple capture modes can be defined by using this parameter multiple times. After this, the capture modes can be used like: sip_capture ("", "CAPTURE_MODE");

params.name: hep_capture_on
params.doc: Parameter to enable/disable capture of HEP (on(1)/off(0))

params.name: raw_ipip_capture_on
params.doc: Parameter to enable/disable IPIP capturing (on(1)/off(0))

params.name: raw_moni_capture_on
params.doc: Parameter to enable/disable monitoring/mirroring port capturing (on(1)/off(0)) Only one mode on raw socket can be enabled! Monitoring port capturing currently supported only on Linux.

params.name: raw_socket_listen
params.doc: Parameter indicate a listen IP address of RAW socket for IPIP capturing. You can also define a port/portrange for IPIP/Mirroring mode, to capture SIP messages in specific ports:

params.name: raw_interface
params.doc: Name of the interface to bind on the raw socket.

params.name: raw_sock_children
params.doc: Parameter define how many children that must be created to listen the raw socket.

params.name: promiscuous_on
params.doc: Parameter to enable/disable promiscuous mode on the raw socket. Linux only.

params.name: raw_moni_bpf_on
params.doc: Activate Linux Socket Filter (LSF based on BPF) on the mirroring interface. The structure is defined in linux/filter.h. The default LSF accept a port/portrange from the raw_socket_listen param. Currently LSF supported only on Linux.

params.name: capture_node
params.doc: Name of the capture node.

params.name: insert_retries
params.doc: The number of times Kamailio should retry to write to the Homer database in case the first attempt failed. The retry is also limited timewise by the insert_retry_timeout parameter. Values allowed range from 0 to 500.

params.name: insert_retry_timeout
params.doc: The time limit in seconds Kamailio retries to write to the Homer database in case the first attempt failed. This parameter is only used together with the insert_retries parameter. Values allowed range from 0 to 300.

params.name: callid_aleg_header
params.doc: Header name used to correlate A-leg with B-leg. It can take a list of headers, separated by semicolon, e.g. "X-CID0;X-CID1". First match wins.

params.name: topoh_unmask
params.doc: If set to 1, call-id will be unmasked using topoh module api (topoh module must be loaded in this case).

params.name: nonsip_hook
params.doc: If set to 1, event route sipcapture:siprequest is run when HEP message is received.

params.name: event_callback
params.doc: The name of the function in the kemi configuration file (embedded scripting language such as Lua, Python, ...) to be executed instead of event_route[...] blocks.

params.name: capture_bad_msgs
params.doc: If set to something different than 0, tries to capture also the broken SIP messages.

functions.name: sip_capture
functions.doc: Store the current processed HEP/IPIP SIP message in a database. It is stored in the form prior applying changes made to it.

functions.name: report_capture
functions.doc: Store the current processed HEP REPORT message in a database.

functions.name: float2int
functions.doc: Return the value of atof(fval) * atoi(ival). On case the result is 0, then -1 is returned.

functions.name: sip_capture_forward
functions.doc: Forward the HEP packet to an address specified by the parameter uri (it has to be a sip uri format). The function should be used inside event_route[sipcapture:request]. After using this function, add a return 0 in order to stop processing further the packet in the local Kamailio instance.

params.name: enable
params.doc: Enable sipdump activity.

params.name: mode
params.doc: Set the type of activity done by the module, the value can be set based on flags index: 0 (value 1) - write to text files; 1 (value 2) - execute event route; 2 (value 4) - write to pcap files; 3 (value 8) - insert the P-KSR-SIPDump header with meta data inside the SIP message written in pcap file.

params.name: wait
params.doc: Wait time (microseconds) when no SIP traffic is received (for wait_time = 0).

params.name: wait_mode
params.doc: If set to 1, the module uses a pthread mutex and contion to signal when SIP messages are available to the writer process. It should use less CPU when idle (on no SIP traffic) than the default polling on timer, but be sure that the OS supports process-shared pthread mutexes and conditions (latest Linux distros have support for them).

params.name: rotate
params.doc: Time interval in seconds to rotate files.

params.name: folder
params.doc: Path to the folder where to save the files.

params.name: fprefix
params.doc: File name prefix. The date is appended to this prefix in the format yyyy-mm-dd--hh-mm-ss. The extension of the text file is ".data", of the meta file is ".meta" and of the pcap file is ".pcap".

params.name: fage
params.doc: Age of created files (in seconds) to be removed if they become older. Cleanup is done on a timer routine running every 600 seconds.

params.name: fagex
params.doc: Age as a time expression for the created files to be removed if they become older. It overwrites the 'fage' parameter. The value can be numbers followed by time units: d - days; h - hours; m - minutes; s - seconds.

params.name: event_callback
params.doc: Name of the KEMI function to be executed instead of the event route.

functions.name: sipdump_send
functions.doc: Send the details of the current SIP message to the writer process and get it stored in the file.

functions.name: sj_serialize
functions.doc: Do the serialization of SIP message attributes into a JSON document.

params.name: hash_size
params.doc: Number of slots in the hash table. It should be power of 2.

params.name: expire
params.doc: Number of seconds until the stored message content expires.

params.name: timer_interval
params.doc: Number of seconds to run the timer routine.

params.name: timer_procs
params.doc: Number of timer processes.

functions.name: sr_msg_push
functions.doc: Push the message content to hash table and associate it with `msgid`. The Call-Id and msgid are needed to pull the message. The rmode is reserved for repo mode, use 0.

functions.name: sr_msg_pull
functions.doc: Pull the message content and execute the route block 'rname'. If rmode is set to "1", the item of the message is removed from siprepo storage, use "0" to keep it.

functions.name: sr_msg_async_pull
functions.doc: Pull the message content and execute the route block 'rname' via async group 'gname'. If rmode is set to "1", the item of the message is removed from siprepo storage, use "0" to keep it.

functions.name: sr_msg_rm
functions.doc: Remove the item of the message from the siprepo storage.

functions.name: sr_msg_check
functions.doc: Check if the message is stored.

functions.name: sipt_destination
functions.doc: updates the IAM in the body if it exists, setting the called party number to “destination” with the nature address specified in “nai” and decrementing the hop counter value if present. If the hop counter header is missing it will be added with the value of “hops”. If “terminator” is set to 1, then F will be appended to digit string to indicate the number is complete (default).

functions.name: sipt_set_calling
functions.doc: updates the IAM in the body if it exists, setting (or adding) the calling party number to “origin” with the nature address specified in “nai” and setting the presentation and screening values to “presentation” and “screening”.

functions.name: sipt_forwarding
functions.doc: updates the IAM in the body if it exists, setting (or adding) the forwarding number to “origin” with the nature address specified in “nai”.

functions.name: sipt_has_isup_body
functions.doc: The function returns true if the SIP message has an ISUP body attached.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: Database URL.

params.name: table
params.doc: Name of the table where to store the SIP messages.

params.name: trace_flag
params.doc: Which flag is used to mark messages to trace without traced user.

params.name: trace_on
params.doc: Parameter to enable/disable trace (on(1)/off(0))

params.name: traced_user_avp
params.doc: The name of the AVP storing the SIP URI of the traced user. If the AVP is set, messages are stored in a database table and the “traced_user” column is filled with AVP's value. You can store the message many times for many users by having multiple values for this AVP.

params.name: trace_table_avp
params.doc: The name of the AVP storing the name of the table where to store the SIP messages. If it is not set, the value of “table” parameter is used. In this way one can select dynamically where to store the traced messages. The table must exist, and must have the same structure as the “sip_trace” table.

params.name: duplicate_uri
params.doc: The address in form of a SIP URI where to send a duplicate of traced message.

params.name: trace_to_database
params.doc: Parameter to enable/disable inserts to the database from this Kamailio.

params.name: trace_local_ip
params.doc: The address to be used in “fromip” field for locally generated messages. If not set, the module sets it to the address of the socket that will be used to send the message.

params.name: trace_sl_acks
params.doc: Parameter to enable/disable tracing of SL-filtered ACKs (on=1 / off=0).

params.name: xheaders_write
params.doc: Parameter to enable/disable writing of x-headers.

params.name: xheaders_read
params.doc: Parameter to enable/disable reading of x-headers.

params.name: hep_mode_on
params.doc: Parameter to enable/disable Homer encapsulate mode (on(1)/off(0))

params.name: hep_version
params.doc: The parameter indicate the version of the HEP protocol. Can be “1”, “2” or “3”. In HEPv2 and HEPv3 the timestamp and capture agent ID will be included in the HEP header.

params.name: hep_capture_id
params.doc: The parameter indicate the capture agent ID for the HEPv2 or HEPv3 protocol. Limitation: 16-bit integer for HEPv2, 32-bit for HEPv3.

params.name: trace_db_mode
params.doc: If set to 1, the module uses “INSERT DELAYED” to store to database (when it is available, otherwise falls back to “INSERT”).

params.name: trace_delayed
params.doc: Kept for backward compatibily, use trace_db_mode instead.

params.name: send_sock_name
params.doc: The name of the local listen socket from where to send the duplicated traffic via SIP or HEP. In the absence of this parameter Kamailio automatically picks an interface. It has priority over 'send_sock_addr' parameter.

params.name: send_sock_addr
params.doc: The local interface in the form of SIP URI from where to send the duplicated traffic. In the absence of this parameter Kamailio automatically picks an interface.

params.name: force_send_sock
params.doc: It is the same as 'send_sock_addr' parameter, this being kept for backward compatibility when 'send_sock_name' and 'send_sock_addr' were introduced.

params.name: trace_init_mode
params.doc: Control what tracing modes are initialized.

params.name: trace_mode
params.doc: If not set to 0, the module uses core events triggered when receiving or sending SIP traffic to store it to database or mirror it to a SIP capture server using HEP or UDP forwarding. It will automatically do the handling of all SIP traffic. It is no longer needed to set the siptrace flag per request or execute sip_trace(), if it is done, then the storing and mirroring is duplicated.

params.name: data_mode
params.doc: A set of flags to control what data is used for the trace. If flag 1 (value 1) is set, then advertised address (when set) is used instead of socket bind address.

params.name: auth_key
params.doc: A string with an authorization key. Supported on HEPv3 only.

params.name: evcb_msg
params.doc: Set the name of KEMI function to be executed instead of event_route[siptrace:msg].

params.name: trace_dialog_ack
params.doc: Enable tracing of in-dialog ACK. Before this param, one must have set the onsend() route and captured the outgoing ACK there.

params.name: trace_dialog_spiral
params.doc: Enable tracing of dialog spirals. A spiraled dialog is a dialog established by a SIP INVITE that loops back to the same kamailio (as next hop). Right now, inside the siptrace code, a spiraled dialog is identified by (*params->param == NULL).

functions.name: sip_trace
functions.doc: Store or forward the current processed SIP message/transaction/dialog in a database. It is stored in the form prior applying changes made to it. Based on mode, one can trace the current message('m'), the current transaction('t') or the current dialog('d'). If no mode is given, it falls back to the default mode - transaction tracking when trace_flag is set, otherwise only the current message.

functions.name: sip_trace_mode
functions.doc: Set the tracing mode: message, transaction or dialog. Only the first character of the parameter matters: m or M for message; t or T for transaction; d or D for dialog.

functions.name: sip_trace_msg
functions.doc: Send the value of vmsg to the HEP capture server located at daddr, by setting saddr as source address and taddr as target address for vmsg. Correlation ID can be provided with corrid parameter or left as an empty string. The saddr and taddr have to be provided in socket address format (proto:ip:port) and the daddr in SIP URI format.

functions.name: hlog
functions.doc: Sends a log event as a HEP3 packet to the homer host configured in duplicate_uri.

params.name: options_accept
params.doc: This parameter is the content of the Accept header field. Note: it is not clearly written in RFC3261 if a proxy should accept any content (the default “*/*”) because it does not care about content. Or if it does not accept any content, which is “”.

params.name: options_accept_encoding
params.doc: This parameter is the content of the Accept-Encoding header field. Please do not change the default value because Kamailio does not support any encodings yet.

params.name: contact_flds_separator
params.doc: First char of this parameter is used as separator for encoding/decoding Contact header.

params.name: options_accept_language
params.doc: This parameter is the content of the Accept-Language header field. You can set any language code which you prefer for error descriptions from other devices, but presumably there are not many devices around which support other languages than the default English.

params.name: options_support
params.doc: This parameter is the content of the Support header field, indicating SIP extensions. Please do not change the default value, because Kamailio currently does not support any of the SIP extensions registered at the IANA.

params.name: rpid_prefix
params.doc: Prefix to be added to Remote-Party-ID header field just before the URI returned from either radius or database.

params.name: rpid_suffix
params.doc: Suffix to be added to Remote-Party-ID header field after the URI returned from either radius or database.

params.name: rpid_avp
params.doc: Full AVP specification for the AVP which stores the RPID value. It used to transport the RPID value from authentication backend modules (auth_db or auth_radius) or from script to the auth function append_rpid_hf and is_rpid_user_e164.

params.name: e164_max_len
params.doc: The maximum length for checking e164 numbers, including the leading '+'.

functions.name: options_reply
functions.doc: This function checks if the request method is OPTIONS and if the request URI does not contain a username. If both are true the request will be answered stateless with “200 OK” and the capabilities from the modules parameters.

functions.name: is_user
functions.doc: Check if the username in credentials matches the given username.

functions.name: has_totag
functions.doc: Check if To header field uri contains tag parameter.

functions.name: uri_param
functions.doc: Find if Request URI has a given parameter with no value

functions.name: uri_param
functions.doc: Find if Request URI has a given parameter with matching value

functions.name: uri_param_any
functions.doc: Find if Request URI has a given parameter with or without value.

functions.name: add_uri_param
functions.doc: Add to RURI a parameter (name=value);

functions.name: get_uri_param
functions.doc: Get the value of RURI parameter.

functions.name: uri_param_rm
functions.doc: Remove parameter from Request URI.

functions.name: tel2sip
functions.doc: Converts URI in first param (pseudo variable or string) to SIP URI, if it is a tel URI. If conversion was done, writes resulting SIP URI to third param (pseudo variable). Returns 1 if conversion succeeded, 2 if no conversion was needed, and -1 in case of error.

functions.name: tel2sip2
functions.doc: Alternative to sip2tel() function that tries to follow closer the RFC requrements (e.g., sort tel: uri parameters copied to the sip: uri in the manner defined in the standard; deletes the phone-context parameter if it is a domain, and, takes visual separators from the phone-context parameter if it is a telephone number).

functions.name: is_e164
functions.doc: Checks if string value of pseudo variable argument is an E164 number.

functions.name: is_uri_user_e164
functions.doc: Checks if userpart of URI stored in pseudo variable is E164 number.

functions.name: is_uri
functions.doc: Checks if string value of pseudo variable argument is a valid uri.

functions.name: is_tel_number
functions.doc: Checks if the parameter value is a telephone number: starting with one optional +, followed by digits. The parameter can include variables.

functions.name: is_numeric
functions.doc: Checks if the parameter value consists solely of decimal digits. The parameter can include variables.

functions.name: is_alphanum
functions.doc: Checks if the parameter value consists solely of decimal digits or alphabetic ASCII characters. The parameter can include variables.

functions.name: is_alphanumex
functions.doc: Checks if the value of parameter 'tval' consists solely of decimal digits, alphabetic ASCII characters and the characters in the second parameter 'eset'. The parameters can include variables.

functions.name: encode_contact
functions.doc: This function will encode uri-s inside Contact header in the following manner sip:username:password@ip:port;transport=protocol goes sip:encoding_prefix*username*password*ip*port*protocol@hostpart.

functions.name: decode_contact
functions.doc: This function will decode the request URI. If the RURI is in the format sip:encoding_prefix*username*password*ip*port*protocol@hostpart it will be decoded to sip:username:password@ip:port;transport=protocol. It uses the default set parameter for contact encoding separator.

functions.name: decode_contact_header
functions.doc: This function will decode URIs inside Contact header. If the URI in the format sip:encoding_prefix*username*ip*port*protocol@hostpart it will be decoded to sip:username:password@ip:port;transport=protocol. It uses the default set parameter for contact encoding separator.

functions.name: cmp_uri
functions.doc: The function returns true if the two parameters matches as SIP URI.

functions.name: cmp_aor
functions.doc: The function returns true if the two parameters matches as AoR. The parameters have to be SIP URIs.

functions.name: cmp_hdr_name
functions.doc: The function returns true (return code 1) if the two parameters matches as header names.

functions.name: append_rpid_hf
functions.doc: Appends to the message a Remote-Party-ID header that contains header 'Remote-Party-ID: ' followed by the saved value of the SIP URI received from the database or radius server followed by the value of module parameter radius_rpid_suffix. The function does nothing if no saved SIP URI exists.

functions.name: append_rpid_hf
functions.doc: This function is the same as Section 4.25, “ append_rpid_hf()”. The only difference is that it accepts two parameters--prefix and suffix to be added to Remote-Party-ID header field. This function ignores rpid_prefix and rpid_suffix parameters, instead of that allows to set them in every call.

functions.name: is_rpid_user_e164
functions.doc: The function checks if the SIP URI received from the database or radius server and will potentially be used in Remote-Party-ID header field contains an E164 number (+followed by up to 15 decimal digits) in its user part. Check fails, if no such SIP URI exists (i.e. radius server or database didn't provide this information).

functions.name: set_uri_user
functions.doc: Sets userpart of SIP URI stored in writable pseudo variable 'uri' to value of pseudo variable 'user'.

functions.name: set_uri_host
functions.doc: Sets hostpart of SIP URI stored in writable pseudo variable 'uri' to value of pseudo variable 'host'.

functions.name: is_request
functions.doc: Return true if the SIP message is a request.

functions.name: is_reply
functions.doc: Return true if the SIP message is a reply.

functions.name: is_sip
functions.doc: Return true if it is a SIP message.

functions.name: is_http
functions.doc: Return true if it is a HTTP message.

functions.name: is_gruu
functions.doc: The function returns true if the uri is GRUU ('gr' parameter is present): 1 - pub-gruu; 2 - temp-gruu.

functions.name: is_supported
functions.doc: Function returns true if given option is listed in Supported header(s) (if any) of the request. Currently the following options are known: path, 100rel, timer, eventlist, gruu, and outbound.

functions.name: is_first_hop
functions.doc: The function returns true if the proxy is first hop after the original sender based on a best effort estimation by checking Via and Record-Route headers.

functions.name: sip_p_charging_vector
functions.doc: Manage the P-Charging-Vector header (RFC7315). The flags can be: 'r' - remove; 'g' - generate; 'f' - force (remove + generate). Once a new PCV has been generated by 'g' or 'f' the PCV cannot be changed again. The icid-generated-at parameter of a generated PCV will be set to the sending interface.IP address.

functions.name: contact_param_encode
functions.doc: This function encodes URI inside Contact headers by building a new URI from 'saddr' parameter and adding a parameter with the name 'pname' containing incoming URI encoded in Base64URL format.

functions.name: contact_param_encode_alias
functions.doc: Similar to contact_param_encode() but it also adds the alias parameter with the encoded source address to the original Contact URI.

functions.name: contact_param_decode
functions.doc: This function decodes URI inside Contact headers by building a new URI from 'pname' parameter, decoding its value from Base64URL.

functions.name: contact_param_decode_uri
functions.doc: This function decodes R-URI (request URI) by building a new R-URI from 'pname' parameter, decoding its value from Base64URL.

functions.name: contact_param_rm
functions.doc: This function removes the parameter from the URIs inside the Contact headers.

functions.name: contact_param_check
functions.doc: This function returns true (1) if the URI inside the Contact header contains the parameter with the name 'pname'. Otherwise it returns false (-1).

functions.name: hdr_date_check
functions.doc: Returns true if sip message has Date header and its value is lower than 'NOW() - tdiff'.

functions.name: sip_parse_headers
functions.doc: Return true if parsing (fast mode) all SIP headers is successful.

params.name: default_code
params.doc: Default reply status code.

params.name: default_reason
params.doc: Default reply reason phrase.

params.name: bind_tm
params.doc: Controls if SL module should attempt to bind to TM module in order to send stateful reply when the transaction is created.

params.name: rich_redirect
params.doc: When sending a 3xx class reply, include additional branch info to the contacts such as path vector and branch flags. * 0 - no extra info is added (default) * 1 - include branch flags as contact header parameter * 2 - include path as contact uri Route header

params.name: event_callback_fl_ack
params.doc: The name of the KEMI callback function to be executed instead of event_route[sl:filtered-ack]. This function receives a string parameter.

params.name: event_callback_lres_sent
params.doc: The name of the KEMI callback function to be executed instead of event_route[sl:local-response]. This function receives a string parameter.

functions.name: sl_send_reply
functions.doc: For the current request, a reply is sent back having the given code and text reason. The reply is sent stateless, totally independent of the Transaction module and with no retransmission for the INVITE's replies.

functions.name: send_reply
functions.doc: For the current request, a reply is sent back having the given code and text reason. The reply is sent stateful or stateless, depending of the TM module: if a transaction exists for the current request, then the reply is sent statefully, otherwise stateless.

functions.name: send_reply_mode
functions.doc: Similar to send_reply() function, with additional third parameter mode, which can specify extra operations to be done along with sending the SIP response.

functions.name: sl_reply_error
functions.doc: Sends back an error reply describing the nature of the last internal error. Usually this function should be used after a script function that returned an error code.

functions.name: sl_forward_reply
functions.doc: Forward statelessly the current received SIP reply, with the option to change the status code and reason text. The new code has to be in the same class. The received reply is forwarded as well by core when the config execution ended, unless it is dropped from config.

functions.name: send_reply_error
functions.doc: For the current request, the internal error code reply is sent back stateful or stateless, depending of the TM module: if a transaction exists for the current request, then the reply is sent statefully, otherwise stateless.

params.name: slack url
params.doc: Slack webhook url

params.name: channel
params.doc: Slack channel name

params.name: username
params.doc: Specify the username for the published message

params.name: icon_emoji
params.doc: specify an emoji (using colon shortcodes, eg. :white_check_mark:) to use as the profile photo alongside the message.

functions.name: slack_send
functions.doc: Send a formatted message to slack channel.

params.name: modems
params.doc: Define and configure one or more GSM modems.

params.name: networks
params.doc: Define and configure used GSM networks.

params.name: links
params.doc: Define from which network each modem should send SMS.

params.name: default_net
params.doc: The default network to use. If no one specified, the first defined network is used. This parameter is useful only if the "sms_send_msg" exported function is used (see Section 4, “Functions”).

params.name: max_sms_parts
params.doc: Shows in how many parts (SMS messages) a SIP message can be split. If exceeded, the SIP message will be sent truncated and the SIP user will get back another message containing the unsent part.

params.name: domain
params.doc: Specify a fake domain name to be used by the gateway. The Contact headers and the From header from the request will be constructed based on this fake domain name. It's useful when the gateway is transparently hidden behind a proxy/register (located on different machines).

params.name: use_contact
params.doc: If a contact header should be added to the outgoing SIP messages. Even if the SIP draft forbids this, some UAS require it.

params.name: sms_report_type
params.doc: If the modem should ask for SMS confirmation from the SMS Center. If the SMSC reply with an error code, the gateway will send back to SIP user a SIP message containing the text (or part of it) that couldn't be sent. Two report mechanisms are implemented: * 1 - the reports are delivered by the GSM device as SMS reports (so far supported only by Nokia modems); * 2 - the reports are delivered as async. CDS responses (supported by almost all modems, except Ericsson).

functions.name: sms_send_msg_to_net
functions.doc: Put the SIP msg in the specified network queue. The function return error if the number encapsulated into SIP message is malformed, if the content_type is incorrect or because of some internal failures.

functions.name: sms_send_msg
functions.doc: The same as the previous one, but use the default network queue.

functions.name: isRPDATA
functions.doc: Returns true, if the message contains RP-Data in its body.

functions.name: smsdump
functions.doc: Dumps the content of a 3GPP-SMS message to the Debug-Log.

params.name: sipEntityType
params.doc: This parameter describes the entity type for this Kamailio instance, and will be used in determining what is returned for the kamailioSIPEntityType scalar. Valid parameters are:

params.name: MsgQueueMinorThreshold
params.doc: The SNMPStats module monitors the number of bytes waiting to be consumed by Kamailio. If the number of bytes waiting to be consumed exceeds a minor threshold, the SNMPStats module will send out a kamailioMsgQueueDepthMinorEvent trap to signal that an alarm condition has occurred. The minor threshold is set with the MsgQueueMinorThreshold parameter.

params.name: MsgQueueMajorThreshold
params.doc: The SNMPStats module monitors the number of bytes waiting to be consumed by Kamailio. If the number of bytes waiting to be consumed exceeds a major threshold, the SNMPStats module will send out a kamailioMsgQueueDepthMajorEvent trap to signal that an alarm condition has occurred. The major threshold is set with the MsgQueueMajorThreshold parameter.

params.name: dlg_minor_threshold
params.doc: The SNMPStats module monitors the number of active dialogs. If the number of active dialogs exceeds a minor threshold, the SNMPStats module will send out a kamailioDialogLimitMinorEvent trap to signal that an alarm condition has occurred. The minor threshold is set with the dlg_minor_threshold parameter.

params.name: dlg_major_threshold
params.doc: The SNMPStats module monitors the number of active dialogs. If the number of active dialogs exceeds a major threshold, the SNMPStats module will send out a kamailioDialogLimitMajorEvent trap to signal that an alarm condition has occurred. The major threshold is set with the dlg_major_threshold parameter.

params.name: snmpgetPath
params.doc: The SNMPStats module provides the kamailioSIPServiceStartTime scalar. This scalar requires the SNMPStats module to perform a snmpget query to the master agent. You can use this parameter to set the path to your instance of NetSNMP's snmpget program.

params.name: snmpCommunity
params.doc: The SNMPStats module provides the kamailioSIPServiceStartTime scalar. This scalar requires the SNMPStats module to perform a snmpget query to the master agent. If you have defined a custom community string for the snmp daemon, you need to specify it with this parameter.

params.name: snmpVersion
params.doc: The SNMPStats module provides the kamailioSIPServiceStartTime scalar. This scalar requires the SNMPStats module to perform a snmpget query to the master agent. You can use this parameter to set specific SNMP version.

params.name: export_registrar
params.doc: The SNMPStats module will export registrar (usrloc) records if this parameter is set to 1. This will result in more memory usage and bigger exporter structure.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: The URL of database where the table containing speed dial records.

params.name: user_column
params.doc: The name of column storing the user name of the owner of the speed dial record.

params.name: domain_column
params.doc: The name of column storing the domain of the owner of the speed dial record.

params.name: sd_user_column
params.doc: The name of the column storing the user part of the short dial address.

params.name: sd_domain_column
params.doc: The name of the column storing the domain of the short dial address.

params.name: new_uri_column
params.doc: The name of the column containing the URI that will be use to replace the short dial URI.

params.name: domain_prefix
params.doc: If the domain of the owner (From URI) starts with the value of this parameter, then it is stripped before performing the lookup of the short number.

params.name: use_domain
params.doc: The parameter specifies whether or not to use the domain when searching a speed dial record (0 - no domain, 1 - use domain from From URI, 2 - use both domains, from From URI and from request URI).

functions.name: sd_lookup
functions.doc: The function lookups the short dial number from R-URI in 'table' and replaces the R-URI with associated address.

params.name: sqlcon
params.doc: The definition of a DB connection. The value of the parameter must have the following format: * "connection_name=>database_url"

params.name: sqlres
params.doc: The definition of a database result ID. The value of the parameter can be any string. Results IDs are also added at fixup time when sql_query() parameters are parsed, so there is no need to declare them via module parameter unless you want to use them from within other modules and be available in all application processes.

params.name: tr_buf_size
params.doc: The size of the transformations for SQL operations.

params.name: log_buf_size
params.doc: The size of the buffer (characters) when logging raw SQL operations.

params.name: connect_mode
params.doc: Control how the module will connect to database. Values: * 0 connect at start up or fail * 1 connect at start up but continue even if connecting to database server fails * 2 do not connect until needed (this will limit the amount of idle connections)

params.name: results_maxsize
params.doc: Set the upper limit of how many result containers are going to be defined.

functions.name: sql_query
functions.doc: Make an SQL query using 'connection' and store data in 'result'. * connection - the name of the connection to be used for the query (defined via the “sqlcon” parameter). * query - SQL query string or pseudo-variables containing SQL query. * result - string name to identify the result. Will be used by $dbr(...) pseudo-variable to access result attributes. If omitted, any resultset will be discarded. The result parameter should normally only be omitted when no result is expected (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE).

functions.name: sql_xquery
functions.doc: Make an SQL query using 'connection' and store data in 'result' xavp. * connection - the name of the connection to be used for the query (defined via the “sqlcon” parameter). * query - SQL query string or pseudo-variables containing SQL query. * result - string name to identify the result xavp. Each row will be added to this xavp, each column can be accessed by its name.

functions.name: sql_pvquery
functions.doc: Make an SQL query using 'connection' and store data in arbitrary pseudo variables specified by 'result' parameter. * connection - the name of the connection to be used for query (defined via the “sqlcon” parameter). * query - SQL query string or pseudo-variables containing SQL query. * result - a list with PV names where to store the result. The format is “$pv;$pv;...”. Every PV that is writable may be used (for example $var, $avp, $xavp, $ru, $du, $sht, etc). The PV are assigned values in the following order: last row to first row, first field to last field. Assignment has the same behavior as assigning in the script itself with one exception for avp's, a NULL value will not delete an avp, but will be skipped over. Beware that if multiple rows are returned, non-(x)avp variables will only hold the last added value, which corresponds to the first returned row. The value type of the PV (string or integer) will be derived from the type of the columns. Please note that only these two datatypes are supported, other datatypes will/may be converted to string.

functions.name: sql_result_free
functions.doc: Free data in SQL 'result'.

functions.name: sql_query_async
functions.doc: Make an async SQL query using 'connection', if implemented by db driver module (e.g. db_mysql). The query is executed in another process and result is not available back to config, thus it should be used only for sql statements that don't return values (e.g. insert, delete, update...). Note that async_workers core parameter must be set in order to enable the asynchronous framework needed by this function. * connection - the name of the connection to be used for the query (defined via “sqlcon” parameter). * query - SQL query string or pseudo-variables containing SQL query.

functions.name: isup_to_json
functions.doc: isup_to_json(proto)

params.name: enable_stats
params.doc: If the statistics support should be enabled or not. Via statistic variables, the module provides information about the dialog processing. Set it to zero to disable or to non-zero to enable it.

params.name: min_se
params.doc: The value is used to set the proxies MIN-SE value and is used in the 422 error reply as the proxies MIN-SE: header value if the “sstCheckMin()” flag is set to true and the check fails.

params.name: timeout_avp
params.doc: This parameter must be set to the same value as the dialog module parameter of the same name, when it is wanted to update dialog timeout using Session-Expires header value. If this parameter is not set, the sst module will not update dialog timeout.

params.name: reject_to_small
params.doc: In the initial INVITE if the UAC has requested a Session-Expires: and its value is smaller than our local policies Min-SE (see min_se above), then the proxy has the right to reject the call by replying to the message with a “422 Session Timer Too Small” and state our local Min-SE: value. The INVITE is NOT forwarded on through the proxy.

params.name: sst_flag
params.doc: Keeping with Kamailio, the module will not do anything to any message unless instructed to do so via the kamailio.cfg script. You must set the sst_flag value in the setflag() call of the INVITE you want the sst module to process. But before you can do that, you need to tell the sst module which flag value you are assigning to sst.

functions.name: sstCheckMin
functions.doc: Check the current Session-Expires / MIN-SE values against the sst_min_se parameter value. If the Session-Expires or MIN_SE header value is less than the modules minimum value, this function will return true.

params.name: variable
params.doc: Name of a new statistic variable. The name may be followed by additional flag which describe the variable behavior: * no_reset : variable cannot be reset.

functions.name: update_stat
functions.doc: Updates the value of the statistic variable with the new value.

functions.name: reset_stat
functions.doc: Resets to zero the value of the statistic variable.

params.name: interval
params.doc: Timer interval when to record the value for statistics.

params.name: items
params.doc: How many items to store for each statistic.

params.name: track
params.doc: Specify the statistics to track. The parameter can be set many times and one value can specify many statistics.

params.name: ip
params.doc: Statsd server IP address.

params.name: port
params.doc: Statsd server port number

functions.name: statsd_set
functions.doc: Sets count the number of unique values passed to a key.

functions.name: statsd_gauge
functions.doc: Gauges are a constant data type. They are not subject to averaging and they don't change unless you change them. That is, once you set a gauge value, it will be a flat line on the graph until you change it again.

functions.name: statsd_histogram
functions.doc: The histograms are a measure of time, but they are calculated at the server side. As the data exported by the client is the same, this is just an alias for the Timer type.

functions.name: statsd_start
functions.doc: statsd_start set an avp with the key name, and when statsd_stop(key) is used, the module will send statsd the difference in milliseconds. This is useful to know the time of a SQL query, or how much time your replies take.

functions.name: statsd_stop
functions.doc: statsd_stop(key) get the avp string with the key and calculate the difference from the start time. When finished the milliseconds used will be sent to statsd.

functions.name: statsd_incr
functions.doc: Increment a statsd counter

functions.name: statsd_decr
functions.doc: Decrement a counter

params.name: as_default_key
params.doc: SSL private key to be used as default. Default key must be set if calls to stirshaken_add_identity() are executed. When set, module starts Authentication Service which makes each call to stirshaken_add_identity() using this key. Default key doesn't need to be set (Authentication Service doesn't need to be running) for the stirshaken_add_identity_with_key(..., key) to be available. This param has no meaning for calls to stirshaken_add_identity_with_key(..., key).

params.name: vs_verify_x509_cert_path
params.doc: If set, then stirshaken_check_identity() will execute X509 certificate path check on certificate referenced in PASSporT. This param has no meaning for calls to stirshaken_check_identity_with_key(key) and stirshaken_check_identity_with_cert(cert).

params.name: vs_ca_dir
params.doc: The path to folder containing CA root certificates with names hashed. If set then must point to existing directory. This must be set when enabled X509 certificate path check, otherwise no end entity certificate will pass that check. This param has no meaning for calls to stirshaken_check_identity_with_key(key) and stirshaken_check_identity_with_cert(cert).

params.name: vs_crl_dir
params.doc: The path to folder containing CRLs. If set, then must point to existing directory. This is optional when X509 certificate path check is enabled, only vs_ca_dir is mandatory. If X509 certificate path check is enabled, and vs_crl_dir is set, then CRLs are loaded from this directory, which renders revoked certificates invalid (not trusted). This param has no meaning for calls to stirshaken_check_identity_with_key(key) and stirshaken_check_identity_with_cert(cert).

params.name: vs_identity_expire_s
params.doc: This parameter defines a maximum time in seconds for which PASSporT is considered valid.

params.name: vs_connect_timeout_s
params.doc: During a call verification with stirshaken_check_identity() a blocking HTTP(s) call is executed to download certificate referenced in PASSporT (unless certificate caching is turned on and a valid cert is found in cache). This parameter defines a maximum time in seconds for this blocking HTTP(s) connection to be established. After this time had passed and connection did not succeed (could not resolve host, address unreachable or other network errors) a call to stirshaken_check_identity() will return with error. This param has no meaning for calls to stirshaken_check_identity_with_key(key) and stirshaken_check_identity_with_cert(cert).

params.name: vs_cache_certificates
params.doc: If set, then certificates caching is turned on. This means that certificates downloaded during call verification with stirshaken_check_identity() are cached inside vs_cache_dir, and will be loaded from that cache as long as they are not there for more than vs_cache_expire_s seconds (see vs_cache_expire_s). If vs_cache_certificates is set then vs_cache_dir must be set too and pointing to existing directory. This param has no meaning for calls to stirshaken_check_identity_with_key(key) and stirshaken_check_identity_with_cert(cert).

params.name: vs_cache_dir
params.doc: If vs_cache_certificates is set then vs_cache_dir must be set too and pointing to existing directory. Cached certificates are saved in this directory and loaded from there when needed during a call verification executed with stirshaken_check_identity(), as long as they are not there for more than vs_cache_expire_s seconds. This param has no meaning for calls to stirshaken_check_identity_with_key(key) and stirshaken_check_identity_with_cert(cert).

params.name: vs_cache_expire_s
params.doc: If vs_cache_certificates is set then cached certificates are saved in vs_cache_dir directory and loaded from there when needed during a call verification executed with stirshaken_check_identity(), as long as they are not there for more than vs_cache_expire_s seconds. If they are in cache for more than vs_cache_expire_s seconds, then a blocking HTTP(s) call is executed to download a new version of (expired) certificate. If this is successful then old version is removed and new version is saved in cache. This param has no meaning for calls to stirshaken_check_identity_with_key(key) and stirshaken_check_identity_with_cert(cert).

params.name: vs_certsubject_pvname
params.doc: If vs_certsubject_pvname is set then the Subject of the authenticated x509 certificate will be written to this pseudo-variable when stirshaken_check_identity() is executed. If the Identity header cannot be fully authenticated the pseudo-variable will be set to $null.

params.name: vs_pptgrants_pvname
params.doc: If vs_pptgrants_pvname is set then the JSON string of the authenticated PASSporT's grants will be written to this pseudo-variable when stirshaken_check_identity() is executed. If the Identity header cannot be fully authenticated the pseudo-variable will be set to $null.

functions.name: stirshaken_check_identity
functions.doc: Check the validity of the Identity header by decoding PASSporT's signature with a certificate referenced in its x5u header and (optionally) checking that certificate for being trusted by X509 certificate check with CA root certificates in vs_ca_dir (and optionally CRLs in vs_crl_dir). PASSporT's iat grant is also checked for being too fresh or expired against vs_identity_expire_s seconds. This function executes a call to a callback which may supply certificates from cache (see vs_cache_certificates param). If certificate needs to be downloaded this call will block for a maximum of vs_connect_timeout_s seconds (see vs_connect_timeout_s param);

functions.name: stirshaken_check_identity_with_key
functions.doc: Check the validity of the Identity header by decoding PASSporT's signature with a key read from the location provided. PASSporT's iat grant is also checked for being too fresh or expired against vs_identity_expire_s seconds. This method does not involve HTTP(s) transcations. This method does not execute a call to a callback (vs_cache_certificates param has no meaning for this method). WARNING: This method only checks if SIP Identity Header was signed by a key corresponding to specified public key. This method doesn't attempt to obtain certificate referenced in PASSporT (but PASSporT should be checked with key corresponding to that certificate). Therefore it is possible that this check will be successful, while PASSporT is not valid (could be signed with key that doesn't match certificate referenced in x5u header). If you want a complete Shaken check or if you are not sure what you're doing, then you should execute w_stirshaken_check_identity() instead (and configure Verification Service to perform X509 certificate path verification with stirshaken_vs_verify_x509_cert_path param set to 1).

functions.name: stirshaken_check_identity_with_cert
functions.doc: Same as stirshaken_check_identity_with_key(keyPath) but the key is read from the certificate which is read from the location provided.

functions.name: stirshaken_add_identity
functions.doc: Add SIP Identity Header to the call using default private key (see as_default_key param). Authenticate call with STIR-Shaken. If origID is empty, a UUID string is generated to fill the field. The origtn_val represents the origination telephone number; desttn_val, represents the destination telephone number; x5u is the HTTP(s) URL referencing to the public key that should be used to verify the signature; attest represents the attestation level (should be "A", "B" or "C").

params.name: xdata
params.doc: Name of a script variable from where to take additional data to be passed to special worker along with the SIP message. Same variable will be set by the special worker, therefore it has to be a writable variable. Moreover, it must be a variable that can be set without the SIP message structure, like $var(name), otherwise it can lead to a crash.

functions.name: sworker_active
functions.doc: Return 1 (true) if the processing happens in an async process, or -1 (false) if the processing is happening in a SIP receiving process.

functions.name: sworker_task
functions.doc: Delegate the processing of SIP message to a group of async workers. The function is restricted to be used inside event_route[core:pre-routing].

params.name: closed_event
params.doc: If set to 0 (globally disabled), the "tcp:closed" event route will never be called on TCP disconnections.

params.name: event_callback
params.doc: The name of the function in the kemi configuration file (embedded scripting language such as Lua, Python, ...) to be executed instead of event_route[...] blocks.

functions.name: tcp_conid_alive
functions.doc: Check the state of a TCP or WS connection ID

functions.name: tcp_con_alive
functions.doc: Check the connection based on target addrt.

functions.name: tcp_conid_state
functions.doc: Check the state of a TCP or WS connection ID

functions.name: tcp_keepalive_enable
functions.doc: Enables keepalive on a TCP connection.

functions.name: tcp_keepalive_disable
functions.doc: Disables keepalive on a TCP connection.

functions.name: tcp_set_connection_lifetime
functions.doc: Sets the connection lifetime of a connection (TCP).

functions.name: tcp_enable_closed_event
functions.doc: Explicitly enables the "tcp:closed" event route on a TCP connection.

functions.name: tcp_get_conid
functions.doc: Get the connection id based on target host:port. The connection id is set in the variable named by pvname parameter.

functions.name: tcp_set_otcpid
functions.doc: Set the value for outbound tcp connection id.

functions.name: tcp_set_otcpid_flag
functions.doc: Set or reset the internal flag for using or not the outbound tcp connection id for sending out. The outbound connection id can be set by module or by config using tcp_set_otcpid(...) function. An example of a module setting the otcpid is registrar via lookup location function, which sets the field to the connection id used to receive the registration request.

functions.name: tcp_close_connection
functions.doc: Trigger a close of the connection corresponding to current SIP message or to connection id 'conid'.

functions.name: search
functions.doc: Searches for the re in the message.

functions.name: search_body
functions.doc: Searches for the re in the body of the message.

functions.name: search_str
functions.doc: Searches for the re in the body of the message.

functions.name: search_hf
functions.doc: Searches for the re in the body of a header field.

functions.name: search_append
functions.doc: Searches for the first match of re and appends txt after it.

functions.name: search_append_body
functions.doc: Searches for the first match of re in the body of the message and appends txt after it.

functions.name: replace
functions.doc: Replaces the first occurrence of re with txt.

functions.name: replace_body
functions.doc: Replaces the first occurrence of re in the body of the message with txt.

functions.name: replace_hdrs
functions.doc: Replaces the first occurrence of re in the SIP headers of the message with txt.

functions.name: replace_all
functions.doc: Replaces all occurrence of re with txt.

functions.name: replace_body_all
functions.doc: Replaces all occurrence of re in the body of the message with txt. Matching is done on a per-line basis.

functions.name: replace_body_atonce
functions.doc: Replaces all occurrence of re in the body of the message with txt. Matching is done over the whole body.

functions.name: replace_str
functions.doc: Replaces the first or all occurrence of 'match' with 'repl' by doing string comparison for matching. It is applied over headers and message body (not over the first line).

functions.name: replace_body_str
functions.doc: Replaces the first or all occurrence of 'match' with 'repl' by doing string comparison for matching. It is applied over the message body.

functions.name: replace_hdrs_str
functions.doc: Replaces the first or all occurrence of 'match' with 'repl' by doing string comparison for matching. It is applied over the part with headers of the SIP message.

functions.name: subst
functions.doc: Replaces re with repl.

functions.name: subst_uri
functions.doc: Runs the re substitution on the message uri (like subst but works only on the uri)

functions.name: subst_user
functions.doc: Runs the re substitution on the message uri (like subst_uri but works only on the user portion of the uri)

functions.name: subst_body
functions.doc: Replaces re with repl in the body of the message.

functions.name: subst_hf
functions.doc: Substitutions in the body of a header field.

functions.name: subst_v
functions.doc: Sed-like substitution subexp applied to itext, with result stored in opv.

functions.name: set_body
functions.doc: Set body to a SIP message.

functions.name: set_body_hex
functions.doc: Set body to a SIP message with the hexa-decoded value of htxt.

functions.name: set_reply_body
functions.doc: Set body to a SIP reply to be generated by Kamailio.

functions.name: set_reply_body_hex
functions.doc: Same as set_reply_body(), but with the body provided as hexa-encoded value. The whitespaces are ignored when decoding the body parameter.

functions.name: filter_body
functions.doc: Filters multipart/mixed body by leaving out all other body parts except the first body part of given type.

functions.name: append_to_reply
functions.doc: Append txt as header to the reply that is going to be generated by Kamailio (e.g., via sl_send_reply(...)).

functions.name: append_hf
functions.doc: Appends 'txt' as header at the end of all the headers, or after last header named 'hdr' if the second parameter is provided.

functions.name: insert_hf
functions.doc: Inserts 'txt' as header before the first header field, or before first header named 'hdr' if the second parameter is provided.

functions.name: append_urihf
functions.doc: Append header field name with original Request-URI in middle.

functions.name: is_present_hf
functions.doc: Return true if a header field is present in message.

functions.name: is_present_hf_pv
functions.doc: Same as is_present_hf() function, but the parameter can contain variables.

functions.name: is_present_hf_re
functions.doc: Return true if a header field whose name matches regular expression 'hf_name_re' is present in message.

functions.name: is_present_hf_re_pv
functions.doc: Same as is_present_hf_re() function, but the parameter can contain variables.

functions.name: append_time
functions.doc: Adds a time header to the reply of the request. You must use it before functions that are likely to send a reply, e.g., save() from 'registrar' module. Header format is: “Date: %a, %d %b %Y %H:%M:%S GMT”, with the legend: * %a abbreviated week of day name (locale) * %d day of month as decimal number * %b abbreviated month name (locale) * %Y year with century * %H hour * %M minutes * %S seconds

functions.name: append_time_to_request
functions.doc: Adds a time header to the request. Header format is: “Date: %a, %d %b %Y %H:%M:%S GMT”, with the legend: * %a abbreviated week of day name (locale) * %d day of month as decimal number * %b abbreviated month name (locale) * %Y year with century * %H hour * %M minutes * %S seconds

functions.name: is_method
functions.doc: Check if the method of the message matches the name. If name is a known method (invite, cancel, ack, bye, options, info, update, register, message, subscribe, notify, refer, prack), the function performs method ID testing (integer comparison) instead of ignore case string comparison.

functions.name: remove_hf
functions.doc: Remove from message all headers with name “hname”. Header matching is case-insensitive. Matches and removes also the compact header forms.

functions.name: remove_hf_pv
functions.doc: Same as remove_hf() function, but the parameter can contain variables.

functions.name: remove_hf_re
functions.doc: Remove from message all headers with name matching regular expression “re”

functions.name: remove_hf_re_pv
functions.doc: Same as remove_hf_re() function, but the parameter can contain variables.

functions.name: remove_hf_exp
functions.doc: Remove from message all headers with name matching regular expression “expmatch”, but not matching regular expression “expskip”.

functions.name: remove_hf_exp_pv
functions.doc: Same as remove_hf_exp() function, but the parameters can contain variables.

functions.name: remove_hf_idx
functions.doc: Remove from message the headers matching by name 'hname' with the index 'idx'.

functions.name: remove_hf_match
functions.doc: Remove from message all headers with name 'hname' matching the body with expression “expr”, based on operator “op”.

functions.name: has_body
functions.doc: The function returns true if the SIP message has a body attached. The check includes also the “Content-Length” header presence and value.

functions.name: is_audio_on_hold
functions.doc: The function returns true if the SIP message has a body attached and at least one audio stream in on hold. The return code of the function indicates the detected hold type: * 1 - RFC2543 hold type: null connection IP detected * 2 - RFC3264 hold type: inactive or sendonly attributes detected

functions.name: is_privacy
functions.doc: The function returns true if the SIP message has a Privacy header field that includes the given privacy_type among its privacy values. See http://www.iana.org/assignments/sip-priv-values for possible privacy type values.

functions.name: in_list
functions.doc: Function checks if subject string is found in list string where list items are separated by separator string. Subject and list strings may contain pseudo variables. Separator string needs to be one character long. Returns 1 if subject is found and -1 otherwise.

functions.name: in_list_prefix
functions.doc: Function checks if any element in list string is a prefix for subject string where list items are separated by separator string. Subject and list strings may contain pseudo variables. Separator string needs to be one character long. Returns 1 if subject is found and -1 otherwise.

functions.name: cmp_str
functions.doc: The function returns true if the two parameters matches as string case sensitive comparison.

functions.name: cmp_istr
functions.doc: The function returns true if the two parameters matches as string case insensitive comparison.

functions.name: starts_with
functions.doc: The function returns true if the first string starts with the second string.

functions.name: ends_with
functions.doc: The function returns true if the first string ends with the second string. The parameters can contain variables.

functions.name: str_find
functions.doc: The function returns true (greater than 0) if the str2 string is found in str1, case sensitive comparison.

functions.name: str_ifind
