functions.doc: Sets additional deny filters. Maximum 6 may be combined. This additional filter will apply only to the current message - it will not have a global effect.

functions.name: set_accept_filter
functions.doc: Sets additional accept filters. Maximum 6 may be combined. This additional filter will apply only to the current message - it will not have a global effect.

functions.name: get_redirects
functions.doc: The function may be called only from failure routes. It will extract the contacts from all 3xx branches and append them as new branches. Note that the function will not forward the new branches, this must be done explicitly from script.

functions.name: get_redirects
functions.doc: The function has same functionality as get_redirects(max) function, but it will produce accounting records.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: This is URL of the database to be used. Value of the parameter depends on the database module used. For example for mysql and postgres modules this is something like mysql://username:password@host:port/database. For dbtext module (which stores data in plaintext files) it is directory in which the database resides.

params.name: user_column
params.doc: This is the name of the column holding usernames. Default value is fine for most people. Use the parameter if you really need to change it.

params.name: domain_column
params.doc: This is the name of the column holding domains of users. Default value is fine for most people. Use the parameter if you really need to change it.

params.name: password_column
params.doc: This is the name of the column holding passwords. Passwords can be either stored as plain text or pre-calculated HA1 strings. HA1 strings are MD5 hashes of username, password, and realm. HA1 strings are more safe because the server doesn't need to know plaintext passwords and they cannot be obtained from HA1 strings.

params.name: rpid_column
params.doc: This is the name of the column holding information for the Remote-Party-ID header field. Default value is fine for most people. Use the parameter if you really need to change it.

params.name: calculate_ha1
params.doc: This parameter tells server whether it should read plaintext password from the database or HA1 string. If the parameter is set to 1 then the server will assume that the column pointed to by plain_password_column contains plaintext passwords and it will calculate HA1 strings on the fly.

params.name: plain_password_column
params.doc: This parameter holds the name of column holding plain text password. This column is used when calculate_ha1 is set.

params.name: password_column_2
params.doc: As described in the previous section this parameter contains name of column holding pre-calculated HA1 string that were calculated including the domain in the username. This parameter is used only when calculate_ha1 is set to 0 and user agent sends credentials containing the domain in the username.

params.name: use_rpid
params.doc: This parameter specifies whether the server should fetch a value for the Remote-Party-ID header field from the database.

functions.name: www_authorize
functions.doc: The function verifies credentials according to RFC2617. If the credentials are verified successfully then the function will succeed and mark the credentials as authorized (marked credentials can be later used by some other functions). If the function was unable to verify the credentials for some reason then it will fail and the script should call www_challenge which will challenge the user again.

functions.name: proxy_authorize
functions.doc: The function verifies credentials according to RFC2617. If the credentials are verified successfully then the function will succeed and mark the credentials as authorized (marked credentials can be later used by some other functions). If the function was unable to verify the credentials for some reason then it will fail and the script should call proxy_challenge which will challenge the user again.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: The URL of the database to be used.

params.name: user_attrs_table
params.doc: Name of the table with user attributes.

When the value of this parameter is zero (default) BUG level message is logged, but the lock is kept, so another process trying to obtain the lock might get stuck. If the value is nonzero, DEBUG level message is sent to the log and all the locks are released.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: This is URL of the database to be used.

params.name: db_mode
params.doc: Database mode. Value 0 means non-caching, 1 means caching is enabled. It is highly recommended to enable caching if you want to use domain-level attributes.

params.name: domain_table
params.doc: Name of table containing names of local domains that the proxy is responsible for. Local users must have in their SIP URI a host part that is equal to one of the domains stored in this table.

params.name: did_col
params.doc: This is the name of the column in domain table that contains the unique identifiers of virtual domains. Domains names found in this table are arranged into virtual domains. Each virtual domain must have a unique identifier and it can contain one or more domain names.

params.name: domain_col
params.doc: Name of column containing domain names in the domain table.

params.name: flags_col
params.doc: This is the name of the column in domain table which stores various flags. Each row in the table has a bunch of generic flags that can be used mark the row disabled, deleted, etc. The flags allow for more flexible administration of the data in the database and they are present in several other tables too.

params.name: domattr_table
params.doc: This parameter can be used to configure the name of the table that is used to store domain-level attributes. Domain level attributes are attributes that are associated with a particular virtual domain. They are typically used to store additional domain-wide settings that should apply to all users who belong to the domain.

params.name: domattr_did
params.doc: Use this parameter to configure the name of the column in domain_attrs table that is used to store the did of the virtual domain the attribute belongs to. Normally there is no need to configure this parameter, unless you want adapt to module to a different database schema.

params.name: domattr_name
params.doc: Use this parameter to configure the name of the column in domain_attrs table that is used to store the name of the attribute. Normally there is no need to configure this parameter, unless you want adapt to module to a different database schema.

params.name: domattr_type
params.doc: Use this parameter to configure the name of the column in domain_attrs table that is used to store the type of the attribute. Normally there is no need to configure this parameter, unless you want adapt to module to a different database schema.

params.name: domattr_value
params.doc: Use this parameter to configure the name of the column in domain_attrs table that is used to store the value of the attribute. Normally there is no need to configure this parameter, unless you want adapt to module to a different database schema.

params.name: domattr_flags
params.doc: This is the name of the column in domain_attrs table which stores various flags. Each row in the table has a bunch of generic flags that can be used mark the row disabled, deleted, etc. The flags allow for more flexible administration of the data in the database and they are present in several other tables too. You do not have to touch this parameter under normal circumstances.

params.name: load_domain_attrs
params.doc: This parameter can be used to enable/disable user of domain-level attributes. Domain-level attributes are variables that can be used to store additional configuration that applies to the whole virtual domain and all users within the virtual domain. Domain-level attributes are stored in domain_attrs. If you set this parameter to a non-zero value then the server will make domain-level attributes available to the script every time you call function lookup_domain. If you set the parameter to 0 then domain-level attributes will be ignored, the domain module will not load them from the database and the lookup function will not make them available to the script.

functions.name: is_local
functions.doc: This function can be used to test whether a given domain name in parameter belongs to one of the virtual domains defined in the domain table. Such domain name is said to be local. The function returns 1 if the domain name is found in the domain table and -1 otherwise.

functions.name: lookup_domain
functions.doc: This is the main function of the domain module. It can be used to implement support for virtual domains in the SIP server. Each virtual domain is identified by a unique identifier (opaque string) and it can have one or more associated domain names. Given a domain name in the second parameter, this function finds the associated virtual domain identifier (known as DID) and stores it in an attribute for later use. In addition to that the function also loads all domain-level attributes for the virtual domain and makes them available to the configuration script.

params.name: initial
params.doc: The initial value of global flags. Each bit in the integer represents one flag.

functions.name: set_gflag
functions.doc: Set the flag identified by flag_num to 1. The range of flag_num is 0 to 31.

functions.name: reset_ugflag
functions.doc: Set the flag identified by flag_num to 0. The range of flag_num is 0 to 31.

functions.name: is_ugflag
functions.doc: Returns 1 when flag identified by flag_num is set, 0 otherwise. The range of flag_num parameter is 0 to 31.

params.name: desc_time_order

params.name: timer_interval
params.doc: Number of seconds between two timer runs. The module uses a timer to delete expired contacts, synchronize with database, send keepalives and other tasks, that need to be run periodically.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: URL of the database that should be used.

params.name: db_mode
params.doc: The usrloc module can utilize a database for persistent contact storage. If a database is used, the location database (contacts) will survive machine restarts or software crashes. The disadvantage is that accessing a database can be very time consuming. Therefore, usrloc module implements four database accessing modes: * 0 - This disables database completely. Only memory will be used. Contacts will not survive restart. Use this value if you need a really fast usrloc and contact persistence is not necessary or is provided by other means. * 1 - Write-Through scheme. All changes to usrloc are immediately reflected in database too. This is very slow, but very reliable. Use this scheme if speed is not your priority but need to make sure that no registered contacts will be lost during crash or reboot. * 2 - Write-Back scheme. This is a combination of previous two schemes. All changes are made to memory and database synchronization is done in the timer. The timer deletes all expired contacts and flushes all modified or new contacts to database. Use this scheme if you encounter high-load peaks and want them to process as fast as possible. The mode will not help at all if the load is high all the time. Also, latency of this mode is much lower than latency of mode 1, but slightly higher than latency of mode 0. * 3 - DB-Only scheme. No memory cache is kept, all operations being directly performed with the database. The timer deletes all expired contacts from database - cleans after clients that didn't un-register or re-register. The mode is useful if you configure more servers sharing the same DB without any replication at SIP level. The mode may be slower due the high number of DB operation. For example NAT pinging is a killer since during each ping cycle all natted contact are loaded from the DB; The lack of memory caching also disable the statistics exports. * 4 - This uses database to load records at startup but uses only memory during the runtime. Records are not written back at all, not even at shutdown. Useful for scenarios when registrations are replicated to a node that does the storage in a database during runtime.

params.name: db_load
params.doc: Determine if the usrloc module should load contacts from the database storage during module initialization. A value of 0 disables the loading from the database, this parameter is ignored if db_mode 4 is set.

params.name: db_insert_update
params.doc: Determine if the usrloc module should do an update when a duplicate key is found while inserting A value of 1 will activate update on duplicate key

params.name: matching_mode
params.doc: What contact matching algorithm to be used. Refer to section ??? for the description of the algorithms.

params.name: cseq_delay
params.doc: Delay (in seconds) for accepting as retransmissions register requests with same Call-ID and Cseq. The delay is calculated starting from the receiving time of the first register with that Call-ID and Cseq.

params.name: fetch_rows
params.doc: The number of the rows to be fetched at once from database when loading the location records. This value can be used to tune the load time at startup. For 1MB of private memory (default) it should be below 4000. The database driver must support fetch_result() capability.

params.name: hash_size
params.doc: The number of entries of the hash table used by usrloc to store the location records is 2^hash_size. For hash_size=4, the number of slots of the hash table is 16.

params.name: preload
params.doc: Preload location table given as value. A location table is loaded based on fixup of registrar functions, therefore you need to use this parameter only to load tables that are not used by registrar module directly in configuration file.

params.name: db_update_as_insert
params.doc: Set this parameter if you want to do INSERT DB operations instead of UPDATE DB operations. It is recommended to set this parameter if you use Cassandra as a DB backend.

params.name: db_check_update
params.doc: Set this parameter to 1 if you want to do DB INSERT if the number of affected rows by contact DB UPDATE operation is 0. The database module driver has to implement affected_rows() DB API function, otherwise this parameter is ignored - e.g., MySQL and Postgres DB connectors offer affected_rows().

params.name: timer_procs
params.doc: Number of timer processes to be started by module. Timer processes take care of checking expired records and synchronization with database. If set to 0, no dedicated timer is started, the one from core will be used.

params.name: xavp_contact
params.doc: The name of XAVP storing the attributes per contact. They are saved in location record and restored at lookup. The tm module parameter xavp_contact must also be set to the same value to use the t_load_contacts and t_next_contacts functions.

params.name: db_ops_ruid
params.doc: If set to 1, database queries for update or delete are done using ruid value. If it is set to 0, the old style using aor, contact and call-id is done.

params.name: handle_lost_tcp
params.doc: If set to 1, Kamailio will remove location records made via TCP/TLS/WS/WSS transports when it looses corresponding tcp connections. Does not currently work in DB-Only scheme.

params.name: close_expired_tcp
params.doc: If set to 1, Kamailio will close the TCP connection when a contact has expired, if the corresponding transport is TCP/TLS/WS/WSS.

params.name: expires_type
params.doc: If set to 1, Kamailio expects to deal with BIGINT type on database columns for expires and last modified values. It allows to handle better the daylight time adjustments. If set to 0, those columns are expected to be on default type 'DATETIME'. When it is 1, the database columns types have to be changed manually to 'BIGINT'.

params.name: db_raw_fetch_type
params.doc: This affect DB-only mode and controls what kind of raw query is used to fetch the contacts from database for specific needs (e.g., sending NAT keepalives). If it is set to 0, then the common SQL query is used (working for MySQL, PostgreSQL, ...). If it is set to 1, the query required by Oracle is used.

params.name: db_insert_null
params.doc: If set to 1, the insert operation to database will add null values in the statement. It has to be set to 1 for the database systems that do not have table definitions that create automatically the null fields (e.g., db_mongodb) for each stored record.

params.name: skip_remote_socket
params.doc: If set to 1, Kamailio will skip location record when loading from database, if socket value of the record does not in kamailio listening socket list.

params.name: db_timer_clean
params.doc: Enable (1) or disable (0) cleaning of expired db records on timer basis for db_mode WRITE-BACK and WRITE-THROUGH. It uses the secondary timer process.

params.name: rm_expired_delay
params.doc: Specify the number of seconds to delay the removal of expired records. For now it works for DB_ONLY mode (db_mode=3).

params.name: server_id_filter
params.doc: Enable (1) or disable (0) filter records by server_id on load and during cleaning of expired db records. It could be useful when you want to use the same location table for several kamailio instances which are configured to work in db_mode=1 or db_mode=2 (cache modes). Otherwise one instance of proxy cleans records made by another proxy and that breaks its cache.

params.name: version_table
params.doc: If set to 0, the module will skip checking the version for location table.

params.name: ka_mode
params.doc: Keepalive mode - control the internal keepalive mechanism. With this feature enabled, the module sends periodically (based on timer interval) SIP requests to location contacts and measures the round trip in microseconds (the round trip value can be seen in the response of the RPC command 'ul.dump').

params.name: ka_method
params.doc: The SIP method type for keepalive requests.

params.name: ka_from
params.doc: The SIP URI to be set in the From header of the keepalive requests.

params.name: ka_domain
params.doc: The domain to be set in To header URI if the multi-domain is not enabled. If multi-domain is enabled, then the domain from the location record is used and this parameter is ignored.

params.name: ka_filter
params.doc: Set filters for keepalive processing.

params.name: ka_timeout
params.doc: The parameter sets the interval in seconds after which a contact is removed from location table if it does not reply to SIP keepalives (usually OPTIONS ping requests).

params.name: ka_interval
params.doc: The parameter sets the interval in seconds after which a new keepalive request should be sent for a location record.

params.name: ka_randomize
params.doc: The parameter sets the the upper limit to the range of random seconds to be added to ka_interval before checking if a new keepalive request has to be sent. It should help to distribute better the sending of keepalive requests. The keepalive for a location record is going to be sent in a random fashion between (ka_interval + 0) and (ka_interval + ka_randomize).

params.name: ka_loglevel
params.doc: The level to print the log message when the keepalive response is received. It should be a value between -5 (L_ALERT) and 3 (L_DBG).

params.name: ka_logmsg
params.doc: The formatted log specification to be added to the message printed when the keepalive is received and roundtrip time is computed. The log message starts with "keepalive roundtrip: %u.%06u sec - ruid [%.*s]", then concatenates the value of this parameter and the end of line.

params.name: ka_reply_codes
params.doc: Comma separated list of reply code values or reply code classes to be considered valid for keepalive processing. If the reply code does not match any of them, then the reply is ignored, not considered a valid response to keepalive request. It could be useful to skip replies from intermediary proxies that could not forward the request.

params.name: load_rank
params.doc: Allows to set the rank of the child SIP worker to load the location records.

params.name: db_clean_tcp
params.doc: If set to 1, when Kamailio starts it removes the contacts with transport TCP, TLS or WSS, no longer loading them. Useful when end points do not listen for incoming connections on contact address, which is quite common (end point use only tcp client connections). On restart, connections are lost, therefore the corresponding contact records become useless.

params.name: forward_active
params.doc: Defines if the forwarding callback should be installed.

params.name: pres_db_url
params.doc: Defines presence server database URL. If not given, the xcap_auth_status function is disabled.

params.name: xcap_table
params.doc: Defines the name of the xcap table in the presence server database. See the xcap_server module documentation for more information.

functions.name: xcap_auth_status
functions.doc: Function checks in the presence server database if a watcher is authorized to subscribe to event “presence” of presentity. Sphere checking is not included.

params.name: keepalive_mechanism
params.doc: The keep-alive mechanism to use for WebSocket connections.

params.name: keepalive_timeout
params.doc: The time (in seconds) after which to send a keep-alive on idle WebSocket connections.

params.name: keepalive_processes
params.doc: The number of processes to start to perform WebSocket connection keep-alives.

params.name: keepalive_interval
params.doc: The number of seconds between each keep-alive process run

params.name: ping_application_data
params.doc: The application data to use in keep-alive Ping and Pong frames.

params.name: sub_protocols
params.doc: A bitmap that allows you to control the sub-protocols supported by the WebSocket server. * 1 - sip (RFC 7118) * 2 - msrp (RFC 7977) - the msrp module must be loaded before the websocket module

params.name: cors_mode
params.doc: This parameter lets you set the "Cross-origin resource sharing" behaviour of the WebSocket server. * 0 - Do not add an "Access-Control-Allow-Origin:" header to the response accepting the WebSocket handshake. * 1 - Add an "Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *" header to the response accepting the WebSocket handshake. * 2 - Add an "Access-Control-Allow-Origin:" header containing the same body as the "Origin:" header from the request to the response accepting the WebSocket handshake. If there is no "Origin:" header in the request no header will be added to the response.

params.name: verbose_list
params.doc: Allows to enable/disable the printing of debug messages when getting the list of websocket connections. If enabled, it prints debug messages every second for ping operations.

params.name: event_callback
params.doc: The name of the function in the kemi configuration file (embedded scripting language such as Lua, Python, ...) to be executed instead of event_route[...] blocks specific for websocket module.

params.name: timer_interval
params.doc: The number of seconds between each timer process run

params.name: rm_delay_interval
params.doc: The number of seconds to wait before destroying the websocket connection once put in remove state.

functions.name: ws_handle_handshake
functions.doc: This function checks an HTTP GET request for the required headers and values, and (if successful) upgrades the connection from HTTP to WebSocket.

functions.name: ws_close
functions.doc: This function closes a WebSocket connection.

params.name: xcap_table

params.name: periodical_query
params.doc: A flag to disable periodical query as an update method for the documents the module is responsible for. It could be disabled when the XCAP server is capable to send the exported management command when a change occurs or when another module in Kamailio handles updates.

params.name: query_period
params.doc: Should be set if periodical query is not disabled. Represents the time interval the XCAP servers should be queried for an update.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: Database URL.

params.name: xcap_table
params.doc: The name of table where to store the xcap documents.

params.name: xcap_root
params.doc: XCAP root URL.

params.name: buf_size
params.doc: Size of local buffer for handling XCAP documents.

params.name: xml_ns
params.doc: Register extra XML namespaces to be used with XPath. You can set the parameter many times to add more namespaces. The format is 'prefix=href'.

params.name: directory_scheme
params.doc: Allows the scheme used in org.openmobilealliance.xcap-directory listings to be set to a specific value.

params.name: directory_hostname
params.doc: Allows the hostname (and port) used in org.openmobilealliance.xcap-directory listings to be set to a specific value.

functions.name: xcaps_put
functions.doc: Handle XCAP PUT command.

functions.name: xcaps_get
functions.doc: Handle XCAP GET command.

functions.name: xcaps_del
functions.doc: Handle XCAP DELETE command.

params.name: url_skip
params.doc: Regular expression to match the HTTP URL. If there is a match, the event route is not executed.

params.name: url_match
params.doc: Regular expression to match the HTTP URL. If there is no match, the event route is not executed. This check is done after url_skip, so if both url_skip and url_match would match then the event route is not executed (url_skip has higher priority).

params.name: event_callback
params.doc: The name of the function in the kemi configuration file (embedded scripting language such as Lua, Python, ...) to be executed instead of event_route[xhttp:request] block.

functions.name: xhttp_reply
functions.doc: Send back a reply with content-type and body.

params.name: xhttp_pi_root
params.doc: It specifies the root path for provisioning http requests. The link to the provisioning web interface must be constructed using the following pattern: http://[server_IP]:[tcp_port]/[xhttp_pi_root]

params.name: xhttp_pi_buf_size
params.doc: It specifies the maximum length of the buffer (in bytes) used to write in the HTML reply information in order to build the HTML response.

params.name: framework
params.doc: It specifies the full path for xml framework descriptor.

params.name: xhttp_prom_buf_size
params.doc: Specifies the maximum length of the buffer (in bytes) used to write the metric reply information in order to build the HTML response.

params.name: xhttp_prom_timeout
params.doc: Specifies a timeout in minutes. A metric not used during this timeout is automatically deleted. Listing metrics does not count as using them.

params.name: xhttp_prom_stats
params.doc: Specifies which internal statistics from Kamailio to show. Possible values: * all - Show whole Kamailio statistics * group_name: - Show all statistics for a group * statistic_name - Show a specific statistic. It automatically finds the group.

params.name: xhttp_prom_pkg_stats
params.doc: Enable or disable internal Kamailio pkg memory statistics.

params.name: xhttp_prom_uptime_stat
params.doc: Enable or disable Kamailio uptime statistic.

params.name: xhttp_prom_beginning
params.doc: Specifies beginning of string the metrics are build with.

params.name: xhttp_prom_metadata_flags
params.doc: Flags to enable Prometheus metadata lines in the output. The flags are defined as a bitmask on an integer value. Bits have the following meaning: * 1 - include TYPE metadata string for user defined metrics. Metrics generated from Kamailio statistics are untyped and can't have TYPE metadata. Example 1.7. xhttp_prom_metadata_flags TYPE example

params.name: xhttp_prom_tags
params.doc: Specifies additional tags for the metrics. These can be useful for evaluating the metrics afterwards.

params.name: prom_counter
params.doc: Create a counter metric.

params.name: prom_gauge
params.doc: Create a gauge metric.

params.name: prom_histogram
params.doc: Create a histogram metric.

functions.name: prom_counter_reset
functions.doc: Get a counter based on its name and labels and reset its value to 0. Name parameter is mandatory. Values of labels are optional (from none up to three). Name in prom_counter_reset has to match same name in prom_counter parameter. Number of labels in prom_counter_reset has to match number of labels in prom_counter parameter. First time a counter is used with this reset function the counter is created if it does not exist already.

functions.name: prom_gauge_reset
functions.doc: Get a gauge based on its name and labels and reset its value to 0. Name parameter is mandatory. Values of labels are optional (from none up to three). Name in prom_gauge_reset has to match same name in prom_gauge parameter. Number of labels in prom_gauge_reset has to match number of labels in prom_gauge parameter. First time a gauge is used with this reset function the gauge is created if it does not exist already.

functions.name: prom_counter_inc
functions.doc: Get a counter identified by its name and labels and increase its value by a number. If counter does not exist it creates the counter, initializes it to zero and adds the number.

functions.name: prom_gauge_inc
functions.doc: Get a gauge identified by its name and labels and increase (or decrease, if amount is negative) its value by a given amount. If gauge does not exist it creates the gauge and assigns the value to it.

functions.name: prom_gauge_set
functions.doc: Get a gauge identified by its name and labels and set its value to a number. If gauge does not exist it creates the gauge and assigns the value to it.

functions.name: prom_histogram_observe
functions.doc: Get a histogram identified by its name and labels and observe a value in it. If histogram does not exist it creates the histogram and accumulate the value in its buckets, counter and sum.

functions.doc: Check if path of HTTP URL equals /metrics. This avoids us to check hu variable from xHTTP module.

params.doc: Specifies the root path for RPC http requests. The link to the RPC web interface must be constructed using the following pattern: http://[server_IP]:[tcp_port]/[xhttp_rpc_root]

params.name: xhttp_rpc_buf_size
params.doc: Specifies the maximum length of the buffer (in bytes) used to write the RPC reply information in order to build the HTML response.

params.name: buf_size
params.doc: Maximum size of the log message.

params.name: force_color
params.doc: When set to 1, forces color codes in log messages even if log_stderror is set to 0.

params.name: long_format
params.doc: When set to 1, outputs the configuration file name in xlogl() and xdbgl() before the line number.

params.name: prefix
params.doc: Prefix to be output before the log message.

params.name: prefix_mode
params.doc: control behaviour of prefix value. if mode = 0 then prefix is treated as string (current behaviour). if mode = 1 then prefix is treated as pv_format specifier and value will be evaluated before output.

params.name: log_facility
params.doc: Syslog facility to be used for the xlog output. By setting this, and configuring syslog, you can get the xlog messages in a separate syslog file than the debug messages issued from the source code.

params.name: log_colors
params.doc: Update terminal colors used by the Kamailio core for log levels (when log_stderr=1 and log_color=1). The value has to be 'logname=colors', where colors is two characters specifying foreground and background in the same format as $C(xy) variable.

params.name: methods_filter
params.doc: The bitmask with internal SIP method ids to be ignored by xlogm() function. The value can be changed at runtime via cfg reload framework:

functions.doc: Output a formatted log message.

functions.name: xdbg
functions.doc: Print a formatted message using DBG function.

functions.name: xinfo
functions.doc: Print a formatted log message at L_INFO level.

functions.name: xnotice
functions.doc: Print a formatted log message at L_NOTICE level.

functions.name: xwarn
functions.doc: Print a formatted log message at L_WARN level.

functions.doc: Similar to xlog(), in addition prints configuration file line number at the beginning of message.

params.name: buf_size
params.doc: Maximum size of the XML buffer.

params.name: xml_ns
params.doc: Register xml namespace prefix. Parameter value must have the format: 'prefix=uri'. It can be set many times to cope with multiple namespaces without prefix.

params.name: route
params.doc: Name of the route called for XMLRPC messages.

params.name: autoconversion
params.doc: Enable or disable automatic parameter type conversion globally, for all the methods parameters. If on, a type mismatch in a method parameter will not cause a fault if it is possible to automatically convert it to the type expected by the method.

params.name: escape_cr
params.doc: Enable CR ('\r') escaping in replies. If enabled each '\r' in the xmlrpc reply will be replaced with "", according to the xml spec.

params.name: double_lf_to_crlf
params.doc:
When enabled double LFs ('

') in the input xmlrpc strings will be replaced with CR LF ('
'). This makes LF LF behave like an escape character for CR LF and is needed for compatibility with Kamailio tools and to work around buggy xmlrpc clients that don't escape the CR in CR LF ('' should be escaped to "" otherwise according to the xml spec "
" will be transformed to '
'), but need to send CR LF in the strings (e.g. they use tm.t_uac_wait).

params.name: mode
params.doc: When set to 1, the xmlrpc module does not register to core the callback functions for non-SIP messages. Useful when another module registers a callback for HTTP request, letting the admin decide when to call the XMLRPC route (or functions).

params.name: url_skip
params.doc: Regular expression to match the HTTP URL. If there is a match, then the xmlrpc route is not executed.

params.name: url_match
params.doc: Regular expression to match the HTTP URL. If there is no match, then xmlrpc route is not executed. This check is done after url_skip, so if both url_skip and url_match would match then the xmlrpc route is not executed (url_skip has higher priority).

params.name: event_callback
params.doc: The name of the function in the kemi configuration file (embedded scripting language such as Lua, Python, ...) to be executed instead of route blocks defined by route parameter for xmlrpc request.

functions.name: dispatch_rpc
functions.doc: This function processes an XMLRPC request, found in the body of the request.

functions.name: xmlrpc_reply
functions.doc: This function can be called from the config script to directly generate an XML-RPC reply.

params.name: backend
params.doc: The mode you are using the module; it can be either "component" or "server".

params.name: domain_separator
params.doc: In the destination address we need an extra character as a domain separator, apart from @. The address of the XMPP(jabber) client looks like this: "sip:usernamejabber_server@gateway_sip_domain". The address of a SIP client has the following pattern : "sip_usernamesip_domain@gateway_xmpp_domain"; A common used character in XMPP transports is "%".

params.name: gateway_domain
params.doc: The domain of the SIP-to-XMPP gateway - it has to be in DNS or SIP UA has to use outbound proxy to SIP-to-XMPP gateway IP address. It has to be used as domain in the destination address of the messages sent by SIP users to XMPP users: "sip:usernamejabber_server@gateway_domain".

params.name: xmpp_domain
params.doc: The XMPP domain of the component or the server, depending on the mode. It can be the same as the gateway_domain. For a server DNS name, you have to add _xmpp-server._tcp SRV records in your DNS zone to enable connections from other XMPP servers.

params.name: xmpp_host
params.doc: The IP address or the hostname for the local XMPP/Jabber server to connect to when the backend is set to "component". For server mode, this is the IP address the XMPP module binds to listen for connections coming from other XMPP servers.

params.name: xmpp_port
params.doc: In component mode, this is the port the XMPP server component interface listens to. In server mode, this is the port the module listens to.

params.name: xmpp_password
params.doc: The password of the local XMPP server.

params.name: outbound_proxy
params.doc: The SIP address used as next hop when sending the message. Very useful when using Kamailio with a domain name not in DNS, or when using a separate Kamailio instance for XMPP processing. If not set, the message will be sent to the address in destination URI.

params.name: gwmap
params.doc: Set the mappings between SIP and XMPP domains. This parameter can be set many times, adding more SIP-XMPP domain mappings. Its value has to be a list of tokens like 'sipdomain=xmppdomain', separated by ';' (e.g., 'sipdomain1=xmppdomain1;sipdomain2=xmppdomain2'.

functions.name: xmpp_send_message
functions.doc: Converts SIP messages to XMPP(jabber) messages, in order to be relayed to a XMPP(jabber) client.
